Returns whether the orbit represented by this object is hyperbolic. A hyperbolic orbit is an orbit with enough speed to escape the central body’s gravitational pull. More specifically, this occurs in orbit’s with an eccentricity value greater than 1.

Returns whether the orbit represented by this object is circular. A circular orbit is an orbit in which the distance, speed, and angular speed are all constant. It is evaluated as having an eccentricity value near 0.

Returns whether the orbit represented by this object is equatorial. An equatorial orbit is an orbit that lies close to the equatorial plane. In terms of orbital elements, it is an orbit with an inclination of 0 or pi degrees.

Returns whether the orbit represented by this object is prograde. A prograde orbit is an orbit in which the satellite moves in the direction opposite the rotation of the central body. In terms of orbital elements, it is an orbit with an inclination of less than pi / 2.

Determines if the calling comm interface can communicate with the specified receiver. This check is model specific, such that this determination is based on the implementation of the comm doing the call. Return a new instance of a WsfConstellationMaker that can be used to generate a general constellation. If there are any input arguments that are out of range, this method will print a message and return an invalid object.

Return a new instance of a WsfConstellationMaker that can be used to generate Walker Delta constellations. These constellations are defined by the total number of satellites, the number of planes, and the inter-plane phasing parameter, f. If the total number of satellites is not evenly divisible by the number of planes, or if the f parameter is not between zero and the number of planes minus one, then this method will return an invalid object.

Creates a platform template of the specified type containing a space mover with a sun-synchronous orbit. The orbital elements of the space mover are set such that the mean circular altitude is aAltitude (in meters) and the local time of the descending node (LTDN) is aLTDN (in hours). The aEpoch refers to the time at which the platform will be added to the simulation (see example below). The mover will be initialized with a true anomaly of zero. In other words, the platform will be injected at the ascending node. The return value is a reference to the created platform template. The WsfPlatform object that is returned can subsequently be populated with the desired attributes and added to the simulation using WsfSimulation.AddPlatform.

This method applies a force with magnitude equal to aMagnitude (in lbs) with an angle of aAngle (deg) to the nose wheel of the model. This method is only intended to be used on ground operations and is useful to simulate pushing back from the gate or towing an aircraft. It can also be used to simulate a catapult on an aircraft carrier. An angle of 0 deg represents a force being pushed against the nose wheel such that the plane will back up, while a force at an angle of 180 will make the aircraft roll forward. If the model does not have landing gear, this function will not do anything. The force is applied until WsfP6DOF_Mover.RemoveExternalForce is called.

This will make the vehicle fall out of control. It allows a realistic crash motion rather than simply removing a dead vehicle. Add a time delay to perception updating or any other cognitive task. This method applies a force with magnitude equal to aMagnitude (in Newtons) with an angle of aAngle (deg) to the nose wheel of the model. This method is only intended to be used on ground operations and is useful to simulate pushing back from the gate or towing an aircraft. It can also be used to simulate a catapult on an aircraft carrier. An angle of 0 deg represents a force being pushed against the nose wheel such that the plane will back up, while a force at an angle of 180 will make the aircraft roll forward. If the model does not have landing gear, this function will not do anything. The force is applied until WsfRigidBodySixDOF_Mover.RemoveExternalForce is called.

Returns the name of the perception master track processor (PMTP). If no such track processor exists, an empty string will be returned. The PMTP is an optional track processor that can be used to augment the master track processor (MTP) of the platform. In many cases, the PMTP includes feeds from more sensors and/or track processors than the MTP – in particular, it often includes eye sensors (aircrew eyesight) that do not route their tracks to the MTP. By using the a PMTP, additional perception can be provided by visual sensors (eyesight) that are not avionics and hence do not have an “electronic path” to the MTP.

This returns the 2D angle-off between the target and the platform (the difference in headings). This calculates angle-off as the angle between the headings of the target and the platform. A positive angle-off is when the difference in between the target heading and the platform heading is positive and is less than or equal to Pi. If the difference is negative and is greater than negative Pi, the angle-off is negative. The angle is in degrees.

This returns the 2D angle-off between the target and the current platform (the difference in headings). This calculates angle-off as the angle between the headings of the target and the platform. A positive angle-off is when the difference in between the target heading and the platform heading is positive and is less than or equal to Pi. If the difference is negative and is greater than negative Pi, the angle-off is negative. The angle is in degrees.

This returns the 3D angle-off between the target and the platform (the difference in heading/velocity). This calculates angle-off as the angle between the velocity vectors of the target and the platform. A positive angle-off is when the target is to the right of the platform. This is determined based on the y-vector of the platform. If the dot-product of the target’s velocity vector and the platform’s right side vector is positive, it is considered a positive angle-off. When the dot-product is negative, the angle-off is a negative value. The angle is in degrees.

This returns the 3D angle-off between the target and the current platform (the difference in heading/velocity). This calculates angle-off as the angle between the velocity vectors of the target and the platform. A positive angle-off is when the target is to the right of the platform. This is determined based on the y-vector of the platform. If the dot-product of the target’s velocity vector and the platform’s right side vector is positive, it is considered a positive angle-off. When the dot-product is negative, the angle-off is a negative value. The angle is in degrees.

This returns the aspect-angle for the target relative to the platform’s position in 2D, meaning the aspect is based on a horizontal plane that contains the target, with the platform’s position projected onto the plane. A positive angle is the “right side” of the target and a negative angle is “left side” of the target. The angle is in degrees.

This returns the aspect-angle for the target relative to the current platform’s position in 2D, meaning the aspect is based on a horizontal plane that contains the target, with the platform’s position projected onto the plane. A positive angle is the “right side” of the target and a negative angle is “left side” of the target. The angle is in degrees.

This returns the aspect-angle for the target relative to the platform’s position in 3D, meaning the aspect is based on the angle between a 3D vector opposite of the target’s velocity vector and the vector from the target to the platform’s position. Right side (positive) and left side (negative) is determined based on the y-vector of the target aircraft. If the vector dot-product of the target y-vector and the vector towards the platform is positive, it is considered “right side”. The angle is measured in degrees.

This returns the aspect-angle for the target relative to the current platform’s position in 3D, meaning the aspect is based on the angle between a 3D vector opposite of the target’s velocity vector and the vector from the target to the platform’s position. Right side (positive) and left side (negative) is determined based on the y-vector of the target aircraft. If the vector dot-product of the target y-vector and the vector towards the platform is positive, it is considered “right side”. The angle is measured in degrees.

A special use case to launch a cyber attack. Typically, cyber attacks are initiated from the platform scope against a target platform. However, not all cyber attacks fit this definition, such as in the case of embedded cyber. The AFSIM cyber framework considers such attacks as self-inflicted, as in the attacking platform is the same as the victim. This method allows self-targeting cyber attacks for use cases such as embedded cyber, from the global scope. The target platform ‘aTarget’ is also the attacker in this method, and uses the attack type ‘aAttackType’. ‘aAttackType’ must be a valid cyber_attack type.

This will disband the formation with the given name. Disbanding a formation will destroy that formation and all its descendant sub-formations. This sets the controls for the control stick (aStickBack and aStickRight), rudder pedals (aRudderRight) and throttle levers (aThrottles). Control stick and rudder pedal values range from -1 (full left or forward) to zero (neutral) to +1 (full right or back). Throttle values range from 0 (idle) to 1 (non-augmented, military power) to 2 (full afterburner). This function requires that TakeDirectControlInput be called prior to use.

Fires the weapon with or without a current track. This method returns ‘true’ if a launch has been successfully scheduled. Some weapons may have a delay between the time when a fire command is issued and the actual time of launch. A successful weapon launch will trigger a WEAPON_FIRED event. This method returns ‘false’ if a launch cannot be scheduled due to several reasons, such as, the weapon quantity is 0, the launch interval has not elapsed, the weapon is reloading and it cannot shoot while reloading, or the weapon is damaged. Additional checks at the time of launch may still result in a launch failure triggering a WEAPON_FIRE_ABORTED event.

subCommands.name: default_sensor
subCommands.description: Specify the name of a default Sensor type definition that will be used to generate the access reports (only in the case where no <sensor-name> is provided in report command specifications). If this command is provided, the sensor type will be cloned and added to the specified <detector-platform>.

subCommands.name: file_prefix
subCommands.description: Specify the output file prefix. The file extension is specified by the file_format command.

subCommands.name: file_format
subCommands.description: Specify the output file format, which must be either of csv (comma-separated variables) or tsv (tab-separated variables).

subCommands.name: report
subCommands.syntax: report { <detector-platform> | all } to { <detectee-platform> | all } [ using { <sensor-name> | all } ]
subCommands.description: Specify which access events are to be reported in the output file. Selections for each detector-detectee pair should be provided. optionally, a sensor name on the detector can also be specified, in which case access is only computed for that particular sensor. If no sensor is specified, all sensors on the detecting platform will be used to compute access separately. For each selection, the keyword all can be inserted, meaning that access will be computed for all detectors, detectees, and / or sensors.

acoustic_signature.description: Name to be given to the signature. This must be unique among all acoustic signatures. A particular signature may be redefined, with the last definition being used.

subCommands.name: data_reference_range
subCommands.description: The reference range that the following acoustic data was calculated or measured at. This value is used to adjust the following acoustic data to a zero slant range value.

subCommands.name: state
subCommands.description: Indicates that the following table definition will be used when the platform is in the signature state <state-name>. If default is specified then the subsequent table will be used if the platform is in a signature state that does not match any of the states defined in the signature.

subCommands.name: freq
subCommands.description: 1/3 octave center frequency of signature value.

subCommands.name: noise_pressure
subCommands.description: Acoustic noise pressure (dB/20 uPa) at specified 1/3 octave center frequency.

subCommands.name: name
subCommands.description: Name the node. The new name will be displayed on the node in the Behavior Tree View in Mystic.

subCommands.name: desc
subCommands.description: Define a description for the node. This will show when the node is hovered over in the Behavior Tree View in Mystic.

subCommands.name: color
subCommands.description: Set the color to display as a platform trace line in Mystic to indicate when the behavior is running.

advanced_behavior_tree.description: Advanced Behavior Trees build upon Behavior Trees, allowing for 3 states (Running, Success, Failure) rather than two (Success, Failure). The addition of a third state allows the AI to be more complex and reactive.

subCommands.name: selector
subCommands.description: Selector nodes execute all children in order (top to bottom in script, left to right in the behavior tree tool). If any child succeeds, the selector will succeed and all children after it will be skipped (they are not considered by the tree). If all children fail, the selector will fail.

subCommands.name: selector_with_memory
subCommands.description: Selector nodes with memory work exactly like normal selector nodes with one caveat: If a node fails the selector will move memory forward, and will not check that child until memory is reset. Memory is reset when a node succeeds, or all children fail.

subCommands.name: sequence
subCommands.description: Sequence nodes execute all children in order (top to bottom in script, left to right in the behavior tree tool). If any child fails its precondition or execute script, the sequence will fail and all children after it will be skipped (they are not considered by the tree). If all children succeed, the sequence will succeed.

subCommands.name: sequence_with_memory
subCommands.description: Sequence nodes with memory work exactly like normal sequence nodes with one caveat: If a node succeeds the sequence will move memory forward, and will not check that child until memory is reset. Memory is reset when a node fails, or all children succeed.

subCommands.name: parallel
subCommands.description: Parallel nodes will execute all children at the same time, regardless of ordering. Parallel nodes make use of a success policy to determine success/failure (See the success_policy command below) If all children have finished executing and the policy has not been hit, the parallel node will fail. By default, parallel nodes use succeed_on_one, which means only one child node needs to succeed for the parallel node to succeed.

subCommands.name: priority_selector
subCommands.description: Priority-Selector nodes choose and execute whichever child is highest valued. The value of a child is determined by its precondition script block. Priority-Selector nodes always execute their highest valued child.

subCommands.name: weighted_random
subCommands.description: Weighted-Random nodes are connector nodes used in the behavior tree in order to randomly choose and execute a child. A uniform weighted random selection is performed, and the weights for each child are determined by their precondition script blocks. For example, if a Weighted-Random node has two children and both return a value of “3”, then they are equally likely to be chosen.

subCommands.name: decorator
subCommands.description: Inverter nodes will invert the return status of its child node. If the child returns success, the inverter will return failure, and if the child returns failure, the inverter will return success.

subCommands.name: name
subCommands.description: Name the tree. This will display on the root node and in the tree selection combo box in the Behavior Tree View in Mystic.

subCommands.name: desc
subCommands.description: Define a description for the tree. This will show when the root node is hovered over in the Behavior Tree View in Mystic.

subCommands.name: btt
subCommands.description: Define whether or not the tree sends the required data to show a tree in the Behavior Tree View in Mystic.

subCommands.name: root_node_type
subCommands.syntax: root_node_type [parallel | priority_selector | selector | selector_with_memory | sequence | sequence_with_memory | weighted_random ]
subCommands.description: Set the composite node type for the root node of this tree.

subCommands.name: success_policy
subCommands.description: Sets the success_policy for a parallel node or an advanced_behavior_tree using root_node_type parallel. Three policies may be set for handling success on a parallel node: Threshold will take an integer amount of nodes that must succeed for the parallel node to succeed. Succeed_on_one will make the parallel node succeed if any child succeeds. Succeed_on_all will make the parallel node succeed only if all children succeed.

subCommands.name: debug
subCommands.description: Enables debug printouts during run time.

subCommands.name: reference_area
subCommands.description: Aerodynamic reference area. This is usually the platform (top view) wing area for an airplane. The reference area is a means to translate a non-dimensional force coefficient into an actual force (force equals coefficient times dynamic pressure times reference area).

subCommands.name: aspect_ratio
subCommands.description: Aspect ratio (AR) for a wing is the wingspan squared divided by its area, a non-dimensional quantity. A higher value tends to produce lift more efficiently, with a lesser quantity of induced drag (drag due to lift). Sailplanes (gliders) are designed with very long slender wings to minimize induced drag. For subsonic airplanes, it is often acceptable to use an idealized parabolic drag polar approximating reality: Cd = Cdo + k * Cl^2, where k = 1.0 / (Pi * AR * e)

subCommands.name: oswalds_factor
subCommands.description: Oswald’s efficiency factor (usually designated e) is an empirically determined value to calculate an amount of induced drag inevitably associated with generation of lift, approximated per the following equation: Cd = Cdo + k * Cl^2, where k = 1.0 / (Pi * AR * e), Cdo is zero-lift drag coefficient, AR is Aspect Ratio, e is Oswald’s factor, Cl is lift coefficient, and Cd is total drag coefficient. (For Oswald’s factor, it is not likely that any but an experienced aerodynamic engineer will have knowledge of what this value is for a given vehicle, so accepting the default is recommended.)

subCommands.name: cl_max
subCommands.description: Lift Coefficient Maximum. This value specifies the maximum lift aerodynamically obtainable by the vehicle. Full airplane Clmax tend to be 1.4 or so.

subCommands.name: zero_lift_cd
subCommands.description: Zero-lift drag coefficient. Single value given for low-speed aerodynamics only, when flow is incompressible.

subCommands.name: mach_and_cd
subCommands.description: Mach number and corresponding Cdo at that Mach number. Specify a drag table by supplying this keyword multiple times, in increasing Mach numbers.

subCommands.name: cd_zero_subsonic
subCommands.description: Zero-lift drag coefficient, just prior to transonic drag rise region. The corresponding Mach number at which this drag rise begins is specified using mach_begin_cd_rise.

subCommands.name: mach_begin_cd_rise
subCommands.description: Mach number at which a transonic drag rise begins. This value must be less than 1.0, and is typically about 0.78 to 0.86. The corresponding drag coefficient at which this drag rise begins is specified using cd_zero_subsonic.

subCommands.name: cd_zero_supersonic
subCommands.description: Zero-lift drag coefficient at the end of the transonic drag rise. The corresponding Mach number at which this drag rise ends is specified using mach_end_cd_rise.

subCommands.name: mach_end_cd_rise
subCommands.description: Mach number at which a transonic drag rise ends. This value must be greater than 1.0, and is typically in the 1.05 to 1.2 region. At Mach numbers greater than this value, Cdo values often begin decreasing, but total drag still increases because of the velocity quadratic relationship. The corresponding drag coefficient at which this drag rise ends is specified using cd_zero_supersonic.

subCommands.name: subsonic_cd_slope
subCommands.description: Change in zero-lift drag coefficient with increasing Mach number, in the region below the transonic drag rise.

subCommands.name: supersonic_cd_slope
subCommands.description: Change in zero-lift drag coefficient with increasing Mach number, in the region above the transonic drag rise. This value may be positive or negative.

subCommands.name: mach_max_supersonic
subCommands.description: Specify this value to arrest a continuous rise or decline in drag coefficient with increasing Mach number, in the region above the transonic drag rise. If the Mach number is higher than this specified value, the zero-lift drag coefficient will be held constant.

minimum_range.description: The shortest engagement range that will be tested. DEFAULT = 1000 meters.

subCommands.name: maximum_range
subCommands.description: The longest engagement range that will be tested. DEFAULT = 120,000 meters.

subCommands.name: range_tolerance
subCommands.description: This is a convergence test value; if two engagement ranges are found which bracket [success, failure], and they differ by less than the tolerance value, the transition edge is considered found.

subCommands.name: maximum_iterations
subCommands.description: This is a terminate search constraint; if convergence is not attained within this many iterations per engagement, iteration is stopped for the engagement.

subCommands.name: aircraft_type
subCommands.description: Define the attributes of an aircraft that can be controlled by the air_traffic manager. The <aircraft-type> name must already be a previously defined platform_type.

subCommands.name: minimum_cruise_altitude
subCommands.description: The minimum altitude this aircraft type can cruise at.

subCommands.name: maximum_cruise_altitude
subCommands.description: The maximum altitude this aircraft type can cruise at.

subCommands.name: mean_cruise_speed
subCommands.description: The average speed this aircraft type will cruise at.

subCommands.name: sigma_cruise_speed
subCommands.description: The speed magnitude of one standard deviation.

subCommands.name: maximum_operating_range
subCommands.description: The maximum distance this aircraft type can fly, which is used to determine what airbases it can fly to.

subCommands.name: minimum_runway_length
subCommands.description: The minimum runway length that this aircraft type can land on, which is used to determine what airbases it can fly to.

subCommands.name: local
subCommands.description: Indicates that this aircraft can be used for local flights.

subCommands.name: mean_loiter_time
subCommands.description: The amount of time this aircraft type will loiter, once it arrives at the local_destination.

subCommands.name: sigma_loiter_time
subCommands.description: The time magnitude of one standard deviation.

subCommands.name: loiter_route
subCommands.description: A loiter pattern that this aircraft will perform once it reaches its local_destination. Note: specify multiple loiter_route commands to use different loiter patterns.

subCommands.name: airbase
subCommands.description: Define the attributes of an airbase from which aircraft can depart or arrive. The airbase block may be specified as many times as necessary to define all of the airbases. The <airbase-name> specifies the name of the airbase. This must be unique within the air traffic definition. The <latitude> <longitude> specifies the latitude and longitude of the airbase. Note: The platform type generated is named “Airbase”, so make sure not to reuse this type name.

subCommands.name: runway_length
subCommands.description: Specify the length of the runway. This command is not required if the runway command is specified.

subCommands.name: runway_heading
subCommands.description: Specify the heading of the runway. Takeoffs and landings will take place in this direction. This command is not required if the runway command is specified.

subCommands.name: runway
subCommands.description: Specify the end points of the runway. This command can be used to precisely specify the location of a runway. This command will override the runway_length and runway_heading commands.

subCommands.name: departure_interval
subCommands.description: This specifies the time interval of all the departures.

subCommands.name: deactivation_time
subCommands.description: This is an optional command that specifies when the airbase is to be ‘deactivated’. This can be used to simulate a situation at the airbase that prevents further arrivals or departures. Aircraft that are currently enroute will be diverted to another airbase.

subCommands.name: aircraft
subCommands.description: Define the fraction (in the range (0..1]) of the traffic that departs from the airbase that will be of the specified type. NOTE: The sum of all of the <fraction> values for a given airbase must be 1.

subCommands.name: destination
subCommands.description: Define the fraction of the traffic that departs from this airbase that will fly to the specified destination. The sum of all of the <fraction> values for a given airbase destinations must be 1. In addition, the aircraft must be listed in the destination airbase definition.

subCommands.name: local_destination
subCommands.description: Specifies a local destination where locally departing aircraft will fly to and loiter. The third argument is the diameter of the region centered about the specified latitude and longitude. Many local_destinations can be specified, however, the sum of their <fractional-quantity>s must be 1.0

subCommands.name: everyone_land_time
subCommands.description: Specifies a time for ALL background air traffic to land.

subCommands.name: remove_completed_flights
subCommands.description: TBD

subCommands.name: side
subCommands.description: Specifies the side for which the aircraft signature parameters apply. The available options are ‘red’ and ‘blue’.

subCommands.name: fuselage_frontal_area
subCommands.description: The frontal area of the aircraft fuselage (projection on the y-z plane) to be used when determining the radar cross section. See Equation (2).

subCommands.name: wing_area
subCommands.description: The wing area of the aircraft to be used when determining the radar cross section. See Equation (2).

subCommands.name: tail_area
subCommands.description: The area of the aircraft’s vertical tail to be used when determining the radar cross section. See Equation (2).

subCommands.name: engine_inlet_area
subCommands.description: The inlet area of the aircraft’s engine to be used when determining the radar cross section. See Equation (2).

subCommands.name: engine_exit_area
subCommands.description: The exit area of the aircraft’s engine to be used when determining the radar cross section. See Equation (2).

subCommands.name: sweep_angle
subCommands.description: The sweep angle of the aircraft’s wing to be used when determining the radar cross section. See Equation (2).

subCommands.name: signature_reduction_factor_overall
subCommands.description: The overall reduction factor of the signature. See Equation (2).

subCommands.name: signature_reduction_factor_nose
subCommands.description: The reduction factor of the signature due to the aircraft’s nose shape. This factor is only used if nose_signature_reduction_angle is more than the azimuth and more than the elevation. See Equation (2).

subCommands.name: nose_signature_reduction_angle
subCommands.description: The nose angle used to determine signature_reduction_factor_nose. If nose_signature_reduction_angle is more than the azimuth and more than the elevation, then the effective radar cross section will be multiplied by signature_reduction_factor_nose.

azimuth_angle_limit.description: The maximum off-boresight angle in azimuth for which clutter returns will be computed.

subCommands.name: azimuth_angle_increment
subCommands.description: The azimuth angle increment used in computingclutter returns.

subCommands.name: maximum_range
subCommands.description: The maximum range at which clutter will be computed. Shorter ranges decrease execution time, especially for simulations utilizing terrain elevation data such as DTED.

subCommands.name: reflectivity
subCommands.description: The reflectivity value used when statistic is set to numerical.

subCommands.name: reflectivity_delta
subCommands.description: Delta clutter reflectivity value about reflectivity used only when statistic is set to numerical. The clutter reflectivity is uniformly randomly distributed over the range: reflectivity reflectivity_delta. This value is optional.

subCommands.name: statistic
subCommands.syntax: statistic [ mean | statistical | maximum | minimum | numerical ]
subCommands.description: Default mean

subCommands.name: random_seed
subCommands.description: The random number seed, only used when statistic is set to statistical, or numerical, with reflectivity_delta set. Random Seed : must be a large number (> 1000).

subCommands.name: sigmac
subCommands.description: Standard deviation of the Gaussian portion of the clutter PSD. Often referred to as the root mean squared clutter frequency spread. A suggested value is 10 Hz for land, and 50 Hz for sea (See ALARM documentation for details).

subCommands.name: decay_constant
subCommands.description: The quadratic decay constant for the inverse quadratic portion of the clutter power spectral density (PSD). A suggested value is 10-6 Hz2 (See ALARM documentation for details).

subCommands.name: use_legacy_data
subCommands.description: Specified whether to use an older set of tables of clutter strength. This older table set was used prior to the release of WSF 1.7.5.

subCommands.name: use_native_terrain_masking
subCommands.description: Specifies whether to use the native AFSIM terrain masking calculation, instead of ALARM’s.

subCommands.name: propagation
subCommands.description: Specify if the multipath propagation model should be used.

subCommands.name: diffraction
subCommands.description: Indicate if the spherical Earth/knife-edge diffraction model should be used.

subCommands.name: soil_moisture
subCommands.description: The percent [0 .. 100] of moisture in the soil.

subCommands.name: soil_moisture_fraction
subCommands.description: The fraction [0 .. 1] of moisture in the soil.

subCommands.name: stddev_surface_height
subCommands.description: Note

subCommands.name: epsilon_one
subCommands.description: Note

subCommands.name: sigma_zero
subCommands.description: Note

subCommands.name: roughness_factor
subCommands.description: Note

subCommands.name: sea_relaxation
subCommands.description: Note

subCommands.name: sea_wind_speed
subCommands.description: Note

subCommands.name: water_temperature
subCommands.description: Note

subCommands.name: water_type
subCommands.description: Default sea

subCommands.name: alternate_locations_global_debug
subCommands.description: If set to ‘on’, enables the global alternate locations debug flag. If set to ‘off’, disables the global debug flag for alternate locations. This setting may be overridden by the debug command within individual blocks. Output for each platform is of the following format:

subCommands.name: alternate_locations_use_global_draw
subCommands.description: If set to ‘on’, directs all alternate locations blocks to use the same draw. Since some blocks may have varying numbers of locations, this is roughly equivalent to choosing a percentile which all blocks will use. If the shared draw is (for example) .32, it will be treated as the 32nd percentile. For a block with three locations, equally-weighted, the first block will be chosen. A block with four, five, or six equally-weighted locations, would choose the second block. Finally, consider a block with unequally-weighted locations, say, [1, 1, 4, 3, 1]. This block would select the third index (spanning from 20.01 to the 60th percentile).

subCommands.name: alternate_locations_global_draw
subCommands.description: If set to a value in the range [0…1], will specify the global draw value to be used in place of the single randomized global draw if alternate_locations_use_global_draw is enabled. If set to -1, a random value will be used. In either case, the draw values will be individually weighted by the sum of location weights specified in each block.

subCommands.name: location
subCommands.syntax: location <latitude-value> <longitude-value> altitude <length-value> [ agl | msl ] heading <angle-value> weight <real-value>
subCommands.description: Adds a new location (required: latitude, longitude; optional: altitude, heading, weight) to the list of locations from which this platform may choose. Altitude, heading, and weight may be provided in any order. Dividing the location’s weight by the sum of all weights in the list yields the location’s probability of being chosen.

subCommands.name: debug
subCommands.description: If set to ‘on’, enables debug output for this block. If set to ‘off’, disables debug output for this block. Takes precedence over the global debug flag.

subCommands.name: reference
subCommands.description: Specifies the reference platform for the alternate_locations block which specifies either the location from which offsets will be applied or the location index which will be used.

subCommands.name: offset_lla
subCommands.description: Specifies a latitude and longitude (altitude and heading optional) from the location chosen by the <reference-platform>. Latitude, longitude, and altitude are offsets with respect to the <reference-platform>; heading sets the current platform’s absolute heading. This command must be the only location specification entry within an alternate_locations block.

subCommands.name: offset_ara
subCommands.description: Specifies a great-circle angle (0 degrees is due north), radius, and altitude offset from the location chosen by the <reference-platform>. The radius indicates the distance away from the <reference-platform> - at the angle provided - to place the new platform. The altitude indicates any change in altitude from the <reference-platform>’s altitude. Altitude and heading are optional; heading is absolute, not relative. This command must be the only location specification entry within an alternate_locations block.

subCommands.name: ignore
subCommands.description: Indicates the sensor should ignore detection attempts against objects that are a member of the specified category. This command may be specified multiple times to ignore multiple categories.

subCommands.name: ignore_domain
subCommands.syntax: ignore_domain [ land | air | surface | subsurface | space ]
subCommands.description: Indicates the sensor should ignore detection attempts against platforms or objects contained on platforms that are of the specified spatial domain. This command may be specified multiple times to ignore multiple domain.

subCommands.name: ignore_side
subCommands.description: Indicates the sensor should ignore detection attempts against platforms or objects contained on platforms that are of the specified side. This command may be specified multiple times to ignore multiple sides.

subCommands.name: ignore_same_side
subCommands.description: Indicates the sensor should ignore detection attempts against platforms or objects contained on platforms that are on the same side of the platform to which the sensor is attached.

subCommands.name: ignore_nothing
subCommands.description: Has the effect of canceling the effect of any previous ignore, ignore_domain, ignore_side and ignore_same_side commands. This is useful if one wants to reuse a sensor definition with embedded ‘ignore’ commands but wished to eliminate or change what is ignored.

subCommands.name: message_length
subCommands.description: Specifies the logical length assigned to the track messages that are created from the sensor.

subCommands.name: message_priority
subCommands.description: Specifies the priority assigned to the track messages that are created from the sensor.

subCommands.name: modifier_category
subCommands.description: The category that maps to the Zone-based attenuation value defined in the zone_set. Setting this value tells the sensor to evaluate zones for attenuation.

subCommands.name: mode_template
subCommands.description: Defines the default values for the modes of the sensor. When a new mode is defined it is first populated with the values from the mode template. This is useful when a sensor has multiple modes and the parameters for each mode are the same with the exception of a few values.

subCommands.name: mode
subCommands.description: Defines a mode, which is nothing more than a selectable set of parameters. The initial or default values of a mode are defined by the mode_template (if provided).

subCommands.name: selection_mode
subCommands.description: Indicates if the sensor supports the simultaneous operation of multiple modes.

subCommands.name: initial_mode
subCommands.description: The operation of this command depends on if selection_mode is single or multiple.

subCommands.name: mode_select_delay
subCommands.description: Specifies the delay when selecting modes.

subCommands.name: OnSensorDetectionAttempt
subCommands.description: Defines an optional script that imposes additional detection constraints on a sensor model. This script is invoked immediately after a detection attempt occurs but prior to any SENSOR_DETECTION_ATTEMPT events in the observer. As a result, the WsfSensorInteraction parameter includes any relevant calculations from the sensor’s inbuilt detection checks and represents what the result would have been if this script was not defined.

subCommands.name: required_pd
subCommands.description: Specifies the constant ‘required_pd’ value to be used if the value of the global simulation command use_constant_required_pd was specified as true. This is applicable only for sensors which implement probabilistic detectors (e.g., The optional Marcum-Swerling detector in WSF_RADAR_SENSOR).

subCommands.name: cue_mode
subCommands.syntax: cue_mode [ fixed | azimuth | elevation | both | azimuth_and_elevation]
subCommands.description: This command, along with azimuth_cue_limits and elevation_cue_limits can be used to limit the cueing capabilities for a particular mode to something less than those which were defined by the articulated part. For instance, a sensor may physically be able to cue in any direction but in a given mode may only cue in azimuth.

subCommands.name: azimuth_cue_limits
subCommands.description: Specifies the minimum and maximum angle about which the sensor can be cued in azimuth. These values are applicable only if cue_mode is azimuth or both. The limits are specified in the subsystem coordinate frame.

subCommands.name: elevation_cue_limits
subCommands.description: Specifies the minimum and maximum angle about which the sensor can be cued in elevation. These values are applicable only if cue_mode is elevation or both. The limits are specified in the subsystem coordinate frame.

subCommands.name: elevation_cue_rate
subCommands.description: Specifies the angular velocities to be employed when slewing the part to satisfy a cueing request. This is primarily used for modeling systems that track single target. It is not used for scanning systems and should not be used for multiple-target tracking systems.

subCommands.name: error_model
subCommands.description: error_model <base-name> …commands… end_error_model

subCommands.name: solar_exclusion_angle
subCommands.description: This sensor will not detect targets if the angle between its line-of-sight with the sun’s limb and the target is less than this value.

subCommands.name: lunar_exclusion_angle
subCommands.description: This sensor will not detect targets if the angle between its line-of-sight with the moon’s limb and the target is less than this value.

subCommands.name: target_solar_illumination_angle
subCommands.description: Defines the bounds of solar illumination required for the target to be detected.

subCommands.name: solar_elevation_at_target
subCommands.description: Defines the bounds of solar elevation at the target’s location required for the target to be detected.

subCommands.name: enable_moon_los_block
subCommands.description: If set to true, this sensor will not detect targets whose line-of-sight is blocked by the moon.

subCommands.name: update_interval
subCommands.description: This value is required when the scheduler is assigned a scheduler-type of physical_scan or sector_scan. It is used in conjunction with the frame_time value defined within the final mode that is read in from the input file for the sensor in order to calculate and physically sweep sectors for radar detections. For example, if the final frame-time value, which is read during the input loading sequence, is set to 20 sec, and if the update_interval is set to 2 sec, then 10 sectors are needed to sweep through 360 degrees during the 20-sec frame. For this example, each sector would cover 36 degrees of azimuth during each 2-sec update_interval.

subCommands.name: frame_time
subCommands.description: Specifies how long the sensor takes to perform one scan of its search volume. How this parameter is actually used depends on the actual sensor implementation. It also signifies how often a sensor detection is reported.

subCommands.name: maximum_request_count
subCommands.description: If this value is greater than zero then this mode only responds to explicit requests as initiated by WsfTaskManager::StartTracking.

subCommands.name: revisit_time
subCommands.description: If maximum_request_count is non-zero, this specifies how often the request should be revisited.

subCommands.name: dwell_time
subCommands.description: If maximum_request_count is non-zero, this specifies how long the sensor will dwell or otherwise take to perform a detection attempt associated with a request.

subCommands.name: search_while_track
subCommands.description: If maximum_request_count is non-zero, this indicates search mode requests can continue to be processed.

subCommands.name: disables_search
subCommands.description: If maximum_request_count is non-zero, this indicates that if this mode is selected then any detection attempts by search modes will be blocked.

subCommands.name: scheduler
subCommands.description: *<scheduler-type>* can be:

subCommands.name: debug_scheduler
subCommands.description: Enables output to the console window for scheduler data.

subCommands.name: range_rate_error_sigma
subCommands.description: Specifies the standard deviation for a Gaussian distribution for errors to be applied to position measurements from the sensor. The standard deviation may be specified as either an angle, length or speed value(as appropriate) or may be specified as a function of ‘percent_of_true_range’ for certain error types. In the latter case, the following formulas are used:

subCommands.name: hits_to_establish_track
subCommands.description: Indicates that <M> of the last <N> attempts to detect an object must be successful in order to establish a track.

subCommands.name: hits_to_maintain_track
subCommands.description: Once a track has been established, <M> of the last <N> attempts to detect an object must be successful in order to maintain a track.

subCommands.name: establish_track_probability
subCommands.description: When the M/N establish track criteria is met (see hits_to_establish_track), this is the probability that a track will be established.

subCommands.name: maintain_track_probability
subCommands.description: As long as the M/N maintain track criteria is met (see hits_to_maintain_track), this is the probability that the track will be maintained.

subCommands.name: reports_range
subCommands.description: The slant range from the sensor to the target is reported.

subCommands.name: reports_bearing
subCommands.description: The bearing from the sensor to the target is reported. This angle is measured in radians from the sensor’s north orientation, and it is in the range { -pi, pi }.

subCommands.name: reports_elevation
subCommands.description: The elevation angle from from the sensor to the target is reported.

subCommands.name: reports_location
subCommands.description: The location (latitude, longitude, altitude) of the target is reported.

subCommands.name: reports_velocity
subCommands.description: The velocity of the target is reported.

subCommands.name: reports_range_rate
subCommands.description: The range-rate of the target is reported.

subCommands.name: reports_iff
subCommands.description: The identify friend-or-foe (IFF) status is reported.

subCommands.name: reports_side
subCommands.description: The side of the target is reported.

subCommands.name: reports_type
subCommands.description: The type of the target is reported.

subCommands.name: reports_signal_to_noise
subCommands.description: The signal-to-noise ratio is reported.

subCommands.name: reports_frequency
subCommands.description: The frequency of the detected signal should be reported.

subCommands.name: reports_pulsewidth
subCommands.description: The pulse-width of the signal is reported.

subCommands.name: reports_pulse_repetition_interval
subCommands.description: The pulse-repetition interval of the signal is reported.

subCommands.name: reports_other
subCommands.description: Specifies what data elements will be reported in tracks from this sensor.

subCommands.name: reports_nothing
subCommands.description: Nothing is reported. This is the default behavior if no reporting flags are specified, and also has the effect of canceling any previous ‘reports_’ commands. This is useful if one wants to reuse an existing sensor definition with embedded ‘reports_’ commands but needs to change what is reported, or in situations where only the detected platform is needed in generated tracks.

subCommands.name: track_quality
subCommands.description: Specifies the ‘quality’ of the track when produced from this mode.

subCommands.name: send_track_drop_on_turn_off
subCommands.description: Indicates if ‘track drop’ messages should be sent for each active track when the sensor is turned off.

antenna_height.description: Defines the subsystem’s height relative to the platform it is attached to.

subCommands.name: antenna_tilt
subCommands.description: Defines the subsystem’s orientation in the pitch plane relative to the platform. This is primarily intended to specify the tilt angle of antenna for simple rotating systems.

subCommands.name: minimum_altitude
subCommands.description: Defines the minimum relative altitude the subsystem is able to observe a target.

subCommands.name: maximum_altitude
subCommands.description: Defines the maximum relative altitude the subsystem is able to observe a target.

subCommands.name: minimum_range
subCommands.description: Specify the minimum range at which the system can interact with another object.

subCommands.name: maximum_range
subCommands.description: Specifies the maximum range at which the subsystem can interact with another object.

subCommands.name: electronic_beam_steering
subCommands.syntax: electronic_beam_steering [ none | azimuth | elevation | both | azimuth_and_elevation ]
subCommands.description: Specifies that the subsystem uses an electronically-steered antenna that is capable of being electronically steered in the specified directions. When specified, the antenna gain is a function of the cosine of the angle relative to the array center. When enabled, the command affects the returned beamwidths of azimuth_beamwidth and elevation_beamwidth.

subCommands.name: electronic_beam_steering_loss_exponent
subCommands.description: Specifies the exponent that will be used in the beam steering loss computation.

subCommands.name: electronic_beam_steering_limit
subCommands.description: Specifies the angular limit that the electronic_beam_steering_loss_exponent will be applied.

subCommands.name: scan_mode
subCommands.syntax: scan_mode [ fixed | azimuth | elevation | both | azimuth_and_elevation]
subCommands.description: Indicates how the subsystem scans in respect to the current cue:

subCommands.name: scan_stabilization
subCommands.description: Specify if the scan volume (defined by the azimuth_scan_limits and elevation_scan_limits) are ‘stabilized’ to counter the effects of platform pitch and roll.

subCommands.name: azimuth_scan_limits
subCommands.description: Specify the minimum and maximum angle about which the subsystem can scan in azimuth. These values are applicable only if scan_mode is azimuth or both. The limits are with respect to the current cue.

subCommands.name: elevation_scan_limits
subCommands.description: Specify the minimum and maximum angle about which the subsystem can be scan in elevation. These values are applicable only if scan_mode is elevation or both. The limits are with respect to the current cue.

subCommands.name: azimuth_field_of_view
subCommands.description: Specify the minimum and maximum angle about which the subsystem can see in azimuth. The limits are with respect to the current cue. In general these values should be greater than or equal to the azimuth_scan_limits (possibly accounting for the width of the beam when the subsystem is positioned to its scan limit).

subCommands.name: elevation_field_of_view
subCommands.description: Specifies the minimum and maximum angle about which the subsystem can see in elevation. The limits are with respect to the current cue. In general these values should be greater than or equal to the elevation_scan_limits (possibly accounting for the width of the beam when the subsystem is positioned to its scan limit).

subCommands.name: field_of_view
subCommands.description: Specifies geometrical limits to determine if a subsystem can potentially interact with another object. Field of views are valid for anything that uses an electromagnetic antenna, including transmitter, receiver, and radar beams.

subCommands.name: minimum_gain
subCommands.description: The minimum gain that will be returned.

subCommands.name: gain_adjustment
subCommands.description: An adjustment factor to be applied to the raw gain. This is especially useful if one wants to reuse a pattern that has been defined by a file (such as the Azimuth/Elevation Table) and simply scale the definition.

subCommands.name: gain_adjustment_table
subCommands.description: This command provides the means to define a frequency-dependent adjustment to the gain. The points define a curve on a plot whose x-axis is the log_10 of the frequency and the y-axis is adjustment factor in dB. Linear interpolation is used to derive the values for intermediate frequencies. Signals whose frequencies are outside the range of the table use the value from the appropriate endpoint (i.e., extrapolation is not performed).

subCommands.name: azimuth_beamwidth
subCommands.description: Defines the width of the beam in azimuth.

subCommands.name: elevation_beamwidth
subCommands.description: Defines the width of the beam in elevation.

subCommands.name: peak_gain
subCommands.description: Defines the peak gain of the antenna referenced to a perfect isotropic antenna.

subCommands.name: beamwidth
subCommands.description: Defines the half-power beamwidth (The angle subtended by points at which the gain becomes one-half the peak gain).

subCommands.name: minimum_elevation_for_peak_gain
subCommands.description: Defines the minimum elevation angle for the peak_gain value.

subCommands.name: elevation_of_peak/csc2_boundary
subCommands.description: Defines the elevation angle for the peak cosecant-squared boundary value.

subCommands.name: maximum_elevation_for_csc2
subCommands.description: Defines the maximum elevation angle for the peak_gain value.

subCommands.name: debug
subCommands.description: Turn debug on.

subCommands.name: element_spacing_x
subCommands.description: The horizontal element spacing for the array. Requires number_elements_x OR length_x to be defined.

subCommands.name: element_spacing_y
subCommands.description: The vertical element spacing for the array. Requires number_elements_y OR length_y to be defined.

subCommands.name: length_x
subCommands.description: The total horizontal array length. Requires number_elements_x OR element_spacing_x to be defined.

subCommands.name: length_y
subCommands.description: The total vertical array length. Requires number_elements_y OR element_spacing_y to be defined.

subCommands.name: number_elements_x
subCommands.description: The number of individual elements in the horizontal direction of the array. Requires length_x OR element_spacing_x to be defined.

subCommands.name: number_elements_y
subCommands.description: The number of individual elements in the vertical direction of the array. Requires length_y OR element_spacing_y to be defined.

subCommands.name: amplitude_quantization_bits
subCommands.description: The number of bits used to quantize the amplitude response of each element in the array. The reference value is set to an amplitude of 1.

subCommands.name: phase_quantization_bits
subCommands.description: The number of bits used to quantize the phase response of each element in the array. The reference value is set to 2*pi radians (360 degrees).

subCommands.name: failed_elements_ratio
subCommands.description: The ratio of failed elements in the array.

subCommands.name: element_pattern
subCommands.description: Specifies the element pattern, via an antenna_pattern name, for all elements in the array.

subCommands.name: back_baffled
subCommands.description: Specifies whether the antenna elements are back baffled for azimuth angles outside [-90 90] degrees.

subCommands.name: lattice
subCommands.description: The lattice type to be used to define the element locations. Types are as as follows:

subCommands.name: distribution_type
subCommands.description: The weighting distribution to apply, available distributions are:

subCommands.name: sidelobe_level_x
subCommands.description: The sideobe level in the x-direction of the array in the range of 15 dB to 55 dB.

subCommands.name: sidelobe_level_y
subCommands.description: The sideobe level in the y-direction of the array in the range of 15 dB to 55 dB.

subCommands.name: n_bar_x
subCommands.description: The number of bars in the x-direction of the array in the range of [1, 2, …].

subCommands.name: n_bar_y
subCommands.description: The number of bars in the y-direction of the array in the range of [1, 2, …].

subCommands.name: file
subCommands.description: The name of the file containing the antenna pattern definition. file_path processing will be applied to the value.

subCommands.name: gain_correction
subCommands.description: An synonym for the gain_adjustment command.

subCommands.name: polarization
subCommands.description: Provide a polarization to match one or more polarizations specified in the antenna pattern file. This input is only necessary if polarizations are specified in the antenna pattern file; otherwise it should be omitted.

subCommands.name: edge_angle_x
subCommands.description: The element rotational shift about the Z-axis with respect to the x-axis. See Edge Angle Pictorial above.

subCommands.name: edge_angle_y
subCommands.description: The element rotational shift about the Z-axis with respect to the y-axis with angle specified from the x-axis. See Edge Angle Pictorial above.

subCommands.name: array_subdivision_table
subCommands.description: This block defines the X and Y subdivision ratios as a function of the beam count. When the system has multiple beams defined then the array is subdivided per the ratios in the table. Format is as follows:

subCommands.name: beam_count
subCommands.description: Specifies the beam count and ratios to apply in the x & y direction respectively. The array length and/or number of elements will be divided by this ratio. The <beam-count-integer-value> should be in the range [1, 2, .., N] in increasing order. The ratios must be greater than 0.0 and less than or equal to 1.0 .

subCommands.name: aperture_efficiencies
subCommands.description: Specifies the value for the aperture efficiencies for the horizontal and vertical (x-y) planes respectively, from 0 to 1.

subCommands.name: aperture_efficiency
subCommands.description: Specifies the single value for the aperture efficiency in the horizontal and vertical (x-y) plane from 0 to 1.

subCommands.name: average_element_spacing_x
subCommands.description: The average horizontal element spacing for the array. Requires number_elements_x OR length_x to be defined.

subCommands.name: average_element_spacing_y
subCommands.description: The average vertical element spacing for the array. Requires number_elements_y OR length_y to be defined.

subCommands.name: element_locations
subCommands.description: A list/table of the element locations and associated weight of the element. Formatting is as follows:

location.description: Specify the location of the origin of the articulated part with respect to the origin of the entity coordinate system.

subCommands.name: yaw
subCommands.description: Specifies the yaw angle of the articulated part with respect to the entity to which it is attached.

subCommands.name: pitch
subCommands.description: Specifies the pitch of the articulated part with respect to the entity to which it is attached.

subCommands.name: roll
subCommands.description: Specifies the roll of the articulated part with respect to the entity to which it is attached.

subCommands.name: tilt
subCommands.description: Used to specify the fixed elevation angle of a launcher that can be cued in azimuth. See the note in the pitch command for the explanation.

subCommands.name: slew_mode
subCommands.syntax: slew_mode [ fixed | azimuth | elevation | both | azimuth_and_elevation]
subCommands.description: The slewing mode (and the corresponding limits) defines the ability of a subsystem to respond to cue. If a system is not cued then it is oriented in the direction specified by yaw, pitch, and roll.

subCommands.name: azimuth_slew_limits
subCommands.description: Specify the absolute minimum and maximum angle about which the subsystem can be slewed in azimuth for both cueing and scanning. The limits are specified in the part coordinate system (PCS).

subCommands.name: elevation_slew_limits
subCommands.description: Specify the minimum and maximum angle about which the subsystem can be slewed in elevation for both cueing and scanning. The limits are specified in the part coordinate system (PCS).

subCommands.name: elevation_slew_rate
subCommands.description: Specify the angular velocities to be employed when slewing the part to satisfy a cueing request. This is primarily used for modeling systems that track or point at a single target such as a mechanical tracker or a gun system. It is not used for scanning systems, and should not be used for multiple-target tracking systems.

subCommands.name: slew_method
subCommands.description: If non-infinite slew rates ares employed, this command specifies how the intermediate steps of a slewing operation will occur. If independent is specified, the amount of movement in each direction within a time interval will be determined independently, meaning that one direction may hit its desired value before the other direction. If coordinated is specified then the rates will be adjusted so azimuth and elevation values will both reach the desired value at the same time.

subCommands.name: masking_pattern
subCommands.description: Specify the name of a masking pattern defined with the global masking_pattern command. Masking patterns are a mechanism for modeling obscuration by structural elements on the platform.

subCommands.name: altitude_and_mach
subCommands.description: Provide the altitude and mach number of the air-to-air missile firing. This setting will override any Speed value provided in speed, below.

subCommands.name: speed
subCommands.description: Provide the launch platform speed for the air-to-air missile firing. This setting will override any Mach value provided in altitude_and_mach.

altitude_and_mach.description: Provide the altitude and mach number of the air-to-ground weapon firing. Functionally equivalent to altitude_and_speed. Multiple launch conditions will be accepted.

subCommands.name: altitude_and_speed
subCommands.description: Provide the launch platform speed for the air-to-air missile firing. Multiple launch conditions will be accepted.

subCommands.name: target_lateral_offsets
subCommands.description: Provide the length and quantity of lateral offsets (from the centerline of the launch platform) at which ground targets will be placed and fired upon. Zero lateral offset from the launch aircraft (target on the centerline of the launch aircraft) is always tested, and the LAR is assumed to be symmetric about the lateral plane of the launch aircraft.

subCommands.name: target_offsets
subCommands.description: Synonym for “target_lateral_offsets” as above (for backward compatibility).

subCommands.name: target_forward_offsets
subCommands.description: Provide the minimum forward offset (most negative; a negative number is allowed), delta length, and quantity of target offsets (from the launch platform) at which ground targets will be placed and fired upon. If the LAR is expected to contain points behind the current aircraft location, then the minimum value must be less than zero. lateral offset from the launch aircraft (target on the centerline of the launch aircraft) is always tested, and the LAR is assumed to be symmetric about the lateral plane of the launch aircraft.

subCommands.name: shrink_factor
subCommands.description: Supply a factor (0.0 < factor < 1.0) to reduce the LAR size to apply conservatism in the employment of the weapon.

subCommands.name: switch_sides
subCommands.description: The default output of the resultant replay file shows the output on the right side of the launching platform. This command switches the output to the left side.

default_atmosphere_type.syntax: default_atmosphere_type [standard_day | hot_day | tropical_day | cold_day | polar_day | custom | simple_dt <temperature value>]
default_atmosphere_type.description: The “standard_day” atmosphere is supplied by default. This command is global in scope, and should be specified before any types are defined that use an atmosphere. Each instance of “simple_dt” type atmosphere must use the same (static) temperature deviation from “standard_day” atmosphere, and is supplied using the global syntax above for “simple_dt”. The default for this value is +10 deg K.

atmosphere_model.description: Define a new atmosphere model with the specified <model-name> that is an instance of the specified <atmosphere-model-type>.

subCommands.name: altitude
subCommands.description: A list of altitudes for which corresponding attenuation and scattering coefficient blocks are provided.

subCommands.name: attenuation
subCommands.description: A list of attenuation coefficients in units of 1/m. Each entry in this block corresponds with the entry in the altitude block.

subCommands.name: scattering
subCommands.description: A list of scattering coefficients in units of 1/m. Each entry in this block corresponds with the entry in the altitude block.

subCommands.name: wavelength
subCommands.description: The wavelength at which the table is valid.

subCommands.name: haze_model
subCommands.description: The haze model used, corresponding with one of the values above (1-5). This should be the same value used as input to the ModTran run.

subCommands.name: atmosphere_model
subCommands.description: The atmosphere model used, corresponding with one of the values above (1-6). This should be the same value used as input to the ModTran run.

subCommands.name: specific_attenuation
subCommands.description: Specifies the signal loss per unit length. This would be applicable where the paths are nearly parallel to the Earth’s surface (such as in air-to-air where the participants are at approximately the same altitude).

subCommands.name: attenuation_factor
subCommands.description: Specifies a constant multiplier (gain factor) of the signal value. The factor must be in the range [ 0 .. 1 ] in absolute units (a dB value less than zero). This option would be applicable where the geometry is fixed (or nearly so), such as communications between two ground stations or between a ground station and a geosynchronous satellite.

attitude_controller.description: Specify the attitude controller for the platform. All platforms having a WSF_SPACE_MOVER or WSF_NORAD_SPACE_MOVER will have an attitude controller of some kind. If no attitude controller block is specified, the mover will operate as if the instant attitude controller was selected.

subCommands.name: maximum_yaw_rate
subCommands.description: Specify the maximum time rate of change for reorientations in the platform’s yaw.

subCommands.name: maximum_pitch_rate
subCommands.description: Specify the maximum time rate of change for reorientations in the platform’s pitch.

subCommands.name: maximum_roll_rate
subCommands.description: Specify the maximum time rate of change for reorientations in the platform’s roll.

subCommands.name: orientation
subCommands.description: Specify how the platform is to be oriented.

subCommands.name: swap_axes
subCommands.description: Swap the pointing and constraint axes for the currently specified orientation.

constant.description: The table being processed is non-dimensional, representing a constant function (i.e. y = c).

subCommands.name: regular_table
subCommands.description: With regular tables, all slices through the table must have the same number of breakpoints. This is efficient but requires the same density of sample points across slices.

subCommands.name: irregular_table
subCommands.description: An irregular table provides greater flexibility by removing the restriction that all slices through the table require the same number of break points. The dependent variable values are assigned according to the number of independent variables defined to complete the cross sections of the table.

subCommands.name: interval_table
subCommands.description: The interval table is similar to the irregular_table, except interval tables provide no option for independent variable extrapolation.

subCommands.name: curve
subCommands.description: A curve is a special form of a regular_table limited to specifying one independent variable.

subCommands.name: file
subCommands.description: The file option is used to read in a file containing the table definition. The table defined in the file must be constructed exactly as it would be defined inline within the program.

subCommands.name: independent_variable
subCommands.description: Specifies the name and units for an independent variable. Optionally, precision and extrapolation may be added. This command may be repeated up to eight times to define the independent variables present in the table.

subCommands.name: dependent_variable
subCommands.description: Specifies the units and optional precision of the dependent variable.

subCommands.name: units
subCommands.description: Specifies the unit of measure for the given variable and must be a valid unit type for the variable defined. For example:

subCommands.name: precision
subCommands.description: An optional subcommand that specifies the precision used to store values in memory. double is at least 64 bits and float is at least 32 bits.

subCommands.name: interpolation
subCommands.description: An optional subcommand that specifies whether table lookups should use multilinear interpolation of the data values, or the nearest value in the table.

subCommands.name: extrapolate
subCommands.description: An optional subcommand used to indicate extrapolation will be performed if the value of the independent_variable is outside the limits of its definition.

subCommands.name: num_points
subCommands.description: An optional subcommand used to specify the number of points that the variable list will have.

subCommands.name: linear_equation
subCommands.description: An optional subcommand used to represent the independent variables values using a linear equation between <point_1> and <point_n> (inclusive) with num_points points.

subCommands.name: binary_data_file
subCommands.description: An optional subcommand that maps the specified file to a raw binary array of floats/doubles for use as a list of datapoints.

subCommands.name: save_as_rectangular_indexed_binary_file
subCommands.description: Save the generated table to file, which can then be passed to the binary_data_file command.

subCommands.name: save_as_morton_indexed_binary_file
subCommands.description: Save the generated table to file, which can then be passed to the binary_data_file command

launch_altitudes.description: Desired launcher altitudes for weapon release. Altitudes are assumed to be the height of the launcher above an ellipsoidal earth.

subCommands.name: launch_speeds
subCommands.description: Speeds of launcher for weapon release.

subCommands.name: target_altitudes
subCommands.description: Altitudes to place targets for prosecution. Altitudes are assumed to be the height of the target above an ellipsoidal earth.

air_target_file.description: Name for the output file containing the generated surface-to-air trajectory data.

subCommands.name: surface_target_file
subCommands.description: Name for the output file containing the generated surface-to-surface trajectory data.

subCommands.name: gnuplot_file
subCommands.description: Name of the plot file written out for post-process visualization.

subCommands.name: minimum_output_time
subCommands.description: Minimum missile time of flight value below which no intercept or impact is considered valid.

subCommands.name: maximum_output_time
subCommands.description: Maximum missile time of flight value beyond which no intercept or impact is considered valid.

subCommands.name: minimum_output_range
subCommands.description: Minimum missile flight ground range below which no intercept or impact is considered valid.

subCommands.name: maximum_output_range
subCommands.description: Maximum missile flight ground range beyond which no intercept or impact is considered valid.

subCommands.name: maximum_output_altitude
subCommands.description: Maximum altitude at which an intercept solution is tested for success.

subCommands.name: limited_to_preapogee
subCommands.description: Flag that precludes consideration of an intercept as viable if the intercept occurs post-apogee.

subCommands.name: loft_angle
subCommands.description: Single value of loft angle to be used for trajectory propagation. Generally used only for small short range ballistic missiles. The independent variable to achieve various downrange trajectories is then propellant burn time.

subCommands.name: loft_angles
subCommands.description: Range of loft angles to be used for trajectory propagation tests.

subCommands.name: burn_time
subCommands.description: Single value of burn time to be used for trajectory propagation.

subCommands.name: burn_times
subCommands.description: Used for generating nominal trajectory profile launch tables (burn time) as a function of desired target range. Make sure to add in the inter-stage delay times when determining min and max duration values. Cannot be used with either loft_angle_range or depress_angle_range keywords.

subCommands.name: pass_1_loft_angle_start
subCommands.description: Beginning loft angle for pass one (coarse traversal) to find optimal loft angle. This value is highly dependent upon missile kinematics… larger (more vertical) for lumbering missiles, smaller (more horizontal) for energetic missiles. CAUTION: Choice of too high or too low a value may cause the generator to erroneously predict the optimal loft angle.

subCommands.name: pass_1_loft_angle_stop
subCommands.description: Ending loft angle for pass one (coarse traversal) to find optimal loft angle. Since iteration is with increasing loft-angle, this value must be larger than pass_1_loft_angle_start. This value is highly dependent upon missile kinematics… larger (more vertical) for lumbering missiles, smaller (more horizontal) for energetic missiles. CAUTION: Choice of too high or too low a value may cause the generator to erroneously predict the optimal loft angle.

subCommands.name: pass_1_loft_angle_step
subCommands.description: Increment value for pass one loft angle (coarse traversal). Recommended starting point is 0.2 degrees.

subCommands.name: pass_2_loft_angle_step
subCommands.description: Increment value for pass one loft angle (fine traversal). Recommended starting point is 0.001 degrees.

subCommands.name: loft_angle_range
subCommands.description: Used only for generating lofted trajectory profile launch tables. Parameters max_angle and max_loft are both independently able to terminate the iteration loop. The max_angle parameter is an absolute value of loft angle, while the max_loft parameter is relative to the pre-calculated optimal loft angle. Cannot be used with burn_times or depress_angle_range keyword.

subCommands.name: depress_angle_range
subCommands.description: Used only for generating depressed trajectory profile launch tables. Parameters min_angle and max_depress are both independently able to terminate the iteration loop. The min_angle parameter is an absolute value of loft angle, while the max_loft parameter is relative to the pre-calculated optimal loft angle. Cannot be used with burn_times or loft_angle_range keyword.

subCommands.name: use_fires_extrapolation
subCommands.description: When creating BallisticPaths, directs whether to extrapolate using an existing WSF_FIRES_MOVER, if present. If not present, or if the flag is set false, the path will be computed from target_data, if available.

subCommands.name: target_data
subCommands.description: Provide mass and aero characteristics associated with the given ballistic type. These data are needed to calculate BallisticPaths when the use_fires_extrapolation flag is disabled. For example:

subCommands.name: aero
subCommands.description: Provide aero characteristics associated with the given type.

subCommands.name: mass
subCommands.description: Provide a mass to be associated with the given type.

subCommands.name: on_init
subCommands.description: Behaviors have an on_init script block to help them initialize any necessary member variables or perform any preprocessing.

subCommands.name: on_message
subCommands.description: Behaviors can received and process messages. Be sure the comm is linked to the processor that the behavior is on. See the script processor on_message section for more information on using this feature.

subCommands.name: precondition
subCommands.description: Every behavior must have a precondition script block that returns either a true/false Boolean value or a real number. Some parent nodes will check a behavior’s precondition and use its return value as a real number and some will use its return value as a Boolean number. If a precondition returns true/false and it’s used a real number, then “true” equates to 1.0 and “false” equates to 0.0. If a precondition returns a real number and it’s used as a Boolean than 0.0 equates to “false” and everything else equates to “true.” Any tree or node that owns this behavior uses the precondition to determine whether or not that behavior will execute, and subsequently how the whole tree will be traversed and processed on each update. The node types that use real numbers are priority_selector and weighted_random connector nodes.

subCommands.name: on_new_execute
subCommands.description: If a behavior node is run and was not ran last update, then this script block is run.

subCommands.name: on_new_fail
subCommands.description: If a behavior node is not run and was ran last update, then this script block is run.

subCommands.name: execute
subCommands.description: If a behavior node is traversed to by the tree, and its precondition returns a value that the parent node uses to select it for execution, then the behavior’s execute script is performed. This script block should be significant, it is what the behavior exists for.

subCommands.name: show_state_evaluations
subCommands.description: Indicates that information about state evaluations should be written to standard output. This essentially shows the true or false status of the evaluation of each next_state block.

subCommands.name: show_state_transitions
subCommands.description: Indicates that information about state transitions should be written to standard output.

subCommands.name: state
subCommands.description: Defines a state in a state machine with the name <state-name>. Notice that states can have their own behavior tree within them; it is updated when the state is evaluated.

behavior_tree.description: The Behavior Tree is an artificial intelligence technology that allows scenario developers to quickly create flexible agents with various tactical modules, called behaviors or behavior nodes. The nodes can be arranged together in interesting and interrelated ways with connector nodes.

subCommands.name: sequence
subCommands.description: Sequence nodes are the 2nd most common connector node used in behavior trees. When a sequence node is reached, it executes all of its children in order, until one of the children fails its precondition. If the first child fails, then none of the children are executed. If all children pass their preconditions, they are all executed. If the first half of the children pass and the next node fails, then the first half of the children are all executed, and the second half are not.

subCommands.name: parallel
subCommands.description: Parallel nodes are connector nodes used in the behavior tree in order to execute every one of their children that passes precondition, regardless of ordering.

subCommands.name: selector
subCommands.description: Selector nodes are the most common connector node used in behavior trees. A selector node dictates the tree to choose only one of its children to execute. The tree will execute the first child of a selector node that passes its precondition.

subCommands.name: priority_selector
subCommands.description: Priority-Selector nodes are connector nodes used in the behavior tree in order to choose and execute whichever child is highest valued. The value of a child is determined by its precondition script block. Priority-Selector nodes always (and only) execute their highest valued child.

subCommands.name: weighted_random
subCommands.description: Weighted-Random nodes are connector nodes used in the behavior tree in order to randomly choose and execute a child. A uniform weighted random selection is performed, and the weights for each child are determined by their precondition script blocks. For example, if a Weighted-Random node has two children and both return a value of “3”, then they are equally likely to be chosen.
