It will be common for Weighted-Random nodes to use the “run_selection” feature, in order to allow their selected child to execute for a while (or until done) before another random selection is made.

subCommands.name: <connector
subCommands.description: (only useful for types: selector, priority_selector, and weighted_random)

subCommands.name: run_selection
subCommands.description: Specify how long a selected child will be executed for, rather than the default: once (repeat 1). If “until_done” is declared, then a child node will be executed until its precondition returns 0.0 or false.

subCommands.name: make_selection
subCommands.description: Specify how many selections will be made, rather than the default: continuous. This doesn’t affect or change whatever is defined by make_selection, but rather it could limit how many times a selector type node will perform.

subCommands.name: execute
subCommands.description: Specify the script that the callback should call when it is triggered. As an optional parameter you can specify a processor that the callback should execute in. To trigger more than one script when the callback occurs, simply include multiple execute statements. To add a callback to a waypoint, see the execute command of the route and the AddCallbackToWaypoint script method.

orientation.description: Specify how the platform is to be oriented.

subCommands.name: swap_axes
subCommands.description: Swap the pointing and constraint axes for the currently specified orientation.

eccentricity.description: The desired eccentricity of the final orbit.

inclination.description: The final inclination of the satellite’s orbit.

raan.description: The right ascension of the ascending node (raan) of the final orbit.

subCommands.name: inclination
subCommands.description: The inclination of the final orbit.

semi_major_axis.description: The desired semi-major axis of the final orbit.

subCommands.name: apoapsis_altitude
subCommands.description: The desired altitude of the final orbit’s apoapsis.

subCommands.name: periapsis_altitude
subCommands.description: The desired altitude of the final orbit’s periapsis.

classification_levels.description: Used to define the list of potential classification levels in a scenario, in order of increasing degree of sensitivity.

subCommands.name: level
subCommands.description: Defines a level that can be used in classification blocks.

subCommands.name: color
subCommands.description: Optionally define the color to be used when displaying the level in the classification banner within the GUI applications.

subCommands.name: classification
subCommands.description: Specifies the classification level of the input file or scenario. An error will occur if the level string does not appear in the classification_levels block.

subCommands.name: caveats
subCommands.description: Specifies the caveats associated with the classification. Each caveat is a string literal specified by the user. The user can provide as many caveats as needed.

subCommands.name: trigraphs
subCommands.description: Specifies the trigraphs associated with the classification. Each trigraph is a string literal specified by the user. The user can provide as many trigraphs as needed.

subCommands.name: use_legacy_data
subCommands.description: Specified whether to use an older set of tables of clutter strength.

subCommands.name: transmit_mode
subCommands.description: Defines if the device transmits intermittently or continuously. This is currently applicable only to devices that transmit over the air (e.g., WSF_RADIO_TRANSCEIVER). intermittent indicates the device radiates only when a message is actually being transmitted. continuous indicates the devices radiates as long as it is ‘on’. continuous would be used to model systems such as television or radio broadcast stations.

subCommands.name: modifier_category
subCommands.description: The category that maps to the attenuation value defined in the zone_set. Setting this value tells the communications device to evaluate zones for attenuation. See Zone-based attenuation for more information.

subCommands.name: channels
subCommands.description: Specify the number of channels available to this comm. This value is intended to represent the number of simultaneous transmissions (multiplexing) the comm is able to support, per its hardware definition. This value is used by the datalink layer to determine how many concurrent messages the datalink layer will forward to the physical layer for transmission.

subCommands.name: queue_type
subCommands.description: Specify the queuing methodology for the device’s transmit queue.

subCommands.name: queue_limit
subCommands.description: Specify the maximum size of the transmit queue. If the queue grows to the maximum size, subsequent messages are dropped.

subCommands.name: purge_interval
subCommands.description: Indicates a period of time in which messages will be removed from the queue (dropped). Once the queue begins filling with pending messages for transmission, this value will be used to determine how long the messages are retained before being removed from the queue.

subCommands.name: retransmit_attempts
subCommands.description: Indicates the number of times a message will attempt transmission before being purged from the queue (dropped).

subCommands.name: retransmit_delay
subCommands.description: Indicates the amount of time to wait between attempts to send a message from the queue after a previously failed attempt. Take care when using this value with the purge_interval, as if the purge_interval is shorter than the retransmit_delay, messages may be purged before attempting retransmit.

subCommands.name: network_name
subCommands.description: Define the network name that this device belongs to. Network names are strings that map directly to a value used to generate a 32-bit IPv4 address. The use of IPv4 does not infer that AFSIM is only capable of IP based communications, it is simply an internally consistent method to identify all comm objects in the simulation. Usage of the IPv4 address to infer anything beyond an identifier and common membership in a “network” or “group” depends entirely on the comm type implementation itself. Due to support for legacy AFSIM behavior, all comm devices on the same network are assumed to have connectivity to every other object in the same network at the beginning of the simulation with default settings (mesh network topology).

subCommands.name: network_address
subCommands.description: Define the device’s network address. If the address provided belongs to an existing network, this comm device will join that network and be provided the lowest available address not currently assigned in that network. If the address is not currently managed by a network, a network will be created based on a combination of the parent platform and comm name (network-name = platform-name.comm-name) and this comm added to the first available address.

subCommands.name: address
subCommands.description: The address command specifies a specific, user provided address for this comm device. If the address is managed by a network, this comm device will join that network - otherwise a new network will be created that is based on the name of the platform owning the comm device, and the comm device (e.g. platform-name.comm-name). Note that this command may fail and halt simulation input processing if the address provided is already utilized elsewhere, which can happen via use of dynamic addressing based on other objects being assigned addresses.

subCommands.name: link
subCommands.description: This command provides a communications link between this comm device and the device specified. Any number of links may be defined on any given comm object. This link is established both via truth in the network manager and locally as a perception-based link (for the legacy protocol only - other protocols MAY use this command on a case-by-case basis, but are not required to). Be mindful that links may be removed during the simulation if the comm implementation reports failed links for removal, such as when a WSF_RADIO_TRANSCEIVER is out of the EM interaction limits to communicate with another comm, or if the particular network object used to enforce topologies does not support the link provided via this input.

subCommands.name: local_link
subCommands.description: This command is equivalent to the link command for comms on the same platform. As such, only the linking comm name is required to establish this link, and is convenient for platform_type definitions where the platform name is not available in that context.

subCommands.name: link_address
subCommands.description: This command performs the same actions as the link command above, except it uses a specific address to create the link to. This assumes that knowledge of the comm address is known at the time of input, as other addressing commands are dynamic in nature.

subCommands.name: router_name
subCommands.description: Specifies by name the router this comm is assigned to as an interface. Router must be located on the same platform instance as the comm.

subCommands.name: gateway
subCommands.description: Specifies the remote interface to be used as the gateway for this comm instance. Since AFSIM allows multiple links per comm interface, the exact destination interface must be specified for gateway usage. This value will only be used if this comm is designated as the gateway interface to be used by the router object.

subCommands.name: propagation_speed
subCommands.description: Sets the speed of message propagation. This is a pass-through command that defines the propagation speed for the medium associated with this comm object, provided for legacy compatability.

subCommands.name: transfer_rate
subCommands.description: Sets the amount of data that can be transmitted by this comm over a set period of time. Any message being sent by this comm uses this value for its transfer rate. Any uninitialized value for transfer_rate is interpreted to be instantaneous transfer for most comm implementations.

subCommands.name: packet_loss_time
subCommands.description: Sets a time that adds to the delay in every transmission by this comm. Although indicated as a delay due to packet loss, this value can be used to introduce a delay to the normal transmission time of any comm device for any reason, or an aggregate delay due to modelling multiple sources of transmission delay.

subCommands.name: frequency_select_delay
subCommands.description: Specifies the delay when selecting between alternate frequencies as defined on the transmitter.

subCommands.name: jamming_perception_timeout
subCommands.description: Specifies the time after which jamming that was perceived is no longer perceived that the perception of jamming will be returned to a ‘false’ state. If jamming is perceived again before this time has elapsed then the perception of jamming will be maintained ‘true’.

subCommands.name: coherent_jamming_perception_threshold
subCommands.description: Specifies the minimum threshold value that jamming will be perceived by the operator. Often used in conjunction with jamming_perception_timeout, JammingPerceived script method.

subCommands.name: conditionals
subCommands.description: Condition testing commands present in this block determine the inclusion of the commands that follow this block.

subCommands.name: feature_present
subCommands.description: Tests that a feature is present. If the feature is not present, the contents of the conditional section is ignored.

subCommands.name: feature_not_present
subCommands.description: Tests that a feature is not present. If the feature is present, the contents of the conditional section is ignored.

subCommands.name: wsf_version
subCommands.description: Compares the WSF version to a version string delimited by periods. If the comparison fails, the conditional section is ignored

subCommands.name: type_not_present
subCommands.description: Determines if a ‘type’ is present. If any sensor, processor, comm, mover, fuel, filter, service or script type exists with the given name, the type is considered present. If the type is not present, the conditional section is ignored.

subCommands.name: file
subCommands.description: Specifies a file to write output to. As many different files with different settings may be specified as needed. The file block may contain any of the commands from the console_output block, except for other file blocks.

subCommands.name: preset
subCommands.description: Overrides the current output types with the preset.

subCommands.name: fatal
subCommands.description: Enables or disables fatal output. Fatal output is prefixed with ***** FATAL:.

subCommands.name: error
subCommands.description: Enables or disables error output. Error output is prefixed with ***** ERROR:.

subCommands.name: warning
subCommands.description: Enables or disables warning output. Warning output is prefixed with ***** WARNING:.

subCommands.name: info
subCommands.description: Enables or disables info output. Info output has no prefix.

subCommands.name: debug
subCommands.description: Enables or disables debug output. Debug output has no prefix.

subCommands.name: developer
subCommands.description: Enables or disables developer output. Developer output is prefixed with ***** DEVELOPER:.

subCommands.name: type
subCommands.description: Enables or disables the output of a custom type. Custom type output has no prefix, unless it is paired with a type that has one. In general, this command is only useful if a WSF plugin is written specifically to take advantage of it.

subCommands.name: single_line
subCommands.description: Sets the output to single-line or multi-line format. In multi-line format, each piece of information is displayed on a separate line. Nested information is indented from the previous line. Example:

subCommands.name: force_flushing
subCommands.description: Enables or disables automatic flushing of output to the console after every log entry.

tracking_sigma.description: Specify the statistical significance to which the track is initially correlated. A value of one indicates that the distance between locations of correlated tracks is equal to sum of the one sigma errors as extracted from the tracks’ covariance matrices, along the direction from one track’s location to the other.

subCommands.name: turning_sigma
subCommands.description: Specify the statistical significance to which the track is correlated if it fails to meet the tracking_sigma correlation threshold. This values should be less than or equal to the tracking_sigma value. A value of one indicates that the distance between locations of correlated tracks is equal to sum of the one sigma errors as extracted from the tracks’ covariance matrices, along the direction from one track’s location to the other.

subCommands.name: coast_time
subCommands.description: Specify the time after which a track is no longer correlated that a “no correlation” result is returned. This time is independent of any sensor or track processor reporting times.

subCommands.name: maximum_correlation_distance
subCommands.description: Specify the maximum distance of track location from truth location, for which a correlation occurs with an existing track. If the distance is beyond this maximum, or there is no existing track associated with the truth body, a new track is created.

subCommands.name: ignore_same_side
subCommands.description: When performing correlations, ignore truth bodies that are on the same side as the track’s reported side (if any).

subCommands.name: evaluation_interval
subCommands.description: Specify a time during which subsequent correlations are performed on a track that has already been correlated.

subCommands.name: ignore_track_target
subCommands.description: Specify whether to ignore truth data associated with the track when making a correlation. If this value is set true, correlations is made identically with the perfect correlator when possible.

file.description: Specify the name of the file that will be produced. The directory into which the file will be created is inherited from the coverage object on which the measure of effectiveness is defined.

subCommands.name: width
subCommands.description: Set the width of the output fields. Setting this value appropriately will lead to output files that are more easily human readable.

subCommands.name: precision
subCommands.description: Set the number of digits of precision to use when writing numerical data to the generated file.

subCommands.name: format
subCommands.description: Set the format of numerical data. Valid format specifiers are:

subCommands.name: justify
subCommands.description: Set the position in the width of the column where the output is generated. Allowed values are: left and right, which place the contents of a field on the left or right side (respectively) of the column.

latitude.description: Produce summary statistics as a function of latitude.

subCommands.name: longitude
subCommands.description: Produce summary statistics as a function of longitude.

subCommands.name: bin_size
subCommands.description: Specify the size of the bins into which the grid points are projected.

subCommands.name: file
subCommands.description: Specify the name of the file that will be produced. The directory into which the file will be created is inherited from the coverage object on which the measure of effectiveness is defined.

subCommands.name: width
subCommands.description: Set the width of the output fields. Setting this value appropriately will lead to output files that are more easily human readable.

subCommands.name: precision
subCommands.description: Set the number of digits of precision to use when writing numerical data to the generated file.

subCommands.name: format
subCommands.description: Set the format of numerical data. Valid format specifiers are:

subCommands.name: justify
subCommands.description: Set the position in the width of the column where the output is generated. Allowed values are: left and right, which place the contents of a field on the left or right side (respectively) of the column.

subCommands.name: file
subCommands.description: Specifies the name of the file to which the csv_event_output is written. If the file already exists, then it will be overwritten. The special name STDOUT indicates the csv_event_output is to be written to standard output. The special name NULL indicates that no csv_event_output is to be written. NULL can be used to cancel a file name specified in an earlier csv_event_output block.

subCommands.name: flush_output
subCommands.description: Specifies if the output buffer should be flushed after each event is written.

subCommands.name: enable
subCommands.description: Specifies the names of the events to be included or excluded in the event log. These commands are typically specified multiple times to select the events of interest. The commands are processed in order of appearance with each successive command selecting or deselecting events as appropriate.

subCommands.name: insert_data_tags
subCommands.description: Specifies if the CSV header is written. This describes the format of each event in the log.

subCommands.name: effect
subCommands.description: A cyber_effect type that models the effect of the attack on the victim. This command may be repeated to specify multiple effects. If multiple effects are associated with this attack, the effects will resolve in the order in which they are listed.

subCommands.name: duration
subCommands.description: A duration will specify how long the effect lasts. When duration is not set but there exists a cyber_protect block associated with the cyber_attack effect then duration will be the summation of the attack_detection_delay_time and attack_recovery_delay_time.

subCommands.name: scan_delay_time
subCommands.description: This specifies the amount of time it takes to perform a scan. This is the amount of time between the call to WsfPlatform.CyberScan and when WsfPlatform.CyberScanStatus returns a non-negative value. Any call to WsfPlatform.CyberScanStatus that occurs before this time elapses will return a negative value, indicating the scan is in progress.

subCommands.name: delivery_delay_time
subCommands.description: This specifies the amount of time it would take to deliver an exploit. This is the amount of time between the call to WsfPlatform.CyberAttack and when WsfPlatform.CyberAttackStatus returns a non-negative value. Any call to WsfPlatform.CyberAttackStatus that occurs before this time elapses will return a negative value, indicating the delivery is in progress.

subCommands.name: probability_of_scan_detection
subCommands.description: This specifies the default value for probability_of_scan_detection of a corresponding attack_response in cyber_protect.

subCommands.name: probability_of_scan_attribution
subCommands.description: This specifies the default value for probability_of_scan_attribution of a corresponding attack_response in cyber_protect.

subCommands.name: probability_of_attack_success
subCommands.description: This specifies the default value for probability_of_attack_success of a corresponding attack_response in cyber_protect.

subCommands.name: probability_of_status_report
subCommands.description: This specifies the default value for probability_of_status_report of a corresponding attack_response in cyber_protect.

subCommands.name: probability_of_attack_detection
subCommands.description: This specifies the default value for probability_of_attack_detection of a corresponding attack_response in cyber_protect.

subCommands.name: probability_of_attack_attribution
subCommands.description: This specifies the default value for probability_of_attack_attribution of a corresponding attack_response in cyber_protect.

subCommands.name: probability_of_future_immunity
subCommands.description: This specifies the default value for probability_of_future_immunity of a corresponding attack_response in cyber_protect.

subCommands.name: scan_detection_draw_frequency
subCommands.description: The frequency of random draws for determining if a scan is detected.

subCommands.name: scan_attribution_draw_frequency
subCommands.description: The frequency of random draws for determining if a scan is attributed.

subCommands.name: attack_success_draw_frequency
subCommands.description: The frequency of random draws for determining if an attack is successful.

subCommands.name: status_report_draw_frequency
subCommands.description: The frequency of random draws for determining if a status report is to be made.

subCommands.name: attack_detection_draw_frequency
subCommands.description: The frequency of random draws for determining if an attack is detectable by the victim.

subCommands.name: attack_attribution_draw_frequency
subCommands.description: The frequency of random draws for determining if an attack is attributed by the victim.

subCommands.name: future_immunity_draw_frequency
subCommands.description: The frequency of random draws for determining if the victim will be immune to future attacks of the same type.

subCommands.name: resources
subCommands.description: Define the amount of total cyber resource available to the platform to use when launching a cyber_attack. Upon successfully launching a cyber_attack with a resource cost, the resource will be spent. If the cyber_attack ends either through its duration finishing, the victim restoring itself, or the victim is destroyed, the resources used will be returned to the attacker.

subCommands.name: attack_degrade
subCommands.description: Define the degradation to the attack <attack_type>. <attack_type> must be a defined cyber_attack type or the word ‘default’, which signifies the attack degradation to use if an attack is received for which there is not a defined attack degradation.

subCommands.name: degrade_probability_of_scan_detection
subCommands.description: The value that will be ADDED to the uniform probability draw that is compared against the accepted threshold value for scan detection. The scan is detected if (uniform_draw + degrade < scan_detection_threshold).

subCommands.name: degrade_probability_of_scan_attribution
subCommands.description: The value that will be ADDED to the uniform probability draw that is compared against the accepted threshold value for scan attribution. The scan is attributed if (uniform_draw + degrade < scan_attribution_threshold).

subCommands.name: degrade_probability_of_attack_success
subCommands.description: The value that will be ADDED to the uniform probability draw that is compared against the accepted threshold value for attack success. The attack is successful if (uniform_draw + degrade < attack_success_threshold).

subCommands.name: degrade_probability_of_status_report
subCommands.description: The value that will be ADDED to the uniform probability draw that is compared against the accepted threshold value for status report availability. The status is available if (uniform_draw + degrade < status_report_threshold).

subCommands.name: degrade_probability_of_attack_detection
subCommands.description: The value that will be ADDED to the uniform probability draw that is compared against the accepted threshold value for attack detection. The attack is detected if (uniform_draw + degrade < attack_detection_threshold).

subCommands.name: degrade_probability_of_attack_attribution
subCommands.description: The value that will be ADDED to the uniform probability draw that is compared against the accepted threshold value for attack attribution. The attack is attributed if (uniform_draw + degrade < attack_attribution_threshold).

subCommands.name: degrade_probability_of_future_immunity
subCommands.description: The value that will be ADDED to the uniform probability draw that is compared against the accepted threshold value for future immunity. The attack is immune in the future if (uniform_draw + degrade < future_immunity_threshold).

subCommands.name: attack_response
subCommands.description: Define the response to the attack <attack_type>. <attack_type> must be a defined cyber_attack type or the word ‘default’, which signifies the attack response to use if an attack is received for which there is not a defined attack response.

subCommands.name: probability_of_scan_detection
subCommands.description: The probability threshold that a scan function will be detected.

subCommands.name: probability_of_scan_attribution
subCommands.description: The probability threshold that a scan function will be attributed.

subCommands.name: probability_of_attack_success
subCommands.description: The probability threshold that an attack will be declared successful.

subCommands.name: probability_of_status_report
subCommands.description: The probability threshold that the attacker will receive immediate notification of the success or failure of an attack.

subCommands.name: probability_of_attack_detection
subCommands.description: The probability threshold that an attack will be detected by the victim.

subCommands.name: probability_of_attack_attribution
subCommands.description: The probability threshold that an attack will be attributed by the victim.

subCommands.name: probability_of_future_immunity
subCommands.description: The probability threshold that the victim will be immune to future attacks of the same type.

subCommands.name: attack_detection_delay_time
subCommands.description: The amount of time it takes before the victim become aware of an attack.

subCommands.name: attack_recovery_delay_time
subCommands.description: The amount of time it takes for the victim to recover from an attack after it becomes aware of the attack.

subCommands.name: IsVulnerable
subCommands.description: Define an optional script that is invoked when a scan or an attack occurs against the platform. This may be used to implement more complex vulnerability assessment based on the operating conditions rather than just using random draws.

subCommands.name: OnScanDetection
subCommands.description: Define an optional script that is invoked when a scan occurs against the platform. This may be used to model such effects as notifying others that something suspicious is occurring.

subCommands.name: OnAttackDetection
subCommands.description: Define an optional script that is invoked after an attack has occurred upon the expiration of the attack_detection_delay_time. This might be used to model effects such notify others of the attack.

subCommands.name: OnAttackRecovery
subCommands.description: Define an optional script that is invoked during an attack after the expiration of the attack_recovery_delay_time. This may be used to model such effects as notifying others that they are once again operational.

subCommands.name: extrapolated_trigger
subCommands.description: Typically, triggers only execute once after the evaluation criteria is met. By setting this command to true, this trigger will continue to evaluate during user defined time intervals. Note that the trigger must still meet its evaluation criteria to execute if indicated to extrapolate. (OnEvaluate return of true)

subCommands.name: execute_trigger
subCommands.description: Indicates whether or not a globally defined trigger should attempt evaluation and execution during the simulation.

subCommands.name: update_interval
subCommands.description: This command block allows for the user specification of the time intervals over which this trigger should attempt evaluation and execution. Overlapping intervals are allowed, and regardless of the number of overlapping intervals, the next evaluation that is scheduled will take the earliest occurring time from any such overlapping intervals. In addition, gaps are allowed in intervals, such that the user may define periods of time where triggers should not evaluate or execute.

subCommands.name: OnEvaluate
subCommands.description: Defines the evaluation script for a trigger. This script must return a value or true or false, where true indicates triggering, followed by a subsequent and immediate execution of the trigger. False indicates that the criteria was not meant for this trigger to activate, and will attempt to re-evaluate by calling this method again in the future (assuming the user defined time interval allows it to do so). The user may run any script as needed in this context, as long as a boolean value is returned.

subCommands.name: OnExecute
subCommands.description: Defines the execution script for a trigger. Once a trigger has evaluated to true, this execution script will be called immediately.

subCommands.name: aperture_diameter
subCommands.description: The aperture diameter of the HEL system. Changing this parameter controls the diffraction-induced beam spread, affecting the beam size on target. The larger the aperture diameter, the smaller the beam on target, and the greater the energy density (energy density ~ (aperture diameter^2)).

subCommands.name: atmospheric_structure
subCommands.description: Specify the atmospheric structure model, or function, used to compute atmospheric turbulence. It has units of .

subCommands.name: beam_quality
subCommands.description: Specify the beam quality of the optical system. The beam quality is a measure of how close the profile is to a perfect gaussian. Specifically it is a multiplicative factor times the diffraction-limited radius. It varies from a value of 1 (diffraction limited) to values of order unity (but still greater than one).

subCommands.name: calculate_incidence
subCommands.description: Specify whether to calculate an incidence angle on target based on aspect, with a head-on aspect to target representing the minimum (0 degree) incidence. Any incidence greater than 90 degrees would be considered ineffective.

subCommands.name: jitter
subCommands.description: Specify the jitter of the system (typically on the order of microradians). The higher the jitter, the more a HEL beam will be “spread out” over the target.

subCommands.name: laser_type
subCommands.description: Specify the high-energy laser type. In turn this specifies the wavelength, which is needed by the various models to calculate diffraction and extinction of the beam.

subCommands.name: power
subCommands.description: This is the actual laser power emitted from the aperture.

subCommands.name: wavelength
subCommands.description: The wavelength at which the laser operates (e.g., 1.064 microns for a Nd-YAG laser). Current supported wavelengths (in nanometers) include

delta_v.description: The given delta-V to be applied. Positive values will be applied in the same direction as the velocity vector, and negative values will be applied in the opposite direction.

subCommands.name: connections
subCommands.description: By default, the dis_interface supports a single input/output (replay file, playback file, or network address). Connection information in this connections block allows for multiple output types. Subcommands available include record, playback, broadcast, multicast, unicast, port, send_port, and receive_port.

subCommands.name: record
subCommands.description: Record the simulation to the specified file.

subCommands.name: playback
subCommands.description: Causes entity state data contained within the specified file to be read and injected into simulation. ONLY entity state data is used - all other PDUs are ignored. The entity_type command is used to define the mapping of DIS entity types to WSF platforms, just as in a standard DIS simulation. Entity state PDUs are also written to the record file if defined.

subCommands.name: broadcast
subCommands.description: Participate in a DIS exercise on the indicated broadcast network. For example, if your ethernet port address is 192.168.1.14 and the netmask is set to 255.255.0.0, the command would be “broadcast 192.168.255.255”.

subCommands.name: multicast
subCommands.description: Participate in the DIS exercise on the specified multicast network. The port command must also be specified.

subCommands.name: unicast
subCommands.description: Communicate DIS traffic with a single endpoint. unicast-address can be an IP address or a host-name. The port command must also be specified.

subCommands.name: port
subCommands.description: Specify the port number for broadcast, multicast, and unicast modes.

subCommands.name: send_port
subCommands.description: Specify the send and receive port numbers for broadcast, multicast, and unicast modes. Both send_port and receive_port must be specified together, and act as a replacement for the port command. This command is primarily used with unicast mode.

subCommands.name: time_to_live
subCommands.description: Specify the ‘time-to-live’ value for multicast communications in the range [0, 255].

subCommands.name: filtered_connection
subCommands.description: Connection information in each filtered_connection block allows for a subset of the DIS PDUs to be output to the specified device. If no device (output type, address, port) exists yet, one is appended to the connections list (as in edit_connections). Subcommands available include record, broadcast, multicast, unicast, port, and allow. The unique subcommand allow provides a way to specify what type of DIS PDUs will be allowed out of this connection to the given device.

subCommands.name: allow
subCommands.description: Specify a WSF entity type that is allowed to be output from the filtered connection.

subCommands.name: protocol_version
subCommands.description: Specify the DIS protocol version in the range [0, 6].

subCommands.name: exercise
subCommands.description: Specify the DIS exercise ID in the range [1, 255].

subCommands.name: site
subCommands.description: Specify the DIS site ID in the range [1, 65534].

subCommands.name: application
subCommands.description: Specify the DIS application ID in the range [1, 65534].

subCommands.name: join_exercise
subCommands.description: Specify if the application should join the exercise (specified by the exercise command) as a participant in a DIS non-real-time scaled-and-stepped simulation.

subCommands.name: autostart
subCommands.description: Do not wait for a Start/Resume PDU to start the simulation.

subCommands.name: no_autostart
subCommands.description: Wait for a Start/Resume PDU to start the simulation. This is the default.

subCommands.name: deferred_connection_time
subCommands.description: The application will defer joining the exercise until the specified simulation time is reached. Prior to that time it will run as fast as possible and not send data to or receive data from the DIS exercise. When the desired time is reached, the application will connect to the network or begin writing the replay file. The simulation clock will behave as defined by the autostart or no_autostart command. The minimum valid time-value for this command is one second.

subCommands.name: absolute_timestamp
subCommands.description: Specify that absolute timestamps are to be used the PDUs produced by this application.

subCommands.name: ignore_pdu_time
subCommands.description: Ignore the time from the PDU and use the current perception of simulation time.

subCommands.name: use_pdu_time
subCommands.description: Use the time from the PDU as the effective event time. It is recommended not to use this command for large simulations.

subCommands.name: mover_update_timer
subCommands.description: If greater than 0, the interface will generate events to force platforms to update their position at the specified interval. This is useful for event-driven simulations where position updates may occur infrequently due to the lack of interaction between objects.

subCommands.name: heartbeat_timer
subCommands.description: Specify the DIS heartbeat timer. For internally controlled entities, this defines the maximum amount of time that can elapse between transmission of Entity State PDUs. The simulation will force an Entity State PDU to be sent if required. To drastically reduce replay file sizes for large simulations, set the heartbeat_timer to a value of 20 or greater.

subCommands.name: heartbeat_multiplier
subCommands.description: Specify the DIS heartbeat multiplier. For externally controlled entities, heartbeat_timer values; heartbeat_multiplier defines the maximum amount time that can elapse without receiving an Entity State PDU before an entity is declared ‘inactive’ and removed from the simulation.

subCommands.name: initial_distribution_interval
subCommands.description: When participating in a distributed exercise (using broadcast or multicast), the interface will spread out transmission of initial state data to avoid overloading the network. This command provides a mechanism to explicitly specify the initial distribution interval.

subCommands.name: entity_position_threshold
subCommands.description: Specify the DIS entity position threshold.

subCommands.name: entity_orientation_threshold
subCommands.description: Specify the DIS entity orientation threshold.

subCommands.name: maximum_beam_entries
subCommands.description: Specify the maximum number of beam entries that will be transmitted in the ‘system’ portion of an Electromagnetic Emission PDU.

subCommands.name: maximum_track_jam_entries
subCommands.description: Specify the maximum number of track-jam entries that will be transmitted in the ‘beam’ portion of an Electromagnetic Emission PDU before the high-density track-jam mode will be selected.

subCommands.name: sensor_update_interval
subCommands.description: This is used to force Electromagnetic Emissions PDUs to be sent out at approximately the specified update interval in addition to the standard rules. This is primarily used to force PDUs to be sent more frequently with an updated ‘Beam Sweep Sync’ in the DIS Beam record. This allows the receiver to have more accurate knowledge of where a scanning sensor is within its scan pattern.

subCommands.name: force
subCommands.description: Specify the DIS force identifier that corresponds to a WSF platform side. This command should be specified for each side that is present in the scenario. If no force commands are provided then the following defaults will be defined:

subCommands.name: entity_type
subCommands.description: Specify the DIS entity type to be used when sending PDUs for platforms or munitions with the indicated WSF platform type. This command should be specified for each WSF platform type that is present in the scenario. If the type of a platform does not have a corresponding DIS entity type then 0:0:0:0:0:0:0 will be used. For proper WSF interaction of received DIS entities from other networked simulations, a corresponding simple platform_type must be created with defined signatures.

subCommands.name: unknown_platform_type
subCommands.description: Specify the type of the WSF platform to be created for an external entity if an applicable entity_type entry does not exist.

subCommands.name: entity_appearance
subCommands.description: Specify the DIS Entity Appearance type and state or ID associated with a specified signature state. To identify the appearance mapping:

subCommands.name: articulated_part
subCommands.description: The articulated part block indicates that a platform type should publish an articulated part to DIS. The part may be a comm, sensor, or visual_part. The block may contain the following commands:

subCommands.name: emitter_type
subCommands.description: Specify the DIS ‘emitter name’ enumeration associated with specified WSF systems that emit electromagnetic energy (e.g., sensors). For outbound electromagnetic emission PDUs this defines the value for the ‘emitter name’ field in the PDU for a given WSF emitter. For inbound PDUs, a reverse lookup is performed to determine the WSF sensor type needed to provide the additional characteristics to properly model interactions with the externally modeled emitter.

subCommands.name: emitter_function
subCommands.description: Specify the DIS ‘emitter function’ enumeration with specified WSF systems that emit electromagnetic energy (e.g., sensors). This is only applicable for outbound electromagnetic emission PDUs.

subCommands.name: beam_type
subCommands.description: Specify the DIS Emissions PDU ‘beam parameter index’ value associated with specified WSF systems that emit electromagnetic energy (e.g., sensors). For outbound electromagnetic emission PDUs this defines the value for the ‘beam parameter index’ field in the PDU for a given WSF emitter beam. For inbound PDUs, this field is NOT currently used within WSF.

subCommands.name: beam_function
subCommands.description: Specify the DIS Emissions PDU ‘beam function’ value associated with specified WSF systems that emit electromagnetic energy (e.g., sensors). This is applicable only for outbound electromagnetic emission PDUs.

subCommands.name: entity_id
subCommands.description: Assign a specific DIS entity number to a WSF platform instance. If no DIS entity number is specified for a given platform instance, the simulation will automatically assign one sequentially, in creation order, (see start_entity). The unique DIS entity ID for a platform is formed by combining the values of site, application and entity number.

subCommands.name: start_entity
subCommands.description: Specify the starting DIS entity in the range [0, 65534]. The simulation will assign DIS entity IDs to DIS platform representations sequentially, in creation order, beginning with this value for the start_entity.

subCommands.name: private
subCommands.description: Indicate that locally owned platforms of the specified name, type, or category are to be considered ‘private’ and not written to the DIS network.

subCommands.name: filter_out_by_site_and_app
subCommands.description: Filter out a site and application pair when running in a DIS environment. The site and application must be set up as a pair. Repeat the entire block for multiple site/application pairs.

subCommands.name: ignore_kind_and_domain
subCommands.description: Filter out DIS entity state PDUs with given DIS entity type kind and domain values. Use of this filter will prevent creation of the corresponding external platforms in the simulation. For example, to filter out all entity state PDUs from land-based platforms (kind = 1; domain = 1):

subCommands.name: ignore_type
subCommands.description: Filter out DIS entity state PDUs of the given DIS entity type. Use of this filter will prevent creation of the corresponding external platforms in the simulation. For example, to filter out all F-15Es in the simulation:

subCommands.name: ignore_pdu_type
subCommands.description: Filter out DIS PDUs of a given type. For instance, to filter out the Stop/Freeze and Signal PDUs:

subCommands.name: filter_out_by_range
subCommands.description: Filter out DIS entity state PDUs based on a given range from a platform. Entities beyond the given range(s) will not be added to the simulation. Multiple platforms may be specified. For example, to filter out all platforms outside a 60 km radius from two 737 platforms, named 737_1A and 737_1B:

subCommands.name: debug_emission_pdu
subCommands.description: Specify the level of debugging information for electromagnetic emission PDUs.

subCommands.name: enumerate
subCommands.description: entity_types: Outputs the list of platform types and the entity_type each one maps to.

subCommands.name: log_created_entities
subCommands.description: Specify that information concerning the creation of DIS entities is to be written to standard output. This is useful for debugging. It is also used to create a DIS entity ID table in conjunction with the make_entity_id_map.pl perl script (located under the tools subdirectory).

subCommands.name: no_periodic_pdus_while_paused
subCommands.description: Will cause entity state and emission PDUs not to be sent while the simulation is paused. This is default behavior.

subCommands.name: multi_thread
subCommands.description: Creates a worker thread, separate from the main thread, that sends/receives DIS PDUs. Use this capability in a multi-threaded frame step simulation. This feature is not applicable for event-based simulations.

subCommands.name: multi_thread_sleep_time
subCommands.description: Allows the user to explicitly set the time in seconds in which the DIS worker thread will sleep when it is not working.

subCommands.name: max_allowed_bad_entity_states
subCommands.description: Specify the number of “bad” DIS entity state PDUs that will be allowed before future PDUs from an entity are suppressed. A bad entity state PDU includes one or more of the following bad data:

subCommands.name: send_periodic_pdus_while_paused
subCommands.description: Will cause entity state and emission PDUs to be sent while the simulation is paused. This change was implemented as external simulations are permitted to time out and remove remote entities if state PDUs are not received for a specified time.

subCommands.name: suppress_non_standard_data
subCommands.description: If this is set to ‘true’, WSF will only output standard DIS data.

subCommands.name: suppress_comm_data
subCommands.description: Specify if Transmitter, Signal, and Receiver PDUs should be written for communications events. This should be set to true if communications PDUs are not important.

subCommands.name: suppress_emissions_data
subCommands.description: Specify if Emissions PDUs should be written for sensor events. This should be set to true if emissions PDUs are not important.

subCommands.name: use_simple_accelerations
subCommands.description: If present, sets the acceleration fields in the DIS Entity State PDU using a simple rate change calculation equation. The related keywords that can be used to set the orientations rates are use_simple_orientation_rates, use_body_angular_velocities, and zero_body_angular_velocities. By default, if no related keywords are present, orientation rate values for psi, theta, and phi angles are set using the ‘use_simple_orientation_rates’ calculations. To override this behavior use one of the related keywords.

subCommands.name: use_simple_orientation_rates
subCommands.description: If present, uses a simple rate calculation to set the orientation rate fields in the DIS Entity State PDU. This is the default behavior. If the entry is omitted, the fields will still be set using this simple rate calculation. To override this behavior, use either keyword, ‘use_body_angular_velocities’ or ‘zero_body_angular_velocities’.

subCommands.name: use_body_angular_velocities
subCommands.description: If present, uses DIS standard world to body calculations to set the DIS Entity State’s orientation rate fields. If omitted, the simple orientation rate calculation, is used in the DIS Entity State’s orientation rate fields. However, if present, this keyword will override both the ‘use_simple_orientation_rates’ and the ‘zero_body_angular_velocities’ keyword behaviors.

subCommands.name: zero_body_angular_velocities
subCommands.description: If present, zeroes out the DIS Entity State’s orientation rate fields. Will override the ‘use_simple_orientation_rates’ calculations. Will not override the ‘use_body_angular_velocities’ behavior if both keywords are present. Default: Entry Omitted

subCommands.name: map_external_entity
subCommands.description: An incoming DIS entity ID will be checked against the dis entity type to platform type mapping. If there is a corresponding platform type, all components defined for that type will be available to the external platform. The external platform will be treated as a local platform within WSF and its components can then be controlled or monitored as with any WSF platform. Any component capable of sending DIS PDUs from WSF will send DIS PDUs, with the exception of the DIS Entity State PDU, which is not sent. The PDUs will have the external platform’s entity ID in their dis-entity-id field.

subCommands.name: map_external_type
subCommands.description: Same as map_external_entity command, except it will map all entities of the given dis-entity-type rather than a specific DIS entity ID.

subCommands.name: munition_type
subCommands.description: Specify the DIS entity type to be used when sending PDUs for platforms or munitions with the indicated WSF platform type. This command should be specified for each WSF platform type that is present in the scenario. If the type of a platform does not have a corresponding DIS entity type then 0:0:0:0:0:0:0 will be used. For proper WSF interaction of received DIS entities from other networked simulations, a corresponding simple platform_type must be created with defined signatures.

subCommands.name: ew_technique_type
subCommands.description: Specify the DIS jamming mode sequence enumeration associated with a specified WSF Electronic Warfare (EW) technique. For outbound electromagnetic emission PDUs this defines the value for the ‘jamming mode sequence’ field in the PDU for a given WSF defined EW technique for a sensor/jammer. For inbound PDUs, a reverse lookup is performed to determine the WSF EW technique type to be used by the sensor/jammer that needs to be used to provide the additional characteristics needed to properly model interactions with the externally modeled EW techniques. If multiple EW techniques are being used on a beam, only one of them will be sent. Currently, this is only valid for (electronic_attack) techniques.

subCommands.name: warhead
subCommands.description: Specify the DIS warhead enumeration to be used within the burst descriptor field of the DIS fire and detonate PDUs. This enumeration is mapped to an WSF category.

subCommands.name: debug_warfare_pdu
subCommands.description: Specify the level of debugging information for warfare PDUs. This is a bitmask. If bit zero is set, verbose information about received fire and detonate PDUs will be printed to the console. If bit one is set, verbose information about weapon transfers will be printed to the console.

subCommands.name: simple_detonations
subCommands.description: Indicates that simpler rules will be applied to determine the effect of detonation event in a received Fire PDU. If this is enabled and simple_detonations_exclude do not exclude the weapon from simple detonation processing, the following rules will be applied:

subCommands.name: simple_detonations_exclude
subCommands.description: If simple_detonations are enabled, this prevents simple detonation processing from occurring for specific weapon platform types or weapon_effects types. Simple detonation processing will not occur if:

subCommands.name: simple_kill_range
subCommands.description: If simple_detonations are enabled and a target was not specified in a received Fire PDU, a target will be selected (see target_priority for the algorithm). The selected target will be killed if distance between it and the detonation point is less than or equal to the value specified by this command.

subCommands.name: simple_miss_reporting
subCommands.description: If true, causes any reported detonation that did not result in the target being killed to be reported as a 6 (NoneOrNoDetonationDud). Only when the target is killed will the reported detonation result be 1 (EntityImpact). This is used when some receiving applications have limited processing of detonation results.

subCommands.name: suppress_directed_energy_data
subCommands.description: Directed energy data include PDUs that are part of the new extended DIS standard; these include the directed energy fire and entity part damage status PDUs. If this flag is set, only the basic fire and detonate PDUs that correspond with the IEEE 1278.1 DIS standard, will be sent for directed energy weapons.

subCommands.name: suppress_cme_detect_beam
subCommands.description: Specifies whether the Electromagnetic Emissions PDU will NOT include the supplemental beam that indicates targets the sensor is detecting but not yet tracking. The CME applications VESPA and Clouseau use this to draw the white detection lines between the sensor and the target.

subCommands.name: suppress_cme_entity_data
subCommands.description: Specifies whether the supplemental DIS ‘Other’ PDU containing additional entity data for the CME applications VESPA and Clouseau will NOT be sent.

subCommands.name: suppress_cme_draw_data
subCommands.description: Specifies whether the WsfDraw DIS ‘Other’ PDUs containing draw commands will NOT be sent.

subCommands.name: suppress_cme_passive_sensor
subCommands.description: Specifies whether emissions PDUs for passive sensors will NOT be sent.

subCommands.name: use_deprecated_cme_draw_data
subCommands.description: If this is set to true, the WsfDraw DIS ‘Other’ PDUs containing draw commands will be sent using the deprecated format.

subCommands.name: target_priority
subCommands.description: This command is used when a Fire PDU is received and a target entity was not specified in the PDU. When a target entity was not specified in the Fire PDU, the simulation will assign each locally-controlled hostile entity (those that are on a side different from the detonating weapon) a priority based on the following formula and then select the entity with the highest priority:

subCommands.name: use_track_jam_for_tracking_requests
subCommands.description: If ‘true’, this provides an approximate method for a receiver to determine all the places an AESA beam may be pointing. Because a single ESA beam can track many targets and moves faster than any reasonable update rate of the Electromagnetic Emissions PDU, it becomes impossible using the standard DIS protocol for receivers to determine where the beam is looking, thus making it impossible for a high-fidelity ESM model to determine if it could detect the beam.

subCommands.name: incoming_weapon_transfer
subCommands.description: A Fire PDU can be used to signify that a weapon that was fired by an external entity is to modeled (‘flown-out’) locally. The weapon entity in a Fire PDU will be transferred to local control if the Munition field in the Burst Descriptor in the Fire PDU, and optionally the Firing Entity ID, match the <dis-entity-type> and <dis-entity-id> values, respectively. If they match, a weapon will be fired from a weapon system of type <weapon-system-type> in order to model the weapon fly-out.

subCommands.name: outgoing_weapon_transfer
subCommands.description: Specifies that weapons that are launched from the indicated weapon system are to be transferred to external control. Some external application is expected to respond to the Fire PDU and assume control of the launched weapon.

subCommands.name: color2
subCommands.description: Sets the primary and secondary colors used to draw the object.

subCommands.name: layer
subCommands.description: Sets the layer name of this draw object. Unless specified, this object will not be drawn in a layer.

subCommands.name: line_size
subCommands.description: Sets the width of the lines used to draw the object.

subCommands.name: point_size
subCommands.description: Sets the size of the points used to draw the object.

draw_file.description: Specifies that items drawn with WsfDraw or draw are to be saved to a .draw file. WsfDraw output will still be provided over DIS or existing interfaces. This provides a way to record a .draw file that can be opened by the IDE.

drift_rate.description: Specify the rate of drift between the initial and final orbits.

subCommands.name: delta_time
subCommands.description: The desired time past the current time for execution of the maneuver. No Optimizations are performed.

subCommands.name: maximum_delta_time
subCommands.description: The maximum time after the current time to be considered for execution of the maneuver. Optimizations in time will occur between the time of the constraint and the provided time.

subCommands.name: maximum_delta_v
subCommands.description: The maximum delta_v to be considered for execution of the maneuver. Optimizations in time to find minimum delta-v will occur between the time of the constraint and any time limit set by maximum_delta_time.

subCommands.name: optimize_time
subCommands.description: Optimize the targeting solution such that it executes at the earliest possible time. This optimization is also constrained by the maximum_delta_v value, if provided.

subCommands.name: optimize_delta_v
subCommands.description: Optimize the targeting solution such that it executes at a time that minimizes total delta-v expended.

subCommands.name: optimize_cost
subCommands.description: Optimize the targeting solution such that the specified cost is minimized. The available cost functions are:

subCommands.name: tolerance
subCommands.description: Specify the solution search tolerance. The default tolerance is 1.0e-9.

subCommands.name: file_prefix
subCommands.description: Specify the output file prefix. The file extension is specified by the file_format command.

subCommands.name: file_format
subCommands.description: Specify the output file format, which must be either of csv (comma-separated variables) or tsv (tab-separated variables).

subCommands.name: report
subCommands.description: Specify platform names for which eclipse events are to be reported in the output file. The keyword all can be inserted, meaning that eclipse data will be computed for all orbiting platforms.

subCommands.name: debug
subCommands.description: Specifies to use a debug mode to output debug data to the standard output.

subCommands.name: debug
subCommands.description: Specifies to use a debug mode to output debug data to the standard output.

subCommands.name: target_protection_type
subCommands.description: Specifies the target protection type to use for an EA effect. Sets the jamming power based on target protection type specified.

subCommands.name: debug
subCommands.description: Specifies to use a debug mode to output debug data to the standard output.

subCommands.name: effect
subCommands.description: Defines the uniquely named effect for this technique and its derived type, if required.

thread_count.description: Specifies the number of threads in the thread pools to be used to complete the SWEET tasks in parallel.

subCommands.name: run
subCommands.description: Note

subCommands.name: output_rate
subCommands.description: Specifies an output_rate configuration by name (<rate-name>) to be used with the output block of the run input block command. Multiples blocks with different names may be defined.

subCommands.name: output_template
subCommands.description: Specifies an output_template configuration by name (<template-name>) to be used with the output block of the run input block command. Multiples blocks with different names may be defined.

subCommands.name: center_location
subCommands.description: Specifies the center location of this run.

subCommands.name: event_output_file_base_name
subCommands.description: This value, along with the suffix ‘.evt’, forms the filename to which the results will be written. If a values is not specified then the event output is not written.

subCommands.name: perform_flyouts
subCommands.description: Specifies if flyouts should be performed.

subCommands.name: record_file_base_name
subCommands.description: This value, along with the suffix ‘.rep’, forms the filename to which the results will be written. If a values is not specified then the record file is not written.

subCommands.name: repetition_count
subCommands.description: Specifies the number of monte-carlo repetitions to run for this configuration.

subCommands.name: launcher_type
subCommands.description: Specifies the launcher platform type name for the run.

subCommands.name: tracker_type
subCommands.description: Specifies the tracker platform type name for the run.

subCommands.name: sites
subCommands.description: Specifies a list of site using the following commands multiple times:

subCommands.name: xyz
subCommands.description: Specifies the site’s x, y, z location.

subCommands.name: heading
subCommands.description: Specifies the site’s heading.

subCommands.name: speed
subCommands.description: Specifies the site’s speed in the direction of the heading.

subCommands.name: site_grid
subCommands.description: Specifies a site grid configuration using the following commands:

subCommands.name: down_range
subCommands.description: Specifies the site grid’s downrange start, end and step respectively.

subCommands.name: cross_range
subCommands.description: Specifies the site grid’s crossrange start, end and step respectively.

subCommands.name: target_speed
subCommands.description: Specifies the target’s speed.

subCommands.name: target_altitude
subCommands.description: Specifies the target’s altitude.

subCommands.name: target_type
subCommands.description: Specifies the target platform type name for the run.

subCommands.name: use_target_path
subCommands.description: Specifies to use the targets defined flight path.

subCommands.name: target_grid
subCommands.description: Specifies a target grid configuration using the following commands:

subCommands.name: altitude
subCommands.description: Specifies the target’s altitude.

subCommands.name: simple_path
subCommands.description: Specifies a target simple path configuration using the following commands:

subCommands.name: x
subCommands.description: Specifies the target path start x position.

subCommands.name: y
subCommands.description: Specifies the target path start y position.

subCommands.name: z
subCommands.description: Specifies the target path start z position.

subCommands.name: flight_path
subCommands.description: Specifies a flight path using the following input format:

subCommands.name: flight_route
subCommands.description: Specifies a flight route using the following input format:

subCommands.name: output
subCommands.description: Specifies the output data that is to be output. The output block can be defined multiple times within the run input block to tailor output to user needs. The following commands are available:

subCommands.name: file
subCommands.description: Specifies the output filename to output the data of the run to.

subCommands.name: phase
subCommands.description: Specifies the phase of the run in which to output data per the given phases above.

subCommands.name: event_output
subCommands.description: Specifies to output event data.

subCommands.name: summary_output
subCommands.description: Specifies to output run summary data.

subCommands.name: rate_table_name
subCommands.description: Specifies the rate table to use by name, as specified by output_rate command.

subCommands.name: items
subCommands.description: Specifies the items in which to be output and format of those items per the following format:

subCommands.name: events
subCommands.description: Specifies the events that are to be enable or disables per the following commands:

subCommands.name: time
subCommands.description: Specifies the time at which the output will be written.

subCommands.name: period
subCommands.description: Specifies the period in which to output the data for the specified output.

subCommands.name: enable_Pk_table_generation
subCommands.description: Enables the generation of Pk tables for the associated run. Note that Pk table generation is only viable with a site grid, and will effectively be disabled for a target grid regardless of this value.

subCommands.name: Pk_table_target_type
subCommands.description: Sets the name of the target when generating the Pk table directory hierarchy and table headers.

subCommands.name: Pk_table_site_type
subCommands.description: Sets the name of the site when generating the Pk table directory hierarchy and table headers.

subCommands.name: Pk_table_output_directory
subCommands.description: The path location to output the generated Pk table data hierarchy

subCommands.name: Pk_output_length_units
subCommands.description: Converts all output values to use this unit for Pk table generation and directory hierarchy.

subCommands.name: Pk_output_speed_units
subCommands.description: Converts all output speed values to use this unit for Pk table generation and directory hierarchy.

subCommands.name: enable_Pk_table_periodic_flush
subCommands.description: Instead of writing all Pk table data when generation is complete, data may be output when all data points associated with an target altitude has completed processing. This allows the possibility of retaining partial Pk data during very long generation routines in the case of an aborted or interrupted process. This will have no effect on the output process unless multiple altitude values are utilized.

subCommands.name: realistic_blurring
subCommands.description: Specifies to apply a Gaussian distrubution to the range error based on the calculated dynamic range error sigma.

subCommands.name: time_reflected_sigma
subCommands.description: Specifies the reflected time measurement sigma. The reflected time, or scatter time (ts), is the time of reception of a signal that travels from transmitter to target and then to receiver.

subCommands.name: time_direct_sigma
subCommands.description: Specifies the direct time measurement sigma. The direct time (tx) is the time of reception of a signal that travels from transmitter directly to the receiver.

subCommands.name: transmitter_position_sigmas
subCommands.description: Specifies a dual-key table of transmitter platform to the sigmas associated with their location measurement sigmas. Note that the transmitter in a bistatic transaction can be on the red/opposite team. The key is a pairing of the side and domain.

subCommands.name: north_position_error_sigma
subCommands.description: Defines the sensing platform’s north target location error.

subCommands.name: east_position_error_sigma
subCommands.description: Defines the sensing platform’s east target location error.

subCommands.name: down_position_error_sigma
subCommands.description: Defines the sensing platform’s down target location errors.

subCommands.name: reference_time_error
subCommands.description: Needs description.

subCommands.name: inter_system_time_delay
subCommands.description: Defines the relative timing error between the targeting sensor and the reference system (e.g., INS/GPS).

subCommands.name: sensor_timing_error
subCommands.description: Defines the targeting sensor’s internal time measurement error.

subCommands.name: atmospheric_refraction_residual
subCommands.description: Defines the atmospheric refraction compensation error, residual part.

subCommands.name: ground_target_altitude_error
subCommands.description: Defines the altitude error to use for the special case of 3 platforms detecting a “land” or “surface” target. The algorithm still requires a master node and at least 3 slave nodes detecting the target for all other types of targets (e.g., air, unknown) or if this value is not defined.

subCommands.name: file
subCommands.description: Specifies the name of the file to which the event_output is written. If the file already exists, then it will be overwritten. The special name STDOUT indicates the event_output is to be written to standard output. The special name NULL indicates that no event_output is to be written. NULL can be used to cancel a file name specified in an earlier event_output block.

subCommands.name: flush_output
subCommands.description: Specifies if the output buffer should be flushed after each event is written.

subCommands.name: enable
subCommands.description: Specifies the names of the events to be included or excluded in the event log. These commands are typically specified multiple times to select the events of interest. The commands are processed in order of appearance with each successive command selecting or deselecting events as appropriate.

subCommands.name: lat_lon_format
subCommands.description: Specifies the format and number of decimal places for displaying <latitude> and <longitude>.

subCommands.name: time_format
subCommands.description: Specifies the format and number of decimal places for displaying <time>.

subCommands.name: print_eci_locations
subCommands.description: Specifies whether position, velocity, and acceleration data are output referenced to the ECI coordinate frame. This will override the standard output of positions in LLA, and velocities and accelerations in NED coordinates.

subCommands.name: print_failed_message_delivery_attempts
subCommands.description: Specifies if MESSAGE_DELIVERY_ATTEMPT events should be printed if the attempt was unsuccessful.

subCommands.name: print_failed_sensor_detection_attempts
subCommands.description: Specifies if SENSOR_DETECTION_ATTEMPT events should be printed if the attempt was unsuccessful. Setting this to false will dramatically reduce the event file size because only successful detection events will be printed.

subCommands.name: print_single_line_per_event
subCommands.description: Specifies if each event should be printed on a single line.

subCommands.name: print_track_in_message
subCommands.description: If a track is part of a message (such as in a WsfTrackMessage) then also print out the contents of the track itself.

subCommands.name: print_track_covariance
subCommands.description: If covariance data is contained in a track that is being logged, the contents of the track’s covariance matrix are also logged.

subCommands.name: print_track_residual_covariance
subCommands.description: If residual covariance data is contained in a track that is being logged, the contents of the track’s residual covariance matrix are also logged.

subCommands.name: file
subCommands.description: Specifies the name of the file to which the event recording is written. If the file already exists then it will be overwritten.

subCommands.name: use_preset
subCommands.description: Configures the messages that will be output. By default, the default preset is used. The messages output presets are as follows:

subCommands.name: enable
subCommands.description: Specifies the names of the event groups to be included or excluded in the file. These commands are typically specified multiple times to select the events of interest. The commands are processed in order of appearance with each successive command selecting or deselecting events as appropriate.

subCommands.name: maximum_mover_update_interval
subCommands.description: If this value is less than a mover’s update_interval, the mover will use this value instead. If this value is set to 0, the event_pipe will take no active role in mover update timing, which may cause odd behavior in movers with no update-interval.

subCommands.name: entity_state_angle_threshold
subCommands.description: Specifies an angle threshold to control entity-state publish rates. Every time a mover is updated, the previous orientation will be compared to the current orientation, and if the difference does not exceed the threshold, a new entity state will be ignored.

subCommands.name: entity_state_position_threshold
subCommands.description: Specifies a length threshold to control entity-state publish rates. Every time a mover is updated, the extrapolated previous location will be compared to the current location, and if the length between them does not exceed the threshold, a new entity state will be ignored.

subCommands.name: disable_entity_state_thresholds
subCommands.description: Disables the entity-state thresholds, causing entity-state to be published at the movers’ update intervals. This may be overwritten by further calls to entity_state_position_threshold or entity_state_angle_threshold.

subCommands.name: entity_state_maximum_interval
subCommands.description: Specifies a maximum interval of time between entity-state updates. If a platform does not receive an update to its location within this interval, a new state, extrapolated from the last state, will be published.

subCommands.name: visual_part_update_interval
subCommands.description: Specifies the update period at which visual part articulations will be published. Time values should be greater than zero. If unset, visual parts’ articulations will not be published.

report_to.syntax: report_to [ commander | peers | subordinates ] via <xmtr-name> [ to <rcvr-name> ]

subCommands.name: external_link
subCommands.syntax: external_link [ commander | peers | subordinates ] via <xmtr-name> [ to <rcvr-name> ]
subCommands.description: Specifies the intended recipients of the message on the default command_chain. This command may be specified multiple times to cause the message to be routed to multiple sets of recipients.

subCommands.name: report_to_group
subCommands.description: Specifies that the comm object members of the given group name are intended recipients of messages sent by this device. This command may be specified multiple times to cause the message to be routed to multiple groups.

subCommands.name: clear_external_links
subCommands.description: Remove all of the currently defined external links defined by the external_link or report_to commands. This is useful if one wants to reuse an existing platform definition with some modifications.

subCommands.name: debug_external_links
subCommands.description: Enables various messages related to internal processing of external links. This command should precede any other external link commands to ensure all debug output is emitted for parsed input commands.

subCommands.name: debug
subCommands.description: Set debug mode.

subCommands.name: false_target_behavior
subCommands.description: Specifies the fidelity of the false target technique.

subCommands.name: multi_radar_behavior
subCommands.description: Specifies the fidelity of the false target technique across multiple radar sites.

subCommands.name: persistence
subCommands.description: Specifies the persistence of the false target from scan to scan. The number of false targets will be reduced by 1 minus this value from scan to scan.

subCommands.name: quantity
subCommands.description: Specifies the number of false targets to create.

subCommands.name: range_constrained
subCommands.description: Specifies whether false targets can be produced forward of the jammer’s position. To be able to produce false targets forward of the jammer requires detailed knowledge of the targeted radar’s PRF sequence.

subCommands.name: scan_time
subCommands.description: Specify the false-target scan rate/time for the random_scan_to_scan false_target_behavior type.

subCommands.name: false_target_movement
subCommands.description: Defines the movement of the false target blips (i.e., tracks) in terms of direction (heading) and speed. To define the false target movement:

subCommands.name: headings
subCommands.description: Specifies the direction of movement for the false targets wrt due north. If minimum and maximum <angle-value> are equal all headings will be the same on the blips, if they are not equal then random headings will be drawn with the limits and set for each false target blip separately as to its speed.

subCommands.name: speeds
subCommands.description: Specifies the minimum and maximum <speed-value> at which the false targets will move in the direction of the heading. If minimum and maximum speeds are equal all speeds will be the same on the blips, if they are not equal then random speeds will be drawn with the limits and set for each false target blip separately as to its speed.

subCommands.name: reference
subCommands.description: Specifies the heading reference for which to move the false target blips if a non-zero speed is entered desired.

subCommands.name: distribution
subCommands.description: Defines the false target dispersion about the distribution_centroid in the direction of the reference_bearing:

subCommands.name: bearing_reference
subCommands.description: Specifies the bearing reference in which to display false-targets. Works in conjunction with the azimuth_extent input.

subCommands.name: radius
subCommands.description: Specifies the radius in which to generate false-targets around the reference_centroid if entered or the receiver if not.

subCommands.name: sector_arc
subCommands.description: Specifies the sector arc in which to generate false-targets.

subCommands.name: azimuth_extent
subCommands.description: Specifies the azimuth extents in the range of [-180 degrees, 180 deg] of which to produce false-targets. Reference azimuth is to the bearing_reference. This input can be repeated for multiple azimuth extents.

subCommands.name: range_extent
subCommands.description: Specifies the range extents in which to generate false targets around the centroid if entered or the receiver if not. This input can be repeated for multiple range extents.

subCommands.name: range_distribution
subCommands.description: Specifies the range distribution statistical model type to use for the range distribution of the false targets.

subCommands.name: distribution_centroid
subCommands.description: Centroid coordinates for the false target distribution. The centroid is able to move in any specified direction so the false target distribution centroid may change to allow for a new distribution center for random_scan_to_scan false_target_behavior type.

subCommands.name: altitude
subCommands.description: Specifies the altitude of the reference centroid on which to generate false-target.

subCommands.name: position
subCommands.description: Specifies the latitude and longitude of the reference centroid on which to generate false-target.

subCommands.name: heading
subCommands.description: Specifies the heading (i.e., direction of movement) for the centroid.

subCommands.name: speed
subCommands.description: Specifies the speed at which the centroid will move.

subCommands.name: debug
subCommands.description: Set debug mode.

subCommands.name: plot_capacity
subCommands.description: Specifies the total number of targets (real and false) which will be allowed to be displayed at a given time.

subCommands.name: track_capacity
