subCommands.description: Specifies the total number of targets the radar can track at a given time.

subCommands.name: transfer_capacity
subCommands.description: Specifies the total number of targets the radar is allowed to pass to a command or fusion center.

subCommands.name: initial_reject
subCommands.description: <behavior-type> : A string input of the false-target behavior-type the following data applies to, valid values are [“random_scan_to_scan” | “consistent_scan_to_scan”]. Specifies an initial rejection ratio which characterizes the screener’s ability to initially reject some number of false targets configured with the specified <behavior-type>. An input of ‘random_scan_to_scan 0.10’ would allow the screener to reject 10% of false targets configured with ‘random_scan_to_scan behavior’ whether detected or not by the sensor.

subCommands.name: reject
subCommands.description: A string input of the false-target blip behavior-type the following data applies to, valid values are [“random_scan_to_scan” | “consistent_scan_to_scan”]. Specifies a rejection ratio which characterizes the screener’s ability to reject some number of total false target blips configured with the specified <behavior-type> each update of the screener. An input of ‘random_scan_to_scan 0.10’ would allow the screener to reject 10% of false targets blips that are being detected by the sensor with ‘random_scan_to_scan behavior’.

subCommands.name: allow_track_reporting_when_flooded
subCommands.description: Specifies as to whether or not false target tracks are to be reported when the transfer capacity is met. If ‘true’ the screener will allow the sensor’s to report a number of randomly selected tracks up to the transfer capacity each frame; if ‘false then the screener will not allow the sensor’s tracker to report any tracks if transfer capacity is exceeded. The current track capacity includes active and forced false and real targets.

subCommands.name: request_based_tracking
subCommands.description: Specifies as to whether the radar/screener should collect all trackable false targets based on track requests. If set ‘true’ will cause false targets to only be screened if a request has been scheduled for a track to be initially detected or updated. Primarily used for tracking type radars and radars that respond to requests only.

subCommands.name: only_screen_false_target_track_requests
subCommands.description: Specifies as to whether the radar/screener should collect all false targets (i.e., ‘false’) or just the ones in which requests have been made (i.e., ‘true’). If set ‘true’ will cause only the requested false target to only be screened. Primarily used for tracking type radars and radars that respond to requests only.

subCommands.name: force_target_tracks
subCommands.description: Defines the conditions in which a target track can be forced to be tracked by the false_target_screener. To define the dispersion,

subCommands.name: range_force
subCommands.description: Specifies the range_type criteria that will check to see if a target track should be forced or not based on false target blip constraining. Allowed types are:

subCommands.name: sector_force
subCommands.description: Specifies the sector arc, centered around the target track location, along with the maximum false target count in which the target track will be forced.

subCommands.name: range_sector_force
subCommands.description: Specifies the range extent and sector arc, centered around the target track location, along with the maximum false target count in which the target track will be forced.

subCommands.name: j_to_s_delta_threshold
subCommands.description: Specifies the J/S delta in which the false targets will be counted within the defined sector, for use by the sector forcing commands input maximum false target counts. Any false target with a J/S within the delta threshold defined will count towards a competing false target within the sector of interest.

azimuth_field_of_view.description: Specify the minimum and maximum angle about which the subsystem can see in azimuth. The limits are with respect to the current cue. In general these values should be greater than or equal to the azimuth_scan_limits (possibly accounting for the width of the beam when the subsystem is positioned to its scan limit).

subCommands.name: elevation_field_of_view
subCommands.description: Specifies the minimum and maximum angle about which the subsystem can see in elevation. The limits are with respect to the current cue. In general these values should be greater than or equal to the azimuth_scan_limits (possibly accounting for the width of the beam when the subsystem is positioned to its scan limit).

subCommands.name: half_angle
subCommands.description: Specify the half angle from the center to the edge of the circle that the subsystem can see.

subCommands.name: azimuth_elevation
subCommands.description: Specify the az and el values to a point defining the polygonal field of view.

subCommands.name: equatorial_field_of_view
subCommands.description: Specify the minimum and maximum angle about which the subsystem can see in the equatorial coordinate (azimuthal angle of the equatorial celestial sphere). The limits are with respect to the current cue.

subCommands.name: polar_field_of_view
subCommands.description: Specifies the minimum and maximum angle about which the subsystem can see in the polar coordinate (polar angle of the equatorial celestial sphere). The limits are with respect to the current cue.

include.description: Temporarily suspends reading commands from the current file and reads commands from the file <filename>. Reading from the current file will continue when all the commands have been read from the file <filename>. This is very useful for creating a library of platform and system types and attributes that can be used in a number of simulations.

subCommands.name: define_path_variable
subCommands.description: Defines the value of a variable than can be substituted into a file name. References to most WSF components that accept file names will allow path variable substitution to be performed on the name. In path variable substitution, the file name is examined for strings of the form ‘$(name)’ or ‘${name}’ (without the quotes). If such a string is found then it is replaced with:

subCommands.name: undefine_path_variable
subCommands.description: Removes the definition of the path variable with the specified name.

subCommands.name: file_path
subCommands.description: Adds an entry for the specified path to the end of the ‘file path’. <path> is either an absolute path or relative to the directory containing this command.

subCommands.name: reset_file_path
subCommands.description: Deletes all entries in the file path list.

subCommands.name: log_file
subCommands.description: Opens the specified file as the current system log. Any existing contents of the file are discarded.

subCommands.name: log
subCommands.description: Writes all of the remaining information on the current line to the current log file (see log_file). This can be used to write out information (such as a file version) that might be useful for ensuring the correct data is being brought into the simulation.

subCommands.name: debug
subCommands.description: Enable extra debugging output.

subCommands.name: detached
subCommands.description: For formations defined in the initial conditions, this will cause this formation to not be attached to its parent. After initialization any attached formation will have its members placed into the correct positions relative to the formation leader. The detached status on a formation also effects the way formation commands are propagated down through the hierarchy. See WsfFormationCommand.

subCommands.name: offset
subCommands.description: Specify the offset of the formation from its parent. This is the means by which the initial relative positioning of the members of a formation is specified. The offset is given as a triplet of a range from the reference point, a relative bearing from the direction of travel of the leader, and a vertical offset (or stack). For example, the following offset would be the point 100 m to the right of the reference point and at 1 m higher altitude.

subCommands.name: section
subCommands.description: Define a section sub-formation. See Section Formation.

subCommands.name: unit
subCommands.description: Define a unit sub-formation. See Unit Formation.

subCommands.name: lead
subCommands.description: When prefixed before a sub-formation command, this indicates that the following formation defined is the lead sub-formation of the enclosing parent formation. Formation defined in input must have one (and only one) lead sub-formation defined.

subCommands.name: maximum_quantity
subCommands.description: Defines the maximum quantity of fuel that can be carried.

subCommands.name: initial_quantity
subCommands.description: Defines the initial quantity of fuel.

subCommands.name: reserve_quantity
subCommands.description: Defines the threshold such that when the quantity of fuel remaining falls below this value, the platform is considered to be operating on reserves. If an on_reserve block is defined, it will be executed when this state is reached.

subCommands.name: bingo_quantity
subCommands.description: Defines the threshold such that when the quantity of fuel remaining falls below this value, the platform is considered to in BINGO. If an on_bingo block is defined, it will be executed when this state is reached.

subCommands.name: mode
subCommands.description: Specifies the name of the mode to be used for fuel types that support modes.

subCommands.name: on_bingo
subCommands.description: Defines a script to be executed when the quantity of fuel remaining falls below the threshold defined by bingo_quantity.

subCommands.name: on_empty
subCommands.description: Defines a script to be executed when all fuel has been expended.

subCommands.name: on_reserve
subCommands.description: Defines a script to be executed when the quantity of fuel remaining falls below the threshold defined by reserve_quantity.

subCommands.name: on_refuel
subCommands.description: Defines a script to be executed when a refueling operation has been completed.

process_noise_sigmas_xyz.description: Defines the noise standard deviation used by the embedded filter. The values correspond with accelerations in the entity coordinate system (ECS) of the tracked platform.

subCommands.name: process_noise_sigmas_XYZ
subCommands.description: Defines the noise standard deviation used by the embedded filter. The values correspond with accelerations in the entity coordinate system (ECS) of the tracked platform.

subCommands.name: propagator
subCommands.description: Specifies the propagator type that will be used in the WSF_ORBIT_DETERMINATION_FILTER to track the target.

subCommands.name: number_of_angle_measurements
subCommands.description: Specify the number of angles-only measurements to be collected before an angles-only initial orbit determination attempt is made.

subCommands.name: angles_only_linear_tolerance
subCommands.description: Specify the linear tolerance required to converge to a solution with the angles-only initial orbit determination algorithm. Specifying a higher value makes it more likely that a valid solution will be found.

subCommands.name: angles_only_maximum_iterations
subCommands.description: Specify the maximum number of iterations for the angles-only initial orbit determination algorithm to find a solution.

subCommands.name: lambert_convergence_tolerance
subCommands.description: Specify a unitless tolerance for convergence of the Lambert universal-variables algorithm of two locations and time.

subCommands.name: debug
subCommands.description: Prints debug information to std::out.

subCommands.name: debug_filter
subCommands.description: Specifies saving of filtering history information (see filter debug).

subCommands.name: range_error_factor
subCommands.description: Specify the factor that is used to compute the range error when fusing an angles-only track with an existing track (from which a range can be estimated). This factor is multiplied times the estimated range to obtain the estimated range error.

subCommands.name: land_cover
subCommands.description: Specify the land cover for the receiver clutter model. Valid values are:

subCommands.name: land_formation
subCommands.description: Specify the land formation for the receiver clutter model. Valid values are:

subCommands.name: sea_state
subCommands.description: Specify the sea state for the receiver clutter model. Valid values are 0 - 6.

subCommands.name: wind_speed
subCommands.description: Specify the wind speed.

subCommands.name: wind_direction
subCommands.description: Specify the wind direction.

subCommands.name: wind_table
subCommands.description: Specify wind-value-data sets using 3 parameters per entry (from lowest altitude to highest): :altitude <length-value> wind direction <angle-value> wind speed <speed-value>.

subCommands.name: cloud_altitude_limits
subCommands.description: Specify the minimum and maximum altitude extent in which clouds are defined to occur. This is used by some attenuation models.

subCommands.name: cloud_water_density
subCommands.description: Specify the density of water within the cloud. This is used by some attenuation models.

subCommands.name: rain_altitude_limit
subCommands.description: Specify the altitude below which rain is present. This is used by some attenuation models.

subCommands.name: rain_rate
subCommands.description: Specify the rainfall accumulation rate. This is used by some attenuation models.

subCommands.name: central_body
subCommands.description: Specify the central body and related ellipsoid model to be used by simulation platforms. Options for <central body type> are the following:

subCommands.name: polar_offset_angles
subCommands.description: Specify the central_body’s polar offset angles ( and , respectively) of the Celestial Intermediate Pole (CIP) with respect to the WCS (ITRS) coordinate system. Providing these values (of the order of tenths of arc-seconds) enables very highly accurate conversions between ECI and WCS coordinates.

subCommands.name: file
subCommands.description: Specifies the input EGM database type and file, respectively. Supported file formats are grid point access database as supplied by NGA EGM Databases.

subCommands.name: test_point
subCommands.description: Specifies a test latitude-longitude pair to perform lookouts and print geoid height value from the database to standard output for debugging purposes. command may be repeated multiple times to test other latitude-longitude pairs as required.

subCommands.name: aux_data
subCommands.description: Defines auxiliary data for a platform. See aux_data.

altitude.description: Specifies a commanded altitude. Typically used to climb or dive to a cruise altitude and hold the altitude. The altitude reference tag (’msl’, or ‘above mean sea level’; ‘agl’, or ‘above ground level’) may be omitted, in which case ‘msl’ is assumed.

subCommands.name: roll
subCommands.description: Specifies a target orientation angle relative to the wind coordinate system (aligned with the velocity vector with no angle of attack or roll). The corresponding rate command specifies the angular rate to be applied to reaching the target angle.

subCommands.name: pitch_fixed
subCommands.description: Specifies a target orientation angle relative to the North-East-Down coordinate system. The corresponding rate command specifies the angular rate to be applied to reaching the target angle.

subCommands.name: roll_rate
subCommands.description: These commands serve two purposes depending on the context:

subCommands.name: reset
subCommands.description: This is the same as setting the yaw, pitch and roll to zero. The rate commands may be used to specify the rate at which the angles are reset.

subCommands.name: flight_path_angle
subCommands.description: Specifies the target flight path angle at which the pitch over is declared complete in the range (0, 90). If not specified, the first of the following that returns a value is used:

subCommands.name: time_constant
subCommands.description: Specifies the exponential time constant for phasing in the pitch specified pitch rate. The pitch rate will achieve its full value approximately 4 time constants after the program starts.

subCommands.name: proportional_navigation_gain
subCommands.description: Specifies the gain for proportional navigation. A value of zero indicates proportional navigation will not be performed.

subCommands.name: proportional_navigation_limit_angle
subCommands.description: Specifies the 3D aspect angle of the target with respect to the weapon at which the navigation method will switch between proportional and velocity pursuit. Proportional navigation will be used if the target aspect angle is less than or equal to this value, otherwise velocity pursuit will be used.

subCommands.name: proportional_navigation_method
subCommands.description: Specifies whether additional acceleration should be commanded because of current target acceleration.

subCommands.name: velocity_pursuit_gain
subCommands.description: Specifies the gain for velocity pursuit navigation. A value of zero indicates velocity pursuit navigation will not be performed.

subCommands.name: ascent_g_bias
subCommands.description: The gravity bias factor to be applied during ascent. Ascent is defined to be when the flight path angle is greater than the value defined in coarse_adjustment_threshold (default of 0.5 degrees).

subCommands.name: maximum_lateral_acceleration
subCommands.description: The maximum lateral acceleration that will be applied to adjust the trajectory during orbit insertion. This does not include any acceleration imposed by gravity.

subCommands.name: minimum_insertion_altitude
subCommands.description: The program will not attempt orbit insertion when the altitude is less than this value.

subCommands.name: coarse_adjustment_threshold
subCommands.description: Defines the flight path angle at which the platform is no longer considered to be in ascent. All gravity bias is disabled when the flight path angle is less this value but greater than the fine_adjustment_threshold. This allows the ascending platform to naturally settle towards a flight path angle of zero.

subCommands.name: fine_adjustment_threshold
subCommands.description: Defines the flight path angle at which ‘fine adjustment’ occurs. When the absolute value of the flight path angle is less than this value then program will actively manage the altitude so as to achieve orbit. This may mean holding the altitude to allow the speed to build to that required to maintain orbit, or if the speed is already too great, let the altitude increase.

subCommands.name: show_orbit
subCommands.description: Write diagnostic information about the orbit conditions when orbit conditions are satisfied.

subCommands.name: on_injection
subCommands.description: Additional actions to take when the program declares orbit conditions are satisfied.

subCommands.name: final_radius
subCommands.description: The semi-major axis (radius) of the final circular orbit.

subCommands.name: side
subCommands.description: One or more sides for which the IFF mapping rules apply. If default is specified then the IFF mapping rules apply to all sides not explicitly defined.

subCommands.name: side-name
subCommands.description: The ‘side’ (‘team’ or ‘affiliation’) for which the IFF mapping applies. Refers to blue, red, country or team name.

subCommands.name: reports
subCommands.description: Indicates the IFF status to report for the given side, category, or by default.

subCommands.name: for_side
subCommands.description: Indicates the IFF mapping between sides.

subCommands.name: for_category
subCommands.description: Indicates the IFF mapping between platforms from a given side and platforms from a given category.

subCommands.name: by_default
subCommands.description: Indicates the IFF mapping between platforms form a given side and all sides and categories not explicitly mapped.

subCommands.name: interpolate_tables
subCommands.description: Specifies whether to apply interpolation to the defined Azimuth-Elevation Table Definition. The type of interpolation can be either linear or logarithmic (see interpolation_type).

subCommands.name: interpolation_type
subCommands.description: Specifies whether to use linear or logarithmic interpolation when interpolating data in the azimuth elevation tables.

subCommands.name: state
subCommands.description: Indicates that the following table definition will be used when the platform is in the signature state <state-name>. If <state-name> is default then the subsequent table will be used if the platform is in a signature state that does not match any of the states defined in the signature.

delta_time.description: The desired time past the current time for execution of the maneuver. No Optimizations are performed.

subCommands.name: maximum_delta_time
subCommands.description: The maximum time after the current time to be considered for execution of the maneuver. Optimizations in time will occur between the time of the constraint and the provided time.

subCommands.name: maximum_delta_v
subCommands.description: The maximum delta_v to be considered for execution of the maneuver. Optimizations in time to find minimum delta-v will occur between the time of the constraint and any time limit set by maximum_delta_time.

subCommands.name: optimize_time
subCommands.description: Optimize the targeting solution such that it executes at the earliest possible time. This optimization is also constrained by the maximum_delta_v value, if provided.

subCommands.name: optimize_delta_v
subCommands.description: Optimize the targeting solution such that it executes at a time that minimizes total delta-v expended.

subCommands.name: optimize_cost
subCommands.description: Optimize the targeting solution such that the specified cost is minimized. The available cost functions are:

subCommands.name: tolerance
subCommands.description: Specify the solution search tolerance. The default tolerance is 1.0e-9.

subCommands.name: define_offset
subCommands.description: Define the offset name and location on the intersection mesh associated with the target area of interest (see example above).

subCommands.name: file
subCommands.description: Define the file for the intersection mesh associated with this definition.

subCommands.name: debug
subCommands.description: Enables debug printouts during run time.

subCommands.name: no_debug
subCommands.description: Disables debug printouts during run time.

subCommands.name: maximum_location_change
subCommands.description: The distance a platform must move when determining whether LOS information needs updating.

subCommands.name: vegetation_layer_masking
subCommands.description: Indicates that line of sight masking is to be performed with the vegetation layer of the terrain instead of the bare earth layer.

subCommands.name: debug
subCommands.description: Writes additional information to standard output when debugging the LOS manager’s main thread logic.

subCommands.name: use_height_for_ground_platforms
subCommands.description: Indicates that a ground platform’s height is to be added to its altitude when doing terrain masking checks.

subCommands.name: multi_thread
subCommands.description: Creates a worker thread for processing line-of-sight calculations.

subCommands.name: debug_thread
subCommands.description: Writes additional information to standard output when debugging the LOS manager’s worker thread logic.

subCommands.name: number_of_priority_levels
subCommands.description: The number of priority levels used when processing line-of-sight calculation requests.

subCommands.name: max_steps_in_priority_level
subCommands.description: The number of requests received for a given LOS interaction required before it moves up in priority.

subCommands.name: processing_rate
subCommands.description: The number of line-of-sight updates performed by the worker thread in one cycle. A cycle consists of processing requests, determining priority, and then updating the LOS data. This keeps the thread from getting stuck processing requests and never getting to actually updating the LOS data. It also facilitates pausing the thread, since this can only be done between cycles.

subCommands.name: tdl_header
subCommands.description: <header-type> : The TDL header type used when writing DIS Signal messages. This can be either 6 or 100.

subCommands.name: swap_tdl_header_100_method
subCommands.description: We support two different ways of transmitting TDL-100. <swap-type> can be fields_only or fields_then_word_boundary.

subCommands.name: print_script_usage
subCommands.description: Outputs information about the WsfTadilJ classes for scripting J-Messages.

subCommands.name: ignore_inbound_messages
subCommands.description: Specifies whether to ignore inbound l16 DIS messages. If this is set to true, WSF will not attempt to process j-messages received over DIS. This does not affect J11 messages.

subCommands.name: pattern-name
subCommands.description: The name to be given to the pattern. This is the name that is referenced by the masking_pattern on a comm or sensor device. A pattern may be redefined, with the last occurrence being used.

subCommands.name: state
subCommands.description: Indicates that the following table definition(s) will be used when the articulated is in the state <state-name>. If default is specified then the subsequent table will be used if the articulated part is in a state that does not match any of the states defined in the signature.

subCommands.name: platform_factor
subCommands.description: Indicates the following table defines a platform-relative masking pattern. The azimuth and elevation angles in the table are relative to the platform.

subCommands.name: part_factor
subCommands.description: Indicates the following table defines a part-relative masking pattern. The azimuth and elevation angles in the table a relative to the part.

subCommands.name: platform_type
subCommands.description: Defines a platform type that can be referenced by the platform command. The <new-type-name> must be unique to the simulation. Convention is to make <new-type-name> uppercase. The <source-type-name> can either be a previously defined platform type or be WSF_PLATFORM. WSF_PLATFORM is the only <source-type-name> predefined platform type in WSF.

subCommands.name: side
subCommands.description: Specify the ‘side’ (‘team’ or ‘affiliation’) to which platforms of this type belong. The side subcommand refers to blue, red, country or team name. Refer to the specific visualization application or tool to see what sides are supported.

subCommands.name: icon
subCommands.description: Specify the name of the icon to be used when platforms of this type are displayed and if the platform type does not have an associated entity_type subcommand in the dis_interface block.

subCommands.name: marking
subCommands.description: Specifies a marking to be applied to the platform. This text field is associated with this platform in the dis_interface.

subCommands.name: indestructible
subCommands.description: Indicates that the platform type is indestructible. Each hit will update the cumulative probability of survival according to the formula:

subCommands.name: on_broken
subCommands.description: Indicates what should be done when the platform is broken.

subCommands.name: spatial_domain
subCommands.syntax: spatial_domain [ land | air | subsurface | surface | space]
subCommands.description: Indicates the primary spatial domain in which the platform operates. This is sometimes used to classify if an object is a ‘land’ object, ‘space’ object, etc.

subCommands.name: acoustic_signature
subCommands.description: Specifies the acoustic signature definition for this platform type. The signature type must have been defined with acoustic_signature.

subCommands.name: infrared_signature
subCommands.description: Specifies the infrared signature definition for this platform type. The signature type must be previously defined with infrared_signature.

subCommands.name: inherent_contrast
subCommands.description: Default None.

subCommands.name: optical_reflectivity
subCommands.description: Specifies the optical reflectivity definition for this platform type. The signature type must have been defined with optical_reflectivity.

subCommands.name: optical_signature
subCommands.description: Specifies the optical signature definition for this platform type. The signature type must have been defined with optical_signature.

subCommands.name: radar_signature
subCommands.description: Specifies the radar signature definition for this platform type. The signature type must have been defined with radar_signature.

subCommands.name: geo_point
subCommands.description: Defines a named location with a latitude, longitude, altitude tuple. The location can be accessed using the WsfPlatform.GeoPoint script method.

subCommands.name: position
subCommands.description: Specifies the latitude and longitude of the platform. This command is only for static platforms without movers.

subCommands.name: nutation_update_interval
subCommands.description: Specifies the time interval between updates to nutation calculations that are used in WCS-ECI coordinate conversions.

subCommands.name: precession_nutation_update_interval
subCommands.description: Specifies the time interval between updates to nutation calculations that are used in WCS-ECI coordinate conversions.

subCommands.name: mgrs_coordinate
subCommands.description: Specifies the coordinates of the platform in the Military Grid Reference System. This command is only for static platforms without movers.

subCommands.name: altitude
subCommands.description: Specifies the altitude of the platform. This command is only for static platforms without movers. It is ignored if a mover is defined in the platform.

subCommands.name: creation_time
subCommands.description: Specifies the simulation time at which the platform is to be added to the simulation. The platform exists in memory but is not yet a player in the simulation.

subCommands.name: heading
subCommands.description: Specifies the orientation of the platform. This command is only for static platforms without movers. It is ignored if a mover is defined in the platform.

subCommands.name: empty_mass
subCommands.description: Specifies the empty mass of the platform, which is usually a fixed quantity.

subCommands.name: fuel_mass
subCommands.description: Specifies the fuel mass of the platform. When specified by a user in an input file, the value is assumed to be a fixed quantity. However, if the platform contains a fuel object, it is permitted and even expected to modify the fuel mass during run time, overwriting what was specified with this keyword.

subCommands.name: payload_mass
subCommands.description: Specifies the payload mass of the platform. When specified by a user in an input file, the value is assumed to be a fixed quantity. However, certain run-time events (e.g., dropping buoys) may change the payload mass.

subCommands.name: concealment_factor
subCommands.description: Used to denote how well a platform is VISUALLY concealed. A value of 0.0 means there is no attempt to hide. A factor of 1.0 means that it is hidden in such a way as to be undetectable (such as in a building or in an underground bunker). Values between the endpoints represent increasing amounts of camouflage. Most sensors will not detect platforms with a concealment factor of 1.0, but any lesser value has no effect.

subCommands.name: initial_damage_factor
subCommands.description: The damage factor is a value in the range [0 .. 1] and is used to indicate the amount of damage to the platform. A value of 0 indicates no damage while a value of 1 indicates the platform is ‘broken.’

subCommands.name: track_manager
subCommands.description: Commands within this block are processed by the platform’s master track manager. See track_manager.

subCommands.name: aux_data
subCommands.description: Defines auxiliary data for a platform. See aux_data.

subCommands.name: width
subCommands.description: Specifies the dimensions of the platform.

subCommands.name: category
subCommands.description: Specifies that the platform is a member of the category specified. Categories can be used to force sensors to ignore the platform. Categories are also accessible through the WsfPlatform.CategoryMemberOf script method.

subCommands.name: clear_categories
subCommands.description: Has the effect of canceling any previous category command.

subCommands.name: group_leave
subCommands.description: Adds or removes the platform from the specified group.

subCommands.name: command_chain
subCommands.description: commander specifies the platform’s immediate superior (commander) in the default chain of command.

subCommands.name: route
subCommands.description: The route subcommand provides a collection of waypoints that define a path, or route, for platform movers.

subCommands.name: mover
subCommands.description: A mover defines the domain in which a platform can move and how it moves within the domain.

subCommands.name: fuel
subCommands.description: A fuel object can be attached to a platform to model the effects of fuel consumption.

subCommands.name: delete
subCommands.description: Adds a component to the platform, modifies or removes an existing component.

subCommands.name: track
subCommands.description: Defines a pre-briefed track.

subCommands.name: use_zone
subCommands.description: Attach a copy of the specified zone to the platform under the name <zone-name>. If the specified zone does not define a pose, the copied zone uses the current pose of the platform. This command can be repeated as necessary.

subCommands.name: zone_set
subCommands.description: The zone and zone_set subcommands define:

subCommands.name: navigation_errors
subCommands.description: The navigation_errors block provides a method to define error in where the platform thinks it is located versus where it is really located. Please see navigation_errors for a description of the inputs.

subCommands.name: on_damage_received
subCommands.description: An optional script that can be defined which will receive control whenever there is damage to the platform.

subCommands.name: on_platform_deleted
subCommands.description: An optional script that can be defined which will receive control just before the platform is removed from the simulation.

subCommands.name: on_subordinate_deleted
subCommands.description: Optional scripts that can be defined which will be executed just before other platforms within the platform’s command_chain hierarchy are removed from the simulation. The single argument to each script is a reference to the platform pending removal.

subCommands.name: callback
subCommands.description: A callback is a named action that can be called via the execute command of a route when the platform reaches a particular waypoint within the route.

subCommands.name: weapon_effects_type
subCommands.description: This command defines name of the weapon_effects for the platform. This is typically used only when the platform is the WSF_EXPLICIT_WEAPON of WSF_EXPLICIT_WEAPON.

subCommands.name: channels
subCommands.description: Defines the number of channels available to a medium, in other words, if multiplexing is available. The number of channels determines how many concurrent transmissions may be handled by this medium, and subsequently by all communication objects utilizing this medium.

subCommands.name: default_mode_name
subCommands.description: Specifies the default mode to be used for transmissions over this medium. Every medium has a default mode named as “default” using default values. Unless this command is used, the “default” mode will be used during typical medium processing. Note that the default mode may be modified by explicitly defining the “default” mode using the mode command.

subCommands.name: use_sharing
subCommands.description: By default, mediums are shared between every object that refers to a particular globally defined medium type. If use_sharing is indicated to be false, then this medium type definition will result in every usage of this medium instantiating their own instance. This allows the type definition to act as a simple template for each instance, while avoiding sharing the actual medium itself.

subCommands.name: mode
subCommands.description: The mode command is used to define an individual mode for this medium. It may be repeated any number of times, with the restriction that each mode must have a unique string name. The actual commands available for any given mode is determined by the medium type being used.

subCommands.name: ModeOnTransmit
subCommands.description: Defines an optional script method that is invoked every time a message is attempting transmission over this medium. A user may specify the mode intended for transmission over this medium by returning the string identifier for the mode.

subCommands.name: comm_type
subCommands.description: Introduces a block of type, sub_type and default commands that define the message sizes and optional priorities for messages that originate from comm devices of the specified <comm-type>.

subCommands.name: default_comm_type
subCommands.description: Introduces a block of type, sub_type and default commands that define the message sizes and optional priorities for messages that originate from comm devices that do not have a corresponding comm_type entry.

subCommands.name: type
subCommands.description: Specifies the size and optional priority for a message of the specified type.

subCommands.name: default
subCommands.description: Specifies the default size and optional priority for messages that did not have an applicable type command.

subCommands.name: subtype
subCommands.description: Specifies the size and optional priority for a message of the specified sub-type, and the most recently specified type (or default).

subCommands.name: side
subCommands.description: Specifies the side for which the WEZ parameters apply. The available options are ‘red’ and ‘blue’.

subCommands.name: type
subCommands.description: Specifies the missile type for which the WEZ parameters apply. The available options are ‘mrm’ (medium-range missile) and ‘srm’ (short-range missile).

subCommands.name: avg_speed
subCommands.description: The average missile speed that will be used in the WEZ calculations.

subCommands.name: max_time_of_flight
subCommands.description: The missile’s maximum time of flight that will be used in the WEZ calculations.

subCommands.name: max_off_boresight_angle
subCommands.description: The maximum angle off the nose from the launching aircraft to the target.

subCommands.name: min_time_of_flight
subCommands.description: The missile’s minimum time of flight that will be used in the WEZ calculations.

subCommands.name: nominal_pk
subCommands.description: The nominal probability of kill used in equation (1) above.

subCommands.name: head_on_pk_reduction
subCommands.description: A reduction factor that accounts for head-on effects. This number must be between 0.0 and 1.0. See equation (1) above for usage.

subCommands.name: broadside_pk_reduction
subCommands.description: A reduction factor that accounts for broadside effects. This number must be between 0.0 and 1.0. See equation (1) above for usage.

final_run_number.description: Set the run number of the final run of the set.

subCommands.name: generate_random_seeds
subCommands.description: This command causes a set of random number seeds to be generated for performing a set of simulation runs. The value is used to specify the initial seed to be used for generating the random number seeds. A vector of random number seeds will be generated when the first run is performed, with the number of seeds generated equal to the value of final_run_number. The random number generator for a particular run will be initialized at the start of using the random number seed associated with the current run number.

subCommands.name: initial_run_number
subCommands.description: Set the run number of the initial run of the set. This command, along with final_run_number is useful for either repeating a specific run or it can be used with the run_number_increment to partition a Monte Carlo set among multiple computers (see run_number_increment for an example).

subCommands.name: run_number_increment
subCommands.description: Set the increment for the runs to be executed. This command is useful for subdividing a large number of Monte Carlo iterations among multiple computers.

subCommands.name: update_interval
subCommands.description: If non-zero, specifies a periodic time interval at which the simulation will call the mover. If zero then the mover will be called only when it is necessary to determine the position of the containing platform.

subCommands.name: update_time_tolerance
subCommands.description: When a position update is requested by the simulation, if the time since the previous update is less than or equal to this value then the mover will ignore the update.

subCommands.name: fidelity
subCommands.description: Defines the fidelity value of the component, which determines which acoustic_signature to use at run-time. Must be between 0 and 1 inclusive. This value maps directly to the fidelity_range defined in the model commands. In other words, if two models are defined with the first having fidelity_range 0 to 0.5 and the second having 0.5 to 1, any fidelity between 0 and 0.5 (but exclusive of 0.5) will select the first model.

subCommands.name: model
subCommands.description: Defines or edits a contained acoustic_signature model with the name given by the string. Implicit adding (or editing if the named model exists) is supported along with explicit adding and editing with the add and edit commands.

subCommands.name: fidelity_range
subCommands.description: Defines the range of fidelity values over which this model should be used. Must be between 0 and 1 inclusive, in increasing order and must not overlap with another model’s fidelity_range on this component.

subCommands.name: default
subCommands.description: If specified, this model will be used as the default choice if no fidelity match is made.

subCommands.name: acoustic_signature
subCommands.description: Defines the acoustic_signature model’s type and parameters specific to this model instantiation. The acoustic_signature is required when first defining a new model, and must not be specified when editing an existing model.

subCommands.name: common
subCommands.description: Defines common parameters to forward to all currently specified acoustic_signature models. These parameters must be valid for all currently defined acoustic_signature models.

target_platform.description: Specify the platform relative to which the executing platform will perform a Teardrop maneuver.

subCommands.name: radial_offset_at_poca
subCommands.description: Specify the distance at the point of closest approach. This distance will be entirely in the radial direction, with a positive value indicating that the teardrop will be above the target_platform. The provided value must be non-zero.

subCommands.name: period
subCommands.description: Specify the time taken to execute the teardrop maneuver. This period must be no greater than about 40.6 percent of the orbital period of the target_platform. The period covers from when the executing platform first passes directly under (over) the target, and when it passes under (over) the target for the last time. These times are at half the given period before the point of closest approach and half the period after the point of closest approach.

subCommands.name: time_to_poca
subCommands.description: Specify the duration after the executing platform is inserted onto the teardrop orbit at which it reaches the point of closest approach to the target_platform. This value must be greater than half of the specified period.

subCommands.name: repetitions
subCommands.description: Specify the number of times the executing platform should traverse the teardrop. This provided value must be positive.

subCommands.name: delta_time
subCommands.description: The desired time past the current time for execution of the maneuver. No Optimizations are performed.

subCommands.name: maximum_delta_time
subCommands.description: The maximum time after the current time to be considered for execution of the maneuver. Optimizations in time will occur between the time of the constraint and the provided time.

subCommands.name: maximum_delta_v
subCommands.description: The maximum delta_v to be considered for execution of the maneuver. Optimizations in time to find minimum delta-v will occur between the time of the constraint and any time limit set by maximum_delta_time.

subCommands.name: optimize_time
subCommands.description: Optimize the targeting solution such that it executes at the earliest possible time. This optimization is also constrained by the maximum_delta_v value, if provided.

subCommands.name: optimize_delta_v
subCommands.description: Optimize the targeting solution such that it executes at a time that minimizes total delta-v expended.

subCommands.name: optimize_cost
subCommands.description: Optimize the targeting solution such that the specified cost is minimized. The available cost functions are:

subCommands.name: tolerance
subCommands.description: Specify the solution search tolerance. The default tolerance is 1.0e-9.

subCommands.name: gps_vertical_error
subCommands.description: Define the standard deviation of a Gaussian distribution, which is used to create the in-track, cross-track and vertical components of the location error vector when GPS is available.

subCommands.name: gps_degraded_multiplier
subCommands.description: Specify a value by which computed GPS location errors will be multiplied when gps_status is degraded (2).

subCommands.name: gps_status
subCommands.description: Set the initial operating state:

subCommands.name: ins_accelerometer_bias_error
subCommands.description: Define the standard deviation of the accelerometer error used when GPS is not available.

subCommands.name: ins_gyroscope_bias_error
subCommands.description: Define the standard deviation of the gyroscope bias error used when GPS is not available.

subCommands.name: ins_vertical_error
subCommands.description: Define the standard deviation of a Gaussian distribution, which is used to create the vertical component of the location error vector when GPS is not available.

subCommands.name: ins_xy_errors
subCommands.description: Specify an custom error model for each axis in the platform’s entity coordinate system (ECS), applicable when gps_status is set to “INS” (-1). Each entry for a given axis represents an term of a polynomial with the specified coefficient and exponent.

subCommands.name: time_history_path
subCommands.description: This enables the writing of a time history file that shows the true position and error components as a function of time. <dir-name> is the name of the directory to which the file will be written. The file name will be:

subCommands.name: randomness
subCommands.description: Specifies whether location errors are computed as gaussian random numbers. If so, the location errors (gps_in_track_error, gps_cross_track_error, and gps_vertical_error) are used as the standard deviations in the random number generation. If disabled, the location errors are interpreted as constant offsets.

subCommands.name: network_address
subCommands.description: If specified, assigns the network to the provided address. The number of assignable objects to this address will also be defined by the address CIDR value. The address provided for this network must not collide with any other network or reserved addresses.

subCommands.name: noise_frequency
subCommands.description: Specifies the number of posts defined in the noise function at the lowest octave. Higher noise frequency will result in more unique clouds in the function.

subCommands.name: noise_octaves
subCommands.description: Specifies the number of octaves defined in the noise function. Each octave adds higher frequency and lower amplitude noise to the noise function. Higher octaves will result in more fractal detail. The table below visually demonstrates the effects of noise_frequency and noise_octaves.

subCommands.name: threshold
subCommands.description: Specifies the threshold of a step function applied to the noise function. Every noise function point above the threshold will be considered cloud, and everything below will be clear sky. The table below visually demonstrates the effect of the threshold.

subCommands.name: scalar
subCommands.description: The 3D noise function is cyclical. The scalar value will determine the frequency of the repetition.

subCommands.name: constant_height
subCommands.description: The constant_height determines how high above sea level the cloud layer will be set.

subCommands.name: thickness
subCommands.description: When a sensor or comm beam intersects a cloud in the layer, this value will be returned as the penetration length.

subCommands.name: use_global_wind
subCommands.description: When this is set, the cloud layer will use the wind_speed and wind_direction defined in the global_environment.

subCommands.name: origin
subCommands.description: Defines the wind origin for the cloud. The wind direction will be most correct around this location.

subCommands.name: sensor_modifier
subCommands.description: This defines the attenuation effect of a cloud hit. sensor devices will indicate they will be attenuated by the cloud layer by using the modifier_category command in their definitions. The value is a number 0 - 1. The attenuation value is set up to be a percentage loss per meter within the zone.

subCommands.name: comm_modifier
subCommands.description: This defines the attenuation effect of a cloud hit. comm devices will indicate they will be attenuated by the cloud layer by using the modifier_category command in their definitions. The value is a number 0 - 1. The attenuation value is set up to be a percentage loss per meter within the zone.

subCommands.name: disable
subCommands.description: Enable or disable a script observer for the specified <EVENT_TYPE>. If the <user defined script name> is the same as the <EVENT_TYPE> actual script name, the <user defined script name> is not required. Not all of the information that is printed with the event_output command is available to the observer.

term.description: Specify a term to be added into the orbital dynamics. Each term will have its own set of input commands to control its contribution to the dynamics.

subCommands.name: wgs84
subCommands.description: Use the WGS84 gravitational parameter.

subCommands.name: egm96
subCommands.description: Use the EGM96 gravitational parameter. This is selected by default.

subCommands.name: gravitational_parameter
subCommands.description: Specify the gravitational parameter in SI units.

subCommands.name: j2
subCommands.description: Specify the strength of the J2 perturbation. The default value is 0.0010826267 (see Vallado, Fundamentals of Astrodynamics and Applications, 4th Edition).

subCommands.name: mean_radius
subCommands.description: Specify the mean radius of the Earth in meters. The default value is 6371 km.

subCommands.name: interpolation_interval
subCommands.description: Specify the interpolation interval for the Moon’s position. Set this to 0.0 to turn off interpolation. The default value is 600 seconds.

subCommands.name: cross_sectional_area
subCommands.description: Specify the cross-sectional area to use when computing the drag.

subCommands.name: drag_coefficient
subCommands.description: Specify the drag coefficient to use when computing the drag.

subCommands.name: atmosphere_model
subCommands.description: Specify the name of the atmosphere model that will be used by this drag term. For details on specifying atmosphere models for use with this term, please see Atmosphere Model.

subCommands.name: script
subCommands.description: Specify the script function defined in the global context that computes an acceleration. The script method provided should return a Vec3 with the computed acceleration. The script method will be provided the following arguments: the WsfIntegratingSpaceMover experiencing this dynamical term, the current mass of the platform, the time at which the script is called as a Calendar, the Vec3 ECI position of the platform, and the Vec3 ECI velocity of the platform.

subCommands.name: maneuver
subCommands.description: Specify an event that is to be executed as part of a executed as part of an orbital mission sequence. A constraint can be specified to delay execution of the event. With many events, a specific constraint type is required, but for some other events it is optional. Consult the documentation for each event type for allowed constraints.

subCommands.name: finite
subCommands.description: Specify that the event is to be executed over a finite time (i.e., it is non-impulsive).

subCommands.name: duration
subCommands.description: The desired duration of finite events. If no duration is specified, the event will be executed as quickly as possible.

subCommands.name: update_interval
subCommands.description: The update_interval for which finite events are updated.

subCommands.name: relative_time
subCommands.description: Execute the event at a relative time in the future.

subCommands.name: apoapsis
subCommands.description: Execute the event once the satellite reaches one of the apses (either periapsis or apoapsis).

subCommands.name: descending_node
subCommands.description: Execute the event once the satellite reaches either the ascending or descending nodes.

subCommands.name: descending_radius
subCommands.description: Execute the event once the satellite reaches the specified radius, and after reaching either the ascending or descending nodes.

subCommands.name: southern_intersection
subCommands.description: Execute the event once the satellite reaches a event-specific northern latitude intersection or a southern latitude intersection.

subCommands.name: eclipse_exit
subCommands.description: Execute the event when the satellite enters or exits earth’s shadow.

integrator.description: Specify the integrator used to propagate the state of the platform. Each integrator will have its own set of inputs that control its behavior.

subCommands.name: tolerance
subCommands.description: This gives the error tolerance for a single step of the integrator. The default value for the tolerance is 1.0e-10.

subCommands.name: max_adjustment_attempts
subCommands.description: The maximum number of timestep adjustments attempts that will be made. If a suitable timestep is not found, a warning will be printed and the simulation will continue, but the satisfaction of the user requested tolerance is no longer guaranteed. The default value for this is 50.

subCommands.name: max_step_size
subCommands.description: The maximum timestep in seconds. If the integrator would adapt its step size to larger than this value, it will use this value for the step size instead. The default value for this is effectively infinite.

subCommands.name: min_step_size
subCommands.description: The minimum allowable timestep in seconds. If the integrator would adapt its step size to smaller than this value, it will use this value for the step size instead. The default value for this is 0.

subCommands.name: initial_step_size
subCommands.description: The size of the initial step size in seconds for the first integration attempt. The default step size for this parameter is 0.1.

subCommands.name: error_criterion
subCommands.description: Set the criterion for assessing the error in a step. The possible values are L_infinity and L_2. Selecting L_infinity will require that the maximum magnitude of any component of the error in the solution be smaller than the specified tolerance. Selecting L_2 will require the square root of the sum of the squared errors be smaller than the tolerance. Further, this error is computed as relative to the difference in the state over the computed step.

speed.description: Specifies the speed of the launching platform. This should used only when the launching platform is an aircraft.

subCommands.name: pitch
subCommands.description: Specifies the pitch angle of the launching platform. This should be used only when the launch platform is an aircraft and the speed is greater than zero.

subCommands.name: leo_data_file
subCommands.description: Name of the file generated for low Earth orbit (LEO) calculations.

subCommands.name: launch_heading
subCommands.description: Single value of launch headings to be used for trajectory propagation.

subCommands.name: launch_headings
subCommands.description: Range of launch headings to be used for trajectory propagation tests.

subCommands.name: loft_angle
subCommands.description: Single value of loft angle to be used for trajectory propagation.

subCommands.name: loft_angles
subCommands.description: Range of loft angles to be used for trajectory propagation tests.

subCommands.name: pitch_rate
subCommands.description: Single value of pitch rate that overrides the value of ‘pitch_rate’ by any FLIGHT_PATH_ANGLE_PROGRAM on the vehicle.

subCommands.name: pitch_rates
subCommands.description: Range of pitch rate values that overrides the value of ‘pitch_rate’ by any FLIGHT_PATH_ANGLE_PROGRAM on the vehicle.

maneuvering.description: Specifiy a model for executing orbital maneuvers in space.

subCommands.name: maneuver_update_interval
subCommands.description: The update interval at which finite maneuvering events are evaluated.

subCommands.name: delta_v
subCommands.description: The total amount of “delta-V” available to the parent platform for performing maneuvers.

subCommands.name: maximum_acceleration
subCommands.description: The maximum acceleration available to perform finite maneuvers.

subCommands.name: specific_impulse
subCommands.description: Provide the specific impulse of the stage in vacuum, typically expressed in seconds.

subCommands.name: thrust
subCommands.description: Provide the total thrust () of the stage.

subCommands.name: burn_rate
subCommands.description: Provide the burn (fuel depletion) rate ().

subCommands.name: exhaust_velocity
subCommands.description: Provide the propellant exhaust velocity ().

subCommands.name: total_mass
subCommands.description: Specify the initial_mass (), defined to be the propellant_mass plus the final_mass.

subCommands.name: empty_mass
subCommands.description: Specify the final (empty) mass (), defined to be the initial_mass minus the propellant_mass.

subCommands.name: fuel_mass
subCommands.description: Specify the propellant mass, defined to be the initial_mass minus the final_mass.

mission_sequence.description: Specify a sequence of pre-determined orbital mission events. The first mission event specified is executed first, then the second, etc. An optional constraint can be specified to delay execution of the sequence; otherwise the mission event will begin executing at the creation time of the platform.

debug_output_wsf.description: Write additional information to standard output that can be processed by the CME tool “sedit’.

subCommands.name: debug_output_oe
subCommands.description: Write additional information about the orbital elements to standard output.

subCommands.name: debug_output_stk
subCommands.description: Write additional information to standard output that can be used for comparing the orbit with the Satellite Tool Kit (STK) from Analytical Graphics, Inc.

subCommands.name: debug_output_xyz
subCommands.description: Write additional information to standard output that can be used for comparing the orbit with the Satellite Tool Kit (STK) from Analytical Graphics, Inc.

subCommands.name: debug
subCommands.description: Enables or disables debugging output to command line (standard out). Provides more verbose information for debugging when true.

subCommands.name: network
subCommands.description: Defines the attributes and vehicles that are generated on the defined route_network as specified by the <route-network-name>.

subCommands.name: vehicle_count
subCommands.description: Specifies the number of vehicles that will be generated on the route network.

subCommands.name: maximum_speed
subCommands.description: The maximum speed any vehicle on the network can travel even if a faster speed is specified in the vehicle block. Generally, it will be more effective to define speed limits for individual routes or to define a maximum speed on the ground mover itself.

subCommands.name: vehicle
subCommands.description: Defines the attributes of a specific vehicle type within the context of this network. To define multiple vehicle types, create multiple vehicle blocks. The <platform-type> must be a previously defined platform_type.

subCommands.name: fraction
subCommands.description: If multiple vehicle blocks are defined, the fraction is the percentage (as a decimal value) of this specific vehicle type that would populate the road network. The sum of all the vehicle fractions must add up to 1.

subCommands.name: mean_speed
subCommands.description: The average speed of all the vehicles defined by this vehicle block. This value will only be used when no speed limits (maximum_speed or minimum_speed) are defined on a particular route or if the ignore_speed_limits flag is set.

subCommands.name: sigma_speed
subCommands.description: The speed magnitude of one standard deviation. This command follows same conditions as mean_speed.

subCommands.name: ignore_speed_limits
subCommands.description: Indicates that vehicles of the specified type do not need to follow the speed limits defined by maximum_speed or minimum_speed

subCommands.name: route_aux_data_mapping
subCommands.description: This block applies to all routes in the route_network, and maps osm_traffic route aux_data variable names to the rules of the road. The parameter for each command is simply a string representation of the variables’ name as defined in the route aux_data input blocks.

subCommands.name: minimum_speed
subCommands.description: Maps an aux_data numeric variable to the route’s minimum speed.

subCommands.name: lanes
subCommands.description: Maps an aux_data integer variable to the number of lanes in the route. This defines the number of lanes traveling in both directions, unless otherwise specified. By default, on a two-way road, there will be two lanes (one for each direction).

subCommands.name: one_way
subCommands.description: Maps an aux_data boolean variable to whether a road is one way or not. This will also affect how lanes are interpreted.

subCommands.name: density
subCommands.description: Maps an aux_data integer variable to a road’s average vehicle density.

subCommands.name: surface
subCommands.description: Maps an aux_data string variable to a road’s surface type.

subCommands.name: waypoint_aux_data_mapping
subCommands.description: This block applies to all waypoints in the route_network, and maps the osm_traffic waypoint aux_data variables names to the rules of the road.

subCommands.name: stop
subCommands.description: Maps an aux_data boolean variable to whether a waypoint is a stop sign.

subCommands.name: traffic_signals
subCommands.description: Maps an aux_data boolean variable to whether a waypoint has a traffic light.

subCommands.name: highway
subCommands.description: Maps an aux_data boolean variable to highway description / type.

aero_data.description: The RB6 geometric data offers two modes: wing-based or reference area. When using wing-based mode, the wing_chord_ft, wing_span_ft, and wing_area_sqft should be specified. When using reference area mode, the ref_area_sqft should be specified. PM6 vehicles do not incorporate chord or span information, and so require only ref_area_sqft.

subCommands.name: wing_chord_ft
subCommands.description: The mean chord of the wing measured in feet. This should be used along with wing_span_ft and wing_area_sqft.

subCommands.name: wing_span_ft
subCommands.description: The wing span of the wing measured in feet. This should be used along with wing_chord_ft and wing_area_sqft.

subCommands.name: wing_area_sqft
subCommands.description: The area of the wing measured in square feet. This should be used along with wing_chord_ft and wing_span_ft.

subCommands.name: ref_area_sqft
subCommands.description: The aerodynamic reference area of the vehicle measured in square feet. If this is used, wing_chord_ft, wing_span_ft and wing_area_sqft should not be used.

subCommands.name: use_reduced_frequency
subCommands.description: This should be true when using the “reduced frequency” stability derivatives. If false, the rate derivatives (e.g. cLq_alpha_mach_table, cnr_mach_table) will be multiplied by their corresponding angular rates. If true, the rate derivatives will instead be multiplied by a non-dimensional reduced frequency. For pitching moment and lift coefficient derivatives, the reduced frequency is calculated as the angular rate times the wing_chord_ft divided by twice the speed. All other coefficient derivatives use wing_span_ft instead of chord. See P6DOF Theory for more information.

subCommands.name: aero_center_x
subCommands.description: The aerodynamic center (x-axis) of the vehicle relative to the reference point in object coordinates. This “aero-center” is the “aerodynamic reference point” at which aerodynamic forces and moments will be calculated. The typical definition of aerodynamic center (as it relates to longitudinal stability) is the location at which the moment does not change regardless of the angle of attack. Thus, the pitching moment remains constant at that particular point. Hence, the aerodynamic center, rather than the center of pressure, is used in the analysis of longitudinal stability.

subCommands.name: aero_center_y
subCommands.description: The aerodynamic center (y-axis) of the vehicle relative to the reference point in object coordinates.

subCommands.name: aero_center_z
subCommands.description: The aerodynamic center (z-axis) of the vehicle relative to the reference point in object coordinates.

subCommands.name: cL_alpha_beta_mach_table
subCommands.description: This is a 3-dimensional regular_table that outputs the lift coefficient (cL) based on Mach, angle of attack (alpha), and angle of sideslip (beta), with a table order of Mach-alpha-beta-value.

subCommands.name: cLq_alpha_mach_table
subCommands.description: This is a 3-dimensional regular_table that outputs the lift coefficient (cL) based on Mach, angle of attack (alpha), and pitch rate (q), with a table order of Mach-alpha-q-value.

subCommands.name: cL_alphadot_alpha_mach_table
subCommands.description: This is a 3-dimensional regular_table that outputs the lift coefficient (cL) based on Mach, angle of attack (alpha), and alpha-dot (the rate of change of alpha), with a table order of Mach-alpha-alphaDot-value.

subCommands.name: flaps_dcL_mach_table
subCommands.description: This is a 1-dimensional table that outputs the lift coefficient (cL) increment from full flaps deployment based on Mach, with a table order of Mach-value.

subCommands.name: spoilers_dcL_mach_table
subCommands.description: This is a 1-dimensional table that outputs the lift coefficient (cL) increment from full spoilers deployment based on Mach, with a table order of Mach-value.

subCommands.name: cd_alpha_beta_mach_table
subCommands.description: This is a 3-dimensional regular_table that outputs the drag coefficient (cd) based on the Mach, angle of attack (alpha), and angle of sideslip (beta), with a table order of Mach-alpha-beta-value.

subCommands.name: flaps_dcd_mach_table
subCommands.description: This is a 1-dimensional table that outputs the cd increment from full flaps deployment based on Mach, with a table order of Mach-value.

subCommands.name: spoilers_dcd_mach_table
subCommands.description: This is a 1-dimensional table that outputs the cd increment from full spoilers deployment based on Mach, with a table order of Mach-value.

subCommands.name: speedbrake_dcd_mach_table
subCommands.description: This is a 1-dimensional table that outputs the cd increment from full speedbrake deployment based on Mach, with a table order of Mach-value.

subCommands.name: cy_alpha_beta_mach_table
subCommands.description: This is a 3-dimensional regular_table that outputs the side force coefficient (cy) based on the Mach, angle of attack (alpha), and angle of sideslip (beta), with a table order of Mach-alpha-beta-value.

subCommands.name: cyr_beta_mach_table
subCommands.description: This is a 3-dimensional regular_table that outputs the cy based on the Mach, beta, and yaw rate (q), with a table order of Mach-beta-q-value.

subCommands.name: cy_betadot_beta_mach_table
subCommands.description: This is a 3-dimensional regular_table that outputs the cy based on the Mach, beta, and rate of change of sideslip (beta-dot), with a table order of Mach-beta-betaDot-value.

subCommands.name: cm_alpha_beta_mach_table
subCommands.description: This is a 3-dimensional regular_table that outputs the pitch coefficient (cm) based on the Mach, angle of attack (alpha), and angle of sideslip (beta), with a table order of Mach-alpha-beta-value.

subCommands.name: cmq_mach_table
subCommands.description: This is a simple table that outputs the pitch damping coefficient due to pitch rate (cmq) based on Mach.

subCommands.name: cmp_mach_table
subCommands.description: This is a simple table that outputs the pitch damping coefficient due to roll rate (cmp) based on Mach.

subCommands.name: cm_alphadot_mach_table
subCommands.description: This is a 2-dimensional regular_table that outputs the pitch (damping) coefficient (cm) based on the Mach and the rate of change of alpha (alpha-dot), with a table order of Mach-alphaDot-value.

subCommands.name: maximum_pitch_acceleration_mach_table
subCommands.description: in deg/s/s, based on Mach, with a table order of Mach-value. The output of this table is reduced with ambient air density, and is modified as a function of angle-of-attack.

subCommands.name: alpha_stabilizing_frequency_mach_table
subCommands.description: based on Mach, with a table order of Mach-value. The output of this table is reduced with ambient air density, and is modified as a function of angle-of-attack.

subCommands.name: cn_alpha_beta_mach_table
subCommands.description: This is a 3-dimensional regular_table that outputs the yaw coefficient (cn) based on the Mach, angle of attack (alpha), and angle of sideslip (beta), with a table order of Mach-alpha-beta-value.

subCommands.name: cn_betadot_mach_table
subCommands.description: This is a 2-dimensional regular_table that outputs the yaw coefficient (cn) based on the Mach and rate of change of sideslip angle (beta-dot), with a table order of Mach-betaDot-value.

subCommands.name: cnr_mach_table
subCommands.description: This is a simple table that outputs the yaw damping coefficient due to yaw rate (cnr) based on Mach.

subCommands.name: cnp_mach_table
subCommands.description: This is a simple table that outputs the yaw damping coefficient due to roll rate (cnp) based on Mach.

subCommands.name: maximum_yaw_acceleration_mach_table
subCommands.description: in deg/s/s, based on Mach, with a table order of Mach-value. The output of this table is reduced with ambient air density, and is modified as a function of sideslip.

subCommands.name: beta_stabilizing_frequency_mach_table
subCommands.description: based on Mach, with a table order of Mach-value. The output of this table is reduced with ambient air density, and is modified as a function of sideslip.

subCommands.name: cl_alpha_beta_mach_table
subCommands.description: This is a 3-dimensional regular_table that outputs the roll coefficient (cl) based on the Mach, angle of attack (alpha), and angle of sideslip (beta), with a table order of Mach-alpha-beta-value.

subCommands.name: clp_mach_table
subCommands.description: This is a simple table that outputs the roll damping coefficient due to roll rate (clp) based on Mach.

subCommands.name: cl_alphadot_mach_table
subCommands.description: This is a 2-dimensional regular_table that outputs the roll coefficient (cl) based on the Mach and the rate of change of angle of attack (alpha), with a table order of Mach-alphaDot-value.

subCommands.name: cl_betadot_mach_table
subCommands.description: This is a 2-dimensional regular_table that outputs the roll coefficient (cl) based on the Mach and the rate of change of angle of sideslip (beta), with a table order of Mach-betaDot-value.

subCommands.name: clr_mach_table
subCommands.description: This is a simple table that outputs the roll damping coefficient due to yaw rate (clr) based on Mach.

subCommands.name: clq_mach_table
subCommands.description: This is a simple table that outputs the roll damping coefficient due to pitch rate (clq) based on Mach.

subCommands.name: maximum_roll_acceleration_mach_table
subCommands.description: in deg/s/s, based on Mach, with a table order of Mach-value. The output of this table is reduced with ambient air density, and is modified as a function of total angle-of-attack.

subCommands.name: roll_stabilizing_frequency_mach_table
subCommands.description: based on Mach, with a table order of Mach-value. The output of this table is reduced with ambient air density, and is modified as a function of angle-of-attack.

subCommands.name: aero_mode
subCommands.description: Aero modes may be defined to allow a vehicle to have discrete aerodynamic modes, such as a retarded-fall bomb that has two aero modes – clean and high-drag. Aero modes support all commands that aero data support with the exception of an aero_mode (aero_modes can not be nested within each other). Each aero mode name must be unique for that object. Aero modes are typically changed using sequencers and the action_change_aero_mode.

subCommands.name: aero_component
subCommands.description: The use of aero components can be simple, such as having three “generic” yaw, pitch and roll aero components, or can be more complex and realistic, such as having sixteen specific components: LeftAileron, RightAileron, LeftStabilator, RightStabilator, LeftRudder, RightRudder, LeftSpeedbrake, RightSpeedbrake, LeftFlap, RightFlap, LeftSpoiler, RightSpoiler, NoseLandingGear, LeftLandingGear, RightLandingGear, and ArrestingHook. During runtime, the position of aero components is controlled by the SixDOF Flight Control System Definition.

subCommands.name: type
subCommands.description: This sets the name/type of the aero component. The name must be unique within the set of aero components for the given rigid_body_vehicle_type.

subCommands.name: cL_angle_alpha_mach_table
subCommands.description: This is a 3-dimensional regular_table that outputs the lift coefficient (cL) based on the Mach, angle of attack (alpha), and control surface angle, with a table order of Mach-alpha-angle-value. Sample 3-dimensional table:

subCommands.name: cd_angle_alpha_mach_table
subCommands.description: This is a 3-dimensional regular_table that outputs the drag coefficient (cd) based on the Mach, angle of attack (alpha), and angle of the control surface, with a table order of Mach-alpha-angle-value. This derivative should be used when drag is only a function of alpha (not beta). When this derivative is used, cd_angle_beta_mach_table and cd_angle_mach_table should not be used.

subCommands.name: cd_angle_beta_mach_table
subCommands.description: This is a 3-dimensional regular_table that outputs the drag coefficient (cd) based on the Mach, angle of sideslip (beta), and angle of the control surface, with a table order of Mach-beta-angle-value. This derivative should be used when drag is only a function of beta (not alpha). When this derivative is used, cd_angle_alpha_mach_table and cd_angle_mach_table should not be used.

subCommands.name: cd_angle_mach_table
subCommands.description: This is a 2-dimensional regular_table that outputs the drag coefficient (cd) based on the Mach and the angle of the control surface, with a table order of Mach-angle-value. This derivative should be used when drag is a function of both alpha and beta. (Although this function does not include either alpha or beta, it is more appropriate than either the pro-alpha or pro-beta derivatives.) When this derivative is used, cd_angle_alpha_mach_table and cd_angle_beta_mach_table should not be used.

subCommands.name: cy_angle_beta_mach_table
subCommands.description: This is a 3-dimensional regular_table that outputs the side force coefficient (cy) based on the Mach, angle of sideslip (beta), and angle of the control surface, with a table order of Mach-beta-angle-value..

subCommands.name: cm_angle_alpha_mach_table
subCommands.description: This is a 3-dimensional regular_table that outputs the pitch coefficient (cm) based on the Mach, angle of attack (alpha), and angle of the control surface, with a table order of Mach-alpha-angle-value.

subCommands.name: cmq_angle_mach_table
subCommands.description: This is a 2-dimensional regular_table that outputs the pitch damping coefficient due to pitch rate (cmq) based on Mach and the angle of the control surface.

subCommands.name: cn_angle_beta_mach_table
subCommands.description: This is a 3-dimensional regular_table that outputs the yaw coefficient (cn) based on the Mach, angle of sideslip (beta), and angle of the control surface, with a table order of Mach-beta-angle-value.

subCommands.name: cnr_angle_mach_table
subCommands.description: This is a 2-dimensional regular_table that outputs the yaw damping coefficient due to yaw rate (cnr) based on Mach and the angle of the control surface.

subCommands.name: cl_angle_alpha_beta_table
subCommands.description: This is a 3-dimensional regular_table that outputs the roll coefficient (cl) based on the angle of the attack (alpha), the angle of slideslip (beta) and the angle of the control surface, with a table order of alpha-beta-angle-value.

subCommands.name: clp_angle_mach_table
subCommands.description: This is a 2-dimensional regular_table that outputs the roll damping coefficient due to roll rate (clp) based on Mach and the angle of the control surface.

subCommands.name: clq_angle_mach_table
subCommands.description: This is a 2-dimensional regular_table that outputs the roll damping coefficient due to pitch rate (clq) based on Mach and the angle of the control surface.

subCommands.name: clr_angle_mach_table
subCommands.description: This is a 2-dimensional regular_table that outputs the roll damping coefficient due to yaw rate (clr) based on Mach and the angle of the control surface.

contrail_min_altitude.description: This is the lowest altitude at which contrailing will occur.

subCommands.name: contrail_max_altitude
subCommands.description: This is the highest altitude at which contrailing will occur.

subCommands.name: control_name
subCommands.description: The primary purpose of the controls provider is to provide the multiple control_input feeds needed by the flight_controls. Each control input represents the positioning and movement of various controls in the cockpit or control signals within autopilots and guidance systems. Control inputs are defined by the control_name command. The name must be unique within a given p6dof_object_type. The flight_controls will “connect” to control inputs via these control names. Typically, multiple control_name commands will be defined for each pilot_manager.

subCommands.name: std_stick_back
