subCommands.description: This provides a mapping from the standard stick back command to the control input name.

subCommands.name: std_stick_right
subCommands.description: This provides a mapping from the standard stick right command to the control input name.

subCommands.name: std_rudder_right
subCommands.description: This provides a mapping from the standard rudder right to the control input name.

subCommands.name: std_throttle_mil
subCommands.description: This provides a mapping from the standard throttle mil command to the control input name.

subCommands.name: std_throttle_ab
subCommands.description: This provides a mapping from the standard throttle ab command to the control input name.

subCommands.name: std_thrust_reverser
subCommands.description: This provides a mapping from the standard thrust reverser back command to the control input name.

subCommands.name: std_thrust_vectoring_yaw
subCommands.description: This provides a mapping from the standard thrust vectoring yaw command to the control input name.

subCommands.name: std_thrust_vectoring_pitch
subCommands.description: This provides a mapping from the standard thrust vectoring pitch command to the control input name.

subCommands.name: std_thrust_vectoring_roll
subCommands.description: This provides a mapping from the standard thrust vectoring roll command to the control input name.

subCommands.name: std_speed_brakes_out
subCommands.description: This provides a mapping from the standard speed brakes command to the control input name.

subCommands.name: std_spoilers_out
subCommands.description: This provides a mapping from the standard spoilers command to the control input name.

subCommands.name: std_flaps_down
subCommands.description: This provides a mapping from the standard flaps command to the control input name.

subCommands.name: std_landing_gear_down
subCommands.description: This provides a mapping from the standard landing gear command to the control input name.

subCommands.name: std_nose_wheel_steering
subCommands.description: This provides a mapping from the standard low-gain nose wheel steering back command to the control input name.

subCommands.name: std_nws_steering
subCommands.description: This provides a mapping from the standard high-gain nose wheel steering command to the control input name.

subCommands.name: std_nws_enabled
subCommands.description: This provides a mapping from the standard NWS enabled command to the control input name.

subCommands.name: std_wheel_brake_left
subCommands.description: This provides a mapping from the standard wheel brake left command to the control input name.

subCommands.name: std_wheel_brake_right
subCommands.description: This provides a mapping from the standard wheel brake right command to the control input name.

subCommands.name: autopilot_config
subCommands.description: The autopilot_config block is structured as follows:

subCommands.name: vertical_middle_loop_rate_factor
subCommands.description: This specifies how many times the vertical channel inner-loop activates before the vertical channel middle-loop activates.

subCommands.name: vertical_outer_loop_rate_factor
subCommands.description: This specifies how many times the vertical channel middle-loop activates before the vertical channel outer-loop activates.

subCommands.name: lateral_middle_loop_rate_factor
subCommands.description: This specifies how many times the lateral channel inner-loop activates before the lateral channel middle-loop activates.

subCommands.name: lateral_outer_loop_rate_factor
subCommands.description: This specifies how many times the lateral channel middle-loop activates before the lateral channel outer-loop activates.

subCommands.name: speed_middle_loop_rate_factor
subCommands.description: This specifies how many times the speed channel inner-loop activates before the speed channel middle-loop activates.

subCommands.name: speed_outer_loop_rate_factor
subCommands.description: This specifies how many times the speed channel middle-loop activates before the speed channel outer-loop activates.

subCommands.name: control_method
subCommands.description: This sets the control method. There are two main methods – bank-to-turn and yaw-to-turn. Bank-to-turn involves banking/rolling in order to perform a turn, like a normal aircraft. Yaw-to-turn involves simply yawing to perform a turn – no rolling/banking is used. The command string should be one of the following:

subCommands.name: use_legacy_beta
subCommands.description: This enables/disables the use of the legacy_beta flag. This should be set to false when the new/improved beta calculations are desired. For example, Mover Creator uses the new beta calculations, so data files created by Mover Creator always set the use_legacy_beta command to false.

subCommands.name: min_taxi_turn_radius
subCommands.description: The defines the minimum taxi turning radius that will be used by the autopilot when performing taxi ground operations.

subCommands.name: use_simple_yaw_damper
subCommands.description: If true, a very “simple” (but not realistic) yaw damper action will be used to zero any sideslip (beta), making the RB6 more like a 5DOF. This will negate any sideslip, and so should only be used for bank-to-turn objects such as fixed-wing aircraft.

subCommands.name: update_interval
subCommands.description: This specifies the update rate of the PID. This is optional and, when defined, takes priority over the loop rate factors defined above. This limits the update rate from below and does not trigger a mover update.

subCommands.name: kp
subCommands.description: This specifies the proportional gain of the PID. When not defined, the gain will be zero.

subCommands.name: ki
subCommands.description: This specifies the integral gain of the PID. When not defined, the gain will be zero.

subCommands.name: kd
subCommands.description: This specifies the derivative gain of the PID. When not defined, the gain will be zero.

subCommands.name: max_error_accum
subCommands.description: This limits the maximum integrated error accumulation to the specified value. If not defined, no limit will be used.

subCommands.name: low_pass_alpha
subCommands.description: This specifies the value for the low-pass filter alpha for the derivative gain.

subCommands.name: ignore_large_error_accum
subCommands.description: This specifies that the PID will not accumulate integrated error if the current error value is greater than the specified value.

subCommands.name: ignore_small_error_accum
subCommands.description: This specifies that the PID will not accumulate integrated error if the current error value is less than the specified value.

subCommands.name: kt_anti_windup_gain
subCommands.description: This specifies the Kt anti-windup gain of the PID. When not defined, the gain will be zero.

subCommands.name: control_value
subCommands.description: This specifies the “control value” for which the PID parameters are used. The value is specified in lbs/ft^2 of dynamic pressure. The PID will interpolate between the appropriate control_value pairs based on the current dynamic pressure.

subCommands.name: afterburner_threshold
subCommands.description: This specifies the value above which afterburner will be used instead of limiting to military power.

subCommands.name: speedbrake_threshold
subCommands.description: This specifies the value below which the speed brake will be used to help slow down.

subCommands.name: pitch_gload_min
subCommands.description: This specifies the minimum pitch g-load value.

subCommands.name: pitch_gload_max
subCommands.description: This specifies the maximum pitch g-load value.

subCommands.name: alpha_min
subCommands.description: This specifies the minimum angle of attack (alpha) in degrees.

subCommands.name: alpha_max
subCommands.description: This specifies the maximum angle of attack (alpha) in degrees.

subCommands.name: pitch_rate_min
subCommands.description: This specifies the minimum pitch rate in degrees/sec.

subCommands.name: pitch_rate_max
subCommands.description: This specifies the maximum pitch rate in degrees/sec.

subCommands.name: vert_speed_min
subCommands.description: This specifies the minimum vertical speed in ft/minute.

subCommands.name: vert_speed_max
subCommands.description: This specifies the maximum vertical speed in ft/minute.

subCommands.name: yaw_gload_max
subCommands.description: This specifies the maximum yaw g-load.

subCommands.name: beta_max
subCommands.description: This specifies the maximum sideslip angle (beta) in degrees.

subCommands.name: yaw_rate_max
subCommands.description: This specifies the maximum yaw rate in degrees/sec.

subCommands.name: roll_rate_max
subCommands.description: This specifies the maximum roll rate in degrees/sec.

subCommands.name: bank_angle_max
subCommands.description: This specifies the maximum bank angle in degrees.

subCommands.name: forward_accel_min
subCommands.description: This specifies the minimum forward acceleration in g’s.

subCommands.name: forward_accel_max
subCommands.description: This specifies the maximum forward acceleration in g’s.

subCommands.name: taxi_speed_max_fps
subCommands.description: This specifies the maximum taxi speed in feet/sec.

subCommands.name: taxi_yaw_rate_max
subCommands.description: This specifies the maximum taxi yaw rate in degrees/sec.

subCommands.name: turn_roll_in_multiplier
subCommands.description: This is a multiplier that can shorten (less than than 1) or extend (greater than 1) the time/distance used when turning when following a route (waypoints).

subCommands.name: route_allowable_angle_error
subCommands.description: This specifies the angular error that is tolerated when rolling-out on a turn when following a route (waypoints). A larger value will allow the vehicle to consider the turn to be complete and switch to route segment control rather than continuing to use turn control.

p6dof_atmosphere.description: Create a P6DOF atmosphere object using the specified file. Only a single p6dof_atmosphere object should be defined for a given scenario.

subCommands.name: p6dof_gravity
subCommands.description: Create a P6DOF gravity object using the specified file. Only a single p6dof_gravity object should be defined for a given scenario.

subCommands.name: p6dof_terrain
subCommands.description: Create a P6DOF terrain object using the specified file. Only a single p6dof_terrain object should be defined for a given scenario.

subCommands.name: p6dof_wind
subCommands.description: Create a P6DOF wind object using the specified file. Only a single p6dof_wind object should be defined for a given scenario.

flight_controls.description: The flight_controls block defines various control surfaces/values (control_surface, control_value, and control_boolean) that control the vehicle and/or effect its performance. The flight_controls block also defines various input/signal modifiers which are referenced within the control surfaces/values (control_surface, control_value, and control_boolean) blocks. It is important to define Control Signal Modifiers before they are referenced in the Control Surfaces and Components blocks.

subCommands.name: mapping_table
subCommands.description: Mapping tables are used to modify a control input signal by modulating with a control value source. The control value can be a range of sources such as mach, alpha, g-load, etc. A table defines the relationship between the control value

subCommands.name: type
subCommands.description: This sets the type of the mapping table. Valid types include:

subCommands.name: table_data
subCommands.description: This table maps a signal/input to an output/value). A typical table is like this:

subCommands.name: gain_table
subCommands.description: This table maps a signal/input to an output/value). A typical table is like this:

subCommands.name: scalar_gain
subCommands.description: The scalar gain consists of a name and a gain value. Once defined, a scalar gain can be used repeatedly within the control_surface, control_value, and control_boolean blocks to scale a control signal.

subCommands.name: gain
subCommands.description: This sets the gain of the scalar gain.

subCommands.name: clamp_gain
subCommands.description: Clamp gains are used to limit a signal between min/max values. The output of signal will be “clamped” to the minimum and maximum values.

subCommands.name: min_clamp
subCommands.description: This sets the minimum value that will be allowed to pass the clamp gain.

subCommands.name: max_clamp
subCommands.description: This sets the maximum value that will be allowed to pass the clamp gain.

subCommands.name: control_surface
subCommands.description: This defines a “control surface” or other component that can produce aerodynamic effects on the platform. Control surfaces include ailerons, elevators, elevons, rudders, spoilers, speedbrakes, etc. but also include things like landing gear, which can produce drag. See Sample Control Surface for an example of a control_surface block.

subCommands.name: min_angle
subCommands.description: This sets the minimum angle of this control surface.

subCommands.name: max_angle
subCommands.description: This sets the maximum angle of this control surface.

subCommands.name: current_angle
subCommands.description: This sets the current angle of this control surface.

subCommands.name: inputs
subCommands.description: Inputs provide a means to modify a “control input/signal” from the active pilot object. If multiple inputs blocks are used, the output from each block is summed with the other inputs for a given control_surface. This can provide a means to “mix” control inputs/signals to drive a particular control surface. For example, an elevon may mix signals from stick_right and stick_back inputs to allow the elevon to be used for both pitch and roll forces/moments.

subCommands.name: control_input
subCommands.description: they are performed in succession with the result from the previous modifier serving as the input of the next, forming a “chain” of modifiers.

subCommands.name: modifier
subCommands.description: they are performed in succession with the result from the previous modifier serving as the input of the next, forming a “chain” of modifiers.

subCommands.name: angle_mapping_table
subCommands.description: This table provides a means to “shape” the mapping of input to control surface angle. In many situations, a non-linear mapping will be used, with a reduced slope near zero and increased slope near the endpoints. This often improves the “feel” of controls and provides more control sensitivity near the zero point. Data in the table is normalized input mapping to a control surface angle in degrees.

subCommands.name: actuator
subCommands.description: This allows an simple model of an actuator.

subCommands.name: max_positive_rate
subCommands.description: This is the maximum rate that the actuator can move in the positive direction.

subCommands.name: max_negative_rate
subCommands.description: This is the maximum rate that the actuator can move in the negative direction.

subCommands.name: control_value
subCommands.description: This defines a “control value” that can be used to drive controls such as throttles and thrust reversers or control other objects on the platform. A control value provides a range of values, constrained by the specified limits.

subCommands.name: min_value
subCommands.description: This is the minimum value of the control value.

subCommands.name: max_value
subCommands.description: This is the maximum value of the control value.

subCommands.name: control_boolean
subCommands.description: This defines a “control boolean” that can be used to drive “button”, “trigger”, and “switch” types of controls on the platform. A control boolean’s output is either true (on) or false (off).

subCommands.name: current_value
subCommands.description: This should be ‘0’ if the control boolean is false (off) or ‘1’ if the control boolean is true (on).

subCommands.name: threshold_value
subCommands.description: This sets the value above which a signal will be considered to be true (on).

p6dof_integrators.description: This will load one or more P6DOF integrators by reading/loading the specified file.

subCommands.name: nws_enable_control_name
subCommands.description: This specifies the nose wheel steering (NWS) enable control input.

subCommands.name: nominal_height_above_ground_on_gear
subCommands.description: This specifies the height above the ground for the reference point of the aircraft when resting on the landing gear.

subCommands.name: control_surface_name
subCommands.description: This specifies the name of the retraction control surface.

subCommands.name: steering_control_surface_name
subCommands.description: This specifies the name of the steering control surface (when NWS is not engaged/active).

subCommands.name: nws_angle_control_surface_name
subCommands.description: This specifies the name of the steering control surface (when NWS is engaged/active).

subCommands.name: is_nose_gear
subCommands.description: This indicates whether or not this ground_reaction_point is a nose gear.

subCommands.name: braking_control_surface_name
subCommands.description: This specifies the name of the braking control surface. If unspecified, no braking is provided for this ground_reaction_point.

subCommands.name: gear_extended_relative_position_x
subCommands.description: This is the x-location (in object coordinates) of the bottom of the landing gear (or contact point) when extended.

subCommands.name: gear_extended_relative_position_y
subCommands.description: This is the y-location (in object coordinates) of the bottom of the landing gear (or contact point) when extended.

subCommands.name: gear_extended_relative_position_z
subCommands.description: This is the z-location (in object coordinates) of the bottom of the landing gear (or contact point) when extended.

subCommands.name: gear_compression_vector_x
subCommands.description: This is the x-direction (in object coordinates) of the compression vector.

subCommands.name: gear_compression_vector_y
subCommands.description: This is the y-direction (in object coordinates) of the compression vector.

subCommands.name: gear_compression_vector_z
subCommands.description: This is the z-direction (in object coordinates) of the compression vector.

subCommands.name: gear_rolling_vector_x
subCommands.description: This is the x-direction (in object coordinates) of the rolling vector.

subCommands.name: gear_rolling_vector_y
subCommands.description: This is the y-direction (in object coordinates) of the rolling vector.

subCommands.name: gear_rolling_vector_z
subCommands.description: This is the z-direction (in object coordinates) of the rolling vector.

subCommands.name: spring_constant_lbs_per_ft
subCommands.description: This is the spring constant in lbs/ft.

subCommands.name: damper_constant_lbs_per_fps
subCommands.description: This is the damper constant in lbs/(ft/sec).

subCommands.name: uncompressed_length
subCommands.description: This is the uncompressed length of the landing gear.

subCommands.name: max_compression
subCommands.description: This is the maximum length of compression.

subCommands.name: rolling_coefficient_of_friction
subCommands.description: This is the rolling coefficient of friction.

subCommands.name: braking_coefficient_of_friction
subCommands.description: This is the braking coefficient of friction.

subCommands.name: scuffing_coefficient_of_friction
subCommands.description: This is the scuffing coefficient of friction.

subCommands.name: ignore_friction
subCommands.description: This indicates if friction should be ignored.

subCommands.name: is_landing_gear
subCommands.description: This indicates if the ground_reaction_point is a landing gear (true) or a contact point (false).

subCommands.name: is_contact_point
subCommands.description: This indicates if the ground_reaction_point is a contact point (true) or a landing gear (false).

subCommands.name: mass
subCommands.description: The (empty) mass of the object, not including fuel.

subCommands.name: moment_of_inertia_ixx
subCommands.description: The (empty) moment of inertia about the x-axis the object, not including fuel.

subCommands.name: moment_of_inertia_iyy
subCommands.description: The (empty) moment of inertia about the y-axis the object, not including fuel.

subCommands.name: moment_of_inertia_izz
subCommands.description: The (empty) moment of inertia about the z-axis the object, not including fuel.

subCommands.name: center_of_mass_x
subCommands.description: The empty center of mass (in the object’s x-direction) relative to the reference point.

subCommands.name: center_of_mass_y
subCommands.description: The empty center of mass (in the object’s y-direction) relative to the reference point.

subCommands.name: center_of_mass_z
subCommands.description: The empty center of mass (in the object’s z-direction) relative to the reference point.

p6dof_object_type.description: The definition of a p6dof_object_type is performed within a p6dof_object_type block. Each p6dof_object_type defines a ‘type’ of vehicle, ranging from a simple, hand-launched drone to a complex spacecraft. A p6dof_object_type may include the definition of mass properties, primary aerodynamics, propulsion system components (including engines and fuel systems), subobjects (such as weapons, fuel tanks, etc.), sequencers (which can produce an “action” based on an “event”), controls providers (which include manual pilots, synthetic pilots, autopilots, and guidance systems), flight control systems (which determine how control inputs are routed/mixed to move control surfaces), secondary aerodynamics (which includes control surface aerodynamics), size factor parameters (which allow an object’s size to vary, such as that of a parachute or balloon), relative positioning (which defines how a subobject is positioned relative to its parent while captive), separation effects (which impart a delta-V or angular rate to a subobject when it is jettisoned from its parent), and other special properties.

subCommands.name: mass
subCommands.description: The (empty) mass of the object, not including fuel.

subCommands.name: moment_of_inertia_ixx
subCommands.description: The (empty) moment of inertia about the x-axis the object, not including fuel.

subCommands.name: moment_of_inertia_iyy
subCommands.description: The (empty) moment of inertia about the y-axis the object, not including fuel.

subCommands.name: moment_of_inertia_izz
subCommands.description: The (empty) moment of inertia about the z-axis the object, not including fuel.

subCommands.name: center_of_mass_x1
subCommands.description: The empty center of mass (in the object’s x-direction) relative to the reference point.

subCommands.name: center_of_mass_y1
subCommands.description: The empty center of mass (in the object’s y-direction) relative to the reference point.

subCommands.name: center_of_mass_z1
subCommands.description: The empty center of mass (in the object’s z-direction) relative to the reference point.

subCommands.name: p6dof_integrator
subCommands.description: This sets the object’s integrator type to the specified name. If no integrator with the specified name exists, an exception will be thrown, since P6DOF objects cannot function without an integrator.

subCommands.name: fuel_transfer
subCommands.description: Regardless of whether a fuel transfer is defined within the propulsion_data block or the p6dof_object_type block, a fuel transfer always consists of a source tank and a target tank. During runtime, the source tank will attempt to transfer fuel to the target tank, limited by the transfer rates of the two tanks.

subCommands.name: source_tank
subCommands.description: The source tank is defined by its string name.

subCommands.name: target_tank
subCommands.description: The target tank is defined by its string name.

subCommands.name: remove_fuel_transfer
subCommands.description: This removes the fuel transfer with the specified name. If a no transfer exists with the name, the command is ignored.

subCommands.name: remove_fuel_tank
subCommands.description: This removes the fuel tank with the specified name. If a no tank exists with the name, the command is ignored.

subCommands.name: modify_fuel_quantity
subCommands.description: This modifies the quantity of fuel in the fuel tank with the specified name. If a no tank exists with the name, the command is ignored.

subCommands.name: parent_rel_x
subCommands.description: This specifies the x-location of the object’s reference point relative to the parent’s reference point using the parent’s body coordinate system.

subCommands.name: parent_rel_y
subCommands.description: This specifies the y-location of the object’s reference point relative to the parent’s reference point using the parent’s body coordinate system.

subCommands.name: parent_rel_z
subCommands.description: This specifies the z-location of the object’s reference point relative to the parent’s reference point using the parent’s body coordinate system.

subCommands.name: parent_rel_yaw
subCommands.description: This specifies the yaw of the object about its reference point relative to the parent’s body coordinate system.

subCommands.name: parent_rel_pitch
subCommands.description: This specifies the pitch of the object about its reference point relative to the parent’s body coordinate system.

subCommands.name: parent_rel_roll
subCommands.description: This specifies the roll of the object about its reference point relative to the parent’s body coordinate system.

subCommands.name: separation_vx
subCommands.description: This specifies the x-component of velocity (in parent body coordinates) that is imparted to the subobject when it separates from the parent.

subCommands.name: separation_vy
subCommands.description: This specifies the y-component of velocity (in parent body coordinates) that is imparted to the subobject when it separates from the parent.

subCommands.name: separation_vz
subCommands.description: This specifies the z-component of velocity (in parent body coordinates) that is imparted to the subobject when it separates from the parent.

subCommands.name: separation_omega_x
subCommands.description: This specifies the x-component of angular velocity (in subobject body coordinates) that is imparted to the subobject when it separates from the parent.

subCommands.name: separation_omega_y
subCommands.description: This specifies the y-component of angular velocity (in subobject body coordinates) that is imparted to the subobject when it separates from the parent.

subCommands.name: separation_omega_z
subCommands.description: This specifies the z-component of angular velocity (in subobject body coordinates) that is imparted to the subobject when it separates from the parent.

subCommands.name: size_factor_radius
subCommands.description: This is the “reference” radius that is the starting radius of the object. This radius is also used to calculate a reference area and a reference volume.

subCommands.name: size_factor_min
subCommands.description: This is the minimum factor (multiplier) that the reference radius is allowed to achieve.

subCommands.name: size_factor_max
subCommands.description: This is the maximum factor (multiplier) that the reference radius is allowed to achieve.

subCommands.name: size_factor_volume_rate_m3_per_sec
subCommands.description: This provides a volume-based rate of change of cubic meters per second. When volume-based mode is used, the area and radius modes should not be used.

subCommands.name: size_factor_area_rate_m2_per_sec
subCommands.description: This provides an area-based rate of change of square meters per second. When area-based mode is used, the volume and radius modes should not be used.

subCommands.name: size_factor_radius_rate_m_per_sec
subCommands.description: This provides an radius-based rate of change of meters per second. When radius-based mode is used, the volume and area modes should not be used.

subCommands.name: use_spherical_earth
subCommands.description: If ‘true’, the P6DOF object will use a spherical earth model rather than a WGS84 (oblate) earth model. This is often a useful simplification when using ballistic missiles and space launch vehicles, since it eliminates latitude issues for guidance associated with an oblate earth.

subCommands.name: use_rotating_earth
subCommands.description: If ‘true’, the P6DOF object will use a rotating earth model rather than a non-rotating earth model. This function is not yet support/implemented.

subCommands.name: ignore_jettisoned_objects
subCommands.description: If ‘true’, any subobjects that are jettisoned from the P6DOF object will be removed immediately and will never have an AFSIM platform. This is often used to speed up runtimes when spent stages from a ballistic missile or space launch vehicle are not needed.

subCommands.name: fixed_object
subCommands.description: If ‘true’, the P6DOF object will not perform kinematic calculations as part of its “update” but will instead remain motionless.

subCommands.name: nominal_max_mach
subCommands.description: This defines the maximum Mach expected by the object. This does not impose a limit on performance, rather it is a hint for functions that calculate performance and/or analysis.

subCommands.name: nominal_max_alpha
subCommands.description: This defines the maximum alpha (angle of attack) expected by the object. This does not impose a limit on performance, rather it is a hint for functions that calculate performance and/or analysis.

subCommands.name: nominal_min_alpha
subCommands.description: This defines the minimum alpha (angle of attack) expected by the object. This does not impose a limit on performance, rather it is a hint for functions that calculate performance and/or analysis.

subCommands.name: nominal_max_beta
subCommands.description: This defines the maximum beta (angle of sideslip) expected by the object. This does not impose a limit on performance, rather it is a hint for functions that calculate performance and/or analysis.

subCommands.name: object_graphical_type_num
subCommands.description: This defines an index number for the object’s graphical type. The index number is dependent on the networked analysis tool being used. This graphical object will be the default graphical object.

subCommands.name: object_graphical_alt_type1_num
subCommands.description: This defines an alternate object #1 for the object’s graphical type. The tool may use an alternate graphical object as desired and/or commanded.

subCommands.name: object_graphical_alt_type2_num
subCommands.description: This defines an alternate object #2 for the object’s graphical type. The tool may use an alternate graphical object as desired and/or commanded.

subCommands.name: object_graphical_alt_type3_num
subCommands.description: This defines an alternate object #3 for the object’s graphical type. The tool may use an alternate graphical object as desired and/or commanded.

map_p6dof_object_to_platform.description: Define a mapping between the specified p6dof_object_type and the specified platform type.

subCommands.name: rel_pos_x
subCommands.description: This is the x-location of the thrust point relative to the parent’s reference point using the parent’s body coordinate system.

subCommands.name: rel_pos_y
subCommands.description: This is the y-location of the thrust point relative to the parent’s reference point using the parent’s body coordinate system.

subCommands.name: rel_pos_z
subCommands.description: This is the z-location of the thrust point relative to the parent’s reference point using the parent’s body coordinate system.

subCommands.name: rel_yaw
subCommands.description: This specifies the yaw of the thrust point about its reference point relative to the parent’s body coordinate system.

subCommands.name: rel_pitch
subCommands.description: This specifies the pitch of the thrust point about its reference point relative to the parent’s body coordinate system.

subCommands.name: rel_roll
subCommands.description: This specifies the roll of the thrust point about its reference point relative to the parent’s body coordinate system.

subCommands.name: fuel_feed
subCommands.description: This specifies the name of the fuel_tank from which the engine will draw fuel. Note – This should not be defined for a solid-propellant rocket motor thrust producer, since its propellant is carried internally.

subCommands.name: fuel_tank
subCommands.description: The fuel tank block provides a means to define tank parameters including fuel quantity, transfer rates, and center of gravity (cg). Multiple tanks can be defined, if desired, or a single tank may be used for simplification. In addition, a propulsion system does not have to contain a fuel tank; engines may draw fuel from tanks located in subobjects, for example. Conversely, an external fuel tank object has a propulsion system that only contains a fuel tank – no engines are included.

subCommands.name: max_fuel_quantity
subCommands.description: This is the maximum quantity of fuel that can be contained in the tank.

subCommands.name: current_fuel_qty
subCommands.description: This is the current quantity of fuel that is in the tank.

subCommands.name: max_flow_rate
subCommands.description: operation, this flow rate should exceed the maximum demands than the engine(s) may demand.

subCommands.name: max_fill_rate
subCommands.description: an in-flight refueling source.

subCommands.name: max_xfer_rate
subCommands.description: to another tank.

subCommands.name: cg_full_x
subCommands.description: relative to the reference point of the carrying vehicle, in body coordinates.

subCommands.name: cg_full_y
subCommands.description: relative to the reference point of the carrying vehicle, in body coordinates.

subCommands.name: cg_full_z
subCommands.description: relative to the reference point of the carrying vehicle, in body coordinates.

subCommands.name: cg_empty_x
subCommands.description: relative to the reference point of the carrying vehicle, in body coordinates.

subCommands.name: cg_empty_y
subCommands.description: relative to the reference point of the carrying vehicle, in body coordinates.

subCommands.name: cg_empty_z
subCommands.description: relative to the reference point of the carrying vehicle, in body coordinates.

subCommands.name: fuel_transfer
subCommands.description: Regardless of whether a fuel transfer is defined within the propulsion_data block or a vehicle type block, a fuel transfer always consists of a source tank and a target tank. During runtime, the source tank will attempt to transfer fuel to the target tank, limited by the transfer rates of the two tanks.

subCommands.name: source_tank
subCommands.description: The source tank is defined by its string name. Source tanks can be access on sub-objects by referencing the sub-object by name, then the source tank name (as shown above).

subCommands.name: target_tank
subCommands.description: The target tank is defined by its string name. Target tanks can be access on sub-objects by referencing the sub-object by name, then the target tank name (as shown above).

subCommands.name: throttle_setting_mil
subCommands.description: This specifies the control_value defined in flight_controls that will be used to control the MIL (military) power throttle setting.

subCommands.name: throttle_setting_ab
subCommands.description: This specifies the control_value defined in flight_controls that will be used to control the AB (afterburner) power throttle setting.

subCommands.name: throttle_setting_reverser
subCommands.description: This specifies the control_value defined in flight_controls that will be used to control the thrust-reverser control setting.

subCommands.name: throttle_setting_yaw
subCommands.description: This specifies the control_value defined in flight_controls that will be used to control the yaw thrust vectoring control setting.

subCommands.name: throttle_setting_pitch
subCommands.description: This specifies the control_value defined in flight_controls that will be used to control the pitch thrust vectoring control setting.

sequencer.description: A sequencer block has an identifier, which is the string argument after ‘sequencer’. This identifier must be unique within the vehicle type. The sequencer block has to include at least one Sequencer Actions, which is the action the sequencer shall perform when it is activated. The sequencer block may include one or more Sequencer Events, if no Sequencer Events are provided the sequencer may only be activated through the WsfSixDOF_Mover.ActivateSequencer script function. The sequencer block may include one or more Nested Sequencers which will be used once the containing sequencer has been activated – this allows for sequential events, where the second event cannot occur until the first event has occurred.

subCommands.name: event_timer
subCommands.description: This event is based on reaching the specified time. The timer will begin counting once the sequencer is being tested. For top-level sequencers, this is equivalent to event_lifetime but if the sequencer is nested, its counter will not begin running until its parent sequencer has been activated.

subCommands.name: event_timer_int_msec
subCommands.description: This event is based on reaching the specified time, which is an integer number of milliseconds. The timer will begin counting once the sequencer is being tested. For top-level sequencers, this is equivalent to event_lifetime_int_msec but if the sequencer is nested, its counter will not begin running until its parent sequencer has been activated.

subCommands.name: event_timer_int_nanosec
subCommands.description: This event is based on reaching the specified time, which is an integer number of nanoseconds. The timer will begin counting once the sequencer is being tested. For top-level sequencers, this is equivalent to event_lifetime_int_nanosec but if the sequencer is nested, its counter will not begin running until its parent sequencer has been activated.

subCommands.name: event_lifetime
subCommands.description: This event is based on reaching the specified lifetime. The lifetime timer begins counting once the platform is active (alive). This timer is different from the event_timer since it uses a platform-centric timer as opposed to a sequencer-centric timer.

subCommands.name: event_lifetime_int_msec
subCommands.description: This event is based on reaching the specified lifetime, which is an integer number of milliseconds. The lifetime timer begins counting once the platform is active (alive). This timer is different from the event_timer_int_msec since it uses a platform-centric timer as opposed to a sequencer-centric timer.

subCommands.name: event_lifetime_int_nanosec
subCommands.description: This event is based on reaching the specified lifetime, which is an integer number of nanoseconds. The lifetime timer begins counting once the platform is active (alive). This timer is different from the event_timer_int_nanosec since it uses a platform-centric timer as opposed to a sequencer-centric timer.

subCommands.name: event_above_alt
subCommands.description: This event is based on the platform being above the specified altitude (MSL).

subCommands.name: event_below_alt
subCommands.description: This event is based on the platform being below the specified altitude (MSL).

subCommands.name: event_dynamic_pressure_above
subCommands.description: This event is based on the platform having a dynamic pressure above the specified value.

subCommands.name: event_dynamic_pressure_below
subCommands.description: This event is based on the platform having a dynamic pressure below the specified value.

subCommands.name: event_static_pressure_above
subCommands.description: This event is based on the platform having a static pressure above the specified value.

subCommands.name: event_static_pressure_below
subCommands.description: This event is based on the platform having a static pressure below the specified value.

subCommands.name: event_fuel_percent_below
subCommands.description: Specify the fuel value as a normalized number (50% is 0.50). This event is based on the fuel level in the “main tank” being below the specified value. The main tank is considered to be the first tank specified in the propulsion_data block.

subCommands.name: event_ground_distance
subCommands.description: This event is based on the platform being beyond the specified distance (great circle) from the point at which it started.

subCommands.name: event_nx_above
subCommands.description: This event is based on the x-acceleration, known as Nx, (in body coordinates) being above the specified value.

subCommands.name: event_nx_below
subCommands.description: This event is based on the y-acceleration, known as Nx, (in body coordinates) being below the specified value.

subCommands.name: event_ny_above
subCommands.description: This event is based on the y-acceleration, known as Ny, (in body coordinates) being above the specified value.

subCommands.name: event_ny_below
subCommands.description: This event is based on the y-acceleration, known as Ny, (in body coordinates) being below the specified value.

subCommands.name: event_nz_above
subCommands.description: This event is based on the z-acceleration, known as Nz, (in body coordinates) being above the specified value.

subCommands.name: event_nz_below
subCommands.description: This event is based on the z-acceleration, known as Nz, (in body coordinates) being below the specified value.

subCommands.name: event_released_from_parent
subCommands.description: This event is based on the platform being newly released from its parent.

subCommands.name: event_manual_input_trigger
subCommands.description: This event allows a trigger pulled input from the P6Net interface to activate.

subCommands.name: event_manual_input_button
subCommands.description: This event allows an input button down from the P6Net interface to activate.

subCommands.name: event_manual_input_button_released
subCommands.description: This event allows an input button release from the P6Net interface to activate.

subCommands.name: event_boolean_input
subCommands.description: This event is based on a control_boolean within flight_controls being true. This allows an event to be controlled by a ManualPilot or SyntheticPilot, for example.

subCommands.name: event_null
subCommands.description: This purpose of this event is for to prevent any action without an external command to active the sequencer (see action_activate_subobject_sequencer).

subCommands.name: all_events
subCommands.description: This flag indicates that the sequencer will be activated only if all events for the sequencer are true.

subCommands.name: action_null
subCommands.description: This action should be specified when no action is desired, such as for a parent sequencer that does not need any action to be performed at its level.

subCommands.name: action_jett_obj
subCommands.description: This action will jettison the specified subobject.

subCommands.name: action_jett_self
subCommands.description: This action will jettison the object from its parent.

subCommands.name: action_ignite_engine
subCommands.description: This action will “ignite” the specified engine and set thrust (if applicable) to 100%.

subCommands.name: action_ignite_subobject
subCommands.description: This action will “ignite” all engines on the specified subobject.

subCommands.name: action_ignite_self
subCommands.description: This action will “ignite” all engines on the object.

subCommands.name: action_terminate_thrust
subCommands.description: This action will terminate the thrust for all engines on the object (shutdown the engines).

subCommands.name: action_shutdown_engine
subCommands.description: This action will “shutdown” the specified engine and set thrust (if applicable) to 0%.

subCommands.name: action_shutdown_subobject
subCommands.description: This action will “shutdown” all engines on the specified subobject.

subCommands.name: action_change_aero_mode
subCommands.description: This action will change the object’s aero_mode to the specified mode.

subCommands.name: action_enable_size_factor
subCommands.description: This action will enable the size factor. See Size Factor Parameters for details.

subCommands.name: action_set_graphical_model
subCommands.description: This action will set the current graphical model for networked tools.

subCommands.name: action_activate_subobject_sequencer
subCommands.description: The first string is the name of the subobject and the second string is the name of the sequencer. This action will activate the sequencer with the specified name on the specified subobject. If no subobject or sequencer exists, no action will be performed.

subCommands.name: action_enable_controls
subCommands.description: This action will enable control input for normal operation. See action_disable_controls to turn off the controls.

subCommands.name: action_disable_controls
subCommands.description: This action will disable control input, zeroing all control inputs. See action_enable_controls to turn on the controls.

subCommands.name: remove_sequencer
subCommands.description: This removes the specified sequencer. It is typically used to remove a sequencer that was derived from a parent class object. If no sequencer with the specified name exists, the command is ignored.

subobject.description: Depending on the defining data, subobjects may effect the performance of their parent platform. For example, a bomb carried on an external pylon may produce additional drag on the parent. It is also possible for a subobject to contribute thrust forces to the parent (such as running Hound Dog missiles on a B-52 during takeoff, or having SRB thrust contribute to the total thrust of a Space Shuttle orbiter). In addition, subobjects will contribute mass properties and inertia to their parent.

subCommands.name: parent_rel_x
subCommands.description: This specifies the x-location of the object’s reference point relative to the parent’s reference point using the parent’s body coordinate system.

subCommands.name: parent_rel_y
subCommands.description: This specifies the y-location of the object’s reference point relative to the parent’s reference point using the parent’s body coordinate system.

subCommands.name: parent_rel_z
subCommands.description: This specifies the z-location of the object’s reference point relative to the parent’s reference point using the parent’s body coordinate system.

subCommands.name: parent_rel_yaw
subCommands.description: This specifies the yaw of the object about its reference point relative to the parent’s body coordinate system.

subCommands.name: parent_rel_pitch
subCommands.description: This specifies the pitch of the object about its reference point relative to the parent’s body coordinate system.

subCommands.name: parent_rel_roll
subCommands.description: This specifies the roll of the object about its reference point relative to the parent’s body coordinate system.

subCommands.name: separation_vx
subCommands.description: This specifies the x-component of velocity (in parent body coordinates) that is imparted to the subobject when it separates from the parent.

subCommands.name: separation_vy
subCommands.description: This specifies the y-component of velocity (in parent body coordinates) that is imparted to the subobject when it separates from the parent.

subCommands.name: separation_vz
subCommands.description: This specifies the z-component of velocity (in parent body coordinates) that is imparted to the subobject when it separates from the parent.

subCommands.name: separation_omega_x
subCommands.description: This specifies the x-component of angular velocity (in subobject body coordinates) that is imparted to the subobject when it separates from the parent.

subCommands.name: separation_omega_y
subCommands.description: This specifies the y-component of angular velocity (in subobject body coordinates) that is imparted to the subobject when it separates from the parent.

subCommands.name: separation_omega_z
subCommands.description: This specifies the z-component of angular velocity (in subobject body coordinates) that is imparted to the subobject when it separates from the parent.

jet_engine_type.description: Definitions for each type of jet engine are performed within the jet_engine_type block. Since the definition is for a ‘type’ of engine and not an ‘instance’ of an engine, no installation position/attitude data is included. Typically, the fuel_feed is specified at the instance-level rather than at the type-level.

subCommands.name: tsfc_idle_pph
subCommands.description: This specifies the thrust specific fuel consumption at idle in lbs-thrust/lbs-fuel/hr.

subCommands.name: tsfc_mil_pph
subCommands.description: This specifies the thrust specific fuel consumption at military power (full power without afterburner) in lbs-thrust/lbs-fuel/hr.

subCommands.name: tsfc_ab_pph
subCommands.description: This specifies the thrust specific fuel consumption using full afterburner in lbs-thrust/lbs-fuel/hr.

subCommands.name: rated_thrust_idle
subCommands.description: This specifies the thrust at idle. Since thrust varies with various conditions, this is a reference value.

subCommands.name: rated_thrust_mil
subCommands.description: This specifies the thrust at military power (full power without afterburner). Since thrust varies with various conditions, this is a reference value.

subCommands.name: rated_thrust_ab
subCommands.description: This specifies the thrust using full afterburner. Since thrust varies with various conditions, this is a reference value.

subCommands.name: thrust_table_idle
subCommands.description: This is a simple table of idle thrust versus altitude. Note that is does not consider Mach-effects. The thrust_idle_mach_alt_table or thrust_idle_alt_mach_table are preferable, but if no Mach data is available, this table can be used.

subCommands.name: thrust_idle_mach_alt_table
subCommands.description: This is an improved table over thrust_table_idle, since it includes Mach-effects. However, most users will prefer the format of the thrust_idle_alt_mach_table instead.

subCommands.name: thrust_idle_alt_mach_table
subCommands.description: This is typically the best thrust table format – it includes Mach-effects and organizes its data in a preferred manner. The thrust_idle_mach_alt_table is an alternative format.

subCommands.name: thrust_table_mil
subCommands.description: This is a simple table of military (MIL) thrust versus altitude. Note that is does not consider Mach-effects. The thrust_mil_mach_alt_table or thrust_mil_alt_mach_table are preferable, but if no Mach data is available, this table can be used.

subCommands.name: thrust_mil_mach_alt_table
subCommands.description: This is an improved table over thrust_table_mil, since it includes Mach-effects. However, most users will prefer the format of the thrust_mil_alt_mach_table instead.

subCommands.name: thrust_mil_alt_mach_table
subCommands.description: This is typically the best thrust table format – it includes Mach-effects and organizes its data in a preferred manner. The thrust_mil_mach_alt_table is an alternative format.

subCommands.name: thrust_table_ab
subCommands.description: This is a simple table of afterburner (AB) thrust versus altitude. Note that is does not consider Mach-effects. The thrust_ab_mach_alt_table or thrust_ab_alt_mach_table are preferable, but if no Mach data is available, this table can be used.

subCommands.name: thrust_ab_mach_alt_table
subCommands.description: This is an improved table over thrust_table_ab, since it includes Mach-effects. However, most users will prefer the format of the thrust_ab_alt_mach_table instead.

subCommands.name: thrust_ab_alt_mach_table
subCommands.description: This is typically the best thrust table format – it includes Mach-effects and organizes its data in a preferred manner. The thrust_ab_mach_alt_table is an alternative format.

subCommands.name: spin_up_mil_per_sec
subCommands.description: This defines how quickly the engine will “spool-up” as the power level is advanced. A value of 1.0 implies that the engine will spin-up from idle to MIL power in 1 second, while a value of 0.1 implies that it will take 10 seconds to spin-up from idle to MIL power.

subCommands.name: spin_up_table_mil_per_sec
subCommands.description: This defines how quickly the engine will “spool-up” as the power level is advanced. Rather than a single value, this command uses a table that is a function of the throttle level (normalized), allowing a more realistic spin-up as a function of current power condition. A value of 1.0 implies that the engine will spin-up from idle to MIL power in 1 second, while a value of 0.1 implies that it will take 10 seconds to spin-up from idle to MIL power.

subCommands.name: spin_up_ab_per_sec
subCommands.description: This defines how quickly the engine will “spool-up” as the power level is advanced. A value of 1.0 implies that the engine will spin-up from MIL to Full AB power in 1 second, while a value of 0.1 implies that it will take 10 seconds to spin-up from MIL to Full AB power.

subCommands.name: spin_up_table_ab_per_sec
subCommands.description: This defines how quickly the engine will “spool-up” as the power level is advanced. Rather than a single value, this command uses a table that is a function of the throttle level (normalized), allowing a more realistic spin-up as a function of current power condition. A value of 1.0 implies that the engine will spin-up from MIL to Full AB power in 1 second, while a value of 0.1 implies that it will take 10 seconds to spin-up from MIL to Full AB power.

subCommands.name: spin_down_mil_per_sec
subCommands.description: This defines how quickly the engine will “spool-down” as the power level is reduced. A value of 1.0 implies that the engine will spin-down from MIL power to idle in 1 second, while a value of 0.1 implies that it will take 10 seconds to spin-down from MIL power to idle.

subCommands.name: spin_down_table_mil_per_sec
subCommands.description: This defines how quickly the engine will “spool-down” as the power level is reduced. Rather than a single value, this command uses a table that is a function of the throttle level (normalized), allowing a more realistic spin-down as a function of current power condition. A value of 1.0 implies that the engine will spin-down from MIL power to idle in 1 second, while a value of 0.1 implies that it will take 10 seconds to spin-down from MIL power to idle.

subCommands.name: spin_down_ab_per_sec
subCommands.description: This defines how quickly the engine will “spool-down” as the power level is reduced. A value of 1.0 implies that the engine will spin-down from Full AB power to MIL power in 1 second, while a value of 0.1 implies that it will take 10 seconds to spin-down from Full AB power to MIL power.

subCommands.name: spin_down_table_ab_per_sec
subCommands.description: This defines how quickly the engine will “spool-down” as the power level is reduced. Rather than a single value, this command uses a table that is a function of the throttle level (normalized), allowing a more realistic spin-down as a function of current power condition. A value of 1.0 implies that the engine will spin-down from Full AB power to MIL power in 1 second, while a value of 0.1 implies that it will take 10 seconds to spin-down from Full AB power to MIL power.

subCommands.name: throttle_setting_mil
subCommands.description: This specifies the control_value defined in flight_controls that will be used to control the MIL (military) power throttle setting. This can be done at the engine-level or in the propulsion_data of the p6dof_object_type.

subCommands.name: throttle_setting_ab
subCommands.description: This specifies the control_value defined in flight_controls that will be used to control the AB (afterburner) power throttle setting. This can be done at the engine-level or in the propulsion_data of the p6dof_object_type.

subCommands.name: throttle_setting_reverser
subCommands.description: This specifies the control_value defined in flight_controls that will be used to control the thrust-reverser control setting. This can be done at the engine-level or in the propulsion_data of the p6dof_object_type.

subCommands.name: throttle_setting_yaw
subCommands.description: This specifies the control_value defined in flight_controls that will be used to control the yaw thrust vectoring control setting. This can be done at the engine-level or in the propulsion_data of the p6dof_object_type.

subCommands.name: throttle_setting_pitch
subCommands.description: This specifies the control_value defined in flight_controls that will be used to control the pitch thrust vectoring control setting. This can be done at the engine-level or in the propulsion_data of the p6dof_object_type.

subCommands.name: thrust_offset
subCommands.description: This is the location of the thrust relative to the engine’s reference point along the x-axis. A positive value is forward of the engine, negative is aft.

subCommands.name: inop_ref_area
subCommands.description: This specifies aerodynamic CD-area product for the engine when it is inoperative. It is the drag coefficient multiplied by the reference area.

subCommands.name: fuel_feed
subCommands.description: This specifies the name of the fuel_tank from which the engine will draw fuel. This is typically specified for a jet_engine_type instance rather than in the type definition.

subCommands.name: engine_smokes_above_power_setting
subCommands.description: This specifies the throttle level (MIL power) above which the engine will produce smoke. For example, a value of 0.8 will produce smoke when the throttle is above 80% power. If afterburner is selected, the smoke will cease. The default is a value of 1.0, which will not produce any smoke. This is useful for simulating engines that produce excessive smoke, such as old F-4 Phantoms and MiG-29s.

subCommands.name: ramjet_engine_type
subCommands.description: Definitions for each type of ramjet engine are performed within the ramjet_engine_type block. Since the definition is for a ‘type’ of engine and not an ‘instance’ of an engine, no installation position/attitude data is included. Typically, the fuel_feed is specified at the instance-level rather than at the type-level.

subCommands.name: tsfc_alt_mach_table
subCommands.description: This specifies the thrust specific fuel consumption as a function of altitude and Mach in lbs-thrust/lbs-fuel/hr. Altitude units are feet.

subCommands.name: thrust_alt_mach_table
subCommands.description: This specifies the thrust as a function of altitude and Mach in lbs. Altitude units are feet. Since the table will clamp rather than interpolate at the end values, it is important to ensure that data at the extreme points goes to zero values. Failure to do so could result in increasing thrust at high Mach, for example.

subCommands.name: afterburner_appearance_when_operating
subCommands.description: This specifies whether or not an afterburner appearance should be used when the ramjet is operating. This only effects the appearance, it has no physical/kinematic effect. When true, and the ramjet is operating, it will have the same appearance of a jet engine using afterburner.

subCommands.name: latch_fuel_injection
subCommands.description: When true, the fuel injection will be latched (locked) into the on condition. This will keep the engine operating, regardless of throttle command, as long as fuel is available. When false, normal throttle control is used. The default value is false.

subCommands.name: use_proportional_throttle
subCommands.description: When true, a proportional throttle control will be used. When false, normal on/off throttle control is used. The default value is false.

subCommands.name: minimum_proportional_thrust
subCommands.description: This is the minimum thrust level that may be used for proportional throttle control. It is often 0.8, but must always be greater than zero. The default value is 0.0.

subCommands.name: liquid_propellant_rocket_type
subCommands.description: Definitions for each type of liquid-propellant rocket engine are performed within the liquid_propellant_rocket_type block. Since the definition is for a ‘type’ of engine and not an ‘instance’ of an engine, no installation position/attitude data is included. Typically, the fuel_feed is specified at the instance-level rather than at the type-level.

subCommands.name: max_thrust_sealevel
subCommands.description: This specifies the maximum thrust that can be produced at sea level conditions. Either max_thrust_sealevel or max_thrust_vacuum should be specified, not both.

subCommands.name: max_thrust_vacuum
subCommands.description: This specifies the maximum thrust that can be produced at vacuum conditions. Either max_thrust_sealevel or max_thrust_vacuum should be specified, not both.

subCommands.name: normalized_thrust_vs_alt
subCommands.description: This is a simple table of “normalized-thrust” versus altitude. Normalized thrust is a value that will be multiplied with a nominal isp-calculated thrust, typically computed using max_thrust_sealevel and isp_vs_alt. This allows altitude-effects on thrust production:

subCommands.name: isp_vs_alt
subCommands.description: This is a simple table of specific impulse (Isp) versus altitude:

subCommands.name: normalized_spinup
subCommands.description: This specifies the spin-up rate in normalized-position/second. A value of 1.0 implies that the engine will spin-up from zero to full thrust in 1 second, while a value of 0.1 implies that it will take 10 seconds to spin-up from zero to full thrust.

subCommands.name: normalized_spindown
subCommands.description: This specifies the spin-down rate in normalized-position/second. A value of 1.0 implies that the engine will spin-down from full thrust to zero thrust in 1 second, while a value of 0.1 implies that it will take 10 seconds to spin-down from full thrust to zero thrust.

subCommands.name: creates_smoke_trail
subCommands.description: This determines whether or not the rocket will generate a smoke trail appearance. By default, liquid-propellant rockets do not produce a smoke trail, but solid-propellant rockets do produce a smoke trail.

subCommands.name: solid_propellant_rocket_type
subCommands.description: Definitions for each type of solid-propellant rocket motor are performed within the solid_propellant_rocket_type block. Since the definition is for a ‘type’ of engine/motor and not an ‘instance’ of an engine/motor, no installation position/attitude data is included. Note that unlike jet engines, ramjets/scramjets, and liquid-propellant rocket engines, a solid-propellant rocket motor does not specify a fuel_feed, since it contains its own propellant.

subCommands.name: rated_thrust
subCommands.description: This specifies the “rated thrust” of the solid-propellant motor. Since thrust depends on a range of conditions, this is a reference number, often used to calculate percent thrust.

subCommands.name: thrust_vs_time_sealevel
subCommands.description: This is a simple table of thrust in lbs as a function of time in seconds at sea level pressure conditions. Either thrust_vs_time_sealevel or thrust_vs_time_vacuum should be specified, but not both.

subCommands.name: thrust_vs_time_vacuum
subCommands.description: This is a simple table of thrust in lbs as a function of time in seconds at vacuum pressure conditions. Either thrust_vs_time_sealevel or thrust_vs_time_vacuum should be specified, but not both.

subCommands.name: propellant_mass
subCommands.description: This specifies the propellant mass in the solid-propellant motor.

subCommands.name: propellant_rel_pos_x
subCommands.description: This specifies the center of mass (in the x-direction of rocket-coordinates) of the propellant mass relative to the reference point of the rocket.

subCommands.name: propellant_rel_pos_y
subCommands.description: This specifies the center of mass (in the y-direction of rocket-coordinates) of the propellant mass relative to the reference point of the rocket.

subCommands.name: propellant_rel_pos_z
subCommands.description: This specifies the center of mass (in the z-direction of rocket-coordinates) of the propellant mass relative to the reference point of the rocket.

automatic_recovery_time.description: Define the time elapsed between damage state 1.0 (complete damage) and queued recovery. Only valid if the time is set to a positive value, and part is declared restorable. After time elapses, the Resurrect() virtual method will be called on the part.

subCommands.name: aux_data
subCommands.description: Define auxiliary data for the object. See the aux_data command for the syntax of defining auxiliary data.

subCommands.name: category
subCommands.description: Declare that the object is a member of the specified category. This command may be specified multiple times to indicate the object is a member of multiple categories. Categories can be queried by the script language method CategoryMemberOf(“*name*”) of WsfPlatformPart.

subCommands.name: clear_categories
subCommands.description: Has the effect of canceling any previous category commands.

subCommands.name: non_critical
subCommands.description: If critical, and the part damage becomes 1.0 (broken), the platform will be removed from the simulation.

subCommands.name: damage_factor
subCommands.description: Initial damage factor of the part. Zero is no damage, 1.0 is totally damaged (functionally broken). If damage factor is 1.0, it must be decreased toward zero before the part can become operational, but non_resurrectible will preclude this. External entities or effects may influence the damage level. It is up to the part implementation to determine how its operations are degraded in response to a non-zero damage factor.

subCommands.name: clear_internal_links
subCommands.description: Remove all of the currently defined internal links defined by the internal_link or processor commands. This is useful if one wants to reuse an existing platform definition with some modifications.

subCommands.name: processor
subCommands.description: Specify that messages that originate from this object are to be routed to the specified platform part object on the same platform. This command may be specified multiple times to route the message to multiple recipients.

subCommands.name: no_debug
subCommands.description: Enables or disables debugging for the object. The actual effect of enabling debugging for an object is implementation-specific. Typically a lot of information will be written to standard output, to allow some control of the information displayed use debug_level.

subCommands.name: debug_level
subCommands.description: Specifies the debugging level from level [1, 3]. Each level normally provides for different types or quantity of debugging information to displayed standard output. Also requires that the debug be set. The actual effect of enabling debugging level for an object is implementation-specific.

subCommands.name: group_leave
subCommands.description: Adds or removes the platform from the specified group.

subCommands.name: is_a_type_of
subCommands.description: The type hierarchy of an object is normally defined by the objects from which the object inherits. This command allows one to define that the object is also of the specified type.

subCommands.name: broken
subCommands.description: Part is declared non_operational, completely damaged, and non_resurrectible. Is functionally equivalent to setting the damage_factor to 1.0, non_restorable, and non_operational simultaneously. The part cannot be repaired.

subCommands.name: on
subCommands.description: Define the initial state of the object to be off or on.

subCommands.name: non_operational
subCommands.description: Define the operational state of the object. An object that is operational can be turned off and on and otherwise used for operations. An object that is non_operational cannot be used until it is made operational.

subCommands.name: non_restorable
subCommands.description: Define the ability of the part to recover from damage factor = 1.0. If non_restorable, the part damage latches at 1.0.

point_mass_vehicle_type.description: The definition of a point_mass_vehicle_type is performed within a point_mass_vehicle_type block. Each point_mass_vehicle_type defines a ‘type’ of vehicle, ranging from a simple, hand-launched drone to a complex spacecraft. A point_mass_vehicle_type may include the definition of mass properties, primary aerodynamics, propulsion system components (including engines and fuel systems), subobjects (such as weapons, fuel tanks, etc.), sequencers (which can produce an “action” based on an “event”), controls providers (which include manual pilots, synthetic pilots, autopilots, and guidance systems), flight control systems (which determine how control inputs are routed/mixed to move control surfaces), secondary aerodynamics (which includes control surface aerodynamics), size factor parameters (which allow an object’s size to vary, such as that of a parachute or balloon), relative positioning (which defines how a subobject is positioned relative to its parent while captive), separation effects (which impart a delta-V or angular rate to a subobject when it is jettisoned from its parent), and other special properties.

subCommands.name: mass
subCommands.description: The (empty) mass of the object, not including fuel.

subCommands.name: moment_of_inertia_ixx
subCommands.description: The (empty) moment of inertia about the x-axis the object, not including fuel.

subCommands.name: moment_of_inertia_iyy
subCommands.description: The (empty) moment of inertia about the y-axis the object, not including fuel.

subCommands.name: moment_of_inertia_izz
subCommands.description: The (empty) moment of inertia about the z-axis the object, not including fuel.

subCommands.name: center_of_mass_x
subCommands.description: The empty center of mass (in the object’s x-direction) relative to the reference point.

subCommands.name: center_of_mass_y
subCommands.description: The empty center of mass (in the object’s y-direction) relative to the reference point.

subCommands.name: center_of_mass_z
subCommands.description: The empty center of mass (in the object’s z-direction) relative to the reference point.

subCommands.name: integrator
subCommands.description: This sets the object’s integrator type to the specified name. If no integrator with the specified name exists, an exception will be thrown, since SixDOF objects cannot function without an integrator.

subCommands.name: fuel_transfer
subCommands.description: Regardless of whether a fuel transfer is defined within the propulsion_data block or the point_mass_vehicle_type block, a fuel transfer always consists of a source tank and a target tank. During runtime, the source tank will attempt to transfer fuel to the target tank, limited by the transfer rates of the two tanks.

subCommands.name: source_tank
subCommands.description: The source tank is defined by its string name.

subCommands.name: target_tank
subCommands.description: The target tank is defined by its string name.

subCommands.name: remove_fuel_transfer
subCommands.description: This removes the fuel transfer with the specified name. If a no transfer exists with the name, the command is ignored.

subCommands.name: remove_fuel_tank
subCommands.description: This removes the fuel tank with the specified name. If a no tank exists with the name, the command is ignored.

subCommands.name: modify_fuel_quantity
subCommands.description: This modifies the quantity of fuel in the fuel tank with the specified name. If a no tank exists with the name, the command is ignored.

subCommands.name: parent_rel_x
subCommands.description: This specifies the x-location of the object’s reference point relative to the parent’s reference point using the parent’s body coordinate system.

subCommands.name: parent_rel_y
subCommands.description: This specifies the y-location of the object’s reference point relative to the parent’s reference point using the parent’s body coordinate system.

subCommands.name: parent_rel_z
subCommands.description: This specifies the z-location of the object’s reference point relative to the parent’s reference point using the parent’s body coordinate system.

subCommands.name: parent_rel_yaw
subCommands.description: This specifies the yaw of the object about its reference point relative to the parent’s body coordinate system.

subCommands.name: parent_rel_pitch
subCommands.description: This specifies the pitch of the object about its reference point relative to the parent’s body coordinate system.

subCommands.name: parent_rel_roll
subCommands.description: This specifies the roll of the object about its reference point relative to the parent’s body coordinate system.

subCommands.name: separation_vx
subCommands.description: This specifies the x-component of velocity (in parent body coordinates) that is imparted to the subobject when it separates from the parent.

subCommands.name: separation_vy
subCommands.description: This specifies the y-component of velocity (in parent body coordinates) that is imparted to the subobject when it separates from the parent.

subCommands.name: separation_vz
subCommands.description: This specifies the z-component of velocity (in parent body coordinates) that is imparted to the subobject when it separates from the parent.

subCommands.name: separation_omega_x
subCommands.description: This specifies the x-component of angular velocity (in subobject body coordinates) that is imparted to the subobject when it separates from the parent.

subCommands.name: separation_omega_y
subCommands.description: This specifies the y-component of angular velocity (in subobject body coordinates) that is imparted to the subobject when it separates from the parent.

subCommands.name: separation_omega_z
subCommands.description: This specifies the z-component of angular velocity (in subobject body coordinates) that is imparted to the subobject when it separates from the parent.

subCommands.name: size_factor_radius
subCommands.description: This is the “reference” radius that is the starting radius of the object. This radius is also used to calculate a reference area and a reference volume.

subCommands.name: size_factor_min
subCommands.description: This is the minimum factor (multiplier) that the reference radius is allowed to achieve.

subCommands.name: size_factor_max
subCommands.description: This is the maximum factor (multiplier) that the reference radius is allowed to achieve.

subCommands.name: size_factor_volume_rate_m3_per_sec
subCommands.description: This provides a volume-based rate of change of cubic meters per second. When volume-based mode is used, the area and radius modes should not be used.

subCommands.name: size_factor_area_rate_m2_per_sec
subCommands.description: This provides an area-based rate of change of square meters per second. When area-based mode is used, the volume and radius modes should not be used.

subCommands.name: size_factor_radius_rate_m_per_sec
subCommands.description: This provides an radius-based rate of change of meters per second. When radius-based mode is used, the volume and area modes should not be used.

subCommands.name: use_spherical_earth
subCommands.description: If ‘true’, the SixDOF object will use a spherical earth model rather than a WGS84 (oblate) earth model. This is often a useful simplification when using ballistic missiles and space launch vehicles, since it eliminates latitude issues for guidance associated with an oblate earth.

subCommands.name: use_rotating_earth
subCommands.description: If ‘true’, the SixDOF object will use a rotating earth model rather than a non-rotating earth model.

subCommands.name: ignore_jettisoned_objects
subCommands.description: If ‘true’, any subobjects that are jettisoned from the SixDOF object will be removed immediately and will never have an AFSIM platform. This is often used to speed up runtimes when spent stages from a ballistic missile or space launch vehicle are not needed.

subCommands.name: fixed_object
subCommands.description: If ‘true’, the SixDOF object will not perform kinematic calculations as part of its “update” but will instead remain motionless.

subCommands.name: nominal_max_mach
subCommands.description: This defines the maximum Mach expected by the object. This does not impose a limit on performance, rather it is a hint for functions that calculate performance and/or analysis.

subCommands.name: nominal_max_alpha
subCommands.description: This defines the maximum alpha (angle of attack) expected by the object. This does not impose a limit on performance, rather it is a hint for functions that calculate performance and/or analysis.

subCommands.name: nominal_min_alpha
subCommands.description: This defines the minimum alpha (angle of attack) expected by the object. This does not impose a limit on performance, rather it is a hint for functions that calculate performance and/or analysis.

subCommands.name: nominal_max_beta
subCommands.description: This defines the maximum beta (angle of sideslip) expected by the object. This does not impose a limit on performance, rather it is a hint for functions that calculate performance and/or analysis.

report.syntax: report [communication | detection | eclipse | engagement | dsv | trajectory]
report.description: Specifies the type of report that is being generated.

subCommands.name: report_name
subCommands.description: Specifies the name of the report. If the folder(s) or file(s) already exist then it will be overwritten. The run number is automatically inserted at the end of the filename, but can be inserted manually also using the %d tag. The date and time tags, %D and %T may also be used to aid in file management.

subCommands.name: data_file
subCommands.description: Specifies the name of the file where the input file(s) are located. To process Monte-Carlo files insert the run number tag %d in the file name.

subCommands.name: output_directory
subCommands.description: Specifies the name of the folder where the output files will be generated. If the folder & files already exist then it will be overwritten. The run number is automatically inserted at the end of the filename, but can be inserted manually also using the %d tag. The date and time tags, %D and %T may also be used to aid in file management.

subCommands.name: monte_carlo_start
subCommands.description: Specifies the starting run number.

subCommands.name: monte_carlo_end
subCommands.description: Specifies the ending run number.

subCommands.name: single_output_file
subCommands.description: Specifies if all formatted run data should be output to a single file. (Currently not implemented)

subCommands.name: write_header_information
subCommands.description: Specifies if headers should be output to the report(s).

subCommands.name: delimiter
subCommands.description: Specifies the delimiter that separates the values.

subCommands.name: length_units
subCommands.description: Specifies the unit of measurement for distances. (Currently not implemented)

subCommands.name: angle_units
subCommands.description: Specifies the unit of measurement for angles. (Currently not implemented)

subCommands.name: track_number_options
subCommands.description: Specifies the track number format options. (Currently not implemented)

subCommands.name: start_time
subCommands.description: Specifies the start time of the desired data.

subCommands.name: end_time
subCommands.description: Specifies the end time of the desired data.

subCommands.name: lat_lon_format
