subCommands.description: Specifies the format and number of decimal places for displaying latitude and longitude values.

subCommands.name: time_format
subCommands.description: Specifies the format and number of decimal places for displaying time values.

subCommands.name: precision
subCommands.description: Specifies the precision of double values.

subCommands.name: report_type
subCommands.description: Specifies the subreport type. (See also: Subreports)

subCommands.name: transmitters
subCommands.description: Specifies the transmitters whose data will be collected.

subCommands.name: receivers
subCommands.description: Specifies the receivers whose data will be collected.

subCommands.name: networks
subCommands.description: Specifies the networks whose data will be collected.

subCommands.name: options
subCommands.description: Specifies other options that applies to the traffic count subreport.

subCommands.name: interval
subCommands.description: Specifies the interval of time desired per data set.

subCommands.name: detected_platforms
subCommands.description: Specifies the detected platforms whose data will be collected.

subCommands.name: detecting_platforms
subCommands.description: Specifies the detecting platforms whose data will be collected.

subCommands.name: platforms
subCommands.description: Specifies the platforms whose data will be collected.

subCommands.name: acting_platforms
subCommands.description: Specifies the acting platforms whose data will be collected.

subCommands.name: against_platforms
subCommands.description: Specifies the target platforms whose data will be collected.

subCommands.name: types_of_actions
subCommands.description: Specifies the detecting platforms whose data will be collected.

subCommands.name: types_of_weapons
subCommands.description: Specifies the types of weapons whose data will be collected. (Currently not implemented)

subCommands.name: update_interval
subCommands.description: If non-zero, specifies a periodic time interval at which the simulation will call the processor. If zero then the processor will only respond to explicit messages.

subCommands.name: soil_moisture_fraction
subCommands.description: Define the moisture content of the soil.

subCommands.name: surface_roughness
subCommands.description: Define the standard deviation of the variation in the height of the surface.

subCommands.name: gmti_adjustment_table
subCommands.description: Defines a function that attempts to capture the effect that a slow moving target is harder for a MTI sensor to detect that a faster moving target of the same size, and that the effect is non-linear. The function defines an adjustment factor (degradation of the received signal) versus either the closing speed or Doppler frequency. The table is defined using one of the following two forms:

subCommands.name: mti_adjustment_file
subCommands.description: Specifies an external MTI table in a comma-separated-value (CSV) file. The file should have one header row and two columns. The 1st column is the independent speed values, while the 2nd column is the dependent attenuation values. All entries should be unit-less. This table only supports speed and dB entries. The assumed units are m/sec and dB.

subCommands.name: mti_adjustment_compound_file
subCommands.description: Specifies an external MTI table in a comma-separated-value (CSV) file. The file should have one header row and ‘more’ than two columns. The last column is the dependent attenuation, while all preceding columns are independent speed values which all map to the dependent attenuation. The convention is that each independent column represents a different frequency, and that frequency is indicated in its header. For example, a column header of “ATTN (db) 30” is the column for 30 MHz. The dependent attenuation column entry can by any string. All entries should be unit-less. Excluding the header, this table only supports speed and dB entries. The assumed units are m/sec and dB.

subCommands.name: mti_maximum_range
subCommands.description: Specifies a maximum range to be used with the MTI “tables” only. If the target is farther away, any MTI table will NOT be applied.

subCommands.name: maximum_range
subCommands.description: Specifies the maximum ground range from the sensor to the target for which MTI processing will occur. MTI processing will be applied only if the target is within this range.

subCommands.name: interpulse_period_2
subCommands.description: Optional values that indicate the interpulse periods.

subCommands.name: number_of_stages
subCommands.description: Specifies the number of stages in the MTI processor.

subCommands.name: clutter_lock
subCommands.description: This is provided for compatibility with the SALRAM model.

subCommands.name: upwind
subCommands.description: This is provided for compatibility with the SALRAM model.

subCommands.name: unfiltered_doppler_speed
subCommands.description: Specifies if the ownship velocity is removed from the Doppler speed computation. A MTI sensor would typically employ filtered_doppler_speed.

subCommands.name: maximum_doppler_speed
subCommands.description: Defines the minimum and maximum target Doppler speed (i.e., opening or closing speed) capable of being detected.

subCommands.name: debug
subCommands.description: Presence of this flag indicates the MTI Signal Processor will output additional operational messages to the system console.

subCommands.name: zvf_switch
subCommands.description: Switch for Zero Velocity Filter effects being applied or not.

subCommands.name: zvf_filter_bandwidth
subCommands.description: Specifies the zero velocity filter bandwidth corresponding to PRF(I), where i is the input integer value. Input 0.0 for each for matched filter.

subCommands.name: zvf_num_filter_poles
subCommands.description: Specifies the number of poles (the order) of the Chebyshev filter. Must be in the range 1 to 7.

subCommands.name: zvf_filter_slr
subCommands.description: Specifies the mainlobe-to-peak sidelobe difference of the Chebyshev filters. Must be greater than 0.0 dB.

subCommands.name: mti_switch
subCommands.description: Switch for Moving Target Indicator (MTI) effects being applied or not.

subCommands.name: mti_num_delays
subCommands.description: Specifies the Number of MTI delay lines.Must be greater than 0.

subCommands.name: mti_min_response
subCommands.description: Specifies the minimum power response of the MTI system, floor value of the MTI power response.

subCommands.name: mti_num_gates
subCommands.description: Specifies the number of MTI gates. Must be between in the range of 1-4. If 0 MTI is off.

subCommands.name: mti_range_limits
subCommands.description: Specifies the MTI gate minimum and maximum range for the Ith MTI gate.

subCommands.name: mti_angle_limits
subCommands.description: Specifies the MTI gate minimum and maximum azimuth for the Ith MTI gate.

subCommands.name: pd_num_filters
subCommands.description: Specifies the number of Doppler filters in the filter bank.

subCommands.name: pd_filter_bandwidth
subCommands.description: Specifies the Radar Doppler filter bandwidth corresponding to PRF(I), where i is the input integer value. Input 0.0 for each for matched filter.

subCommands.name: pd_num_filter_poles
subCommands.description: Specifies the number of poles (the order) of the Chebyshev filter. Must be in the range 1 to 7.

subCommands.name: pd_filter_slr
subCommands.description: Specifies the mainlobe-to-peak sidelobe difference of the Chebyshev filters. Must be greater than 0.0 dB.

subCommands.name: stc_type
subCommands.description: Indicate the type of STC signal processing that will be used. Valid values are min_range, max_range, min_max_range, or data_table.

subCommands.name: stc_min_response
subCommands.description: Specifies the minimum STC response level. Entered as a ratio, valid values are 0 dB or less (0.0 1.0 absolute). This value is required for all STC types. This value is required for all STC types.

subCommands.name: stc_min_range
subCommands.description: Specifies the minimum slant range at which STC response will begin in min_range and min_max_range STC types. At ranges less than the minimum range STC response is the stc_min_response value.

subCommands.name: stc_max_range
subCommands.description: Specifies the maximum slant range that STC response will be applied in max_range and min_max_range STC types. At ranges greater than the maximum range an STC response is 0 dB.

subCommands.name: stc_order
subCommands.description: Order of the STC response curve used for min_range, max_range, and min_max_range STC types. Valid values are real numbers greater than or equal to zero.

subCommands.name: stc_data_table
subCommands.description: Defines STC response as a function of the slant range. Required if stc_type is data_table. Table values are a length value and ratio pair. The independent and dependent variable units commands are optional, but if they are not specified the units are assumed to be meters and dB.

subCommands.name: use_bisector_for_bistatic
subCommands.description: Specifies if a bistatic signature will be approximated for bistatic detection attempts.

subCommands.name: interpolate_tables
subCommands.description: Specifies whether to apply interpolation to the defined Azimuth-Elevation Table Definition. The type of interpolation can be either linear or logarithmic (see interpolation_type).

subCommands.name: interpolation_type
subCommands.description: Specifies whether to use linear or logarithmic interpolation when interpolating data in the azimuth elevation tables.

subCommands.name: state
subCommands.description: Indicates that the following table definitions will be used when the platform is in the signature state <state-name>.

subCommands.name: polarization
subCommands.syntax: polarization [ horizontal | vertical | slant_45 | slant_135 | left_circular | right_circular | default ]
subCommands.description: Indicates that the following table(s) (up to the next polarization or state) are to be used when the sensing radar is operating with the specified polarization.

subCommands.name: frequency_limit
subCommands.description: Indicates the upper frequency bound to which the following table applies. These must occur in increasing order within a single state/polarization grouping. For a radar is operating with a particular polarization and frequency, the table selected will be the first one with the proper state and polarization where the frequency less than frequency_limit.

subCommands.name: plt_file
subCommands.description: Loads a PLT file, in either 3- or 5-column format, that includes multiple Az/El table definitions indexed by polarization and frequency. Because the polarization and frequency are embedded within the file, any previous polarization or frequency_limit command will be ignored. Optionally, a polarization (horizontal or vertical) to be used as the default may be specified. However, since every state must have a default polarization, if this optional argument is omitted, one must be defined explicitly using the polarization command.

subCommands.name: bistatic_signature
subCommands.description: Defines a bistatic radar signature for a platform type. This signature is used for bistatic interactions (i.e. interactions involving a transmitter and receiver not colocated). This input block is defined within the radar_signature block and defines a separate table to be used for bistatic interactions RCS lookups.

subCommands.name: interpolate_transmitter_angles
subCommands.description: Specifies whether or not to interpolate between the tables for the specified target->transmitter angles. If ‘false’ then the next lower azimuth/elevation angle table is used for the given target->transmitter azimuth/elevation pair.

subCommands.name: transmitter_angles_interpolation_type
subCommands.description: Specifies whether to use linear or logarithmic interpolation when interpolating target->transmitter angles.

subCommands.name: azimuth
subCommands.description: Specifies the minimum target->transmitter azimuth angle, between [-180.0, 180.0] degrees, for the entered table. Must specify at least two monotonically increasing angles with tables. Tables are a function of the target->receiver angles.

subCommands.name: elevation
subCommands.description: Specifies the minimum target->transmitter elevation angle, between [-90.0, 90.0] degrees, for the entered table. Must specify at least two monotonically increasing angles. Tables are a function of the target->receiver azimuth/elevation angles.

receiver.description: The receiver block defines the attributes of an electromagnetic receiver. Various sensor and communication objects make use of receivers.

subCommands.name: antenna_ohmic_loss
subCommands.description: This value, along with noise_figure and receive_line_loss, provides one method to determine the receiver noise power. It specifies the ohmic resistance of the antenna.

subCommands.name: antenna_pattern
subCommands.description: Specifies the name of the antenna gain pattern used by the receiver. The pattern must be defined using the antenna_pattern command.

subCommands.name: antenna_pattern_table
subCommands.description: This command allows the definition of frequency-dependent or polarization- and frequency-dependent antenna gain pattern. Each named antenna pattern must be defined using the antenna_pattern command.

subCommands.name: attenuation
subCommands.syntax: attenuation ….. (attenuation is a synonym for attenuation_model)
subCommands.description: Specify the attenuation model. See the global command attenuation_model for more information about the available attenuation models and how to configure the models.

subCommands.name: aux_data
subCommands.description: Defines application-specific ‘auxiliary data’. See aux_data.

subCommands.name: bandwidth
subCommands.description: [ frequency - 1/2 bandwidth, frequency + 1/2 bandwidth ]

subCommands.name: beam_tilt
subCommands.description: This is only to be used when defining systems that employ multiple beams (e.g., when using multiple beams in WSF_RADAR_SENSOR). It specifies the elevation angle of the beam center above the horizontal plane.

subCommands.name: check_terrain_masking
subCommands.description: Toggles the computation of terrain and horizon line of sight. This may be set to ‘off’ to either reduce computation or model sensors and comm devices which do not have line of sight limitations. By default, horizon masking is checked first, followed by a separate terrain masking check if terrain is loaded. The simple horizon masking check assumes a smooth bald spherical Earth and that any object below zero mean sea level is obscured. For subsurface sensors, horizon checking can be disabled by setting the terrain_masking_mode to terrain_only.

subCommands.name: check_transmitter_masking
subCommands.description: Toggles the computation of terrain and horizon line of sight for transmitter checks. This may be set to ‘off’ to either reduce computation or model sensors and comm devices which do not have line of sight limitations, e.g. bistatic sensors.

subCommands.name: terrain_masking_mode
subCommands.description: Sets the mode or type of masking checks to perform. By default, both horizon and terrain masking checks are enabled.

subCommands.name: detection_threshold
subCommands.description: Specifies the signal-to-noise ratio above which the signal is declared to be detectable.

subCommands.name: effective_earth_radius
subCommands.description: Specify either the multiplier for Earth’s radius, or the effective earth radius, used to compute the effects of atmospheric refraction of radio-frequency signals.

subCommands.name: wavelength
subCommands.description: Specifies the center frequency to which the receiver is tuned. The receiver will accept signals whose frequency is between:

subCommands.name: instantaneous_bandwidth
subCommands.description: Specifies the instantaneous bandwidth of the receiver. For a frequency hopping or scanning system, this would be the bandwidth that is processed during an individual hop or scan point.

subCommands.name: internal_loss
subCommands.description: A single number can be used account for miscellaneous losses. This value occurs in the denominator:

subCommands.name: noise_figure
subCommands.description: This value, along with antenna_ohmic_loss and receive_line_loss, provide one method to specify the receiver noise power.

subCommands.name: noise_power
subCommands.description: Specifies the explicit noise power. This is one mechanism for specifying the receiver noise.

subCommands.name: polarization
subCommands.syntax: polarization [ horizontal | vertical | slant_45 | slant_135 | left_circular | right_circular | default ]
subCommands.description: Specify the primary polarization of the signals which the receiving antenna will receive.

subCommands.name: polarization_effect
subCommands.syntax: polarization_effect [ horizontal | vertical | slant_45 | slant_135 | left_circular | right_circular ] <fraction>
subCommands.description: This command defines the fraction of a received signal of the specified polarization that will be processed. This allows one to override the default behavior when a receiver attempts to receive a signal that is of a different polarization that its primary polarization.

subCommands.name: propagation_model
subCommands.description: Specify the propagation model. See global command propagation_model for more information about the available propagation models and how to configure the models.

subCommands.name: receive_line_loss
subCommands.description: This value, along with antenna_ohmic_loss and noise_figure, provide one method to specify the receiver noise power. It specifies the RF component line loss between the antenna and the receiver.

subCommands.name: electronic_protect
subCommands.description: A block that defines the Electronic Protection (EP) capabilities within the receiver. See electronic_protect for the available commands.

rigid_body_vehicle_type.description: The definition of a rigid_body_vehicle_type is performed within a rigid_body_vehicle_type block. Each rigid_body_vehicle_type defines a ‘type’ of vehicle, ranging from a simple, hand-launched drone to a complex spacecraft. A rigid_body_vehicle_type may include the definition of mass properties, primary aerodynamics, propulsion system components (including engines and fuel systems), subobjects (such as weapons, fuel tanks, etc.), sequencers (which can produce an “action” based on an “event”), controls providers (which include manual pilots, synthetic pilots, autopilots, and guidance systems), flight control systems (which determine how control inputs are routed/mixed to move control surfaces), secondary aerodynamics (which includes control surface aerodynamics), size factor parameters (which allow an object’s size to vary, such as that of a parachute or balloon), relative positioning (which defines how a subobject is positioned relative to its parent while captive), separation effects (which impart a delta-V or angular rate to a subobject when it is jettisoned from its parent), and other special properties.

subCommands.name: mass
subCommands.description: The (empty) mass of the object, not including fuel.

subCommands.name: moment_of_inertia_ixx
subCommands.description: The (empty) moment of inertia about the x-axis the object, not including fuel.

subCommands.name: moment_of_inertia_iyy
subCommands.description: The (empty) moment of inertia about the y-axis the object, not including fuel.

subCommands.name: moment_of_inertia_izz
subCommands.description: The (empty) moment of inertia about the z-axis the object, not including fuel.

subCommands.name: center_of_mass_x
subCommands.description: The empty center of mass (in the object’s x-direction) relative to the reference point.

subCommands.name: center_of_mass_y
subCommands.description: The empty center of mass (in the object’s y-direction) relative to the reference point.

subCommands.name: center_of_mass_z
subCommands.description: The empty center of mass (in the object’s z-direction) relative to the reference point.

subCommands.name: integrator
subCommands.description: This sets the object’s integrator type to the specified name. If no integrator with the specified name exists, an exception will be thrown, since SixDOF objects cannot function without an integrator.

subCommands.name: fuel_transfer
subCommands.description: Regardless of whether a fuel transfer is defined within the propulsion_data block or the rigid_body_vehicle_type block, a fuel transfer always consists of a source tank and a target tank. During runtime, the source tank will attempt to transfer fuel to the target tank, limited by the transfer rates of the two tanks.

subCommands.name: source_tank
subCommands.description: The source tank is defined by its string name.

subCommands.name: target_tank
subCommands.description: The target tank is defined by its string name.

subCommands.name: remove_fuel_transfer
subCommands.description: This removes the fuel transfer with the specified name. If a no transfer exists with the name, the command is ignored.

subCommands.name: remove_fuel_tank
subCommands.description: This removes the fuel tank with the specified name. If a no tank exists with the name, the command is ignored.

subCommands.name: modify_fuel_quantity
subCommands.description: This modifies the quantity of fuel in the fuel tank with the specified name. If a no tank exists with the name, the command is ignored.

subCommands.name: parent_rel_x
subCommands.description: This specifies the x-location of the object’s reference point relative to the parent’s reference point using the parent’s body coordinate system.

subCommands.name: parent_rel_y
subCommands.description: This specifies the y-location of the object’s reference point relative to the parent’s reference point using the parent’s body coordinate system.

subCommands.name: parent_rel_z
subCommands.description: This specifies the z-location of the object’s reference point relative to the parent’s reference point using the parent’s body coordinate system.

subCommands.name: parent_rel_yaw
subCommands.description: This specifies the yaw of the object about its reference point relative to the parent’s body coordinate system.

subCommands.name: parent_rel_pitch
subCommands.description: This specifies the pitch of the object about its reference point relative to the parent’s body coordinate system.

subCommands.name: parent_rel_roll
subCommands.description: This specifies the roll of the object about its reference point relative to the parent’s body coordinate system.

subCommands.name: separation_vx
subCommands.description: This specifies the x-component of velocity (in parent body coordinates) that is imparted to the subobject when it separates from the parent.

subCommands.name: separation_vy
subCommands.description: This specifies the y-component of velocity (in parent body coordinates) that is imparted to the subobject when it separates from the parent.

subCommands.name: separation_vz
subCommands.description: This specifies the z-component of velocity (in parent body coordinates) that is imparted to the subobject when it separates from the parent.

subCommands.name: separation_omega_x
subCommands.description: This specifies the x-component of angular velocity (in subobject body coordinates) that is imparted to the subobject when it separates from the parent.

subCommands.name: separation_omega_y
subCommands.description: This specifies the y-component of angular velocity (in subobject body coordinates) that is imparted to the subobject when it separates from the parent.

subCommands.name: separation_omega_z
subCommands.description: This specifies the z-component of angular velocity (in subobject body coordinates) that is imparted to the subobject when it separates from the parent.

subCommands.name: size_factor_radius
subCommands.description: This is the “reference” radius that is the starting radius of the object. This radius is also used to calculate a reference area and a reference volume.

subCommands.name: size_factor_min
subCommands.description: This is the minimum factor (multiplier) that the reference radius is allowed to achieve.

subCommands.name: size_factor_max
subCommands.description: This is the maximum factor (multiplier) that the reference radius is allowed to achieve.

subCommands.name: size_factor_volume_rate_m3_per_sec
subCommands.description: This provides a volume-based rate of change of cubic meters per second. When volume-based mode is used, the area and radius modes should not be used.

subCommands.name: size_factor_area_rate_m2_per_sec
subCommands.description: This provides an area-based rate of change of square meters per second. When area-based mode is used, the volume and radius modes should not be used.

subCommands.name: size_factor_radius_rate_m_per_sec
subCommands.description: This provides an radius-based rate of change of meters per second. When radius-based mode is used, the volume and area modes should not be used.

subCommands.name: use_spherical_earth
subCommands.description: If ‘true’, the SixDOF object will use a spherical earth model rather than a WGS84 (oblate) earth model. This is often a useful simplification when using ballistic missiles and space launch vehicles, since it eliminates latitude issues for guidance associated with an oblate earth.

subCommands.name: use_rotating_earth
subCommands.description: If ‘true’, the SixDOF object will use a rotating earth model rather than a non-rotating earth model.

subCommands.name: ignore_jettisoned_objects
subCommands.description: If ‘true’, any subobjects that are jettisoned from the SixDOF object will be removed immediately and will never have an AFSIM platform. This is often used to speed up runtimes when spent stages from a ballistic missile or space launch vehicle are not needed.

subCommands.name: fixed_object
subCommands.description: If ‘true’, the SixDOF object will not perform kinematic calculations as part of its “update” but will instead remain motionless.

subCommands.name: nominal_max_mach
subCommands.description: This defines the maximum Mach expected by the object. This does not impose a limit on performance, rather it is a hint for functions that calculate performance and/or analysis.

subCommands.name: nominal_max_alpha
subCommands.description: This defines the maximum alpha (angle of attack) expected by the object. This does not impose a limit on performance, rather it is a hint for functions that calculate performance and/or analysis.

subCommands.name: nominal_min_alpha
subCommands.description: This defines the minimum alpha (angle of attack) expected by the object. This does not impose a limit on performance, rather it is a hint for functions that calculate performance and/or analysis.

subCommands.name: nominal_max_beta
subCommands.description: This defines the maximum beta (angle of sideslip) expected by the object. This does not impose a limit on performance, rather it is a hint for functions that calculate performance and/or analysis.

subCommands.name: network
subCommands.description: Defines the attributes and vehicles that are generated on the defined route_network as specified by the <route-network-name>.

subCommands.name: vehicle_count
subCommands.description: The number of vehicles generated and placed on the road network. If the <vehicle_count> is not specified, it will be set using <vehicle_density>.

subCommands.name: vehicle_density
subCommands.description: Instead of specifying a specific number of vehicles, a density number of vehicles per unit length can be specified (i.e., 5 per 1km)

subCommands.name: maximum_speed
subCommands.description: The maximum speed any vehicle on the network can travel even if a faster speed is specified in the vehicle block. This could simulate a speed limit.

subCommands.name: mean_travel_time
subCommands.description: The average travel time of all the vehicles in the network.

subCommands.name: sigma_travel_time
subCommands.description: The travel time magnitude of one standard deviation. When a vehicle reaches the end of its path or travel time, it travels off road by some amount and then pauses for a given amount of time before being removed from the simulation. The following three items (<minimum_distance_off_road>, maximum_distance_off_road, and pause_time_off_road) define the parameters, which define this process.

subCommands.name: minimum_distance_off_road
subCommands.description: The minimum distance that a vehicle travels off-road.

subCommands.name: maximum_distance_off_road
subCommands.description: The maximum distance that a vehicle travels off-road.

subCommands.name: pause_time_off_road
subCommands.description: The time that a vehicle pauses at the end of its route after traveling off-road.

subCommands.name: end_of_path_option
subCommands.description: This determines what should be done to vehicles at the end of their route. By default vehicles are re-spawned with a different route.

subCommands.name: vehicle
subCommands.description: Defines the attributes of a specific vehicle type within the context of this net work. To define multiple vehicle types, create multiple vehicle blocks. The <platform-type> must be a previously defined platform_type.

subCommands.name: fraction
subCommands.description: If multiple vehicle blocks are defined, the fraction is the percentage (as a decimal value) of this specific vehicle type that would populate the road network. The sum of all the vehicle fractions must add up to 1.

subCommands.name: mean_speed
subCommands.description: The average speed of all the vehicles defined by this vehicle block.

subCommands.name: sigma_speed
subCommands.description: The speed magnitude of one standard deviation.

subCommands.name: convoy
subCommands.description: This command defines a convoy (a series of vehicles that follow each other), that moves between two endpoints.

subCommands.name: start_position
subCommands.description: This defines the initial location of the convoy with a latitude and longitude value.

subCommands.name: end_position
subCommands.description: This defines the final location of the convoy as a latitude and longitude value.

subCommands.name: spacing
subCommands.description: This defines the spacing between each of the vehicles in the convoy.

subCommands.name: speed
subCommands.description: This defines the speed that the convoy will travel.

subCommands.name: use_closest_waypoint
subCommands.description: If this option is present, the convoy will start at the closest waypoint to the specified start position and end at the closest waypoint to the end position.

subCommands.name: weighted_region
subCommands.description: This command defines a region in the network where a higher density of vehicles will be created. For instance, this command can be used to generate more vehicles in a city region than in the country. Weighted regions have an inner and outer radius and weight. The weights are linearly interpolated between the inner and outer radii. This allows the simulation to vary the density of vehicles linearly between the inner and outer radii.

subCommands.name: latitude
subCommands.description: Specifies the center latitude of the weighted region.

subCommands.name: longitude
subCommands.description: Specifies the center longitude of the weighted region.

subCommands.name: inner_radius
subCommands.description: Specifies the inner radius of the weighted region.

subCommands.name: outer_radius
subCommands.description: Specifies the outer radius of the weighted region.

subCommands.name: inner_weight
subCommands.description: Specifies the weight that corresponds to the inner radius. The larger the weight number, the higher the density of vehicles.

subCommands.name: outer_weight
subCommands.description: Specifies the weight that corresponds to the outer radius. The larger the weight number, the higher the density of vehicles.

subCommands.name: navigation
subCommands.description: Defines the block input for Navigation Commands used to enter the route waypoints and other navigational data.

subCommands.name: aux_data
subCommands.description: Defines auxiliary data for a route. See aux_data for more commands and information.

subCommands.name: label
subCommands.description: Associates a string label with the immediately following waypoint definition. This can be used as the target of a goto command.

subCommands.name: position
subCommands.description: Specifies the latitude and longitude of the waypoint.

subCommands.name: mgrs_coordinate
subCommands.description: Specifies the coordinate of the waypoint in the Military Grid Reference System.

subCommands.name: offset
subCommands.description: Go to a point relative to the current location of the platform. Each offset waypoint is relative to the position of the previous waypoint (or platform’s position if it is the first waypoint), and orientation is set using the heading at the first offset waypoint and remains constant for all subsequent offset waypoints. The +X axis is in the direction of the initial heading and the +Y axis is 90 degrees to the right of the initial heading.

subCommands.name: turn_right
subCommands.description: Initiate a turn to effect the specified heading angle change.

subCommands.name: turn_to_heading
subCommands.description: Initiate a turn to the specified absolute heading angle. The direction of the turn will be in the direction that requires the least amount of heading angle change.

subCommands.name: goto
subCommands.description: When this waypoint is reached, go to the waypoint with the specified label in the current route.

subCommands.name: altitude
subCommands.description: Specifies the altitude at the waypoint. if agl or msl is omitted, the default altitude reference is defined by the mover. msl is assumed for WSF_AIR_MOVER and agl for all others.

subCommands.name: depth
subCommands.description: Specifies the sub-surface depth at the waypoint.

subCommands.name: heading
subCommands.description: Specifies the heading at the waypoint. This is really only effective for a route with one point. If more than one waypoint is given then heading will be determined automatically.

subCommands.name: turn
subCommands.description: Specifies the direction to turn if a turn is required.

subCommands.name: speed
subCommands.description: Specifies the speed at the waypoint.

subCommands.name: linear_acceleration
subCommands.description: Specifies the linear acceleration to be used for changing speed on the route segment that starts with this waypoint. <acceleration-value> may also be default to use the mover’s default linear_acceleration.

subCommands.name: radial_acceleration
subCommands.description: Specifies the radial acceleration to be used for turns when making heading changes on the route segment that starts with this waypoint. <acceleration-value> may also be default to use the mover’s default radial_acceleration.

subCommands.name: bank_angle_limit
subCommands.description: Specifies the maximum bank angle to be used for turns when making heading changes on the route segment that starts with this waypoint. This effectively sets the radial_acceleration to .

subCommands.name: turn_g_limit
subCommands.description: Specifies the maximum turn g-load to be used for turns when making heading changes on the route segment that starts with this waypoint. This effectively sets the radial_acceleration to .

subCommands.name: dive_rate
subCommands.description: Specifies the rate of climb or dive for changing altitude on the route segment that starts with this waypoint. <speed-value>* may also be default to use the mover’s default climb_rate. Note: the commands climb_rate and dive_rate are synonymous – specifying a dive_rate will replace a previously specified climb_rate.

subCommands.name: pause_time
subCommands.description: When the waypoint is reached, stop moving for the specified time.

subCommands.name: execute
subCommands.description: Specify a script or callback to be executed upon reaching the waypoint. <script-name>/<callback-name> must be the name of a ‘script’ defined for the platform or platform_type.

subCommands.name: remove
subCommands.description: Indicates to the mover what is to be done when this waypoint is encountered and there are no more waypoints in the route. The possible actions are:

subCommands.name: switch_on_approach
subCommands.description: Defines the condition when the mover should declare that it has reached this waypoint and should start moving towards the next waypoint. switch_on_passing is sometimes known as ‘turn long’ and causes the switch to occur when the platform passes over or along side of the waypoint. switch_on_approach is sometimes known as ‘turn short’ and causes the switch to occur before the waypoint.

subCommands.name: time
subCommands.description: If the waypoint is a turn_left, turn_right or turn_to_heading and the next waypoint is also one of the same class, this command specifies how long or how far to move until switching to the next waypoint.

subCommands.name: time_to_point
subCommands.description: If specified, the mover will change speed in attempt to reach this waypoint after the specified duration. <time-value> is the length of time it should take the platform to move from the previous waypoint to the current one. time_to_point may only be specified for position waypoints.

subCommands.name: node_id
subCommands.description: This command is used only if the route is part of a route_network. Waypoints that share the same node_id within a set of routes within a route_network are assumed to intersect or connect at those points.

subCommands.name: transform_absolute_route
subCommands.description: Translate the named route the specified about and insert it into the current route. Only position points will be translated.

subCommands.name: use_route
subCommands.description: Include the route type with the specified name as part of the route definition. Repeat as required to specify the route network.

subCommands.name: test
subCommands.description: During initialization, test all possible paths between each node_id in all route’s to solve the shortest path. A count of Nodes in the route_network tested is output to the console. See Example 1 - route_network with test command.

subCommands.name: test_nodes
subCommands.description: During initialization, test all routes to solve the shortest path between <from-node-id> and <to-node-id> (specified as integers).

subCommands.name: verbose
subCommands.description: Generates additional debug data when used with the test command. The following data is output to the console for each path tested:

subCommands.name: gateway_address
subCommands.description: If provided, defines the particular interface associated with this router that should be used to forward messages if the router is unable to find a destination for a message received on one of the router’s defined comm interfaces. The destination used for the selected comm gateway is defined on the comm itself.

subCommands.name: gateway
subCommands.description: If provided, defines the particular interface associated with this router that should be used to forward messages if the router is unable to find a destination for a message received on one of the router’s defined comm interfaces. The destination used for the selected comm gateway is defined on the comm itself.

subCommands.name: hop_limit
subCommands.description: Specifies the number of nodes/comms that a message may visit on the way to the destination before the message is simply discarded. Often referred to as time to live (TTL). The hop_limit applies to any messages initiated from this router’s interfaces. This value ensures that messages that may enter circular routing are eventually dropped.

subCommands.name: automated_interface_linking
subCommands.description: If set to true, all interfaces specified for this router will have connections created between members. This ensures that router interfaces are correctly represented as having direct connections to each other via the router hardware interface.

subCommands.name: use_default_protocol
subCommands.description: A convenience setting to determine if the router should use the default legacy routing protocol. True indicates to use this routing_protocol, false to remove it.

subCommands.name: use_multicast_protocol
subCommands.description: A convenience setting to determine if the router should use the default multicast routing protocol. True indicates to use this routing_protocol, false to remove it.

test_matrix.description: Within this block are delineated the list of target track test conditions to be evaluated for successful missile intercept. Four different arrays are to be provided: lateral_offsets, altitudes, speeds, and ranges. Each of the four arrays may be set by using the following syntax: a) from <start-value> to <end-value> by <delta-value>, or b) a listing, such as <value-1> <value-2> <value-3> … <end-value>. All values must be in increasing order, but the intervals need not be even, and the from-to-by syntax and enumerated list may be used in combination.

subCommands.name: altitudes
subCommands.description: The altitudes at which tracks are evaluated for intercept. Format as given in test_matrix above.

subCommands.name: lateral_offsets
subCommands.description: The lateral_offsets at which tracks are evaluated for intercept. Format as given in test_matrix above.

subCommands.name: ranges
subCommands.description: The target ground ranges at which tracks are evaluated for intercept. Format as given in test_matrix above.

subCommands.name: speeds
subCommands.description: The speeds at which tracks are evaluated for intercept. Format as given in test_matrix above.

subCommands.name: post_generation_interpolation_tests
subCommands.description: For debug purposes only, and is optional. Inside this block one may place one or more lateral_offset, altitude, ground_range, and target_speed specifications. Each time the keyword ‘test’ appears, the most recent value of (offset, altitude, speed, range) is saved off as a test point, and stored into a test point array. After the launch computer is generated, each of these test points will be evaluated, and the corresponding time-of-flight value will be printed to the screen. The example given below saves off three points for testing.

subCommands.name: lateral_offset
subCommands.description: Specify the track lateral_offset of the interpolation test point.

subCommands.name: altitude
subCommands.description: Specify the track altitude of the interpolation test point.

subCommands.name: ground_range
subCommands.description: Specify the track ground_range of the interpolation test point.

subCommands.name: target_speed
subCommands.description: Specify the track target speed of the interpolation test point.

subCommands.name: test
subCommands.description: Save off the most recent values for (offset, altitude, range, and speed), and store them as a point to be interpolation tested. Results will be printed to the screen.

subCommands.name: re_parse_produced_input_file
subCommands.description: After generating and writing the launch computer, re-open the file and attempt to read it back in through normal stream input processing. The file is not checked by default.

subCommands.name: tracker_height
subCommands.description: Set the height above ground for a tracking radar. This is used in horizon masking calculations, which will disable weapon launch for a target engagement that is masked by curvature of earth. If no value is input for this parameter, horizon masking is not considered, and missile kinematics alone are used to calculate a launch envelope.

subCommands.name: tracker_name
subCommands.description: Alternate way to set the tracker height by specifying the sensor’s name. If a tracker height wasn’t specified and tracker name was, the tracker height is resolved from its definition. The specified sensor must be present on the launching platform.

subCommands.name: tracker_elevation_limits
subCommands.description: Set the minimum and maximum elevation angles at which the tracking radar will function. Target elevation angles outside these limits will inhibit weapon launch.

subCommands.name: effective_earth_radius
subCommands.description: Set the effective earth radius ratio. Must be greater than zero.

scan_scheduling.description: Specifies how new platforms are added to the scan scheduling queue when using the default sensor scheduler:

subCommands.name: initial_heading
subCommands.description: Specifies the initial heading of the sensor where the sectors begin sweeping. If not specified, a random value is chosen.

subCommands.name: frame_based_scheduling
subCommands.description: Non-imaging sensors perform framed-based sector scan scheduling by default. This default behavior provides only one detection chance per target to take place for all sectors in a scan (or one detection chance per frame). To override frame-based scheduling for a non-imaging sensor, set this command to false. This command is not applicable to imaging sensors.

subCommands.name: type
subCommands.description: Specify the type of sector.

subCommands.name: start_azimuth
subCommands.description: Define the start azimuth of an azimuth or azimuth_and_elevation scan sector. Allowed values are in the range from -180.0 degrees to 180 degrees.

subCommands.name: end_azimuth
subCommands.description: Define the end azimuth of an azimuth or azimuth_and_elevation scan sector. Allowed values are in the range from -180.0 degrees to 180 degrees.

subCommands.name: start_elevation
subCommands.description: Define the start elevation of an elevation or azimuth_and_elevation scan sector. Allowed values are in the range from -90.0 degrees to 90.0 degrees.

subCommands.name: end_elevation
subCommands.description: Define the end elevation of an elevation or azimuth_and_elevation scan sector. Allowed values are in the range from -90.0 degrees to 90.0 degrees.

subCommands.name: azimuth
subCommands.description: Specify a fixed azimuth in an elevation scan.

subCommands.name: elevation
subCommands.description: Specify a fixed elevation in an azimuth scan.

subCommands.name: azimuth_rate
subCommands.description: Specify an azimuth rate value to use for an azimuth or azimuth_and_elevation scan sector.

subCommands.name: elevation_rate
subCommands.description: Specify an elevation rate value to use for an elevation or azimuth_and_elevation scan sector.

subCommands.name: azimuth_scan_direction
subCommands.description: Define the azimuth scan direction for azimuth and azimuth_and_elevation sector types to be either in the positive (clockwise) or negative (counter-clockwise) direction.

subCommands.name: scan_period
subCommands.description: Specifies the amount of time necessary for the sensor to complete 1 full rotation.

subCommands.name: clockwise
subCommands.description: Specifies whether the sensor scans clockwise or counter-clockwise. A value of true indicates clockwise scanning, and a value of false indicates counter-clockwise scanning.

subCommands.name: starting_beam_azimuth
subCommands.description: Specifies the starting angle of the sensor scan. This angle is relative to the +X axis of the sensor’s Part Coordinate System.

subCommands.name: starting_azimuth_randomized
subCommands.description: Specifies the starting angle of the sensor scan to be determined randomly. Unlike most AFSIM commands, this will warn user if it is subsequently overridden by the starting_beam_azimuth command.

script_call_trace.description: Controls whether a trace of script method calls will be written to standard output. This can be very useful for debugging complex scripts. If enabled, a line indicating the time, platform, platform part name and script name is written prior to calling the method. Upon return from the method another line is written which contains the function return value.

subCommands.name: script_debug_writes
subCommands.description: Controls whether the script debug write statements write_d and writeln_d are executed. If enabled, write_d and writeln_d statements are executed.

subCommands.name: script_abort_on_null_references
subCommands.description: When a script method is called with an invalid object or argument, an error is printed to the screen. When this option is enabled, the application will also terminate immediately. This command is only available in a global context.

subCommands.name: script_abort_on_assert
subCommands.description: When a call to assert() in script fails, the application will usually abort. Setting this option to ‘off’ will still print an error but will not abort the application.

subCommands.name: script
subCommands.description: Defines a script.

subCommands.name: script_variables
subCommands.description: Allows users to declare a set of variables that are accessible to scripts within a given context. For example, if the script_variables command is used inside the platform command, then all scripts defined within that platform have access to the variables that are defined. In addition, any scriptable platform parts can access their parents variables by using the extern keyword.

subCommands.name: script_interface
subCommands.description: Configures the scripting system. Multiple script_interface blocks may be provided. If the same subcommand is specified in multiple blocks then the last value given will be used

subCommands.name: debug
subCommands.description: Tells the compiler to produce a source listing and any errors that may occur during compilation (by default debug output is turned off).

subCommands.name: no_debug
subCommands.description: Tells the compiler not to produce the source and detailed error listing. The compiler will still display a simple message if an error occurs during compilation.

subCommands.name: uncloneable
subCommands.description: Specify that instances of this script_struct cannot be cloned.

on_initialize.description: Define a script that is executed when the event is initialized. This initialization occurs when the mission event is scheduled, which is either when the mission sequence is scheduled for the first event of a mission sequence, or immediately upon completion of the previous event of a mission sequence.

subCommands.name: on_update
subCommands.description: Define a script that executes with the update_interval and duration of the event, starting from the time at which the event’s constraint is first met. If duration is not defined the script is always executed once. If the is_complete script is defined and the event is finite, it is also updated at subsequent constraint times, until the is_complete script returns true. Alternately, if duration is defined, the event will execute at the specified update_rate for the given duration (see examples, below).

subCommands.name: on_complete
subCommands.description: Define a script that executes on completion of a mission event.

subCommands.name: is_complete
subCommands.description: Define a script that determines whether the script event is complete. If false, the event continues to execute; if true, the event is considered complete, and the on_complete script is called. If defined, this script is called immediately after each event update, and it overrides any duration command.

subCommands.name: port
subCommands.description: Defines a port that ship traffic originates and terminates at.

subCommands.name: position
subCommands.description: Defines the location and size of the port. The third argument is used as a diameter so ships entering the port will end up inside of a circle with the given diameter, centered about the specified latitude and longitude.

subCommands.name: port_route
subCommands.description: Defines the route ship traffic uses for entering and exiting the port. This gives the ability to navigate ships around obstacles after leaving the main shipping lane. Specify multiple positions to build up a path entering the port. When ships leave a port they use the reverse of the defined port route.

subCommands.name: local_traffic_region
subCommands.description: The region where local traffic from this port will travel to. The fraction specifies the fraction of traffic from this port that goes to this region.

subCommands.name: departure_interval
subCommands.description: Specifies the ship departure interval from the port.

subCommands.name: use_all_lanes
subCommands.description: Ship traffic departing and terminating at the port will use all available ship lane_s.

subCommands.name: lane
subCommands.description: Specifies a lane ship traffic can use. The weighting factor is used to spread traffic amongst the various lanes.

subCommands.name: ship
subCommands.description: Defines the attributes of a specific ship type.

subCommands.name: fraction
subCommands.description: Controls how much ship traffic will use this ship type.

subCommands.name: mean_speed
subCommands.description: The mean speed the ship traffic will travel at.

subCommands.name: sigma_speed
subCommands.description: The standard deviation for the ship’s speed.

subCommands.name: local_traffic
subCommands.description: Defines the shipping traffic that will leave a port and head to a local_traffic_region. The fractional-quantity is the percentage of ships that leave a port, which are going to a local region. This fraction and the departure_traffic fraction must sum to 1.0.

subCommands.name: mean_loiter_time
subCommands.description: Specifies how long the ship type will loiter in a local_traffic_region.

subCommands.name: sigma_loiter_time
subCommands.description: The standard deviation of the ship’s loiter time.

subCommands.name: loiter_route
subCommands.description: The ship type will use the specified route for its loiter. More than 1 loiter_route can be entered.

subCommands.name: debug
subCommands.description: Enable extra debugging output.

subCommands.name: detached
subCommands.description: For formations defined in the initial conditions, this will cause this formation to not be attached to its parent. After initialization any attached formation will have its members placed into the correct positions relative to the formation leader. The detached status on a formation also effects the way formation commands are propagated down through the hierarchy. See WsfFormationCommand.

subCommands.name: offset
subCommands.description: Specify the offset of the formation from its parent. This is the means by which the initial relative positioning of the members of a formation is specified. The offset is given as a triplet of a range from the reference point, a relative bearing from the direction of travel of the leader, and a vertical offset (or stack). For example, the following offset would be the point 100 m to the right of the reference point and at 1 m higher altitude.

subCommands.name: unit
subCommands.description: Define a unit sub-formation. See Unit Formation.

subCommands.name: lead
subCommands.description: Specify that the following unit sub-formation is to be the lead sub-formation of this section. Sections defined in input files must have one of their sub-formations designated as the lead sub-formation.

response_limits.description: Defines the region in which the sensor can detect signals.

subCommands.name: wavelength
subCommands.description: The response_curve block defines the response of the sensor as a function of wavelength. The sensor model will use this curve to determine the response for the wavenumber bins.

subCommands.name: noise_equivalent_irradiance
subCommands.description: Default None - must be provided.

subCommands.name: detection_threshold
subCommands.description: Default None - either this command or the detection_threshold_above/below_horizon command defined below must be provided.

subCommands.name: installation_adjustment_table
subCommands.description: Specifies the name of a file which contains a table that defines a function whose independent variables are the azimuth and elevation of the target with respect to the sensing platform, and the dependent variable is a factor between 0 and 1 inclusive that used to scale the target irradiance. This is typically used to account for occlusion by structure or variable window transmittance.

subCommands.name: atmosphere
subCommands.description: Default DEFAULT

subCommands.name: resolution
subCommands.description: Default 20 cm-1

subCommands.name: antenna_plot
subCommands.description: Generates files 2D constant azimuth or elevation or 3D polar plot files.

subCommands.name: clutter_table
subCommands.description: Generates a radar clutter table that is used in an WSF simulation.

subCommands.name: flight_path_analysis
subCommands.description: Generates a plot of variables along a flight path.

subCommands.name: horizontal_map
subCommands.description: Generates a plot of variables over a matrix of down-range and cross-range values.

subCommands.name: horizontal_coverage
subCommands.description: Generates a ‘horizontal coverage diagram’ (or ‘horizontal coverage envelope’) plot file.

subCommands.name: spherical_map
subCommands.description: Generates a plot of variables at a specified range over a matrix of viewing angles.

subCommands.name: vertical_map
subCommands.description: Generates a plot of variables over a matrix of altitude and ground_range values.

subCommands.name: vertical_coverage
subCommands.description: Generates a ‘vertical coverage diagram’ (or ‘vertical coverage envelope’) plot file.

subCommands.name: ignore_block
subCommands.description: Causes all data starting with the word <word> up to the word end_<word> to be ignored.

subCommands.name: ignore_line
subCommands.description: Causes the word <word> and all subsequent words on the same line to be ignored.

subCommands.name: ignore_word
subCommands.description: Causes the word <word> to be ignored.

subCommands.name: pattern_name
subCommands.description: Specifies the name of the pattern to be processed. This must be the name of an antenna pattern defined with the antenna_pattern command.

subCommands.name: axes
subCommands.description: Specifies the type of data file to be produced:

subCommands.name: azimuth_range
subCommands.description: Specifies the azimuth limits for axes horizontal or axes both.

subCommands.name: azimuth_step
subCommands.description: Specifies the increment between azimuth samples for axes horizontal or axes both.

subCommands.name: elevation_range
subCommands.description: Specifies the elevation limits for axes vertical or axes both.

subCommands.name: elevation_step
subCommands.description: Specifies the increment between elevation samples for axes vertical or axes both.

subCommands.name: tilt_angle
subCommands.description: Specifies the elevation tilt angle between [-90 90] degrees of the antenna pattern with respect to the normal of the pattern.

subCommands.name: frequency
subCommands.description: Specifies the frequency which the pattern is to be plotted for.

subCommands.name: polarization
subCommands.syntax: polarization [ horizontal | vertical | slant_45 | slant_135 | left_circular | right_circular | default ]
subCommands.description: Specifies the polarization which the pattern is to be plotted for.

subCommands.name: electronic_beam_steering
subCommands.syntax: electronic_beam_steering [ none | azimuth | elevation | both | azimuth_and_elevation ]
subCommands.description: Specifies that the subsystem uses an electronically-steered antenna that is capable of being electronically steered in the specified directions. When specified, the antenna gain is a function of the cosine of the angle relative to the array center. When enabled, the command affects the returned beamwidths of azimuth_beamwidth and elevation_beamwidth.

subCommands.name: electronic_beam_steering_loss_exponent
subCommands.description: Specifies the exponent that will be used in the beam steering loss computation.

subCommands.name: azimuth_steering_angle
subCommands.description: Specifies the azimuth steering angle between [-180 180] degrees of a steered array antenna pattern with respect to the normal of the pattern.

subCommands.name: elevation_steering_angle
subCommands.description: Specifies the elevation steering angle between [-90 90] degrees of a steered array antenna pattern with respect to the normal of the pattern.

subCommands.name: output_file
subCommands.description: Specifies the name to which the output is to be written.

subCommands.name: gnuplot_file
subCommands.description: Specifies the name to which the gnuplot output is to be written.

subCommands.name: header_line_3
subCommands.description: Specifies the text to be contained in the first three lines of the output file when axes both is specified.

subCommands.name: output_column_limit
subCommands.description: Specifies the maximum number of columns per physical line in the output file when axes both is specified.

subCommands.name: sensor_platform_type
subCommands.description: Specify the platform type upon which the sensor is placed.

subCommands.name: target_platform_type
subCommands.description: Specify the platform type to be used to represent the target.

subCommands.name: altitudes
subCommands.description: Specify the set of altitudes for which clutter values are sampled in the table. From minimum to maximum by delta

subCommands.name: ranges
subCommands.description: Specify the set of ranges for which clutter values are sampled in the table. From minimum to maximum by delta

subCommands.name: bearings
subCommands.description: Specify the set of bearings for which clutter values are sampled in the table from minimum to maximum angle values by delta angle.

subCommands.name: output_file_name
subCommands.description: Specify the clutter table file name.

subCommands.name: output_object_name
subCommands.description: Specify the clutter table’s name as it appears in the output file.

subCommands.name: altitude_units
subCommands.description: Specify an alternate altitude unit type that will appear in the table.

subCommands.name: range_units
subCommands.description: Specify an alternate range unit type that will appear in the table.

subCommands.name: sensor_platform_latitude
subCommands.description: Specify the latitude portion of the sensor platform’s location.

subCommands.name: sensor_platform_longitude
subCommands.description: Specify the longitude portion of the sensor platform’s location.

subCommands.name: sensor_platform_altitude
subCommands.description: Specify the altitude portion of the sensor platform’s location.

subCommands.name: sensor_platform_yaw
subCommands.description: Specify the sensor platform’s yaw value.

subCommands.name: sensor_platform_pitch
subCommands.description: Specify the sensor platform’s pitch value.

subCommands.name: sensor_platform_roll
subCommands.description: Specify the sensor platform’s roll value.

subCommands.name: reverse_evaluations
subCommands.description: Normally the flight_path_analysis function creates the output file using the results of detection attempts against the platform defined by target_platform_name performed by all the sensors on the other defined platforms (subject to the exclude and no_exclude commands). If the value of this command is ‘true’, the output file is created using the results of the sensors on target_platform_name against all other platforms in the scenario. This is primarily used for evaluating passive systems (e.g.: ESM, EO, IR)

subCommands.name: sensor_platform_roll
subCommands.description: Specify the orientation of the sensing platform with respect to the direction of flight. The yaw angle is added to the heading and the pitch and roll angles are used directly as specified. This is useful for examining sensor coverage when the platform is flying in some other condition other than straight-and-level. Default 0 degrees for all angles

subCommands.description: If ‘true’, the sensor will be cued to point at the target when performing a detection chance. If ‘false’, the sensor will be remain in its initial condition.

subCommands.description: Specifies the platform that will be used to calculate the required jamming power. This input is to be used when plotting the ‘required_jamming_power’ variable for the location of the jammer system.

subCommands.name: jammer_to_signal_reference

subCommands.name: target_platform_name
subCommands.description: Specify the name of the target platform.

subCommands.description: Define the sample points in standard waypoint format. The points are defined using the following commands

subCommands.name: alarm_fpa_file
subCommands.description: Specify the name of an ALARM flight path analysis file that contains target sample points.

subCommands.name: tspi_file
subCommands.description: Specify the name of a time-space-position-information (TSPI) file that contains the target sample points.

subCommands.name: sample_interval
subCommands.description: The time interval to be used for generating sample points when using a route on the target platform.

subCommands.name: script_variable

subCommands.name: detection_reference

subCommands.description: Specifies the units to be used for column 6 (altitude) in the output file.

subCommands.name: range_units

subCommands.name: y_units

subCommands.name: output_max_height
subCommands.description: If specified, the program will write a message to standard output indicating the maximum height (altitude) at which the target was detected.

subCommands.name: output_max_range

There are cases, however, where it is desirable to exchange the role of the sensor and target (i.e.: the sensor is moved about the target region and the target is fixed at the center). This is typically used when on has a passive sensor that one wants to move around an emitting target.

subCommands.description: Specifies the jammer-to-signal (J/S) reference to be used when plotting the ‘required_jamming_power’ variable.

This is primarily used for certain types of infrared sensor plots where it desired to hold the sensor-to-target viewing angle a constant. In those cases the target_heading will be omitted and the value of this command will be set to the desired sensor-to-target viewing angle.

subCommands.description: Specifies the latitude limits of the target region.

subCommands.name: latitude_step
subCommands.description: Specifies the increment between sample points in the latitude direction.

subCommands.name: longitude_limits
subCommands.description: Specifies the longitude limits of the the target region.

subCommands.name: longitude_step
subCommands.description: Specifies the increment between sample points in the longitude direction.

subCommands.name: sensor_relative_orientation
subCommands.description: If true, when the target is moved, it is oriented with the same NED coordinate system as the sensor’s. This corrects issues with maps rendered with a very large area (~>100 nautical miles on a side), or for maps near the poles (more than ~+-80 degrees latitude). If false, the target is oriented relative to its local NED frame.

subCommands.name: down_range_limits
subCommands.description: Specifies the downrange limits (minimum, maximum) of the target region.

subCommands.name: down_range_step
subCommands.description: Specifies the increment between samples points in the down_range direction.

subCommands.name: cross_range_limits
subCommands.description: Specifies the crossrange limits (minimum, maximum) of the target region.

subCommands.name: cross_range_step
subCommands.description: Specifies the increment between samples points in the cross_range direction.

subCommands.name: line_of_sight_masking

subCommands.description: Specifies the limits of the elevation angles to be sampled.

subCommands.name: elevation_step
subCommands.description: Specifies the elevation step between successive elevation angle samples.

subCommands.name: maximum_range
subCommands.description: Specifies the maximum range at which the algorithm will start the search for the edge of the detection envelope. The value of maximum_range will be determined from the first of the following:

subCommands.name: large_range_step
subCommands.description: Specifies the large step size to use in the envelope edge detection algorithm.

subCommands.name: small_range_step
subCommands.description: Specifies the small step size to use in the envelope edge detection algorithm.

subCommands.name: output_file
subCommands.description: Specifies the filename to which the results will be written. If not specified then the value of output_base will be used to create a file name.

subCommands.name: output_base
subCommands.description: If output_file is not specified then this value, along with the suffix ‘.vcd’, forms the filename to which the results will be written. If a values is not specified then the type name of the sensor will be used.

subCommands.name: altitude_units
subCommands.description: Specifies the units to be used for column 6 (altitude) in the output file.

subCommands.name: range_units
subCommands.description: Specifies the units to be used for column 2 (slant range) and column 5 (ground range) in the output file.

subCommands.name: x_units
subCommands.description: Specifies the units to be used for column 3 (X) in the output file.

subCommands.name: y_units
subCommands.description: Specifies the units to be used for column 4 (Y) in the output file.

subCommands.name: output_max_height
subCommands.description: If specified, the program will write a message to standard output indicating the maximum height (altitude) at which the target was detected.

subCommands.name: output_max_range
subCommands.description: If specified, the program will write a message to standard output indicating the maximum range at which the target was detected.

subCommands.name: mode_name
subCommands.description: Specifies the name of the mode to be used if the sensor is a multi-mode sensor.

subCommands.name: jammer_to_signal_reference
subCommands.description: Specifies the jammer-to-signal (J/S) reference to be used when plotting the ‘required_jamming_power’ variable.

subCommands.name: jamming_platform_name
subCommands.description: Specifies the platform that will be used to calculate the required jamming power. This input is to be used when plotting the ‘required_jamming_power’ variable for the location of the jammer system.

subCommands.name: target_platform_type
subCommands.description: Specify the platform type to be used to represent the target.

subCommands.name: target_mach
subCommands.description: Specify the speed at which the target is to be considered moving. This is only used if the sensor needs to performs Doppler processing. The speed may be specified using either an absolute speed (target_speed) or a Mach number (target_mach). If both are specified the last value takes precedence.

subCommands.name: target_heading
subCommands.description: Specifies the heading at which the target will be placed.

subCommands.name: target_yaw
subCommands.description: Specify the yaw angle with respect to the target heading at which the target will be placed. This is primarily used for certain types of infrared sensor plots where it desired to hold the sensor-to-target viewing angle a constant. In those cases the target_heading will be omitted and the value of this command will be set to the desired sensor-to-target viewing angle.

subCommands.name: target_pitch
subCommands.description: Specify the pitch angle at which the target will be placed.

subCommands.name: target_roll
subCommands.description: Specify the roll angle at which the target will be placed.

subCommands.name: ground_range_limits
subCommands.description: Specifies the ground range limits of the sample mesh.

subCommands.name: ground_range_step
subCommands.description: Specifies the increment between sample points in the ground range direction.

subCommands.name: altitude_limits
subCommands.description: Specifies the altitude limits of the sample mesh.

subCommands.name: altitude_step
subCommands.description: Specifies the increment between sample points in the altitude direction.

subCommands.name: script_variable
subCommands.description: Specify the name of the ‘global’ script variable to use to derive and manipulate a variable from the sensor detection attempt interaction result.

subCommands.name: detection_reference
subCommands.description: The reference signal-to-noise ratio used to determine the required_rcs or rcs_required variable.

subCommands.name: pd_map_file
subCommands.description: Specifies the name of the file to which ‘pd map’ output will be written. The name does not imply that only pd can be written but rather denotes a common file format.

subCommands.name: header_line_3
subCommands.description: Specifies the text to be contained in the first three lines of the output file when pd_map_file is specified.

subCommands.name: output_column_limit
subCommands.description: Specifies the maximum number of columns per physical line in the output file when pd_map_file is specified.

subCommands.name: gnuplot_file
subCommands.description: Specifies the name of the file to which ‘gnuplot’ output will be written.

subCommands.name: gnuplot_player_file
subCommands.description: Specifies the name of the file to which player’s Down range/Cross range or Latitude/Longitude will be written. Will not output target locations.

subCommands.name: file
subCommands.description: Specifies the asi output filename.

subCommands.name: hit_icon
subCommands.description: Sets the icon that will display in SIMDIS on a weapon hit. Setting this value to NULL will disable hit icons.

subCommands.name: kill_icon
subCommands.description: Sets the icon that will display in SIMDIS on a platform kill. Setting this value to NULL will disable kill icons.

subCommands.name: event_duration
subCommands.description: Sets the duration of the hit and kill icons in SIMDIS.

subCommands.name: enable_beams
subCommands.description: Enables or disables track beams in SIMDIS.

subCommands.name: default_beam_color
subCommands.description: This sets the default track beam color in SIMDIS. These values may either be color names, or hexadecimal values (0xAABBGGRR)

subCommands.name: beam_color
subCommands.description: This sets the color of track beams generated by a specific sensor type in SIMDIS. This will override the default_beam_color. The values may either be color names, or hexadecimal values (0xAABBGGRR). Beams with zero alpha will not be drawn (ie. 0x00000000).

subCommands.name: reference_lla
subCommands.description: This sets the camera starting location in SIMDIS.

subCommands.name: define_fhn
subCommands.description: This sets the friendly/hostile/neutral association with the given side. May be input multiple time for each side.

clock_rate.description: Specify the number of simulation seconds for each second of wall clock time for a real-time simulation.

subCommands.name: delta_universal_time
subCommands.description: Specify the difference between universal time (UT1, defined by the earth’s rotation), and Coordinated Universal Time (UTC, defined with a fixed offset to atomic clocks).

subCommands.name: delta_atomic_time
subCommands.description: Specify the fixed offset in integer seconds between atomic time (TAI) and Coordinated Universal Time (UTC). This is equivalent to the cumulative number of leap seconds inserted into the calendar until the start_epoch.

subCommands.name: end_time
subCommands.description: Specify the end time of the simulation.

subCommands.name: enumerate
subCommands.description: This command ‘enumerates’ (or lists) the registered type names of the specified list to the indicated file. <list-name> must be one of platform_types, sensor_types, processor_types, comm_types or dictionary. The format of the resulting file is a header line identifying the list followed by one line for each type where the line contains a unique number that represents the string followed by the actual string, enclosed in single quotes.

subCommands.name: frame_rate
subCommands.description: Specify the frame rate for the frame-stepped simulation executive. Either this command or frame_time can be used to define the length of time allocated for each frame.

subCommands.name: frame_time
subCommands.description: Specify the frame time for the frame-stepped simulation executive. Either this command or frame_rate can be used to define the length of time allocated for each frame.

subCommands.name: minimum_mover_timestep
subCommands.description: This is applicable only for event-stepped simulations. The value specifies the minimum amount of time that must elapse between two successive position updates for a given platform. During the course of a simulation, requests are made to platforms to update their position to the current simulation time. A position update for a given platform will be ignored if the elapsed time since the last position update is less than the value specified by this command.

subCommands.name: on_platform_injection
subCommands.description: Defines a script allowing the user to prevent or delay the injection of a platform. This script is executed prior to adding any platform to the simulation. true should be returned to continue adding the platform normally. false should be returned to prevent the platform from being injected. WsfPlatform.SetCreationTime may be used in this script to delay the creation of the platform.

subCommands.name: platform_availability
subCommands.description: This command is used to specify the availability of platforms when added during simulation initialization (i.e., it does not apply to platforms added after simulation initialization). One can define probabilistic constraints based on platform name or type or can define geographic constraints based on exclusion or inclusion within zones.

subCommands.name: quantitative_track_quality
subCommands.description: Specify whether track quality is to be computed based on quantitative simulation parameters, such as sensor measurement errors and target behavior models. If disabled, only the input track_quality information is used, and for a given sensor’s tracks, it generally does not change during the course of the simulation.

subCommands.name: random_seed
subCommands.description: Specify the random seed for the simulation. This command should typically be used when you want to run a single iteration with a particular random seed. For running multiple runs within a single execution of the program, consider the use of the generate_random_seeds command documented in Monte Carlo Iteration or the random_seeds defined below.

subCommands.name: random_seeds
subCommands.description: Specifies the random seeds for each run of Monte Carlo Iteration collection of runs. This command implicitly defines initial_run_number to be 1 and final_run_number to the number of seeds entered. The values of initial_run_number and final_run_number may be subsequently redefined and will be limited by the number of entries in the list. If an empty list is provided then only a single iteration will be run using the random seed defined by random_seed (or the default random seed if not specified).

subCommands.name: random_seed_time
subCommands.description: Use the clock to set the random seed for this run. This command should typically be used when you want to run a single iteration where the seed is not determined beforehand.

subCommands.name: randomize_radar_frequencies
subCommands.description: Forces the initial frequency to use at simulation startup to be chosen randomly for WSF_RADAR_SENSOR sensor types with alternate_frequency, frequency_channels or frequency_list defined.

subCommands.name: realtime
