subCommands.description: Specify the name of the file into which the intervals that were filtered out of the coverage computation will be written. The format of these files will match the output from raw_data_file produced files.

subCommands.name: device
subCommands.description: Specify that access intervals involving the named device will be filtered according to the given <constraint-type>.

subCommands.name: device_type
subCommands.description: Specify that access intervals involving devices with the given <device-type> will be filtered according to the given <constraint-type>.

grid.description: Specify a coverage grid. See Predefined Coverage Grid Types for a list of available coverage grid types.

subCommands.name: grid_data_file
subCommands.description: Specify the name of an output file that will be created containing details of the points in this grid. The specified file is created at the end of the simulation.

subCommands.name: central_body
subCommands.description: Specify the central body and related ellipsoid model to be used by simulation platforms. Options for <central body type> are the following:

subCommands.name: polar_offset_angles
subCommands.description: Specify the central_body’s polar offset angles ( and , respectively) of the Celestial Intermediate Pole (CIP) with respect to the WCS (ITRS) coordinate system. Providing these values (of the order of tenths of arc-seconds) enables very highly accurate conversions between ECI and WCS coordinates.

subCommands.name: suppress_grid_platforms
subCommands.description: This command allows for the suppression of grid asset platforms in DIS output and in distributed simulations. This suppression only applies for platforms created by a grid. This suppression is enabled by default.

moe.description: Specify a measure of effectiveness for the coverage to compute. See Predefined Measures of Effectiveness for a list of all available coverage types.

subCommands.name: output
subCommands.description: Specify a form of output to produce for a measure of effectiveness. The allowed values for <output_type> are:

subCommands.name: model_list
subCommands.description: Contains a list of models to be used. The models are structured <platform-name> <component-type> for unnamed components and <platform-name> <component-type> <component-name> for named components.

subCommands.name: default_fidelity
subCommands.description: Contains a list of fidelity values to use as defaults on the list of models. If the number of runs exceeds the number of rows on fidelity_table and looping is disabled, the simulation will fall back on these default values.

subCommands.name: fidelity_table
subCommands.description: Contains a MxN table of <real-value> entries, where M is the number of models in model_list and N is the desired number of runs. Each row in this table corresponds to a run, and each column corresponds to the model which will be assigned the column’s entries.

subCommands.name: loop_after_table_end
subCommands.description: Tells the simulation whether to loop through the entries in fidelity_table, or to fall back on the entries in default_fidelity when the number of runs exceeds the number of rows in fidelity_table. If enabled, this allows users to do multiple runs of each row, which may be desired if the users want to also use randomized variables for other aspects of the simulation.

subCommands.name: port
subCommands.description: This is the only command required to set up the weapon server as a host that listens for “RELEASE_STORE” commands, fires, and manages weapon fly-outs. The weapon server will listen for connections on the given port, and a theoretically infinite number of clients can connect and request weapon fires. It is important to note that the weapon server will only be able to handle requests for weapon types that it knows about, so any weapon types referenced in the received RELEASE_STORE commands should already be defined in the WSF input files that mission loads.

subCommands.name: host
subCommands.description: TBD

subCommands.name: outgoing_weapon_server
subCommands.description: If this command is used then mission will act as regular, but will send off “RELEASE_STORE” commands to an external weapon server specified by the given host and port. It will only send off such fire requests for weapon types that are specified with the “outgoing_weapon_type” command. See below.

subCommands.name: outgoing_weapon_type
subCommands.description: This command is only relevant for mission acting as a weapon server client; it instructs mission on which weapon types should be hosted externally by another weapon server.

subCommands.name: rpi_multiplier
subCommands.description: TBD

subCommands.name: tn_to_disid_mapping
subCommands.description: The ‘tn_to_disid_mapping’ block allows an external platform acting as a weapon controller (linker) to be set as a weapon’s commander upon launch. Track numbers for external platforms do not get stored internally. This approach allows the user to map a track number (decimal value) to a DisEntityId of an external platform using the keyword ‘tn_to_disid’.

subCommands.name: tn_to_disid
subCommands.description: The ‘tn_to_disid_mapping’ block allows an external platform acting as a weapon controller (linker) to be set as a weapon’s commander upon launch. Track numbers for external platforms do not get stored internally. This approach allows the user to map a track number (decimal value) to a DisEntityId of an external platform using the keyword ‘tn_to_disid’.

subCommands.name: weapon_lar_mapping
subCommands.description: The ‘enum_to_type’ block allows the external application to map a user defined weapon enumeration (integer) to a WSF weapon system type name. When a request for LAR data is made via a DisSetData PDU data is received, the weapon enumeration field is mapped to a weapon. If the WSF weapon has valid launch computer, data is retrieved and sent back in a DisData PDU.

subCommands.name: enum_to_type
subCommands.description: TBD

subCommands.name: weapon_mapping
subCommands.description: The ‘weapon_name_mapping’ block allows the external application to map a user defined weapon name to WSF weapon system type name, eliminating the need to be aware of AFSIM types or to easily switch weapon types with no affect on the user’s simulation.

subCommands.name: weapon_name_mapping
subCommands.description: The ‘weapon_name_mapping’ block allows the external application to map a user defined weapon name to WSF weapon system type name, eliminating the need to be aware of AFSIM types or to easily switch weapon types with no affect on the user’s simulation.

subCommands.name: release_store
subCommands.description: The only required parameters are at least one entry from each of the first three parameter sets: shooter (e.g., disid), weapon type (wpn_type), target (e.g., target_disid). If the weapon is to have a working J11 interface, then the ctrl_track_num and wpn_tail_number parameters are required, as they specify the J11 track numbers of the two interfacing J11 platforms.

subCommands.name: nameid
subCommands.description: [Required] (one of these parameters are required in the command string). They specify the identity of the shooter: the dis entity id or the WSF platform name. If both are sent, the last to be specified in the command will be used.

subCommands.name: alt
subCommands.description: [Optional] Required (one of these parameters are required in the command string). These parameters specify the identity of the target: the dis entity id, the WSF platform name, or its geodetic location. lat & lon must be given together if at all. It is acceptable to send more than one of these parameters, the weapon server will search for the target in this order: dis id, name, then location.

subCommands.name: wpn_type
subCommands.description: [Required] It specifies the name of the WSF weapon type.

subCommands.name: lch_type
subCommands.description: [Optional] Specifies the domain of the target. 0 = air, 1 = ground. This parameter is not useful or relevant at this time.

subCommands.name: ctrl_track_num
subCommands.description: [Optional] Only required if the weapon is to have a working J11 interface. Specifies the J11 controller (shooter) track number.

subCommands.name: wpn_tail_number
subCommands.description: [Optional] Only required if the weapon is to have a working J11 interface. Specifies the J11 weapon track number.

subCommands.name: usetailnuminpdus
subCommands.description: [Optional] Default is zero. Specifies that the weapon j11 track number should be used (if possible) as the dis entity id as well. Even if this parameter is set to 1, the weapon server will still only give a best effort to accommodate, as other clients could already have weapons with the given dis entity id.

subCommands.name: broadcast
subCommands.description: Specifies a broadcast IP address and port that will be used to communicate with other WSF applications.

subCommands.name: multicast
subCommands.description: Specifies a multicast IP address, interface, and port that will be used to communicate with other WSF applications.

subCommands.name: unicast
subCommands.description: Specifies an address to communicate with other WSF applications. A port specification is required directly after the unicast command.

subCommands.name: port
subCommands.description: Specifies the port used for a connection command. Must be used directly after multicast, broadcast, or unicast command.

subCommands.name: receive_port
subCommands.description: Specifies the send and receive ports used for a connection command. Must be used directly after multicast, broadcast, or unicast command. This is an alternative to the port command, and allows different ports for sending and receiving.

subCommands.name: mover_update_timer
subCommands.description: If greater than 0, the interface will generate events to force platforms to update their position at the specified interval. This is useful for event-driven simulations where position updates may occur infrequently due to the lack of interaction between objects.

subCommands.name: entity_position_threshold
subCommands.description: Specify the entity position threshold used for some interfaces.

subCommands.name: entity_orientation_threshold
subCommands.description: Specify the entity orientation threshold used for some interfaces.

subCommands.name: connect_to_simulations
subCommands.description: Specifies that the WSF application should try to connect to other WSF simulations. By default, most simulation applications, like SAGE, will not connect to each other. This command is not required when connecting only to WSF display applications such as trackview.

subCommands.name: application
subCommands.description: Specifies the application’s name as text. The application name communicated between applications primarily for user identification. This value is optional.

subCommands.name: debug
subCommands.description: Enables or suppresses XIO status information printed to the screen.

subCommands.name: auto_dis_mapping
subCommands.description: Enables or disables automatic mapping of DIS entities. Currently this option will only work for pure WSF exercises, and does not support DIS exercises with non-WSF applications. In this mode, platform types of DIS objects are communicated over XIO. The entity_type command is not required in this case.

subCommands.name: no_auto_map_application
subCommands.description: <site>: Site number to which this command applies. Must either be an integer in the range 1-65534, or an asterisk (*).

subCommands.name: maximum_modelled_sensors
subCommands.description: Specifies the maximum number of external sensor modelling request the application is able to handle simultaneously.

subCommands.name: debug_modelled_sensors
subCommands.description: Specifies that external sensors modeled locally will be put in debug mode.

subCommands.name: falling_behind_threshold
subCommands.description: Specifies how far a simulation must fall behind real time before notifying connected simulations.

subCommands.name: send_aux_data_updates
subCommands.description: Enables or suppresses aux_data updates for local platforms.

subCommands.name: debug
subCommands.description: Enables debug messages during run time when performing zone constraint checking. Especially useful when using the PointIsInside script methods.

subCommands.name: minimum_altitude
subCommands.description: Minimum altitude constraint (mean sea level).

subCommands.name: maximum_altitude
subCommands.description: Maximum altitude constraint (mean sea level).

subCommands.name: position
subCommands.description: Statically defines the origin of a relative zone.

subCommands.name: heading
subCommands.description: Used with position to statically specify the orientation of the zone.

subCommands.name: reference_platform
subCommands.description: Defines the pose of a relative global zone using the pose of the specified platform and moves using the ECS reference frame of the platform. Whenever a zone containment check is performed, the pose of the indicated platform is used as that of the zone.

subCommands.name: references
subCommands.description: A reference to another zone. Zones which specify the references command are Reference Zones. The geometry of the referenced zone is copied and properties may be overridden through the use of other valid geometry commands. .. note:: Commands which are unrelated to the inherited geometry should not be used and if used may result in unexpected behavior.

subCommands.name: negative
subCommands.description: Specifies whether the zone is negative or positive. A negative zone has the exact opposite area as would be defined by the zone commands. For example, if a circular zone is specified, negating it would represent the area outside the circle.

subCommands.name: aux_data
subCommands.description: Defines auxiliary data for a zone. See aux_data.

subCommands.name: fill_color
subCommands.description: Defines the fill color for a zone.

subCommands.name: line_color
subCommands.description: Defines the line color for a zone.

subCommands.name: minimum_radius
subCommands.description: Minimum radius constraint.

subCommands.name: maximum_radius
subCommands.description: Maximum radius constraint.

subCommands.name: start_angle
subCommands.description: Defines the angular constraint. The angular region starts at start_angle and proceeds clockwise to stop_angle. An angle of zero degrees points in the direction of the reference heading (North in WCS, entity heading in ECS).

subCommands.name: lateral_axis
subCommands.description: Lateral axis constraint for an elliptically-shaped zone.

subCommands.name: longitudinal_axis
subCommands.description: Longitudinal axis constraint for an elliptically-shaped zone.

subCommands.name: polygonal
subCommands.description: A polygonal zone is defined by a sequence of node points. The following conditions must be observed:

subCommands.name: point
subCommands.description: A single point in the polygonal-shaped zone, specified using the relative x/y input format. The positive X axis points in the direction of the reference heading and the positive Y axis is 90 degrees clockwise.

subCommands.name: polar
subCommands.description: Indicates the point data are provided using bearing-range format (by default the data are assumed to be in relative x/y format).

subCommands.name: lat_lon
subCommands.description: Indicates the point data are provided using latitude, longitude format (by default the data are assumed to be in relative x,y format). Zones which specify lat_lon are absolute.

subCommands.name: mgrs
subCommands.description: Indicates the point data are provided in the form of an MGRS location format (by default the data are assumed to be in relative x,y format). Zones which specify mgrs are absolute.

subCommands.name: modifier
subCommands.description: Specify attenuation to be applied to comm and sensor device detections. Computed attenuation is proportional to the penetration distance through the zone along detection lines of sight. <category-name> is the name used as a corresponding modifier_category (comm modifier_category and sensor modifier_category). <real-value> is a number between 0.0 and 1.0, representing the attenuation value as a percentage loss per meter within the zone. For example, a modifier value of 0.1 means that 10 meters of penetration will cause 100% attenuation.

subCommands.name: zone
subCommands.description: Create an embedded zone that will act as an inclusion zone for this zone_set.

subCommands.name: exclude_zone
subCommands.description: Create an embedded zone that will act as an exclusion zone for this zone_set.

subCommands.name: use_zone
subCommands.description: Declare that the specified shared zone is to be an inclusion zone for this zone set.

subCommands.name: use_exclude_zone
subCommands.description: Declare that the specified shared zone is to be an exclusion zone for this zone set.

subCommands.name: fill_color
subCommands.description: Defines the fill color for a zone.

subCommands.name: line_color
subCommands.description: Defines the line color for a zone.

subCommands.name: attenuation_parameters
subCommands.description: Defines the variables necessary to define attenuation to the given zone_set. Zone-based attenuation provides a mechanism to attenuate an RF or optical signal from a communications or sensor device without resorting to complex propagation algorithms. In order to use this capability, the user must first create comm and sensor definitions which include the modifier_category command. Then the user must create one or more zone_sets which define the attenuation to be applied for signals that pass through the zone.

subCommands.name: file
subCommands.description: Declare shape file (.shp) to be imported to represent this zone_set. <file-name> is the name of the ESRI shapefile. Leave the extension off.

subCommands.name: use_dted
subCommands.description: If included, the vertical offsets defined in the currently loaded DTED file will be used.

subCommands.name: height_parameter
subCommands.description: A parameter in the .dbf file used to define the height of the individual shapes. “” is acceptable input.

subCommands.name: constant_height
subCommands.description: A constant height to use for all shapes. height_parameter overrides this value.

subCommands.name: base_altitude_parameter
subCommands.description: A parameter in the .dbf file used to define the base altitude of the individual shapes. “” is acceptable input.

subCommands.name: constant_base_altitude
subCommands.description: A constant base altitude to use for all shapes. base_altitude_parameter overrides this value.

subCommands.name: projection
subCommands.description: Define the projection type to be used. Currently geocentric and geodetic are acceptable.

subCommands.name: sensor_modifier
subCommands.description: Declare that this zone_set modifies all sensors with modifier_category <modifier-name> with the attenuation value defined in <modifier-value>

subCommands.name: comm_modifier
subCommands.description: Declare that this zone_set modifies all comm devices with comm <modifier-name> with the attenuation value defined in <modifier-value>

configItems.name: subtype
configItems.description: Specify the computation subtype.

configItems.name: output
configItems.description: Specify a form of output to produce for a measure of effectiveness. The allowed values for <output_type> are:

configItems.name: detection_threshold
configItems.description: Defines the acoustic detection threshold relative to human hearing threshold.

configItems.name: acoustic_type
configItems.description: Defines the type of acoustic sensor.

configItems.name: background_noise
configItems.syntax: background_noise [ jungle_day | jungle_night | industrial | rural | residential ]
configItems.description: Defines the type of acoustic background.

configItems.name: debug
configItems.description: Set debug mode for this effect.

configItems.name: agility_type
configItems.description: Input block to provide the agility-type of this effect and associated input commands for this agility-type. The specified agility-type is applied when a comm system or radar sensor perceives jamming. For this effect to properly function a radar sensor’s jamming_perception_threshold and jamming_perception_timeout or a comm’s jamming_perception_threshold and jamming_perception_timeout should be properly defined.

configItems.name: update_interval
configItems.description: If non-zero, specifies a periodic time interval at which the simulation will call the mover. If zero then the mover will be called only when it is necessary to determine the position of the containing platform.

configItems.name: update_time_tolerance
configItems.description: When a position update is requested by the simulation, if the time since the previous update is less than or equal to this value then the mover will ignore the update.

configItems.name: altitude_offset
configItems.description: When set, this offset will offset the parent platform’s location by the given amount from the current waypoint’s altitude.

configItems.name: at_end_of_path
configItems.description: Specify the action to take when the mover reaches the end of its defined path.

configItems.name: draw_route
configItems.description: This command is the same as print_route, except the route text is not printed, only drawn with WsfDraw.

configItems.name: on_turn_failure
configItems.description: Defines the behavior of the mover when a point on a route cannot be reached exactly due to the turn radius.

configItems.name: pathfinder
configItems.description: The name of the pathfinder object to use.

configItems.name: print_route
configItems.description: When enabled, the route is printed to the screen whenever it is modified. Additionally, WsfDraw is used to output a visual of the route, which can be viewed with many visualization tools.

configItems.name: start_at
configItems.description: The label identifying the waypoint in the route to use as the starting location.

configItems.name: start_time
configItems.description: Indicates the platform is to start moving at the time specified. The current velocity is set to zero and once the simulation time is reached, the platform starts moving at the speed specified in the first waypoint. If an elapse time is desired at a waypoint, use the subcommand pause_time.

configItems.name: switch_on_approach
configItems.description: Switches to the next waypoint when approaching within one turn radius of the current target waypoint.

configItems.name: switch_on_passing
configItems.description: Switches to the next waypoint only when abreast of the current target waypoint.

configItems.name: turn_failure_threshold
configItems.description: Defines the threshold for which the on_turn_failure behavior is triggered, given as a ratio of the turn radius. For example, a turn_failure_threshold of 0.01 and a turn radius of 1000 meters, on_turn_failure logic would be triggered if the point is missed by more than 10 meters.

configItems.name: use_route
configItems.description: Supplies the name of the route to follow. The route is assumed to be a predefined absolute route.

configItems.name: angle_of_attack_table
configItems.description: speed <speed-value> angle <angle-value> speed <speed-value> angle <angle-value>

configItems.name: altitude
configItems.description: Specifies the altitude that the subsequent data is valid for. The altitude blocks must be in increasing numerical order. Linear interpolation of the altitude blocks is used.

configItems.name: speed
configItems.description: Specifies the speed that the listed angle of attack is valid for. The speed entries must be in increasing numerical order. The angle of attack will be computed using a linear interpolation of the speed data.

configItems.name: angle
configItems.description: The angle of attack. The angle of attack entries must be in increasing numerical order.

configItems.name: bank_angle_limit
configItems.description: The roll angle limit. Value must be between 0 degrees to 85 degrees. Used to calculate the maximum radial acceleration.

configItems.name: body_g_limit
configItems.description: The body g-limit. Value must be greater than the acceleration of earth’s gravity.

configItems.name: heading_pursuit_gain
configItems.description: The heading pursuit gain.

configItems.name: maximum_climb_rate
configItems.description: Specifies the maximum climb rate and dive rate used when changing altitude. Other climb rates specified by waypoints or scripts are bounded by this value.

configItems.name: maximum_flight_path_angle
configItems.description: Specifies maximum flight path angle (angle of climb/dive). Value must be greater than or equal to 0.

configItems.name: maximum_linear_acceleration
configItems.description: Specifies the maximum linear acceleration to use when acceleration is necessary. This value is used if the waypoint does not include a linear _acceleration specification.

configItems.name: maximum_radial_acceleration
configItems.description: Specifies the maximum radial acceleration to use when turning. This value is used if the waypoint does not include a radial_acceleration specification.

configItems.name: maximum_altitude
configItems.description: Maximum altitude constraint.

configItems.name: minimum_altitude
configItems.description: Minimum altitude constraint.

configItems.name: maximum_speed
configItems.description: Maximum speed constraint. Value must be greater than 0.

configItems.name: minimum_speed
configItems.description: Minimum speed constraint. Value must be greater than or equal to 0.

configItems.name: path_variance_radius
configItems.description: This value will randomly vary the location of the waypoint within the radius given. A random bearing and distance are chosen and applied to the next waypoint when calculating the path.

configItems.name: roll_rate_limit
configItems.description: The roll rate limit. Value must be greater than 0. Note: When applied to a WSF_AIR_MOVER or other waypoint mover types, the roll rate will not affect the platform’s movement along a route. To affect route following behavior use maximum_radial_acceleration.

configItems.name: speed_variance_percent
configItems.description: This value will randomly vary the speed at each waypoint as the mover travels within +/- the pct given. Value must be greater than 0.

configItems.name: turn_rate_limit
configItems.description: The turn rate limit. Value must be greater than 0.

configItems.name: no_pitch
configItems.description: Restricts the mover from pitching the platform. This has no effect on kinematics.

configItems.name: on_road
configItems.description: Restricts the mover from rolling the platform. This has no effect on kinematics.

configItems.name: off_road
configItems.description: Turns off the ‘on_road’ option. This allows the platform to roll.

configItems.name: path_compute_timestep
configItems.description: Waypoint movers precompute movement along paths. This behavior forces turns to have a constant radius. If path_compute_timestep is specified as a positive value, the turn rate will update on that interval if any changes in speed occur.

configItems.name: maximum_impact_speed
configItems.description: Specify the maximum speed above which the associated platform intersects terrain and is considered ‘crashed into the ground’. A crashed platform will notify observers via the WsfSimulationObserver::CrashedIntoGround() method and remove itself from the simulation. If impact speed is below this maximum, the platform is considered to be ‘landing’. The default behavior is to always land, rather than crash.

configItems.name: load_table
configItems.description: Specifies a separate file to include. This included file must contain the launch_computer_table block.

configItems.name: launch_computer_table
configItems.description: Specifies the data table for expected results for weapon engagements. This block may be included in-line in the launch computer block, and need not be in a separate file as in load_table above. All of the subcommand inputs listed below are to be embedded within this block.

configItems.name: no_escape_manuever
configItems.description: The acceleration used to define the target “turn tail to missile” evade tactic capability. Begins at missile launch.

configItems.name: independent_variables
configItems.description: This block contains the data that defines the valid ranges of each of the independent variables for the engagement. Each IV must be given in increasing values. If there are N shooter altitudes, M shooter Machs, P target altitudes, Q target Machs, R target aspect angles, and S target lead angles, then the intercept_results block must have NxMxPxQxRxS x 6 data values in it.

configItems.name: shooter_altitudes
configItems.description: Specifies the shooter altitudes. May be uneven but must be in increasing numerical order. (Minimum delta = 100.0 m)

configItems.name: shooter_machs
configItems.description: Specifies the shooter Mach numbers. May be uneven but must be in increasing numerical order. (Minimum delta = 0.05)

configItems.name: target_altitudes
configItems.description: Specifies the target altitudes. May be uneven but must be in increasing numerical order. (Minimum delta = 100.0 m)

configItems.name: target_machs
configItems.description: Specifies the target Mach numbers. May be uneven but must be in increasing numerical order. (Minimum delta = 0.05)

configItems.name: target_aspect_angles
configItems.description: Specifies the target aspect angles (nose on = 0 deg). May be uneven but must be in increasing numerical order. (Minimum delta = 2.0 deg)

configItems.name: target_lead_angles
configItems.description: Specifies the target lead angles. May be uneven but must be in increasing numerical order. (Minimum delta = 2.0 deg)

configItems.name: target_lead_angle_limits
configItems.description: Specifies the target lead angles using a shorten notation. This is an alternate to the previous target_lead_angles command. (Minimum delta = 2.0 deg)

configItems.name: intercept_results
configItems.description: This block contains all the data points that define the intercept envelope. There must be as many entries/lines as there are engagement conditions (see independent_variables). Any value of -1.0 indicates not-achievable. It is recommended that this data be generated using the LAR generator tool called weapon_tools.

configItems.name: Rmin
configItems.description: Minimum range and time-of-flight for this condition, below which intercept is unsuccessful.

configItems.name: Rne
configItems.description: No-escape range and time-of-flight for this condition.

configItems.name: Rmax
configItems.description: Maximum range and time-of-flight for this condition, beyond which intercept is unsuccessful.

configItems.name: alpha
configItems.description: Defines the filter’s alpha (position) parameter.

configItems.name: beta
configItems.description: Defines the filter’s beta (velocity) parameter.

configItems.name: debug
configItems.description: Writes debugging information to the standard output.

configItems.name: alpha
configItems.description: Defines the filter’s alpha (position) parameter.

configItems.name: beta
configItems.description: Defines the filter’s beta (velocity) parameter.

configItems.name: gamma
configItems.description: Defines the filter’s gamma (acceleration) parameter.

configItems.name: debug
configItems.description: Writes debugging information to the standard output.

configItems.name: library_name
configItems.description: Specifies the ARGO library for the missile. Do not include the file extension (.so or .dll). These libraries sit in the library directory in the build.

configItems.name: missile_name
configItems.description: Specifies name of missile. Necessary but doesn’t actually affect flyout so can be named anything.

configItems.name: missile_type
configItems.description: Specifies the ARGO missile model type to use. Currently standard will cover most Brawler missile models.

configItems.name: argo_log_file_path
configItems.description: Specifies the log file path in which to log the ARGO output too for debug purposes. Automatically turns on logging when specified.

configItems.name: guidance_update_interval
configItems.description: Specifies the update rate of guidance track data. Affects truth and track data rate. This rate is also dependent on sensor frame rate, if sensor frame rate polls at slower interval, the missile will not update at rate specified by this command.

configItems.name: guidance_method
configItems.description: Specifies whether to use truth or track data while the missile is being guided by the shooter. An uplink is not necessary for truth.

configItems.name: seeker_method
configItems.description: Specifies once seeker turns on whether it guides on truth or track. Seeker will turn on from argo output or if seeker is defined on missile, script user has control over when seeker turns on. Once the sensor turns on in script, the model will recognize it as on and no longer abide by the guidance update interval.

configItems.name: output_fuze_data
configItems.description: If included as command, will output fuze state for all missiles launched. If engagement of missile is ended through other means than the argo mover, no output will be displayed.

configItems.name: endgame_gees
configItems.description: Specifies minimum number of g’s at endgame is required for the missile to fuze.

configItems.name: filter_dead_tracks
configItems.description: If true, makes a truth call to see if the target is alive before considering for inclusion in the threat array.

configItems.name: max_track_grouping_distance
configItems.description: Sets the grouping distance for track strength deterinations. Note that tracks are not merged if grouped, simply incremented in strength count.

configItems.name: max_assignments
configItems.description: This command sets the maximum number of active assignments for the asset.

configItems.name: assignment_delay
configItems.description: This command sets the assignment delay for the Asset Manager.

configItems.name: decision_update_delay
configItems.description: This command sets the routing for assignments.

configItems.name: log_status
configItems.description: This command sets status logging on or off for the Asset Manager.

configItems.name: subord_yellow_timeout
configItems.description: Specifies how long to wait without a status report before setting subordinate status to YELLOW (unavailable).

configItems.name: subord_red_timeout
configItems.description: Specifies how long to wait without a status report before setting subordinate status to RED (unavailable).

configItems.name: report_position_every
configItems.description: Specifies how often position messages should be transmitted if the platform is moving.

configItems.name: or_every
configItems.description: Specifies how often position messages should be transmitted.

configItems.name: report_status_every
configItems.description: Specifies how often status messages should be transmitted.

configItems.name: aggregate_unit_status
configItems.description: Include GREEN status subordinates when determining if requirements for status GREEN are met.

configItems.name: stationary_opns_only
configItems.description: Require the asset be stationary for status GREEN.

configItems.name: weapon_required
configItems.description: Require a weapon with ammunition for status GREEN.

configItems.name: require_all_weapons
configItems.description: Require all weapons on the platform to have ammunition for status GREEN.

configItems.name: ew_required
configItems.description: An EW radar is required for status GREEN.

configItems.name: tar_required
configItems.description: A TAR radar is required for status GREEN.

configItems.name: ttr_required
configItems.description: A TTR radar is required for status GREEN.

configItems.name: intercept_results
configItems.description: This block contains the data that defines the intercept envelope. It is recommended that this data be generated using the LAR generator weapon tool.

configItems.name: number_of_aspect_angle_bins
configItems.description: Specifies the number of azimuth angle bins in the intercept envelope. The azimuthal coverage will be from 0 to 180 degrees. Azimuthal symmetry is assumed.

configItems.name: azimuth_bin_count_end_limit
configItems.description: Similar to number_of_aspect_angle_bins but limits the azimuthal coverage to the specified value.

configItems.name: elevation_bin_count_min_and_max_limits
configItems.description: Specifies the number of elevation angle bins in the intercept envelope between the specified minimum and maximum angles.

configItems.name: range_rate_bin_count_min_and_max_limits
configItems.description: Specifies the number of range rate (i.e., closing velocity) bins in the intercept envelope between the specified minimum and maximum rates.

configItems.name: firing_range_bin_count_and_values
configItems.description: Specifies the number of launch range bins and the corresponding range in the intercept envelope.

configItems.name: time_of_flight_values
configItems.description: The intercept envelope (a series of time-of-flight values) for the above specified (m X n X p X q X r) rectangular matrix of engagement parameters. Any time-of-flight given as 0.0 indicates no intercept is possible under these conditions.

configItems.name: aspect_angle_bin_count
configItems.description: Specifies how many azimuth bins that will be used to generate the intercept envelope.

configItems.name: azimuth_limit
configItems.description: Specifies the maximum azimuth angle that will be used to generate the intercept envelope.

configItems.name: elevation_bin_count
configItems.description: Specifies the number of elevation bins that will be used to generate the intercept envelope.

configItems.name: elevation_lower_limit
configItems.description: Specifies the minimum elevation angle that will be used to generate the intercept envelope.

configItems.name: elevation_upper_limit
configItems.description: Specifies the maximum elevation angle that will be used to generate the intercept envelope.

configItems.name: range_rate_bin_count
configItems.description: Specifies the number of range rate bins that will be used to generate the intercept envelope.

configItems.name: range_rate_lower_limit
configItems.description: Specifies the minimum range rate that will be used to generate the intercept envelope.

configItems.name: range_rate_upper_limit
configItems.description: Specifies the maximum range rate that will be used to generate the intercept envelope.

configItems.name: range_bin_count
configItems.description: Specifies the number of range bins that will be used to generate the intercept envelope.

configItems.name: minimum_ground_range
configItems.description: Specifies the minimum range that will be used to generate the intercept envelope.

configItems.name: maximum_ground_range
configItems.description: Specifies the maximum range that will be used to generate the intercept envelope.

configItems.name: debug_lars
configItems.description: Enables debug output during run time for all LARs defined in the launch computer.

configItems.name: launch_acceptable_region
configItems.description: Enables debug output during run time for a single LAR.

configItems.name: debug
configItems.description: Enables debug output during run time for a single LAR.

configItems.name: delta_altitude
configItems.description: Difference in altitude between the launch platform and target platform. A positive value indicates the launch platform is above the target (as expected for an air-to-ground engagement).

configItems.name: launch_speed
configItems.description: Speed of the launch platform.

configItems.name: sensitivity_range_per_10m_altitude
configItems.description: Additional forward offset applied to the LAR (in meters) to compensate for an altitude that is 10 meters higher than the nominal value, specified by delta_altitude.

configItems.name: sensitivity_range_per_10ms_velocity
configItems.description: Additional forward offset applied to the LAR (in meters) to compensate for a launch velocity that is 10 meters/sec higher than the nominal value, specified by launch_speed.

configItems.name: sensitivity_range_per_percent_gradient
configItems.description: Additional forward offset applied to the LAR (in meters) to compensate for a flight path angle gradient above the horizontal.

configItems.name: use_zone
configItems.description: Specifies the zone that defines the LAR.

configItems.name: launch_altitudes
configItems.description: Specifies the minimum launch altitude, the altitude increment and number of altitudes that constitute the intercept envelope. Altitudes are assumed to be the height of the launcher above an ellipsoidal earth.

configItems.name: launch_speeds
configItems.description: Specifies the minimum launch speed, the speed increment and number of launch speeds that constitute the intercept envelope.

configItems.name: target_altitudes
configItems.description: Specifies the minimum target altitude, the altitude increment and number of altitudes that constitute the intercept envelope. Altitudes are assumed to be the height of the target above an ellipsoidal earth.

configItems.name: times_of_flight_values
configItems.description: The time-of-flight value for the weapon, when released at the specified launch altitude, target altitude and launch speed. The number of value given must equal the number of launch altitudes X number of target altitudes X number of launch speeds, and the latter indices cycle faster than the former (typical “matrix” order).

configItems.name: downrange_values
configItems.description: The down range distance from launch location to impact location, when the weapon is released at the specified launch altitude, target altitude and launch speed. The number of values provided must equal the number of launch altitudes X number of target altitudes X number of launch speeds, and the latter indices cycle faster than the former (typical “matrix” order).

configItems.name: surface_to_surface_table
configItems.description: Specify the file name to use when computing a launch solution associated with this missile. The launch computer assumes that the missile is computing a ground intercept.

configItems.name: surface_to_air_table
configItems.description: Specify the file name to use when computing a launch solution associated with this missile. The launch computer assumes that the missile is computing an air intercept.

configItems.name: maximum_launch_slant_range
configItems.description: Specify the maximum slant range to the target that is defined to be acceptable for launch. This is typically used to enforce the need for the target to be within range of a tracking sensor (assumed to be colocated with the launcher) at the time of launch.

configItems.name: maximum_intercept_slant_range
configItems.description: Specify the maximum allowable slant range to the intercept point. This is typically used to enforce the need for the target to be within the range of a tracking sensor (that is is colocated with the launcher) at the time of intercept.

configItems.name: minimum_intercept_altitude
configItems.description: Specify the minimum altitude at which a surface-to-air intercept is defined to be acceptable.

configItems.name: maximum_intercept_altitude
configItems.description: Specify the maximum altitude at which a surface-to-air intercept is defined to be acceptable.

configItems.name: maximum_intercept_angle
configItems.description: Specify the maximum intercept angle for which a surface-to-air intercept is defined to be acceptable. A value of 0 degrees represents a head-on impact while a value of 180 degrees is an impact from the rear.

configItems.name: minimum_intercept_velocity
configItems.description: Specify the minimum relative intercept velocity for which a surface-to-air intercept is defined to be acceptable.

configItems.name: integration_timestep
configItems.description: For surface-to-air launch solutions, specify the integration step for which the ballistic target representation is propagated forward in time. The smaller the time interval, the more accurate the forward ballistic representation, and the more accurate the launch solution will be. Typically this value should be of the same order as the time steps of entries in the launch computer’s table. For example if the time steps in the table are spaced 0.1 sec apart, a good value would also be 0.1 sec.

configItems.name: ground_range_sample_interval
configItems.description: Specify the sample interval for creating the internal surface-to-air intercept table.

configItems.name: allow_boost_phase_intercept
configItems.description: Specify if intercepts are allowed during boost phase. By default intercept calculations are not performed while the target is still in ‘boost phase’ because trajectory prediction is very inaccurate. Setting this to ‘true’ allows intercepts to be attempted.

configItems.name: compute_end_point
configItems.description: Specify if the launch computer should compute the weapon ‘end point and time’ for surface-to-air intercept calculations. The ‘end point and time’ is an estimate of where the weapon (interceptor) would hit the Earth’s surface if it followed a ballistic trajectory and did not hit its intended target. The results can be extracted using the methods described in WsfLaunchComputer.

configItems.name: predicted_trajectory_error_limit
configItems.description: Specify the maximum allowable error between the predicted target trajectory and the actual target trajectory before forcing a recalculation of the predicted target trajectory.

configItems.name: show_graphics
configItems.description: For surface-to-air engagements, show graphics for maximum kinematic envelope, projected ballistic trajectory, intercept calculation, and intercept points (these graphical displays are drawn in many visualization tools). The kinematic envelope shows the maximum extent to which intercepts can occur from the parent platform’s launcher, displayed in cyan. Projected ballistic trajectory is drawn in green when an initial intercept time is calculated, and a green point is plotted at the first possible intercept point. Otherwise, for detailed intercept solutions, the trajectories are plotted in red, with red points indicating test points at which the launch computer attempts to calculate a solution (these may not be valid, however). Valid intercept points are plotted along these red trajectories in purple.

configItems.name: show_results
configItems.description: Show the results of a surface-to-air or surface-to-surface intercept calculation. If successful, the intercept point and loft angle / burn time will be displayed on the standard output and will be transmitted/saved in the DIS stream as a comment.

configItems.name: debug
configItems.description: In addition to show_results, display detailed information associated with the determination of the launch solution.

configItems.name: aero
configItems.description: Specify the name of the aero type to be used for computing drag data.

configItems.name: mass
configItems.description: Specify the expended mass to be associated with this target type.

configItems.name: commit_authority
configItems.description: This command sets commit authority on or off. If the associated asset manager is not set to filter_dead_tracks, stale or invalid tracks may be assigned to a weapon. Additionally, unusually high or low purge intervals on track processors can cause unusual assignment behavior.

configItems.name: project_tracks_by_delays
configItems.description: This command sets track projection by assignment delays on or off for assignment creation.

configItems.name: project_targets_forward
configItems.description: This command allows configurable forward projection times of targets for weapon assessment purposes. Note that HELIOS defaults these depending on the model, but they can be overridden by this scripting setting.

configItems.name: by
configItems.description: This command allows configuration of the forward projection time increment for weapon assessment purposes.

configItems.name: unknowns
configItems.description: Default: False

configItems.name: neutrals
configItems.description: Default: False

configItems.name: friendlies
configItems.description: Default: False

configItems.name: hostiles
configItems.description: Default: False

configItems.name: angular_resolution
configItems.description: Specify the angular resolution of the sensor.

configItems.name: perfect_correlation
configItems.description: Specify whether the sensor will perfectly correlate when tracking from an initial cue.

configItems.name: type
configItems.description: Determines the type of mode. Using the type input simplifies the task of modeling the beam director as a set of finer and finer tracking modes. One typically specifies a scanning mode, one or more locked modes, and finally, a cued mode. Once the cued mode is entered, a message is sent to the associated WSF_CUED_LASER_WEAPON, and HEL lasing commences.

configItems.name: min_pixels_for_cue
configItems.description: Specify the minimum number of pixels required to initiate a successful transition to a cued mode.

configItems.name: aero_file
configItems.description: Defines the absolute path for the brawler aero file that will determine the fuel flow rate. Fuel flow rate is calculated based on the platform’s defined performance at different mach and altitude values.

configItems.name: initial_quantity_ratio
configItems.description: Specifies the initial quantity of fuel as a ratio of the maximum fuel capacity defined in the aero_file configuration.

configItems.name: aero_file
configItems.description: Specify the file name of a BRAWLER aircraft definition file. The contents of the file will fully define the flight capabilities of this mover.

configItems.name: draw_projection
configItems.description: If specified, yellow dots will be rendered to the DIS replay file that represent the forward projection of the BRAWLER mover given its current maneuver command.

configItems.name: mind_file
configItems.description: Specify a BRAWLER mind file for modeling mind and consciousness event updating. The MIND files in the BRAWLER unclassified release are 100% compatible.

configItems.name: mover
configItems.description: Defines the BRAWLER mover to be used by the BRAWLER platform.

configItems.name: debug
configItems.description: If specified, debug information for every alternative evaluation will be printed to the standard output.

configItems.name: draw_alternatives
configItems.description: If specified, color coded dots of every forward-projected alternative will be rendered to the DIS replay file. Green means the alternative evaluated close to the maximum value seen so far, red means the opposite, yellow/orange is in between.

configItems.name: draw_nominal_states
configItems.description: If specified, color coded dots of my target’s forward-projected nominal state will be rendered to the DIS replay file. Blue dots are mine and purple dots are my target. BRAWLER nominal states projection is simply a physics based forward projection where acceleration is ignored and velocity in locked constant for the projection. The nominal states are often used in the evaluation functions.

configItems.name: time_allowed_per_sector_search
configItems.description: Supposed to represent that time allowed to search a sector of the sky. Affects consciousness event timing.

configItems.name: consciousness_event_update_time
configItems.description: Override BRAWLER consciousness event timing. If specified, all consciousness events will occur at this interval. Otherwise a dynamic timing calculation will regularly occur to determine proper consciousness event update times.

configItems.name: d_zero
configItems.description: The value of in the range [0 .. 1].

configItems.name: lethal_area
configItems.description: Specify the lethal area (LA) for a target of the specified type. This command should be repeated for all target types to which this lethality object will be applicable.

configItems.name: bloom_diameter
configItems.description: Specifies the diameter to which the parcel blooms asymptotically, as time goes to infinity.

configItems.name: bloom_time_constant
configItems.description: Specifies the expansion time constant () in the bloom equation above. The smaller the value, the faster the parcel approaches its bloom_diameter.

configItems.name: terminal_velocity
configItems.description: Free fall velocity of the parcel. Parcels are assumed to reach terminal velocity instantaneously upon ejection.

configItems.name: deceleration_rate
configItems.description: The rate at which the parcel decelerates upon ejection. This should specify a positive value, giving the magnitude of the acceleration vector that is aligned opposite the initial velocity vector.

configItems.name: expiration_time
configItems.description: The time at which the parcel will be removed from the simulation, after ejection, unless it hits the ground first.

configItems.name: debug
configItems.description: If true, will print debugging information about parcel status to the console.

configItems.name: frequency_maximum_rcs_table
configItems.description: Defines the maximum RCS response of the parcel as a function of frequency. This table is used to look up the value of in the parcel RCS equation above. Format expected:

configItems.name: number_dipoles
configItems.description: If the frequency_maximum_rcs_table is not defined, can be computed as a function of the number of chaff dipoles and the radar wavelength, assuming randomly oriented half-wave dipoles, according to the equation above.

configItems.name: cloud_update_interval
configItems.description: If non-zero, specifies a periodic time interval at which the simulation will update the state (position, velocity, size, etc.) of dispensed chaff parcels. If zero, parcels will only be updated when necessary to determine their state. See update_interval for movers.

configItems.name: draw_cloud_approximations
configItems.description: If true, will use WsfDraw to draw an ellipsoid representing cloud approximations for debugging purposes. Can be used to visualize the presented area of the cloud used in RCS calculations.

configItems.name: launched_platform_type
configItems.description: Although required in WSF_EXPLICIT_WEAPON this command is optional for WSF_CHAFF_WEAPON. Can be specified to add user-defined scripts to dispensed parcels, or other custom platform commands. However, it is an error to define a mover or radar_signature on this platform type, since these components are modeled internally to the simulation.

configItems.name: quantity
configItems.description: Specifies the number of parcels that are initially available in the ejector.

configItems.name: parcel_type
configItems.description: Specifies the type of chaff parcel that this ejector dispenses. The specified value must represent a valid parcel type that must be defined when this ejector is initialized in the simulation.

configItems.name: location
configItems.description: Specifies the location of the ejector in the entity coordinate system of the dispensing platform.

configItems.name: ejection_azimuth
configItems.description: Specifies the magnitude, azimuth, and elevation of the vector in the entity coordinate system that represents the additional velocity, relative to the dispensing platform, provided by the launching mechanism. Similar to launch_delta_v except specified in spherical rather than cartesian coordinates.

configItems.name: sensors
configItems.description: Specifies the name of the sensor, <sensor-name>, on the same platform as the processor.

configItems.name: sensor
configItems.description: Specifies the name of the sensor, <sensor-name>, on the same platform as the processor.

configItems.name: platform_sensor
configItems.description: Specifies the name of the sensor, <sensor-name>, on an external platform with name <platform-name>.

configItems.name: detection_threshold
configItems.description: An alternative method of defining the receiver’s detection threshold. The value can be entered here for readability of the input file.

configItems.name: use_target_result
configItems.description: Specifies if ‘true’ that the target result from each sensor should be used. If ‘false’ use each of the sensor results, a culmination of each mode and beam dependent upon sensor capabilities.

configItems.name: coast_time
configItems.description: Specifies the maximum amount of time that may elapse between updates before a track is dropped.

configItems.name: result_processing_type
configItems.description: Specifies the results processing type to be used to calculate the resulting Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) from the non-local sensor or target results to the local result to be used in track formation.

configItems.name: fusion_method
configItems.syntax: fusion_method [ replacement | weighted_average | MTT(Multi-Target Tracker) mtt ]
configItems.description: Specifies the fusion algorithms used by the results processing.

configItems.name: message_length
configItems.description: Specify the logical length assigned to the track messages that are created from the image.

configItems.name: message_priority
configItems.description: Specify the priority assigned to the track messages that are created from the image.

configItems.name: bit_error_rate
configItems.description: Specifies the Bit Error Rate (BER) to apply. Can be used for inducing or mitigating. Automatically sets the message_behavior to distort.

configItems.name: message_behavior
configItems.description: Input block to provide the behavior type this communication effect exhibits.

configItems.name: propagation_speed
configItems.description: Sets the speed of message propagation.

configItems.name: transfer_rate
configItems.description: Sets the amount of data that can be transmitted by this medium over a set period of time.

configItems.name: packet_loss_time
configItems.description: Sets a time that adds to the delay in every transmission over this medium. Although indicated as a delay due to packet loss, this value can be used to introduce a delay to the normal transmission time over the medium for any reason, or as an aggregate delay due to modeling multiple sources of transmission delay.

configItems.name: snr_transfer_rate_table
configItems.description: Specifies a table that maps signal-to-noise-ratio values to message transfer rates. The SNR-Transfer-Rate table will be interpolated. If a table is specified, the table transfer rate values will override the value specified with the transfer_rate command.

configItems.name: bit_error_probability
configItems.description: Optional parameter that defines the system designed bit error rate probability. It is used to pick the Eb/No values from the Eb/No vs. BER table. Must be greater than or equal to zero.

configItems.name: error_correction
configItems.description: Optional parameter that determines how much error correction will be applied when using Eb/No to calculate data rate. Must be between 0.0 and 1.0. Units are assumed dB.

configItems.name: bit_error_rate_ebno_table
configItems.description: Optional table that defines the Energy per Bit to the Spectral Noise Density (Eb/No) vs. Bit Error Rate (BER). Used in conjunction with the bit_error_probability and error_correction to calculate the data transfer rate over the medium. When using this table Data Rate = SNR* Error Correction * ( Bandwidth / Eb/No ). The Bit-Error-Rate-EbNo-Table will be interpolated. If a table is specified, the table transfer rate values will override the value specified with the transfer_rate command.

configItems.name: update_rate
configItems.description: Specifies the rate that this network will perform updates to the network state by creating and removing linkage. Every comm in the network that does not have an update rate specific to that instance will use this rate.

configItems.name: comm_update_rates
configItems.description: This block allows users to specify a unique update rate for a particular comm interface designated by the platform name and comm name. Any comm interface with an update rate specified in this manner will use this update rate for modifying outgoing links from that interface, not the general update rate specified via update_rate.

configItems.name: remove_comm_update_rate
configItems.description: Removes a unique update rate entry for the comm specified by platform and comm name. Sets the specified comm to use the general update rate assigned via the update_rate command.

configItems.name: address_update_rates
configItems.description: This block allows users to specify a unique update rate for a particular comm interface designated by the comm interface address. Any comm interface with an update rate specified in this manner will use this update rate for modifying outgoing links from that interface, not the general update rate specified via update_rate.

configItems.name: remove_address_update_rate
configItems.description: Removes a unique update rate entry for the comm specified by comm address. Sets the specified comm to use the general update rate assigned via the update_rate command.

configItems.name: comm_list
configItems.description: Members of this network may be specified by identifying a comm object by its owning platform name and the name of the comm. Each entry in this list is prefixed by the “member” command.

configItems.name: address_list
configItems.description: Members of this network may be specified by identifying a comm object by its address. Each entry in this list is prefixed by the “member” command. This list is only available to comm objects that have specified addresses in input, as comms without specified addresses will be dynamically allocated at runtime.

configItems.name: comm_list
configItems.description: Members of this network may be specified by identifying a comm object by its owning platform name and the name of the comm. Each entry in this list is prefixed by the “member” command.

configItems.name: address_list
configItems.description: Members of this network may be specified by identifying a comm object by its address. Each entry in this list is prefixed by the “member” command. This list is only available to comm objects that have specified addresses in input, as comms without specified addresses will be dynamically allocated at runtime.

configItems.name: comm_link_list
configItems.description: Specifies a link between comm objects specified by their owning platform name, and the comm name, represented as directional pairs. The order specified matters, as a link is only created from the first comm specified, to the second comm specified. Each entry in this list is prefixed by the “link” command.

configItems.name: address_link_list
configItems.description: Specifies a link between comm objects defined by their addresses. The order specified matters, as a link is only created from the first address specified to the second. Each entry in this list is prefixed by the “link” command.

configItems.name: hub_named
configItems.description: Specifies the star network hub comm object by its owning platform name, and the comm name. This hub must be a member of the network.

configItems.name: hub_address
configItems.description: Specifies the star network hub comm object by its address. This hub must be a member of the network.

configItems.name: join_multicast_group
configItems.description: Adds this comm to the multicast group specified. Any messages sent to this address will attempt carrying the message to this comm, assuming no routing failures.

configItems.name: leave_multicast_group
configItems.description: Removes this comm from the specified multicast group. Specifically intended to allow removal of indicated multicast group specification from derived comms.

configItems.name: level_0_multicast
configItems.description: Indicates that this multicast protocol instance is of type 0, indicating no actual multicast support.

configItems.name: level_1_multicast
configItems.description: Indicates that this multicast protocol instance is of type 1, indicating that this comm is capable of sending multicast messages, but cannot receive them.

configItems.name: level_2_multicast
configItems.description: Indicates that this multicast protocol instance is of type 2, indicating that this comm has full multicast capabilities, and can both send and receive multicast messages.

configItems.name: join_delay
configItems.description: Specifies the time required to join a multicast group, for more advanced modeling of network characteristics. This may also affect how other protocols who use multicast (such as OSPF) function, due to delayed propogation of multicast group data amongst routers. Future plans of script capabilities in joining and leaving multicast groups will be affected by this value.

configItems.name: leave_delay
configItems.description: Specifies the time required to leave a multicast group, for more advanced modeling of network characteristics. This may also affect how other protocols who use multicast (such as OSPF) function, due to delayed propagation of multicast group data amongst routers. Future plans of script capabilities in joining and leaving multicast groups will be affected by this value.

configItems.name: comm_added_delay_time
configItems.description: Defines the delay to be taken between when a network being monitored adds a comm interface and when this protocol will execute the OnCommAdded script method, potentially adding an interface to the network state graph.

configItems.name: comm_removed_delay_time
configItems.description: Defines the delay to be taken between when a network being monitored removes a comm interface and when this protocol will execute the OnCommRemoved script method, potentially removing an interface on the network state graph.

configItems.name: connection_added_delay_time
configItems.description: Defines the delay to be taken between when a network being monitored adds a link or connection and when this protocol will execute the OnConnectionAdded script method, potentially adding a connection to the network state graph.

configItems.name: connection_removed_delay_time
configItems.description: Defines the delay to be taken between when a network being monitored removes a link or connection and when this protocol will execute the OnConnectionRemoved script method, potentially removing a connection from the network state graph.

configItems.name: OnCommAdded
configItems.description: Defines an optional script that is invoked (after delays) when a comm interface is added. This is only invoked when the interface being added shares a network with one of the interfaces on the router this protocol belongs to, or pertains directly to one of the router interfaces.

configItems.name: OnCommRemoved
configItems.description: Defines an optional script that is invoked (after delays) when a comm interface is removed. This is only invoked when the interface being removed shares a network with one of the interfaces on the router this protocol belongs to, or pertains directly to one of the router interfaces.

configItems.name: OnConnectionAdded
configItems.description: Defines an optional script that is invoked (after delays) when a connection is added. This is only invoked when one of the involved interfaces (either the source or destination) shares a network with one of the interfaces on the router this protocol belongs to.

configItems.name: OnConnectionRemoved
configItems.description: Defines an optional script that is invoked (after delays) when a connection is removed. This is only invoked when one of the involved interfaces (either the source or destination) shares a network with one of the interfaces on the router this protocol belongs to.

configItems.name: OnMessageRouting
configItems.description: Defines an optional script that is invoked immediately when a message requires routing on an interface belonging to this protocol’s router.

configItems.name: ospf_area
configItems.description: Defines the area this comm/router belongs to in the OSPF AS. Multiple areas may be assigned if this member has a direct connection to another member in that area, defining this member as a “border router”.

configItems.name: remove_ospf_area
configItems.description: Removes an area defined for this protocol. Specifically provided for editing derived objects in input.

configItems.name: backbone
configItems.description: Defines the specified area as a backbone. This only has to be done on a protocol instance for this setting to be applied across an entire OSPF connected AS.

configItems.name: remove_backbone
configItems.description: This command removes the backbone specification for this protocol type or instance. Used in cases where a protocol type is inherited from, but the specified backbone setting is not wanted.

configItems.name: ospf_dr_priority
configItems.description: Sets the priority for this router becoming the “designated router” or “backup designated router” (DR, BDR) for its network within an area. These routers hold all of the detailed routing data for a specific area as common points of communication for all other routers in the same network. This value must be positive, where a lower value indicates a higher priority. This value also affects subsequent re-selection of these routers dynamically at runtime. Any router entering a network and area does not preempt any already established DR or BDR, even if it has a higher priority.

configItems.name: hello_interval
configItems.description: Defines the amount of time between sending the OSPF heartbeat, the “hello” packet. If these are not received before the defined hold time, the router will be considered non-connected or non-functional and removed from network state data for routing purposes. In addition, this defines how soon a new member is detected, as this is also the method in which new members are detected.

configItems.name: hold_timer
configItems.description: Defines the amount of time that before a member is dropped if a hello packet is not received. Note that the default value allows multiple hello packet transmission windows before actually being dropped due to hold time. Ensure that this value is greater than the hello_interval to avoid dropping all members from network state knowledge.

configItems.name: update_interval
configItems.description: Specifies how often a router will send an update to other routers. As specified for the RIPv2 spec (RFC 2543), this is base time. Each time an update is scheduled, the time can change by +/- 5 seconds.

configItems.name: invalidation_timeout
configItems.description: The amount of time that must pass before a route is marked as inactive. Once a router has not been heard from for this amount of time, routes learned from that router are marked as inactive.

configItems.name: garbage_collection_timeout
configItems.description: The amount of time that once a route has been marked as inactive, it will be purged from the routing table.

configItems.name: poisoned_reverse
configItems.description: Specifies whether to use split horizon, or split horizon with poisoned reverse. Split horizon is a scheme for avoiding sending routes in updates to routers from which they were learned. Poisoned reverse includes such routes in updates, but sets their metrics to be unusable.

configItems.name: grid_data_file

Providing these values (of the order of tenths of arc-seconds) enables very highly accurate conversions between ECI and WCS coordinates.

configItems.description: This command allows for the suppression of grid asset platforms in DIS output and in distributed simulations. This suppression only applies for platforms created by a grid. This suppression is enabled by default.

configItems.name: subgrid
configItems.description: Add a sub-grid of the given <grid-type> with the given <name> to this grid. The subgrid is then configured according to the selected type, and will support any command that the selected grid type supports. The types of sub-grids supported are those that create their own platforms.

configItems.name: state
configItems.description: Indicates that the following table definition will be used when the platform is in the signature state <state-name>. If default is specified then the subsequent table will be used if the platform is in a signature state that does not match any of the states defined in the signature.

configItems.name: location
configItems.description: Specify the location of the origin of the surface with respect to the origin of the entity coordinate system. The location of a surface is not important except to ensure that adjacent faces of surfaces are correctly detected. Other than excluding adjacent faces, the projected area of each surface is computed independently.

configItems.name: temperature
configItems.description: Specifies the inherent temperature of the surface used in computing the temperature to be used for the blackbody model. This represents the temperature that is a result of self-production (engines, heaters, etc.) or skin friction. It does NOT include the temperature due to warming by the Sun.

configItems.name: temperature_offset
configItems.description: Specify a temperature offset to be added to the ambient temperature when ‘temperature ambient’ is specified. This value may be specified as a negative value.

configItems.name: recovery_factor
configItems.description: Specify the recovery factor for the adiabatic wall temperature model (described below).

configItems.name: gamma
configItems.description: Specify the ratio of specific heats for the adiabatic wall temperature model (described below).

configItems.name: yaw
configItems.description: Specifies the yaw angle of the surface with respect to the entity to which it is attached.

configItems.name: pitch
configItems.description: Specifies the pitch of the surface with respect to the entity to which it is attached.

configItems.name: roll
configItems.description: Specifies the roll of the surface with respect to the entity to which it is attached.

configItems.name: size
configItems.description: Defines the size of a box. The first value is the dimension along the part coordinate system (PCS) X axis, the second is the dimension along the PCS Y axis, and the third is the dimension along the PCS Z axis. One of the dimensions may be zero. This is provided so that two-sided objects like solar panels or SAR antennas may be defined.

configItems.name: length
configItems.description: Defines the length of the cone.

configItems.name: radius
configItems.description: Defines the radius of the base of the cone.

configItems.name: projected_area
configItems.description: Specifies an azimuth-elevation table definition.

configItems.name: operating_mode
configItems.description: Defines how the constituent sensors are managed.

configItems.name: sensor
configItems.description: Defines the name of a constituent sensor. This command must be repeated one or more times specifying the names of the ‘constituent’ sensors that make up the ‘composite’ sensor. In general, all of the constituent sensors should be of the same general type. At the current time the sensors should be a type that reports tracks (WSF_RADAR_SENSOR, WSF_IRST_SENSOR, WSF_PASSIVE_SENSOR).

configItems.name: filter
configItems.description: Defines a filter to be applied to the stream of tracks for a target when the operating_mode is independent.

configItems.name: track_quality
configItems.description: Specifies the track quality to be assigned to the composite tracks produced by this sensor when the operating_mode is independent. This value is used only if it is greater than zero. If the value is zero then the track quality for the constituent tracks will be used.

configItems.name: probability_of_cover
configItems.description: Specifies the the probability, in the range [0.0, 1.0], that the cover pulse is covering the skin return. A probability draw is done and if the draw is outside this probability then the effectiveness is 0.0.

configItems.name: required_j_to_s
configItems.description: Specifies the minimum J/S ratio required for effectiveness.

configItems.description: Input block to provide the system type (e.g., SENSOR-TYPE, JAMMER-TYPE) specific data necessary to implement this technique for a given system type. Default data can be set up for system types not defined using the “default” string as the system type.

The origin must be within the given latitude_span and longitude_span. The default value of the grid’s origin point is the point at minimum latitude and minimum longitude.
