configItems.description: Specifies a WSF_BEAM_DIRECTOR object to attach to this cued laser weapon. When specified, the cued laser weapon will search for a beam director on the same platform with the specified name. If the beam director is found, the weapon will link to it. If the beam director is not found on the platform, initialization will fail.

configItems.name: use_default_beam_director
configItems.description: Disables the ability to specify a WSF_BEAM_DIRECTOR to link the WSF_CUED_LASER_WEAPON with. When this command is used, the laser will not search for the WSF_BEAM_DIRECTOR specified by the beam_director command, instead linking to the first WSF_BEAM_DIRECTOR it encounters.

configItems.name: policy
configItems.description: Specifies how the evaluated scripts from the input triggers will be logically combined. Valid options for this command are and and or.

configItems.name: triggers
configItems.description: Specifies the triggers whose results of OnEvaluate should be logically combined to trigger this effect.

configItems.name: weapon_type
configItems.description: All weapons that inherit from the specified weapon type (as long as they are of base type WSF_EXPLICIT_WEAPON) will be detonated upon successful attack.

configItems.name: weapon_name
configItems.description: All weapons on a victim platform that have the specified weapon name (as defined by the user in a scenario) will be detonated.

configItems.name: platform_type
configItems.description: Define the affected comms and effect behaviors for a platform type. This command may be repeated as necessary.

configItems.name: platform
configItems.description: Define the affected comms and effect behaviors for a specific platform. This command may be repeated as necessary.

configItems.name: default
configItems.description: Define the default comms and behaviors of the attack if the victim is not of any previously specified platforms or platform types.

configItems.name: target_list
configItems.description: Specifies comm devices by name on the victim platform that will be affected by this effect. If a comm is listed, but does not exist on the victim platform when the effect is applied, then it will be disregarded.

configItems.name: all
configItems.description: Specifies that all comms on the victim platform will be affected by this effect.

configItems.name: exfiltrate
configItems.description: Specifies that this comm should attempt to forward every message it receives back to the attacker. This will attempt to send the message to the first comm on the attacker that is reachable from the victim comm. Any message exfiltrated this way will be marked with an EXFILTRATED_MESSAGE aux-data field. The forwarded message will be marked with the EXFILTRATION_MESSAGE aux-data field.

configItems.name: OnSend
configItems.description: A provided script that will be called when a specified comm attempts to send a message. This script allows for the ability to alter, delay, or drop a WsfMessage.

configItems.name: OnReceive
configItems.description: A provided script that will be called when a specified comm attempts to receive a message. This script allows for the ability to alter, delay, or drop a WsfMessage.

configItems.name: platform_type
configItems.description: Define the effect scripts for a platform type. This command may be repeated as necessary.

configItems.name: platform
configItems.description: Define the effect scripts for a specific platform. This command may be repeated as necessary.

configItems.name: default
configItems.description: Define the effect scripts for any victim that does is not specified by platform or platform_type. This command is only valid once, and multiple instances of this block will only use the last declared instance of this block.

configItems.name: platform

configItems.name: default

configItems.name: attack
configItems.description: The ‘Attack’ script is invoked when the attack has been determined that it will occur. The method should take the necessary actions to cause whatever is needed to implement the effect.

configItems.name: restore
configItems.description: The ‘Restore’ script is invoked when it has been determined that the victim has recovered from the attack. The method should take the necessary actions to rescind whatever actions were taken by the Attack script (essentially restoring the platform to the state that existed prior to the attack).

configItems.name: platform

configItems.description: A target_list defines the names of the comms that should be disabled by this effect. Any comm name matching the provided names will be turned off. All other comms will be unaffected.

configItems.name: select_all
configItems.description: Specifying this command in lieu of the target_list will disable all comms on the victim platform. Defining both the select_all and target_list block commands will result in an error in loading the scenario input.

configItems.name: select_all

configItems.name: inactive_track_purging
configItems.description: Defines if this effect allows for inactive track purging during the lifetime of the effect.

configItems.name: inactive_raw_track_purging
configItems.description: Defines if this effect allows for inactive raw track purging during the lifetime of the effect.

configItems.name: local_track_history_purging
configItems.description: Defines if this effect allows for local track history purging during the lifetime of the effect.

configItems.name: queuing_method
configItems.description: Specifies how incoming messages are to be queued if all of the servers are busy. A value of none indicates the message will be discarded.

configItems.name: number_of_servers
configItems.description: Specifies the maximum number of messages that can be ‘in process’ at any given instant of time. If a new message is received and all of the servers are busy, the message will be queued according to the queuing_method

configItems.name: time_distribution
configItems.description: Defines that simulated processing time will a constant value with the specified time.

configItems.name: fuse_all_collects
configItems.description: If enabled, all measurements for a given target will be used for direction finding. Otherwise if the expected value of the location error, after the pair are utilized, is greater than the current value, the pair will not be fused.

configItems.name: collect_replacement_interval
configItems.description: Specifies a time interval after which an existing measurement that has not been used for direction finding, will be updated with a more recent measurement.

configItems.name: maximum_expected_error
configItems.description: Specifies a maximum value in a single dimension, that the expected direction-finding error value should not exceed.

configItems.name: use_truth_altitude
configItems.description: Specifies that the actual altitude should be used when reporting the locations of air targets.

configItems.name: filter
configItems.description: Associates a filter type with this processor. All incoming tracks of that have no filter, will be assigned this type. If this command isn’t indicated, a WsfKalmanFilter type will be used.

configItems.name: filter_bypass
configItems.description: Allows bypassing the filter, such that the output will be the ‘measurement’, which is just the intersection point from a successful triangulation.

configItems.name: minimum_baseline_distance
configItems.description: Specifies the minimum distance between origin locations of pairs of measurements being fused.

configItems.name: maximum_time_difference
configItems.description: Specifies the maximum time difference allowed between measurements. Measurements that exceed this time difference, will not be fused. This helps reduce errors when the targets are moving. If this field is not included, there is no maximum time difference - all pairs will be fused, assuming all other things being equal.

configItems.description: Set the size of the grid. The first value gives the number of rows in the grid. The second value gives the number of points in each row. The resulting number of grid points will be the product of the two provided values.

configItems.name: step_distance
configItems.description: Specify the distance between adjacent grid points. The first value gives the separation distance between one row and the next. The second value gives the separation distance between points in the same row.

configItems.name: origin_index
configItems.description: Specify the position in the grid that is at the location given by the origin command. These values start from 0 and count from the south west corner. For example:

configItems.name: origin
configItems.description: Set the origin point in the grid, the point from which the other rows and members in each row are spaced. There will be one row in the grid at the given latitude, and there will be one point in each row of the grid at the given longitude.

configItems.name: altitude
configItems.description: Set the altitude of the grid points. <altitude-reference> can be either ‘msl’, in which case the altitude refers to a height above the mean sea level, or ‘agl’, in which case the altitude refers to a height above the ground level set by any terrain in the scenario.

configItems.description: Specify the assets associated with this grid will be instances of <platform-type> and will use the device with the name <device-name>. The given <device-name> may also be ‘none’ if the grid points are passive targets for the coverage computation in question.

configItems.name: verbose
configItems.description: Also produce detailed output about certain known messages. At the current time this is limited to WsfTrackMessage and WsfTrackDropMessage.

configItems.name: default_on
configItems.description: Set the behavior of the technique to be active. Otherwise, technique will remain inactive until commanded to become active.

configItems.name: mitigation_class_name
configItems.description: Set the technique’s mitigation class name. Used to map electronic attack techniques to electronic protection techniques that can mitigate them using the mitigated_technique_classes command.

configItems.name: pk_tables_path
configItems.description: Specifies the path to the Pk table files. May be a relative or absolute path.

configItems.name: default_pk
configItems.description: The default constant Pk value to be used in a weapon engagement when no Pk table lookup is available for a given launcher and target platform type.

configItems.name: file_filter
configItems.description: The filter to use when recursively scanning the pk_tables_path directory for Pk table files. Any file whose name matches the filter will be loaded. Wild-carding using ‘*’ is suggested (e.g. *.*; *.pk*) and the filter may be surrounded by quotation marks if it contains white space characters.

configItems.name: call_sensor_track_observers
configItems.description: Specifies if the ‘sensor track observers’ should be called. If true, sensor track observer events will be invoked, which enables the generation of data that allows visualization tools to display detection lines during the image formation process. These extra events, however, may cause problems to some observers if they haven’t been modified to ignore these events, which is the reason for the default being ‘false’.

configItems.name: angular_resolution
configItems.description: Specifies the angle subtended by a pixel.

configItems.name: pixel_count
configItems.description: Specifies the width and height in pixels of images from this sensor. If this command is specified, angular_resolution is ignored. Instead, the angular resolution is computed by the ratio (azimuth FOV)/(horizontal-count) and (elevation FOV)/(vertical-count).

configItems.name: band
configItems.syntax: band [ visual | short | medium | long | very_long ]
configItems.description: Defines the band of radiation that the sensor will detect. The wavelengths of the bands are defined as follows:

configItems.name: atmospheric_attenuation
configItems.description: Sometimes called the the extinction coefficient, this is the fraction of the signal (in the closed range 0 to 1) that is attenuated per unit of distance traveled at sea level. The value is adjusted to account for the density of air with the change in altitude.

configItems.name: background_radiance
configItems.description: Specifies the radiance of the background.

configItems.name: background_radiance_below_horizon
configItems.description: These two commands provide an alternative to the fixed background radiance provided by background_radiance. This is useful for airborne sensors where the sensor may be looking up and the sky is the background, or looking down where the ground is the background.

configItems.name: background_transition_angle
configItems.description: This command is used along with background_radiance_above_horizon and background_radiance_below_horizon to specify a region where the transition is made from using the below horizon and above horizon background radiance values. The specified angles are relative to the local angle to the horizon with positive values being above the horizon and negative values being below the horizon. If the target is within the transition region defined by these angles, the resulting background radiance will be linearly interpolated between the above horizon and below horizon values.

configItems.name: detection_threshold
configItems.description: Defines the ratio of signal to noise required to declare a successful detection.

configItems.name: noise_equivalent_irradiance
configItems.description: The “noise equivalent irradiance’ (NEI) of the receiver.

configItems.name: antenna_pattern
configItems.description: Defines the name of a pseudo-antenna pattern (defined with the antenna_pattern command, which can be used to account for aspect-dependent effects caused by the aperture through which the sensor is looking.

configItems.name: internal_loss
configItems.description: Defines an additional constant loss that can be applied to the computation.

configItems.name: default_on
configItems.description: Set the behavior of the technique to be active. Otherwise, technique will remain inactive until commanded to become active.

configItems.name: externally_controlled
configItems.description: Specify to prohibit the automatic use of technique internally and allow only external (i.e., scripted or commanded) control. This action is not the default for applying EP techniques and is overridden by the default_on

configItems.name: internally_controlled
configItems.description: Specify to allow the automatic use of the technique internally, any external control may be overridden. This action modifies the default_on value to be on if the technique is required to be used and is the default method for applying EP techniques.

configItems.name: mitigated_techniques
configItems.description: Defines the EA techniques this EP technique can attempt to mitigate.

configItems.name: mitigated_technique_classes
configItems.description: Defines the EA technique classes this EP technique can attempt to mitigate.

configItems.name: reported_target_type
configItems.description: Defines how the ESM sensor reports target type information in tracks.

configItems.name: default_time_to_declare
configItems.description: Defines the duration of time after the initial detection that is required to make a determination of the target type.

configItems.name: default_time_to_reevaluate
configItems.description: Defines the time interval used for reevaluating the identification of the target. A value of 0 seconds indicates no reevaluation will take place.

configItems.name: type
configItems.description: Specifies the truth type to which the following subcommands apply.

configItems.name: default_type
configItems.description: Specifies that the following type subcommands apply for any type not defined with the type command.

configItems.name: time_to_declare
configItems.description: Defines the duration of time after the initial detection that is required to make a determination of the target type.

configItems.name: time_to_reevaluate
configItems.description: Defines the time interval used for reevaluating the identification of the target.

configItems.name: report_type
configItems.description: Defines the reporting type-name as the target type based on the listed emitter-type(s) being reported in the emitter list. Currently exact matches between the emitter’s defined for the report_type and a track’s emitter list must happen for the given report_type to be reported. If there are differences another report_type or the default_type will be reported.

configItems.name: report_truth
configItems.description: Specifies that the sensor will report the truth type. This is only valid under the default_type command.

configItems.name: reported_emitter_type
configItems.description: Defines how the ESM sensor reports emitter type information in tracks.

configItems.name: unframed_detection_optimization
configItems.description: This command indicates if unframed detection optimization will be used. If enabled, once the sensor successfully detects a given transmitter within a frame, subsequent attempts to detect the same transmitter in the same frame will be suppressed. For instance, if multiple messages are sent from a single transmitter during the ESM frame, the ESM sensor will only report on the first message that it can detect (if any). If the first message cannot be detected because of transmitter antenna pointing, it will report the second message if it can be detected, an so on.

configItems.name: unframed_detection_coast_time
configItems.description: If the ESM sensor is running at a faster frame time than the sensors it is trying to detect, it may detect the transmitter one frame and not the next. This can cause a lot of track creation and deletion. This value indicates how long a successful detection from a transmitter will be reported.

configItems.name: frequency_band
configItems.description: Defines a band of frequencies this sensor can detect. This command may be specified more than once if the sensor can detect multiple bands.

configItems.name: revisit_time
configItems.description: These two commands pertain to the immediately preceding frequency_band and define how long the sensor dwells in the band and the interval between dwells. These commands are effectively only when the scan_on_scan_model is enabled and are used to determine the temporal probability that the sensor would be looking at the frequency of the target emitter when a detection chance occurs.

configItems.name: detection_sensitivity
configItems.description: Defines the minimum signal strength that can be ‘reliably’ detected. If detection_probability is defined then this is the signal strength that would result in a Pd of 0.5. If detection_probability is not defined then this defines the signal strength for which a successful detection will be declared.

configItems.name: detection_sensitivities
configItems.description: This command allows the definition of frequency-dependent or signal-type- and frequency-dependent detection sensitivities.

configItems.name: detection_threshold
configItems.description: This is an alternative to detection_sensitivity. It defines the minimum signal-to-noise ratio that can be ‘reliably’ detected. If detection_probability is defined then this is the signal-to-noise ratio that would result in a Pd of 0.5. If detection_probability is not defined then this defines the signal-to-noise ratio for which a successful detection will be declared.

configItems.name: detection_thresholds
configItems.description: This command allows the definition of frequency-dependent or signal-type- and frequency-dependent detection thresholds.

configItems.name: detection_probability
configItems.description: Defines a function of probability of detection (Pd) versus received signal strength (expressed as a ratio of the received power to the detection sensitivity). The table is defined as follows:

configItems.name: scan_on_scan_model
configItems.description: Specifies if the Probabilistic Scan-On-Scan (PSOS) model should be employed. This model attempts to probabilistically capture the temporal effects in which the ESM sensor is scanning in frequency and the emitter may be scanning in angle.

configItems.name: range_error_sigma_table
configItems.description: These commands provide the ability to define error sigmas that are a function of the frequency of the received signal instead of the fixed sigmas that are provided by the single-valued azimuth_error_sigma, elevation_error_sigma and range_error_sigma commands. The points define a curve on a plot whose x-axis is the log_10 of the frequency and the y-axis is the error sigma. Linear interpolation is used to derive the values for intermediate frequencies. Signals whose frequencies are outside the range of the table use the value from the appropriate endpoint (i.e., extrapolation is not performed).

configItems.name: ranging_time
configItems.description: Adds range information to any track generated by this sensor after the specified time has elapsed. This basically simulates that the system could triangulate and get the range after a sufficient period of time.

configItems.name: ranging_time_track_quality
configItems.description: If the ranging time is used to generate a track with range information, this parameter controls the track quality once range is valid. The quality-value must be non-negative.

configItems.name: commodity
configItems.description: A tender of ‘commodity’ is to propose an exchange of some named tangible goods, noting the kind, amount, and rate of a planned requested or offered exchange. It does _not_ specify the direction of flow, which is dictated by the transactor is_offeror or is_requestor setting.

configItems.name: service
configItems.description: A tender of ‘service’ is to propose an exchange of some named intangible service, noting the kind, amount, and rate of a planned requested or offered exchange. It does _not_ specify the direction of flow, which is dictated by the transactor is_offeror or is_requestor setting.

configItems.name: quantity
configItems.description: Specifies the current number of services available or desired.

configItems.name: maximum_quantity
configItems.description: Specifies the limiting number of services available or desired. Syntactical convenience to indicate the maximum size of a container (see below).

configItems.name: mass_quantity
configItems.description: Specifies the current mass of commodity available or desired.

configItems.name: maximum_mass_quantity
configItems.description: Specifies the limiting quantity of commodity available or desired. Syntactical convenience to indicate the maximum size of a container (see below).

configItems.name: rate
configItems.description: Specifies the rate of services offered per unit time.

configItems.name: service_interval
configItems.description: Specifies the time required to accomplish a unit of service. 30 minutes = Two repairs per hour.

configItems.name: mass_rate
configItems.description: Specifies the rate of commodities exchanged services offered per unit time. The real value must be followed with a correct mass rate specification, such as kg/sec, etc.

configItems.name: container
configItems.description: The <container-name> specifies the name of the object, as a way for the WSF_EXCHANGE_PROCESSOR to differentiate between perhaps several containers owned by the processor. The container block quantifies a container; its name, what it holds, maximum, and current quantities of the commodity or service. While a service (i.e. engine-repair) is not a tangible to be held in a container, for the purposes of simulation book-keeping, it is treated as such. Transactions are always “piped” into or out of a named container. No transaction is permitted which transfers more of a commodity or service than may be added to or decremented from a container, given its maximum capacity and current quantity. A constraining operation will always bound/clamp the transaction to abide by the container’s constraint. Any convenient number of containers may be defined as needed, and a container may have more than one transaction “piped” into it, such as a tanker aircraft which may both on-load fuel from another tanker and offload fuel to a receiver simultaneously, both linked to the same container.

configItems.name: initial_quantity
configItems.description: Specifies the beginning number of services available in the container, which must be less than or equal to the maximum container size in the above tender specification.

configItems.name: initial_mass_quantity
configItems.description: Specifies the beginning amount of a commodity available in the container, which must be less than or equal to the maximum container size in the above tender specification.

configItems.name: transactor
configItems.description: The <transactor-name> specifies the name of the object, as a way for the WSF_EXCHANGE_PROCESSOR to differentiate between perhaps several transactors owned by the processor. The transactor block quantifies a transaction; its name, the direction of flow of the commodity or service, and current quantities of the transaction in-progress. Regardless of direction, quantities tend toward zero as the transaction progresses (is_offeror starts with amount available and reaches zero when exhausted, is_requestor starts with amount desired and reaches zero as fully satisfied). Transactions are always “piped” into or out of a named container. Regardless of the initial amount of Reserve() or Request(), the transaction starts only after being constrained to what may come from or fit into the named container.

configItems.name: is_offeror
configItems.description: Transactor is configured as an offeror/provider of goods or services.

configItems.name: is_requestor
configItems.description: Transactor is configured as a requestor/consumer of goods or services.

configItems.name: hook_to_fuel
configItems.description: Transactor will increment or decrement the quantity of fuel on its platform after every successful transaction. Will not decrement below a zero quantity.

configItems.name: hook_to_payload
configItems.description: Transactor will increment or decrement the quantity of payload on its platform after every successful transaction. Will not decrement below a zero quantity.

configItems.name: exclusive_hook_to_payload
configItems.description: Transactor will directly control the quantity of payload or fuel, forcing it to match what is currently in the named container. It will be permitted to ignore and override any other process which sets the fuel or payload quantity, including input file specifications. Will not decrement below a zero quantity.

configItems.name: proximity_limit
configItems.description: Specifies the maximum distance allowed between two platforms in order to exchange. Default is zero, or distance ignored.

configItems.name: time_out_clock_interval
configItems.description: Specifies the maximum interval allowed to wait for a response to an offer or request. If a request is received, and a corresponding offer is sent out, and then no response is subsequently received, the offer is canceled after this period of time, in order to allow the transactor to be freed up to offer to another requestor.

configItems.name: commodity_and_capability_pairing
configItems.description: This keyword creates an association between a commodity name, and a Platform Capability, as supplied in the DIS Entity State PDU. If an exchange processor has a transactor which is currently offering a fuel commodity, then this processor will assure that the platform capability “SUPPLY_FUEL” will be flagged as present. (See example input above.) Other bits may indicate that fuel or payload can be provided, but only if they are properly indicated with the keyword above. Multiple pairings may be provided.

configItems.name: service_and_capability_pairing
configItems.description: This keyword creates an association between a service type name, and a Platform Capability, as supplied in the DIS Entity State PDU. If an exchange processor has a transactor which is currently offering a repair service, then this processor will assure that the platform capability “VEHICLE_REPAIR” will be flagged as present. Other bits may indicate that vehicle repair or vehicle recovery, is available, but only if they are properly indicated with the keyword above. Multiple pairings may be provided. (Capability Automated Data Service - Broadcast (ADS_B) is currently not supported.)

configItems.name: ignore_all_proximity_checks
configItems.description: If set true, command ignores, and overrides all the transactor ‘proximity_limit’ values above, forcing them to zero. No transactions will fail due to a proximity limit check. Default is ‘false’.

configItems.name: force_transactions_instantaneous
configItems.description: If set true, command ignores all specifications of tender ‘rate’, ‘service_interval’, or ‘mass_rate’. Once successfully negotiated, the resulting transactions will take zero simulated time.

configItems.name: debug
configItems.description: Command prompts console output of assistance in debugging processor operations.

configItems.name: edit
configItems.description: Command allows the edit of a previously named transactor or container. This command will begin a block, which must be concluded with the normal end_block syntax. Inside the block, any commands may be used which are appropriate for the chosen object_type.

configItems.name: Transactor
configItems.description: If the named Container (1st arg) exists, will return a reference to the Transactor to interact with. Returned object should be checked for IsValid() before use.

configItems.name: Array<int>
configItems.description: Returns an array of the platform indices for the simulated entities currently known to be providing payload, regardless of their proximity.

configItems.name: WsfPlatform
configItems.description: Returns a reference to the platform which is the closest known provider of the capability represented by the supplied commodity Item name. Returned object should be checked for IsValid() before use.

configItems.name: grid_data_file
configItems.description: Specify the name of an output file that will be created containing details of the points in this grid. The specified file is created at the end of the simulation.

configItems.name: central_body
configItems.description: Specify the central body and related ellipsoid model to be used by simulation platforms. Options for <central body type> are the following:

configItems.name: polar_offset_angles
configItems.description: Specify the central_body’s polar offset angles ( and , respectively) of the Celestial Intermediate Pole (CIP) with respect to the WCS (ITRS) coordinate system. Providing these values (of the order of tenths of arc-seconds) enables very highly accurate conversions between ECI and WCS coordinates.

configItems.name: suppress_grid_platforms
configItems.description: This command allows for the suppression of grid asset platforms in DIS output and in distributed simulations. This suppression only applies for platforms created by a grid. This suppression is enabled by default.

configItems.name: platform
configItems.description: Specify that the platform with the given <platform-name> should be added the grid and use device with the given <device-name> for the coverage computation. This command can be used for as many platforms as desired.

configItems.name: impact_angle_and_pk
configItems.description: Specify an entry in the Pk versus impact angle interpolation table. Any number of entries may be made. Constraints are zero to 180 degrees.

configItems.name: impact_velocity_and_pk
configItems.description: Specify an entry in the Pk versus impact velocity interpolation table. Any number of entries may be made. Impact velocity must be greater than zero.

configItems.name: launched_platform_type
configItems.description: Specifies the type of platform to be created when a weapon of this type is launched. The specified value must represent a valid platform type that must be defined when this object is initialized in the simulation.

configItems.name: launch_delta_v
configItems.description: Specifies the vector that represents the additional velocity, relative to the launching platform, provided by the launching mechanism. This value is specified in the entity coordinate system (+X is forward, +Y to the right and +Z down) of the launching part (see Articulated Part Commands).

configItems.name: ignore_launch_platform_velocity
configItems.description: Specifies that the initial velocity of a launched explicit weapon will ignore the vector component of launch platform velocity. Normally the initial weapon velocity is the vector sum of launch_delta_v plus the launching platform velocity.

configItems.name: require_intercept_point
configItems.description: Indicates that the launch_computer must have provided the attribute specified by the command.

configItems.name: commander
configItems.description: Specifies the commander(s) of the launched platform. If command_chain is not provided, the default command chain will be assumed. <commander> may be one of the following values:

configItems.name: dis_entity_id_offset
configItems.description: Adds this value onto the value of the platform index and sets the the weapon dis entity id. This value is used in the entity id fields in all DIS PDUs associated with this weapon. It is a way for the user to have some control of assigning weapon ids to weapons prior to launch and/or in a DIS environment. The the sum of the platform index and the value must not exceed 65535.

configItems.name: on_create
configItems.description: Defines a script that is called immediately after the weapon platform is created but before it is actually inserted into the simulation. This script is typically used to modify attributes of the weapon platform that must change before the weapon is added to the simulation. ‘aWeapon’ is a reference to the newly created weapon platform and ‘aTarget’ is a reference to the target track object.

configItems.name: maximum_radius
configItems.description: The maximum blast radius within which this weapon has some effect.

configItems.name: maximum_radius
configItems.description: Defines the maximum slant range (distance from the detonation/impact point to the target) at which this weapon could possibly have an effect. Note that this is only used for limiting the number of platforms that must be checked for possible damage, effectively eliminated ‘far-away’ objects from consideration.

configItems.name: false_target_name
configItems.description: Specifies the false-target name of the false_target definition to be used by this effect.

configItems.name: jamming_duty_cycle
configItems.description: Specifies the jammer pulse density in range [0,1] for generating false targets. This input will override the specified quantity if a false target name is input and is mutually exclusive with number_of_false_targets. This input is used to calculate the number of false targets according to the following:

configItems.name: number_of_false_targets
configItems.description: Specifies the number of false targets that will be created for this radar type. This input will override the specified quantity if a false target name is input and is mutually exclusive with the jamming_pulse_density. This input is used to calculate the Jamming_pulse_density according to the following:

configItems.name: track_speeds
configItems.description: Specifies the minimum and maximum <speed-value> at which the false target blips will move. If minimum and maximum speeds are equal all speeds will be the same on the blips; if they are not equal then random speeds will be drawn with the limits and set for each false target blip separately as to its speed. The false_target, as defined with the false_target_name, definition for speeds inside the track_movement block has priority if defined, if not defined then this speed will be used. This definition will aid in Doppler radars that reject nonmoving targets.

configItems.name: system_type_data
configItems.description: Input block to provide the system type (e.g., SENSOR-TYPE, JAMMER-TYPE) specific data necessary to implement this technique for a given system type. Default data can be set up for system types not defined using the “default” string as the system type.

configItems.name: fires_table
configItems.description: Define a fires table with multiple entries for range, maximum ordinate, and time of flight. Ranges and maximum ordinates are measured in meters; times of flight are measured in seconds. Each entry (1, 2, … n) for range, max. ord. and time-of-flight represents a discrete possible trajectory.

configItems.name: SystemMunition
configItems.description: Provide the System+Munition type to which this table refers. This name should be the same as the launched platform type of the launching weapon.

configItems.name: range_values
configItems.description: Define a set of characteristic trajectory values for range.

configItems.name: maximum_ordinate_values
configItems.description: Define a set of characteristic trajectory values for maximum ordinate.

configItems.name: elevation_angle_values
configItems.description: Define a set of characteristic trajectory values for initial elevation angle.

configItems.name: time_of_flight_values
configItems.description: Define a set of characteristic trajectory values for time of flight.

configItems.name: remove_on_impact
configItems.description: Defines whether to remove the launched platform on impact and terminate any active weapon engagement.

configItems.name: use_simple_propagation
configItems.description: Defines whether to use a simple parabolic trajectory, using only values of maximum_height and time_of_flight.

configItems.name: constrain_to_simple_propagation
configItems.description: In the case where a solution cannot be computed for the given values of range, max. height, and time of flight, use the solution given by the use_simple_propagation option.

configItems.name: impact_range
configItems.description: Defines the range from the launching platform where the munition will detonate.

configItems.name: initial_bearing
configItems.description: Defines the bearing from the launch platform that the munition will travel in its trajectory.

configItems.name: impact_location
configItems.description: impact_location geo-point-tag 38n 90w 100 ft // altitude

configItems.name: time_of_flight
configItems.description: Specifies the time of flight of the munition.

configItems.name: maximum_ordiante
configItems.description: Specifies the maximum height the munition will attain in its trajectory.

configItems.name: update_interval
configItems.description: If non-zero, specifies a periodic time interval at which the simulation will call the mover. If zero then the mover will be called only when it is necessary to determine the position of the containing platform.

configItems.name: update_time_tolerance
configItems.description: When a position update is requested by the simulation, if the time since the previous update is less than or equal to this value then the mover will ignore the update.

configItems.name: position
configItems.description: Default: 0n 0e

configItems.name: altitude
configItems.description: Initial altitude above ellipsoid. (msl)

configItems.name: speed
configItems.description: Initial speed.

configItems.name: heading
configItems.description: Initial heading.

configItems.name: body_g_limit
configItems.description: The body g-limit. Value must be greater than the acceleration of earth’s gravity.

configItems.name: maximum_bank_angle
configItems.description: Maximum allowable bank angle. Value must be between 5 degrees to 85 degrees.

configItems.name: maximum_axial_acceleration
configItems.description: Maximum axial acceleration to use when acceleration is necessary.

configItems.name: maximum_radial_acceleration
configItems.description: Maximum radial acceleration to use when turning.

configItems.name: maximum_climb_rate
configItems.description: The climb rate to use when an altitude change is necessary. This value is used if the waypoint does not include a climb_rate specification.

configItems.name: maximum_roll_rate
configItems.description: Maximum roll rate. Value must be greater than 0.

configItems.name: maximum_turn_rate
configItems.description: Maximum roll rate. Value must be greater than 0.

configItems.name: maximum_speed
configItems.description: Maximum speed constraint. Value must be greater than 0

configItems.name: minimum_speed
configItems.description: Minimum speed constraint. Value must be greater than 0.

configItems.name: velocity_pursuit_gain
configItems.description: The factor of proportion applied to the heading change required to null the velocity vector to point at the offset point from the leader. This is the desired lateral acceleration when roll rate limits are imposed. Value must be greater than 0.

configItems.name: lead_aircraft
configItems.description: The name of the lead platform.

configItems.name: formation_rolls_with_lead
configItems.description: The formation rolls with the lead platform.

configItems.name: offset_forward_from_lead
configItems.description: Offset forward from the lead platform.

configItems.name: offset_right_from_lead
configItems.description: Offset to the right of the lead platform.

configItems.name: offset_down_from_lead
configItems.description: Offset below the lead platform.

configItems.name: initialize_at_offset
configItems.description: The follower platform is initially placed at the supplied offset from the lead platform instead of the initial position (latitude, longitude, altitude).

configItems.name: false_target_name
configItems.description: Specifies the false-target name of the false_target definition to be used by this effect.

configItems.name: jamming_duty_cycle
configItems.description: Specifies the jammer pulse density in range [0,1] for generating false targets. This input will override the specified quantity if a false target name is input. This input is used to calculate the number of false targets according to the following:

configItems.name: scan_rate_multiplier
configItems.description: Specifies the false target generation scan rate multiplier for regenerating false targets. This input will be multiplied by the specified scan_rate if a false target name is input, else the scan rate of the false targets is equal to the frame_time times the scan_rate_multiplier.

configItems.name: system_type_data
configItems.description: Input block to provide the system type (e.g., SENSOR-TYPE, JAMMER-TYPE) specific data necessary to implement this technique for a given system type. Default data can be set up for system types not defined using the “default” string as the system type.

configItems.name: consumption_rate
configItems.description: Defines the fixed rate at which fuel will be consumed.

configItems.name: plot_capacity
configItems.description: Defines the number of targets that can be plotted on the radar scope.

configItems.name: frame_time
configItems.description: Defines the update rate of the fusion center in seconds.

configItems.name: track_capacity
configItems.description: Defines the number of tracks that can be maintained by the fusion center.

configItems.name: random_to_multiple_radars
configItems.description: Defines the ratio of false-targets that will be rejected that appear on any radar.

configItems.name: consistent_to_multiple_radars
configItems.description: Defines the ratio of false-targets that will be rejected that appear on multiple radars.

configItems.name: radar_site
configItems.description: Specifies the name of a radar site to be fused. Repeat this command for each radar site. Name refers to the radar platform’s player name.

configItems.name: consistency_constrained
configItems.description: Defines whether a track must must be detected by all radar sites in order to be fused by the fusion center. False means the track needs only to appear on one radar site.

configItems.name: platform_type
configItems.description: Defines the maximum detection range for targets with platform type of <platform-type>. If the keyword default is provided, the range will apply to all platform types that do not have their own entry for detection range or pd-range table.

configItems.name: detection_range
configItems.description: Defines the maximum detection range for targets with platform type of <platform-type>. If the keyword default is provided, the range will apply to all platform types that do not have their own entry for detection range or pd-range table.

configItems.name: pd_range_table
configItems.description: Defines a Probability of detection vs range table for targets with the platform_type of <platform-type>. Example:

configItems.name: check_terrain_masking
configItems.description: Determines if the sensor will perform terrain and horizon masking checks on a target. By default, horizon masking is checked first, followed by a separate terrain masking check if terrain is loaded. The simple horizon masking check assumes a smooth bald spherical Earth and that any object below zero mean sea level is obscured. For subsurface sensors, horizon checking can be disabled by setting the terrain_masking_mode to terrain_only.

configItems.name: terrain_masking_mode
configItems.description: Sets the mode or type of masking checks to perform. By default, both horizon and terrain masking checks are enabled.

configItems.name: effective_earth_radius
configItems.description: Specify either the multiplier for Earth’s radius, or the effective earth radius, used to compute the effects of atmospheric refraction of electromagnetic radiation.

configItems.name: minimum_range_rate
configItems.description: This sensor will not detect targets with a range rate less than this value.

configItems.name: maximum_range_rate
configItems.description: This sensor will not detect targets with a range rate greater than this value.

configItems.name: interpolated
configItems.description: This keyword specifies a flag denoting whether the Pk is interpolated within two concentric rings or stays constant from one boundary to the other.

configItems.name: use_2d_radius
configItems.description: Miss distance is computed as either the slant range or horizontal distance between the weapon and target.

configItems.name: target_type
configItems.description: Introduce a set of radius and Pk values that pertain to the specified target type. All subsequent radius_and_pk and pk_and_radius commands up to the next command that does not define a radius/Pk pair are part of the table. An optional end_target_type command may be used to explicitly terminate the block.

configItems.name: pk_and_radius
configItems.description: Specify an entry in the current Pk vs. miss distance table.

configItems.name: update_interval
configItems.description: If non-zero, specifies a periodic time interval at which the simulation will call the mover. If zero then the mover will be called only when it is necessary to determine the position of the containing platform.

configItems.name: update_time_tolerance
configItems.description: When a position update is requested by the simulation, if the time since the previous update is less than or equal to this value then the mover will ignore the update.

configItems.name: altitude_offset
configItems.description: When set, this offset will offset the parent platform’s location by the given amount from the current waypoint’s altitude.

configItems.name: at_end_of_path
configItems.description: Specify the action to take when the mover reaches the end of its defined path.

configItems.name: draw_route
configItems.description: This command is the same as print_route, except the route text is not printed, only drawn with WsfDraw.

configItems.name: on_turn_failure
configItems.description: Defines the behavior of the mover when a point on a route cannot be reached exactly due to the turn radius.

configItems.name: pathfinder
configItems.description: The name of the pathfinder object to use.

configItems.name: print_route
configItems.description: When enabled, the route is printed to the screen whenever it is modified. Additionally, WsfDraw is used to output a visual of the route, which can be viewed with many visualization tools.

configItems.name: start_at
configItems.description: The label identifying the waypoint in the route to use as the starting location.

configItems.name: start_time
configItems.description: Indicates the platform is to start moving at the time specified. The current velocity is set to zero and once the simulation time is reached, the platform starts moving at the speed specified in the first waypoint. If an elapse time is desired at a waypoint, use the subcommand pause_time.

configItems.name: switch_on_approach
configItems.description: Switches to the next waypoint when approaching within one turn radius of the current target waypoint.

configItems.name: switch_on_passing
configItems.description: Switches to the next waypoint only when abreast of the current target waypoint.

configItems.name: turn_failure_threshold
configItems.description: Defines the threshold for which the on_turn_failure behavior is triggered, given as a ratio of the turn radius. For example, a turn_failure_threshold of 0.01 and a turn radius of 1000 meters, on_turn_failure logic would be triggered if the point is missed by more than 10 meters.

configItems.name: use_route
configItems.description: Supplies the name of the route to follow. The route is assumed to be a predefined absolute route.

configItems.name: angle_of_attack_table
configItems.description: speed <speed-value> angle <angle-value> speed <speed-value> angle <angle-value>

configItems.name: altitude
configItems.description: Specifies the altitude that the subsequent data is valid for. The altitude blocks must be in increasing numerical order. Linear interpolation of the altitude blocks is used.

configItems.name: speed
configItems.description: Specifies the speed that the listed angle of attack is valid for. The speed entries must be in increasing numerical order. The angle of attack will be computed using a linear interpolation of the speed data.

configItems.name: angle
configItems.description: The angle of attack. The angle of attack entries must be in increasing numerical order.

configItems.name: bank_angle_limit
configItems.description: The roll angle limit. Value must be between 0 degrees to 85 degrees. Used to calculate the maximum radial acceleration.

configItems.name: body_g_limit
configItems.description: The body g-limit. Value must be greater than the acceleration of earth’s gravity.

configItems.name: heading_pursuit_gain
configItems.description: The heading pursuit gain.

configItems.name: maximum_climb_rate
configItems.description: Specifies the maximum climb rate and dive rate used when changing altitude. Other climb rates specified by waypoints or scripts are bounded by this value.

configItems.name: maximum_flight_path_angle
configItems.description: Specifies maximum flight path angle (angle of climb/dive). Value must be greater than or equal to 0.

configItems.name: maximum_linear_acceleration
configItems.description: Specifies the maximum linear acceleration to use when acceleration is necessary. This value is used if the waypoint does not include a linear _acceleration specification.

configItems.name: maximum_radial_acceleration
configItems.description: Specifies the maximum radial acceleration to use when turning. This value is used if the waypoint does not include a radial_acceleration specification.

configItems.name: maximum_altitude
configItems.description: Maximum altitude constraint.

configItems.name: minimum_altitude
configItems.description: Minimum altitude constraint.

configItems.name: maximum_speed
configItems.description: Maximum speed constraint. Value must be greater than 0.

configItems.name: minimum_speed
configItems.description: Minimum speed constraint. Value must be greater than or equal to 0.

configItems.name: path_variance_radius
configItems.description: This value will randomly vary the location of the waypoint within the radius given. A random bearing and distance are chosen and applied to the next waypoint when calculating the path.

configItems.name: roll_rate_limit
configItems.description: The roll rate limit. Value must be greater than 0. Note: When applied to a WSF_AIR_MOVER or other waypoint mover types, the roll rate will not affect the platform’s movement along a route. To affect route following behavior use maximum_radial_acceleration.

configItems.name: speed_variance_percent
configItems.description: This value will randomly vary the speed at each waypoint as the mover travels within +/- the pct given. Value must be greater than 0.

configItems.name: turn_rate_limit
configItems.description: The turn rate limit. Value must be greater than 0.

configItems.name: no_pitch
configItems.description: Restricts the mover from pitching the platform. This has no effect on kinematics.

configItems.name: on_road
configItems.description: Restricts the mover from rolling the platform. This has no effect on kinematics.

configItems.name: off_road
configItems.description: Turns off the ‘on_road’ option. This allows the platform to roll.

configItems.name: path_compute_timestep
configItems.description: Waypoint movers precompute movement along paths. This behavior forces turns to have a constant radius. If path_compute_timestep is specified as a positive value, the turn rate will update on that interval if any changes in speed occur.

configItems.name: show_status
configItems.description: Specifies that information should be written to standard output whenever a phase or stage transition occurs.

configItems.name: show_diagnostics
configItems.description: Specifies that diagnostic information from guidance programs should be written to standard output. This is typically used when attempting to tune the guidance computer for generating orbital launch computers with weapon_tools.

configItems.name: show_commands
configItems.description: Specifies that calls from script commands should be written to standard output.

configItems.name: show_evaluations
configItems.description: Specifies that phase change rule evaluations should be written to standard output.

configItems.name: guide_to_truth
configItems.description: Specifies if the guidance target should be the location specified in the current target track (false), or should be the true location of the platform specified in the current target track (true).

configItems.name: phase
configItems.description: The ‘phase’ block is used to define the guidance for the various phases of flight and the rules to transition between phases.

configItems.name: edit
configItems.description: This command is typically used when creating a new guidance computer type by deriving from another guidance computer type.

configItems.name: program
configItems.description: Defines a guidance program with the specified <name> using the predefine guidance program <type> (See Guidance Program Types.) The program can then be selected for use in a phase by specifying use_program <name>.

configItems.name: guidance_delay
configItems.description: Specifies the elapsed time since the start of the phase when guidance commands should start being computed. This is useful during lift-off and other phases where pursuit of the target is not desirable.

configItems.name: on_entry
configItems.description: These commands define scripts to be executed when entering and exiting the phase.

configItems.name: on_update
configItems.description: Define a script to be executed on every phase update.

configItems.name: guidance_target
configItems.description: Overrides the top-level guide_to_truth command for the current phase. This is expanded to include the options:

configItems.name: aimpoint_altitude_offset
configItems.description: Modify the aimpoint to be above or below the perceived target location. This is typically used to create an air burst.

configItems.name: aimpoint_azimuth_offset
configItems.description: These commands provide a method to produce an aimpoint that is laterally offset from the perceived target location. This is typically used to meet some tactical requirement.

configItems.name: aimpoint_evaluation_interval
configItems.description: Controls how often a new aimpoint is computed when using aimpoint_azimuth_offset and aimpoint_range_offset. This is a fairly time-consuming operation that does not need to be performed on every call to the guidance computer.

configItems.name: allow_route_following
configItems.description: If true, the computer will follow a route if it has been provided to the associated mover. If the mover does not have a route then this command has no effect. Conventional target point selection will resume at the end of the route.

configItems.name: use_program
configItems.description: Specifies that the named program defined in a program block outside of the phase will be used. It is useful to define a program if it is going to be used in multiple phases.

configItems.name: proportional_navigation_gain
configItems.description: Specifies the gain for proportional navigation. A value of zero indicates proportional navigation will not be performed.

configItems.name: proportional_navigation_limit_angle
configItems.description: Specifies the 3D aspect angle of the target with respect to the weapon at which the navigation method will switch between proportional and velocity pursuit. Proportional navigation will be used if the target aspect angle is less than or equal to this value, otherwise velocity pursuit will be used.

configItems.name: proportional_navigation_method
configItems.description: Specifies whether additional acceleration should be commanded because of current target acceleration.

configItems.name: velocity_pursuit_gain
configItems.description: Specifies the gain for velocity pursuit navigation. A value of zero indicates velocity pursuit navigation will not be performed.

configItems.name: g_bias
configItems.description: Specifies the bias factor used to overcome gravity. This is typically used during mid-course to prevent the trajectory from sagging. If zero is specified then gravity bias will not be applied.

configItems.name: lateral_g_bias
configItems.description: Specifies the bias factor used skew the horizontal component of the trajectory in a particular direction. If zero is specified then gravity bias will not be applied.

configItems.name: commanded_altitude
configItems.description: Specifies a commanded altitude. Typically used to climb or dive to a cruise altitude and hold the altitude. The altitude reference tag (’msl’, or ‘above mean sea level’; ‘agl’, or ‘above ground level’) may be omitted, in which case ‘msl’ is assumed.

configItems.name: commanded_azimuth_offset
configItems.description: Specifies the azimuth angle to the target that should be maintained. The angle is defined to be the angle in the local horizontal plane between the weapon velocity vector and the line-of-sight vector from the weapon to the target. (This is consistent with the ‘target_azimuth’ conditional tests in the next_phase command.)

configItems.name: commanded_flight_path_angle
configItems.description: Specifies a commanded flight path angle. If from_launch_computer is specified then the value produced by the launch computer will be used (if present).

configItems.name: commanded_mach
configItems.description: Specifies the commanded speed/mach to be used during this phase. Typically used for cruise.

configItems.name: commanded_throttle
configItems.description: Specifies a throttle factor in the range [0..1] that overrides and throttle specification in the mover.

configItems.name: maximum_commanded_g
configItems.description: Specifies the magnitude of the maximum acceleration that can be commanded.

configItems.name: maximum_ascent_rate
configItems.description: Specifies the maximum rate of ascent or descent to be used to reach the commanded_altitude.

configItems.name: maximum_pitch_angle
configItems.description: Specifies the absolute value of the maximum flight path angle that may be used to ascend or descend to the commanded_altitude.

configItems.name: pitch_change_gain
configItems.description: Specifies the gain factor for changing the pitch angle when trying to achieve the commanded_altitude.

configItems.name: next_phase
configItems.description: The next_phase command defines a condition under which a phase transition occurs. A phase block may have multiple next_phase commands to define a number of conditions that might trigger a phase change. The next_phase commands are evaluated on each guidance update and are evaluated in the order specified.

configItems.name: integration_timestep
configItems.description: Specifies the integration timestep to be used. If a value of zero is specified the mover will not break update requests into smaller intervals.

configItems.name: integration_method
configItems.description: Select the method for integrating the equations of motion as one of the following:

configItems.name: compute_all_forces_each_substep
configItems.description: Specify whether Runge-Kutta methods should compute all forces for each integration sub-step. If this is false, then only the gravitational force will be computed for each sub-step, and the aerodynamic and thrust forces will be computed once from the state at the start of the integration step. This option is ignored when the integration_method is trapezoidal. The default value for this option is false, which matches how the WSF_GUIDED_MOVER had been implemented in pre-2.9 versions of AFSIM.

configItems.name: coordinate_frame
configItems.description: Specify the coordinate frame in which the equations of motion are integrated as either:

configItems.name: maintain_inclination
configItems.description: When modeling an orbital launch vehicle (using coordinate_frame eci), the inclination of the parking orbit is a function of the launch latitude and launch azimuth (or heading). For a non-rotating spherical Earth, the inclination of the orbit is defined by:

configItems.name: show_status
configItems.description: Causes a message to be written to standard output whenever a staging operation takes place. This is automatically enabled if debug is also enabled.

configItems.name: show_trajectory
configItems.description: Enables a printout of downrange distance, speed, Mach number, and applied aerodynamic forces to standard output.

configItems.name: align_heading_with_velocity
configItems.description: If true, use the velocity of the owning platform (if non-zero) to determine the projected heading. Otherwise, use orientation.

configItems.name: check_for_ground_impact
configItems.description: Enables internal checking for ground impact. This can be used where the mover is simply being used to model an orbital launch vehicle or the spent stage of a rocket. Formerly one had to define an instance of WSF_GROUND_TARGET_FUSE on such platforms to detect if they crashed into the ground. If this was not done the platform would keep going and never be deleted.

configItems.name: time_history_path
configItems.description: If specified, indicates the path.

configItems.name: aero
configItems.description: Specifies the aerodynamics type name for this stage. Type must be known at initialization time.

configItems.name: empty_mass
configItems.description: Specifies the mass of the stage without fuel.

configItems.name: fuel_mass
configItems.description: Specifies the mass of the fuel on the stage.

configItems.name: total_mass
configItems.description: Specifies the total mass of the stage, which is the sum of empty_mass and fuel_mass but does not include the mass of any upper stages on top of this one (considered payload).

configItems.name: vacuum_thrust
configItems.description: Specifies the thrust of the propulsion system.

configItems.name: vacuum_thrust_table
configItems.description: Defines thrust as a function of time.

configItems.name: reverse_thrust
configItems.description: Indicates the thrust is to be applied in the reverse direction (i.e., it is acting as a braking force instead of a propelling force).

configItems.name: vacuum_specific_impulse
configItems.description: Specify the specific impulse of the propulsion system with respect to a particular condition.

configItems.name: nozzle_exit_area
configItems.description: Specifies the exit area of the engine nozzle. This is used to adjust a sea level or vacuum reference thrust or specific impulse values from the reference value to the value at the current operating altitude.

configItems.name: thrust_duration
configItems.description: Specifies the amount of time the engine will produce the specified thrust.

configItems.name: burn_rate
configItems.description: Specifies the propellant burn rate while thrusting.

configItems.name: burn_rate_table
configItems.description: Defines propellant burn rate as a function of time.

configItems.name: throttle
configItems.description: This provides a function to adjust the current thrust and burn rate (The adjustment is just a multiplication). The dependent value is the non-dimensional throttle factor is greater than or equal to zero. A value of zero corresponds to no thrust and one corresponds to full thrust. Values greater than one are allowed when the base thrust and burn rate values are less than the maximum.

configItems.name: thrust_vectoring_angle_limit
configItems.description: Specifies the maximum angle to which the thrust vector can be steered.

configItems.name: thrust_vectoring_time_limits
configItems.description: Specifies the minimum and maximum times (relative to the ignition time of the current stage) in which thrust vectoring can be employed.

configItems.name: lateral_thrust_gain
configItems.description: Lateral forces may be applied by vectoring the thrust of the engine or through the use of thrusters. These forces typically typically have a large moment arm (the engine is at the end of a rocket and is some distance from the center of gravity) and as such, introduces a rotation which then causes a change in the direction of the velocity vector. This issue is that this model treats the body as a point-mass (See Overview) and does not consider angular rates - it operates by ‘pushing’ the mass to change direction. It takes more force to ‘push’ the mass to change direction by a given angle than it takes to rotate the same amount. Because more force is needed, a higher vectoring angle is needed, thus stealing more thrust from the axial component.

configItems.name: divert_thrust
configItems.description: Specifies the amount of thrust to be considered available from thrusters. The ‘divert’ capability is a trivial implementation of real thrusters. It was initially provided so vehicles could still maneuver at high altitudes where available aerodynamic forces are small or non-existent.

configItems.name: divert_fuel_mass
configItems.description: Specifies the initial mass of fuel available for divert thrust. When divert_thrust is used it will expend the divert fuel until it is no longer available.

configItems.name: divert_fuel_flow_rate
configItems.description: Specifies the rate at which the divert fuel will be used when full divert thrust is employed. If only some of the divert thrust is required to satisfy the current request then the fuel flow rate will be decreased proportionally.

configItems.name: divert_altitude_limits
configItems.description: Specifies the minimum and maximum altitudes in which divert thrust will be considered for use.

configItems.name: pre_ignition_coast_time
configItems.description: Specifies the amount of time that will elapse between the start of the stage and when the engine will ignite.

configItems.name: pre_separation_coast_time
configItems.description: Specifies the amount of time that will elapse between the burnout of this stage and its separation from the vehicle. This command has no effect for single-stage vehicles or the last stage of a multistage vehicle.

configItems.name: ignition_failure_probability
configItems.description: A value in the range [ 0 .. 1 ] that specifies the probability that the engines on this stage will fail to ignite. If ignition fails the results are as follows:

configItems.name: separation_failure_probability
configItems.description: A value in the range [ 0 .. 1 ] that specifies the probability that this stage will be unable to separate from the succeeding stage. If separation fails the results are as follows:

configItems.name: angle_of_attack
configItems.description: By default the model simply aligns the platform with the velocity vector with no angle-of-attack (See Overview). This provides a mechanism to apply an angle of attack.

configItems.name: skid_to_turn
configItems.description: By default the model simply aligns the vehicle with the velocity vector with no roll (See Overview) ‘bank_to_turn’ indicates that a bank angle should be imposed. This angle is proportional to the amount of sideways aerodynamic forces being applied.

configItems.name: on_stage_ignition
configItems.description: Process the ignition of stage ‘aStage’.

configItems.name: on_stage_burnout
configItems.description: Process the burnout of stage ‘aStage’.

configItems.name: on_stage_separation
configItems.description: Process the separation of stage ‘aStage’.

configItems.name: damage_radius
configItems.description: Specifies the radius over which the beam is effective. If this is smaller than the beam size, only that part of the beam incident within the circular region will be used for lethality calculations. If it is larger than the beam size, the entire beam will be used. If specified, the area represented by the damage radius will be used in the energy density calculation. If not specified, the full beam size will be used in the energy density calculation.

configItems.name: minimum_energy
configItems.description: Specifies the minimum energy deposition on target necessary to apply the lethality to the target.

configItems.name: minimum_energy_density
configItems.description: Specifies the minimum energy density (in j/cm^2 or equivalent) deposition on target necessary to apply the lethality to the target.

configItems.name: pk_energy_table
configItems.description: Define a probability of kill vs. threshold energy table. The table should have the following form:

configItems.name: manage_kills
configItems.description: Tells the simulation whether it can kill and remove platforms. For an API-based simulation, this should be disabled, otherwise, it should be enabled.

configItems.name: update_interval
configItems.description: If non-zero, specifies a periodic time interval at which the simulation will call the mover. If zero then the mover will be called only when it is necessary to determine the position of the containing platform.

configItems.name: update_time_tolerance
configItems.description: When a position update is requested by the simulation, if the time since the previous update is less than or equal to this value then the mover will ignore the update.

configItems.name: follower_mover
configItems.description: The name of the predefined follower mover.

configItems.name: waypoint_mover
configItems.description: The name of the predefined waypoint mover (i.e., WSF_AIR_MOVER, WSF_GROUND_MOVER, or WSF_SURFACE_MOVER).

configItems.name: current_mover
configItems.description: Sets the current mover to either the follower mover or the waypoint mover.

configItems.name: auto_switch
configItems.description: If the current mover is the follower and the lead no longer exists then switch back to the waypoint mover and return to the given route entering at the closest point.

configItems.name: coast_time
configItems.description: Specifies the maximum amount of time that may elapse between updates before a track is dropped.

configItems.name: filter
configItems.description: A filter can be used to take an incoming video stream to produce smoothed position and velocity estimates. <filter-type> can be one of the Predefined Filter Types or a filter derived from one of those types.

configItems.name: reports_velocity
configItems.description: Indicates if velocity is reported in the produced tracks.

configItems.name: reports_type
configItems.description: Indicates if ‘type’ is to be reported in the produced tracks.

configItems.name: reports_side
configItems.description: Indicates if ‘side’ is to be reported in the produced tracks.

configItems.name: reports_bearing_elevation
configItems.description: Indicates that tracks are to be populated with bearing and elevation instead of location data.

configItems.name: message_length
configItems.description: Specify the logical length assigned to the track messages that are created from the image.

configItems.name: message_priority
configItems.description: Specify the priority assigned to the track messages that are created from the image.

configItems.name: include_unstable_residual_covariance
configItems.description: When a filter is employed, the state covariance and residual covariance are not reliable during initial creation and perhaps for one or two updates (the number depends on the filter employed). When these values are false (the default), these unreliable values are not passed to the output track.

configItems.name: target_recognition
configItems.description: Enable this processor’s target recognition capabilities for target detection, classification, and identification.

configItems.name: launched_platform_type
configItems.description: As documented in WSF_EXPLICIT_WEAPON, this command specifies the type of platform to be created when a weapon of this type is launched. Although implicit weapons do not create new platforms, this command may be required if the implicit weapon uses a launch computer. Launch computer documentation will list this requirement if applicable.

configItems.name: quantity
configItems.description: This command is identical to quantity; however, the default value for implicit weapons is different.

configItems.name: interpolate_tables
configItems.description: Specifies whether to apply interpolation to the defined Azimuth-Elevation Table Definition. The type of interpolation can be either linear or logarithmic (see interpolation_type).

configItems.name: interpolation_type
configItems.description: Specifies whether to use linear or logarithmic interpolation when interpolating data in the azimuth elevation tables.

configItems.name: state
configItems.description: Indicates that the following table definition will be used when the platform is in the signature state <state-name>. If <state-name> is default then the subsequent table will be used if the platform is in a signature state that does not match any of the states defined in the signature.

configItems.name: band
configItems.syntax: band [ short | medium | long | very_long | default ]
configItems.description: Indicates that the following table will be used when the sensing infrared sensor is operating with the specified band. Where:

configItems.name: integrator
configItems.description: Specify the integrator used to propagate the state of the platform. Each integrator will have its own set of inputs that control its behavior.

configItems.name: dynamics
configItems.description: Specify the dynamical model used by the WSF_INTEGRATING_SPACE_MOVER. The dynamical model is used to update the state of the owning platform during the simulation. Dynamical models are collections of dynamical terms representing the various contributions to spacecraft dynamics.

configItems.name: term
configItems.description: Specify a term to be added into the orbital dynamics. Each term will have its own set of input commands to control its contribution to the dynamics.

configItems.name: orbital_state
configItems.description: Specify the orbital state in the form of an epoch or epoch_date_time, and one of the following:

configItems.name: position
configItems.description: Sets the initial location of the space mover. This command must be used in conjunction with the velocity command.

configItems.name: velocity
configItems.description: Sets the initial velocity of the space mover. This command must be used in conjunction with the position command.

configItems.name: epoch
configItems.description: Specify the epoch that corresponds with the reference epoch at which the orbital elements are valid.

configItems.name: epoch_date_time
configItems.description: Specify the date and time that corresponds with the reference epoch at which the orbital elements are valid.

configItems.name: designator
configItems.description: Specify the designator for the space mover.

configItems.name: eccentricity
configItems.description: Specify the eccentricity of the orbit. The specified value must be greater than or equal to zero (circular orbit).

configItems.name: semi_major_axis
configItems.description: Specify the semi-major axis of the ellipse defining the orbit.

configItems.name: revolutions_per_day
configItems.description: Specify the number revolutions per day the satellite orbits the Earth.

configItems.name: periapsis_radius
configItems.description: Specify the periapsis radius of the ellipse defining the orbit. This is the smallest distance between the satellite and the center of the central body.

configItems.name: apoapsis_radius
configItems.description: Specify the apoapsis radius of the ellipse defining the orbit. This is the largest distance between the satellite and the center of the central body.

configItems.name: periapsis_altitude
configItems.description: Specify the periapsis altitude of the ellipse defining the orbit. This is the smallest distance between the satellite and the surface of the central body.

configItems.name: apoapsis_altitude
configItems.description: Specify the apoapsis altitude of the ellipse defining the orbit. This is the largest distance between the satellite and the surface of the central body.

configItems.name: raan
configItems.description: Specify the right ascension of the ascending node (“raan”). This is the angle, measured counterclockwise along the celestial equator from the vernal equinox (the angle of right ascension) that the satellite crosses the equator from south to north (the ascending node).

configItems.name: inclination
configItems.description: Specify the separation angle of the tangent to the orbital plane with the Earth’s axis of rotation.

configItems.name: mean_anomaly
configItems.description: Specify the angular location of the satellite in its orbit at the epoch time. This angle is measured from the periapsis and represents the angle the satellite would traverse at a constant angular rate.

configItems.name: true_anomaly
configItems.description: Specify the angular location of the satellite in its orbit at the epoch time. This angle is measured from the periapsis and represents the true angular location of the satellite.

configItems.name: argument_of_periapsis
configItems.description: Specify the angle of the perigee (periapsis) with respect to the Earth’s surface. This angle is measured from the ascending node.

configItems.name: descriptor
configItems.description: Specify an arbitrary descriptor (tag) for the space vehicle.

configItems.name: initial_state
configItems.description: Set the initial state of the platform using ECI kinematics.

configItems.name: j2000
