configItems.description: Specify that the initial kinematics are given in the J2000 frame. If this command is absent, the specified kinematics are taken to be in the ECI frame.

configItems.name: integrator
configItems.description: Specify the integrator used to propagate the state of the platform. Each integrator will have its own set of inputs that control its behavior.

configItems.name: dynamics
configItems.description: Specify the dynamical model used by the WSF_INTEGRATING_SPACE_MOVER. The dynamical model is used to update the state of the owning platform during the simulation. Dynamical models are collections of dynamical terms representing the various contributions to spacecraft dynamics.

configItems.name: term
configItems.description: Specify a term to be added into the orbital dynamics. Each term will have its own set of input commands to control its contribution to the dynamics.

configItems.name: conjunction_setup
configItems.description: Set this spacecraft’s initial conditions such that a conjunction with a given target spacecraft will occur at a specified time. During initialization an attempt will be made to find a solution with the given boundary conditions. If successful, this platform’s state will be set so that the specified conjunction occurs. If there is no solution (for example, the orbit would take the satellite through the Earth), the velocity of the spacecraft will be set to a default value (see below).

configItems.name: from_lla
configItems.description: Set the initial position of this spacecraft to the given latitude, longitude and altitude. If there is no solution to the conjunction, the velocity of the spacecraft will be set to that of a circular orbit with a heading of 90 degrees.

configItems.name: from_eci
configItems.description: Set the initial position of this spacecraft to the given position in the ECI frame. If there is no solution to the conjunction, the velocity of the spacecraft will be set to that of a circular orbit with a heading of 90 degrees.

configItems.name: from_initial
configItems.description: Set the initial position of this spacecraft using other means to specify the initial orbit of the spacecraft. If there is no solution to the conjunction, the velocity of the spacecraft will be set to that provided by the other initialization methods.

configItems.name: with_target
configItems.description: Specify the name of the target platform of the conjunction. This spacecraft will move to the position of the target platform at the time specified in the at_time command. The specified target must be the name of a platform that moves in the space spatial domain.

configItems.name: at_time
configItems.description: Specify the time at which this spacecraft should suffer a conjunction with the specified target.

configItems.name: tolerance
configItems.description: Specify the tolerance for the conjunction solution. The default value of the tolerance is 1.0e-9.

configItems.name: attitude_controller
configItems.description: Specify the attitude controller for the platform. All platforms having a WSF_SPACE_MOVER or WSF_NORAD_SPACE_MOVER will have an attitude controller of some kind. If no attitude controller block is specified, the mover will operate as if the instant attitude controller was selected.

configItems.name: maneuvering
configItems.description: Specifiy a model for executing orbital maneuvers in space.

configItems.name: mission_sequence
configItems.description: Specify a sequence of pre-determined orbital mission events. The first mission event specified is executed first, then the second, etc. An optional constraint can be specified to delay execution of the sequence; otherwise the mission event will begin executing at the creation time of the platform.

configItems.name: define_offset
configItems.description: Define the offset name and location on the intersection mesh associated with the target area of interest (see example above).

configItems.name: intersect_mesh
configItems.description: Define the file for the intersection mesh associated with this processor.

configItems.name: atmospheric_attenuation
configItems.description: The fraction of the signal (in the closed range 0 to 1) that is attenuated per unit of distance traveled at sea level. The attenuation is adjusted to account for the density of air with the change in a altitude.

configItems.name: background_radiance
configItems.description: Specifies the radiance of the background. If ‘dynamic’ is specified then the experimental dynamic background model will be used. The dynamic model is currently valid only for targets at a positive elevation angle from from the sensor (i.e.: looking up at something like a satellite).

configItems.name: background_radiance_below_horizon
configItems.description: These two commands provide an alternative to the fixed background radiance provided by background_radiance. This is useful for airborne sensors where the sensor may be looking up and the sky is the background, or looking down where the ground is the background.

configItems.name: background_transition_angle
configItems.description: This command is used along with background_radiance_above_horizon and background_radiance_below_horizon to specify a region where the transition is made from using the below horizon and above horizon background radiance values. The specified angles are relative to the local angle to the horizon with positive values being above the horizon and negative values being below the horizon. If the target is within the transition region defined by these angles, the resulting background radiance will be linearly interpolated between the above horizon and below horizon values.

configItems.name: band
configItems.description: Define the band of radiation that the sensor will detect. The wavelengths of the bands are defined as follows:

configItems.name: detect_negative_contrast
configItems.description: Declares if the sensor will detect targets who contrast versus the background is negative (i.e. the radiant intensity of the target is less than the radiant intensity of the background). If this is true then a negative contrast will be treated as positive, and thus potentially be detected. If this is false, then a negative contrast will be clamped to zero and detection will not occur.

configItems.name: detection_threshold
configItems.description: Defines the ratio of signal to noise required to declare a successful detection.

configItems.name: noise_equivalent_irradiance
configItems.description: The “noise equivalent irradiance’ (NEI) of the receiver.

configItems.name: antenna_pattern
configItems.description: Defines the name of a pseudo-antenna pattern (defined with the antenna_pattern command, which can be used to account for aspect-dependent effects caused by the aperture through which the sensor is looking.

configItems.name: internal_loss
configItems.description: Defines an additional constant loss that can be applied to the computation.

configItems.name: orbital_state
configItems.description: Specify the orbital state in the form of an epoch or epoch_date_time, and one of the following:

configItems.name: position
configItems.description: Sets the initial location of the space mover. This command must be used in conjunction with the velocity command.

configItems.name: velocity
configItems.description: Sets the initial velocity of the space mover. This command must be used in conjunction with the position command.

configItems.name: epoch
configItems.description: Specify the epoch that corresponds with the reference epoch at which the orbital elements are valid.

configItems.name: epoch_date_time
configItems.description: Specify the date and time that corresponds with the reference epoch at which the orbital elements are valid.

configItems.name: designator
configItems.description: Specify the designator for the space mover.

configItems.name: eccentricity
configItems.description: Specify the eccentricity of the orbit. The specified value must be greater than or equal to zero (circular orbit).

configItems.name: semi_major_axis
configItems.description: Specify the semi-major axis of the ellipse defining the orbit.

configItems.name: revolutions_per_day
configItems.description: Specify the number revolutions per day the satellite orbits the Earth.

configItems.name: periapsis_radius
configItems.description: Specify the periapsis radius of the ellipse defining the orbit. This is the smallest distance between the satellite and the center of the central body.

configItems.name: apoapsis_radius
configItems.description: Specify the apoapsis radius of the ellipse defining the orbit. This is the largest distance between the satellite and the center of the central body.

configItems.name: periapsis_altitude
configItems.description: Specify the periapsis altitude of the ellipse defining the orbit. This is the smallest distance between the satellite and the surface of the central body.

configItems.name: apoapsis_altitude
configItems.description: Specify the apoapsis altitude of the ellipse defining the orbit. This is the largest distance between the satellite and the surface of the central body.

configItems.name: raan
configItems.description: Specify the right ascension of the ascending node (“raan”). This is the angle, measured counterclockwise along the celestial equator from the vernal equinox (the angle of right ascension) that the satellite crosses the equator from south to north (the ascending node).

configItems.name: inclination
configItems.description: Specify the separation angle of the tangent to the orbital plane with the Earth’s axis of rotation.

configItems.name: mean_anomaly
configItems.description: Specify the angular location of the satellite in its orbit at the epoch time. This angle is measured from the periapsis and represents the angle the satellite would traverse at a constant angular rate.

configItems.name: true_anomaly
configItems.description: Specify the angular location of the satellite in its orbit at the epoch time. This angle is measured from the periapsis and represents the true angular location of the satellite.

configItems.name: argument_of_periapsis
configItems.description: Specify the angle of the perigee (periapsis) with respect to the Earth’s surface. This angle is measured from the ascending node.

configItems.name: descriptor
configItems.description: Specify an arbitrary descriptor (tag) for the space vehicle.

configItems.name: orbit
configItems.description: Specify a Two Line Element (TLE) that defines mean orbital elements and other data used to propagate a satellite. Two Line Elements are usually acquired from an existing source such as the Spacetrak database (http://www.space-track.org) or Celestrak (http://www.celestrak.com/NORAD/elements). Unlike ordinary AFSIM inputs, the column formatting, field length, and character format must be exactly as specified below.:

configItems.name: central_body
configItems.description: Specify the central body and related ellipsoid model that defines the origin of the coordinate system used for orbital propagation. Depending on the propagator type, propagation is affected by the central body’s associated gravitational parameter.

configItems.name: polar_offset_angles
configItems.description: Specify the central_body’s polar offset angles ( and , respectively) of the Celestial Intermediate Pole (CIP) with respect to the WCS (ITRS) coordinate system. Providing these values (of the order of tenths of arc-seconds) enables very precise conversions between ECI and WCS coordinates.

configItems.name: central_body
configItems.description: Specify the central body and related ellipsoid model to be used by simulation platforms. Options for <central body type> are the following:

configItems.name: polar_offset_angles
configItems.description: Specify the central_body’s polar offset angles ( and , respectively) of the Celestial Intermediate Pole (CIP) with respect to the WCS (ITRS) coordinate system. Providing these values (of the order of tenths of arc-seconds) enables very highly accurate conversions between ECI and WCS coordinates.

configItems.name: solar_flux
configItems.description: Set the 10.7 cm solar flux, in units of , that will be used by this atmosphere model. Reasonable values for this are in the range [50, 400]. This value is the average of the flux on the day of interest.

configItems.name: average_solar_flux
configItems.description: Set the average of the 10.7 cm solar flux, in units of , that will be used by this atmosphere model. Reasonable value for this are in the range [50, 400]. This value is the 81 day running average flux centered on the day of interest.

configItems.name: geomagnetic_index
configItems.description: Set the geomagnetic activity, . The provided value must be in the range [0, 9].

configItems.name: command_chain
configItems.description: Maps a command chain name to a slot group name, which allows platforms to form slot groups based on their command chain.

configItems.name: maximum_range
configItems.description: Defines the maximum range between the receiver and transmitter. This value will override any maximum_range explicitly defined in an antenna block. For JTIDS terminals, the Normal range is 300 nm and the Extended range is 500 nm. All JTIDS units in the same network should have identical range settings; however, this model does not enforce this restriction.

configItems.name: time_per_slot
configItems.description: Overrides the amount of time per time slot.

configItems.name: slot_size
configItems.description: Overrides the amount of data than can be contained in a slot (at the ‘normal’ packing density).

configItems.name: sets_per_frame
configItems.description: Overrides the number of interleaved sets per frame. Must be a value greater than zero.

configItems.name: slots_per_set
configItems.description: Overrides the number of slots per set within a frame. Must be a value greater than one.

configItems.name: network
configItems.description: The JTIDS network number in the range [0, 127].

configItems.name: tsec
configItems.description: The JTIDS cryptovariable specified for transmission security (TSEC) in the range [0, 127]. This model does not perform encryption/decryption of data. This value is used in Link-16 message headers.

configItems.name: msec
configItems.description: The JTIDS cryptovariable specified for message security (MSEC) in the range [0, 127]. This model does not perform encryption/decryption of data. This value is used in Link-16 message headers.

configItems.name: queue_limit
configItems.description: The maximum transmit queue size in the range [0, infinity].

configItems.name: packing_limit
configItems.description: The packing format for messages, which affects the number of time slots needed to transmit a message. In Extended Range Mode (ERM) (i.e. a maximum range setting of 500 nm), a JTIDS terminal does not support the p2dp and p4sp packing structure. This model does not enforce this restriction.

configItems.name: relay_slot_offset
configItems.description: The offset of the paired relay slot group from the source slot group. The offset should be in the range of [1, infinity].

configItems.name: npg
configItems.description: The network participation group. The NPG may be either:

configItems.name: slots_per_frame
configItems.description: Slots per frame provides a simplified way to allocate TSBs. The number of slots per frame must in the range [1, terminal’s number of slots per frame].

configItems.name: per_unit_slots_per_frame
configItems.description: The number of fractional slots that this slot group will use per frame.

configItems.name: receive_only
configItems.description: Indicates that this slot group can receive only.

configItems.name: receive_slot_block
configItems.description: Creates a receive slot block with the specified set (e.g., A, B, C), slot index, and recurrence rate number (RRN). The recurrence rate number must be in the range [1, 15].

configItems.name: transmit_slot_block
configItems.description: Creates a transmit slot block with the specified set (e.g., A, B, C), slot index, and recurrence rate number (RRN). The recurrence rate number must be in the range [1, 15].

configItems.name: process_noise_sigmas_XYZ
configItems.description: Defines the filter’s noise standard deviation for the three directions. The values are accelerations in the entity coordinate system (ECS) of the tracked platform. They must be entered in meters per second squared. See Process Noise Recommended Values below for example inputs.

configItems.name: process_noise_model
configItems.description: Selects the filter’s process noise model, either one based on a constant velocity of the target or a constant acceleration of the target.

configItems.name: debug
configItems.description: Writes debugging information to the standard output.

configItems.name: range_measurement_sigma
configItems.description: Defines the standard deviation that is applied to the measurement’s range prior to filtering.

configItems.name: bearing_measurement_sigma
configItems.description: Defines the standard deviation that is applied to the measurement’s bearing prior to filtering.

configItems.name: elevation_measurement_sigma
configItems.description: Defines the standard deviation that is applied to the measurement’s elevation prior to filtering.

configItems.name: debug
configItems.description: Writes debugging information to the standard output.

configItems.name: range_measurement_sigma
configItems.description: Defines the standard deviation that is applied to the measurement’s range prior to filtering.

configItems.name: bearing_measurement_sigma
configItems.description: Defines the standard deviation that is applied to the measurement’s bearing prior to filtering.

configItems.name: process_noise_sigmas_XY
configItems.description: Defines the filter’s noise standard deviation for the two directions. The values must be entered in meters.

configItems.name: orbital_state
configItems.description: Specify the orbital state in the form of an epoch or epoch_date_time, and one of the following:

configItems.description: Sets the initial location of the space mover. This command must be used in conjunction with the velocity command.

configItems.name: periapsis_altitude
configItems.description: Specify the periapsis altitude of the ellipse defining the orbit. This is the smallest distance between the satellite and the surface of the central body.

configItems.name: apoapsis_altitude

configItems.description: Specify the angle of the perigee (periapsis) with respect to the Earth’s surface. This angle is measured from the ascending node.

configItems.name: polar_offset_angles

Providing these values (of the order of tenths of arc-seconds) enables very precise conversions between ECI and WCS coordinates.

configItems.name: detailed_debug
configItems.description: Enables debug output to the standard output.

configItems.name: prefer_canopy_up
configItems.description: Causes the platform to roll to the local vertical at all times. Mutually exclusive to bank_to_turn.

configItems.name: bank_to_turn
configItems.description: Causes the platform to roll into the acceleration vector, but still prefers the vertical when not accelerating in a turn. Mutually exclusive to prefer_canopy_up.

configItems.name: broach_at_sea_level
configItems.description: This mover was originally developed to define a torpedo mover. However, the capability of the model is such that it can be used above sea level. This flag assures that the motion must remain below local sea level, once subsurface.

configItems.name: target_speed
configItems.description: Once supplied, the platform will accelerate or decelerate to match the target (desired) speed, subject to maximum_linear_acceleration constraint.

configItems.name: initial_speed
configItems.description: Initial linear speed. After initialization, speed is varied to maintain target_speed.

configItems.name: initial_flight_path_angle
configItems.description: Initial flight path angle. After initialization, flight path angle will vary to guide to a desired waypoint in a defined route.

configItems.name: maximum_linear_acceleration
configItems.description: Defines the linear (velocity direction) acceleration limit constraint.

configItems.name: maximum_radial_acceleration
configItems.description: Defines the radial (normal to velocity direction) acceleration limit constraint. This constraint is imposed simultaneously with maximum_body_turn_rate, the most restrictive is used.

configItems.name: maximum_body_roll_rate
configItems.description: Defines the maximum rate at which the platform will try to capture desired target bank angle.

configItems.name: maximum_body_turn_rate
configItems.description: Defines the maximum rate at which the velocity vector will rotate in three-dimensional space. This constraint is imposed simultaneously with maximum_radial_acceleration, the most restrictive is used.

configItems.name: velocity_pursuit_gain
configItems.description: Defines the factor of proportion between target azimuth and elevation (in radians), and the applied lateral or vertical acceleration (in m/sec^2) to null the velocity vector to point at the target. See comments in header above.

configItems.name: waypoint_switch_on_ground_turning_radius
configItems.description: If this input value is set to true, only horizontal offsets are considered when deciding to advance to the next waypoint in a route; vertical miss values are ignored. If set false, then a 3-dimensional slant offset is considered when deciding if a waypoint is sufficiently close to be considered “hit”.

configItems.name: proportional_navigation_gain
configItems.description: Defines the factor of proportion between the target line-of-sight-rate (in rad/sec), and the applied lateral or vertical acceleration (in m/sec^2) to null the velocity vector to intercept the target’s future position at time of intercept. See comments in header above.

configItems.name: use_route
configItems.description: Supplies the name of the route to follow. The route is assumed to be a predefined absolute route.

configItems.name: background_irradiance
configItems.description: These commands are used to define the background irradiance used to calculate the background noise due to the reflectance of ambient light from the target into the receiver (See the section ‘Computation of Noise’ below for more details.)

configItems.name: integration_gain
configItems.description: Defines the gain achieved by integrating multiple pulses.

configItems.name: detection_threshold
configItems.description: Defines the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) that results in a Pd of 0.5.

configItems.name: detection_probability
configItems.description: If this command is provided it defines a table that is used to determine the probability of detection as a function of signal-to-noise ratio. The user must provide pairs of numbers (signal-to-noise ratio and probability of detection, in that order) that define the curve of Pd vs. SNR.

configItems.name: aperture_diameter
configItems.description: Defines the aperture diameter of the LADAR transmitter. Changing this parameter controls the diffraction-induced beam spread, affecting the beam size on target. The larger the aperture diameter, the smaller the beam on target, and the greater the energy density (energy density ~ (aperture diameter^2)).

configItems.name: optics_transmission_factor
configItems.description: Defines the percentage of the transmitted laser light that passes through the transmitter optics.

configItems.name: beam_divergence_angle
configItems.description: Specifies the ‘beam width’ of the the transmitted beam.

configItems.name: quantum_efficiency
configItems.description: The fraction of the signal (number of photons) that is converted into photoelectrons.

configItems.name: detector_gain
configItems.description: The gain of the detector.

configItems.name: circuit_capacitance
configItems.description: These are optional commands used to specify the data needed compute the thermal noise component as described in the ‘Computation of Noise’ section below. Both commands must be specified to enable computation of thermal noise.

configItems.name: dark_current
configItems.description: These are optional commands used to specify data needed to compute dark count term in background noise component as described in the ‘Computation of Noise’ section below). One or the other may be specified depending on preference.

configItems.name: focal_length
configItems.description: Specifies the focal length of the receiver optical system.

configItems.name: detector_size
configItems.description: Specifies the length of one side of the physical detector. It is assumed the detector is square.

configItems.name: aero_optic_transmission_factor
configItems.description: For laser communications devices on air platforms, specify the fraction of laser energy transmitted through turbulent air near the aircraft.

configItems.name: atmospheric_structure
configItems.description: Specify the atmospheric structure model, or function, used to compute atmospheric turbulence. It has units of .

configItems.name: attenuation
configItems.description: Reference a model (typically WSF_OPTICAL_ATTENUATION) for computing atmospheric attenuation.

configItems.name: attenuation_transmission_factor
configItems.description: Specify the fraction of laser energy transmitted through the atmosphere from transmitter to receiver.

configItems.name: background_radiance
configItems.description: Specify a background spectral radiance at the receiver aperture (see Background Values for Wavelengths of Interest, below)

configItems.name: background_irradiance
configItems.description: Specify a background spectral irradiance at the receiver aperture (see Background Values for Wavelengths of Interest, below)

configItems.name: turbulence_transmission_factor
configItems.description: Specify the fraction of laser energy transmitted that is not lost due to turbulence.

configItems.name: show_link_budget
configItems.description: If enabled, print a summary link budget when a message is transmitted.

configItems.name: average_power
configItems.description: Specify the average output power of the transmitter. The transmitter peak power will be calculated based on the modulation_type-dependent duty cycle.

configItems.name: aperture_diameter
configItems.description: Defines the aperture diameter of the transmitter. Changing this parameter controls the diffraction-induced beam spread, affecting the beam size. The larger the aperture diameter, the smaller the beam on target, and the greater the energy density (energy density ~ (aperture diameter^2)).

configItems.name: beamwidth
configItems.description: Specifies the ‘beam width’ of the the transmitted beam.

configItems.name: modulation_type
configItems.description: Specify the Modulation Type to utilize when computing data transfer rate and duty cycle of the transmitter.

configItems.name: ppm_order
configItems.description: When using the ppm modulation_type, specify the ppm order. This value must be greater than or equal to 2, and it is usually equal to a power of 2 (2, 4, 8, 16, etc.).

configItems.name: slot_width
configItems.description: Specify the number of communication “slots” or possible pulse widths, per second; or alternately, specify the time width of a slot. The two are reciprocals of one another.

configItems.name: optics_loss
configItems.description: Defines the fraction of the transmitted laser light that passes through the transmitter optics. This factor typically takes into account optical element transmission and reflection losses.

configItems.name: wavefront_loss
configItems.description: Specifies the fraction of laser light that passes through a the transmitter optical path as a function of wavefront error (also, see wavefront_error)

configItems.name: wavefront_error
configItems.description: Specify the wavefront error of the optical path in fractions of a wave. If this value is specified, the value for wavefront_transmission_factor will be calculated according to the equation:

configItems.name: pointing_loss
configItems.description: Specify the fraction of laser light transmitted after pointing errors are considered.

configItems.name: bandpass
configItems.description: Specify the optical bandpass for transmission of light to the receiver. It will typically be a very narrow value about the wavelength of the transmitter laser wavelength.

configItems.name: quantum_efficiency
configItems.description: The fraction of the incident signal photons that is converted into photoelectrons.

configItems.name: responsivity
configItems.description: An alternative to quantum_efficiency, responsivity is the number of photocurrent amps generated per watt of incident power. It is related to quantum_efficiency through the relation:

configItems.name: detector_gain
configItems.description: The gain of the detector.

configItems.name: circuit_resistance
configItems.description: These are optional commands used to compute the thermal noise component as described in the Computation of Noise section below. Circuit_temperature must be specified, along with either circuit_capacitance or circuit_resistance.

configItems.name: dark_current
configItems.description: These are optional commands used to specify the amplified “bulk” dark count term in background noise component as described in the Computation of Noise section below). One or the other may be specified depending on preference.

configItems.name: excess_noise_factor
configItems.description: For an avalanche photodiode (APD) receiver, specify the excess noise factor (gain value), due to non-ideal amplification, when computing photoelectrons from amplified noise.

configItems.name: surface_dark_current
configItems.description: These are optional commands used to specify the non-amplified, or “surface” dark count term in background noise component as described in the Computation of Noise section below). One or the other may be specified depending on preference.

configItems.name: firing_time
configItems.description: Specify the firing time per shot.

configItems.name: firing_update_interval
configItems.description: Specify the interval at which the engagement will be updated and fluence on target integrated.

configItems.name: number_of_shots
configItems.description: Specify the number of shots the laser can fire before it must cool down for a specified interval (see cooling_time). Either these inputs are used, or they are determined automatically with a thermal_system.

configItems.name: cooling_time
configItems.description: Specify a cooldown time, starting after the specified number_of_shots has been exhausted. Once this time interval has elapsed, the original shot number will be restored.

configItems.name: cooling_update_interval
configItems.description: Specify an interval to check whether the cooling cycle is complete.

configItems.name: efficiency
configItems.description: Specifies the efficiency of the HEL system for converting input power into output laser power.

configItems.name: high_temperature_limit
configItems.description: This is the temperature at which firing ceases and cooldown begins (the thermal system does not accept heat above this temperature).

configItems.name: low_temperature_limit
configItems.description: This is the temperature at which maximum firing time is available (the thermal system does not cool below this temperature).

configItems.name: minimum_total_firing_time
configItems.description: When in a cooldown cycle, the weapon will not be available until this much firing time has been restored to the system.

configItems.name: minimum_delta_altitude
configItems.description: Specifies the minimum and maximum difference between the target and the weapon. (Target higher than launch altitude is positive delta.)

configItems.name: minimum_opening_speed
configItems.description: Specifies the minimum and maximum approaching and receding target rates the weapon can engage. (Launcher-to-target distance decreasing is a positive closing speed; launcher-to-target distance increasing is positive opening speed.)

configItems.name: minimum_slant_range
configItems.description: Specifies the minimum and maximum target ranges the weapon can engage.

configItems.name: maximum_time_of_flight
configItems.description: Specifies the weapon’s maximum allowed time of flight.

configItems.name: maximum_boresight_angle
configItems.description: Specifies the weapon’s maximum off-boresight angle capability.

configItems.name: thrust_duration
configItems.description: SAM system missile thrust duration.

configItems.name: coast_duration
configItems.description: SAM system missile coast duration.

configItems.name: burnout_speed
configItems.description: SAM system missile burn-out velocity.

configItems.name: minimum_terminal_speed
configItems.description: The slowest speed at which the SAM still exhibits adequate terminal maneuver capability.

configItems.name: c2
configItems.description: Specifies if the platform is a C-2 platform. This is used to populate some Tadil-J fields.

configItems.name: callsign
configItems.description: Specifies the platform’s callsign used to populate some Tadil-J fields.

configItems.name: comm
configItems.description: Specifies the name of the WSF_JTIDS_TERMINAL which is used to communicate.

configItems.name: ignore_surveillance
configItems.description: Specifies if this processor should process J3 series messages as a WsfTrack, populating the track manager.

configItems.name: output_dis
configItems.description: Determines if the messages sent using this processor are also sent over DIS.

configItems.name: output_wsf
configItems.description: Determines if the messages sent using this processor are sent to other WSF platforms. Setting this to no will reduce overhead of Link-16 if DIS output is the primary objective.

configItems.name: decimal_track_number
configItems.description: Specifies the Source Track Number for messages sent using this processor. Must be in the range (0, 32767).

configItems.name: octal_track_number
configItems.description: Specifies the Source Track Number for messages sent using this processor using an octal-integer. Must be in the range (00, 077777).

configItems.name: iff_color_mapping
configItems.description: Defines the mapping of identity types to colors. The identity type must one of the following: pending, unknown, assumed_friend, friend, neutral, suspect, hostile, undefined.

configItems.name: message_processor
configItems.description: Adds a message processor to the Link-16 computer.

configItems.name: command_chain
configItems.description: This command specifies which command chain is used to receive and send messages for this message processor. Each message processor must specify a command chain. In turn, each command chain must be linked to a distinct Slot Group Commands on the WSF_JTIDS_TERMINAL. This defines a mapping between the slot group and the messages which are sent and received over the slot group. This command is required for each message processor.

configItems.name: script
configItems.description: If a script in this format is defined, it will be executed whenever this message processor sends a message. The primary use for this is to customize the message before it is sent by changing field values. This example sets the ‘flight-leader’ field in each sent message:

configItems.name: network
configItems.description: The JTIDS network number in the range [0, 127].

configItems.name: npg
configItems.description: The network participation in the range [0, 512].

configItems.name: slot_number
configItems.description: The slot number packed into the JTIDS header. This value may usually be ignored.

configItems.name: msec
configItems.description: The JTIDS MSEC value in the range [0, 127].

configItems.name: tsec
configItems.description: The JTIDS TSEC value in the range [0, 127].

configItems.name: environment
configItems.description: Used to explicitly specify what type of PPLI to send. If unspecified, the platform’s mover will be used to determine the message type to send.

configItems.name: land_or_point
configItems.description: Used to explicitly specify what type of land PPLI to send when the environment command was not set and the platform’s mover is being used to determine the message type to send.

configItems.name: ignore_reporting_responsibility
configItems.description: If true, reporting responsibility rules for tracks are ignored.

configItems.name: maximum_send_interval
configItems.description: Specifies the interval to queue unmodified tracks to send. Modified tracks are queued immediately.

configItems.name: send_non_sensor_reports
configItems.description: Specifies whether non-sensor (fused) tracks or raw sensor tracks in the master track list should be sent.

configItems.name: suppress_dead_targets
configItems.description: If true, suppresses the sending of J3 messages for platforms that are fully damaged or no longer in the simulation.

configItems.name: suppress_domain
configItems.description: If specified, tracks from the given domain will not be sent over Link-16.

configItems.name: suppress_sensor
configItems.description: If specified, reports from the named sensor will not be sent over Link-16.

configItems.name: track_number_range
configItems.description: Specifies the range of track numbers used when sending surveillance tracks. Track numbers are formatted XXOOO where X is 0-7 or A-Z and O is 0-7.

configItems.name: report_weapon_quantity_3
configItems.description: These commands are used to set the number of stores and the store type fields in the C2 word of the J13.2 message. The <weapon-name> must match a weapon on the platform in order to find the current quantity. The <integer-value> represents the store type.

configItems.name: detailed_debug
configItems.description: Enables debug output to the standard output.

configItems.name: prefer_canopy_up
configItems.description: Causes the platform to roll to the local vertical at all times. Mutually exclusive to bank_to_turn.

configItems.name: bank_to_turn
configItems.description: Causes the platform to roll into the acceleration vector, but still prefers the vertical when not accelerating in a turn. Mutually exclusive to prefer_canopy_up.

configItems.name: broach_at_sea_level
configItems.description: Betraying the development of this class to model torpedo motion, this flag assures that the motion must remain below local sea level, once subsurface.

configItems.name: target_speed
configItems.description: Once supplied, the platform will accelerate or decelerate match the target speed, subject to maximum_linear_acceleration constraint.

configItems.name: initial_speed
configItems.description: Initial linear speed. After initialization, speed is varied to maintain target_speed.

configItems.name: initial_flight_path_angle
configItems.description: Initial flight path angle. After initialization, flight path angle will vary to guide to desired waypoint.

configItems.name: maximum_linear_acceleration
configItems.description: Defines the linear (velocity direction) acceleration limit constraint.

configItems.name: maximum_lateral_acceleration
configItems.description: Defines the lateral (normal to velocity direction) acceleration limit constraint. This constraint is imposed simultaneously with maximum_axial_body_turn_rate, the most restrictive is used.

configItems.name: maximum_axial_body_roll_rate
configItems.description: Defines the maximum rate at which the platform will try to capture desired target bank angle.

configItems.name: maximum_axial_body_turn_rate
configItems.description: Defines the maximum rate at which the velocity vector will rotate in three-dimensional space. This constraint is imposed simultaneously with maximum_lateral_acceleration, the most restrictive is used.

configItems.name: velocity_pursuit_gain
configItems.description: Defines the factor of proportion between target azimuth and elevation (in radians), and the applied lateral or vertical acceleration (in m/sec^2) to null the velocity vector to point at the target. See comments in header above.

configItems.name: proportional_navigation_gain
configItems.description: Defines the factor of proportion between the target line-of-sight-rate (in rad/sec), and the applied lateral or vertical acceleration (in m/sec^2) to null the velocity vector to intercept the target’s future position at time of intercept. See comments in header above.

configItems.name: use_route
configItems.description: Supplies the name of the route to follow. The route is assumed to be a predefined absolute route.

configItems.name: queuing_method
configItems.description: Specifies how incoming messages are to be queued if all of the servers are busy. A value of none indicates the message will be discarded if no server is available.

configItems.name: number_of_servers
configItems.description: Specifies the maximum number of messages that can be ‘in process’ at any given instant of time. If a new message is received and all the servers are busy, the message will be queued according to the queuing_method

configItems.name: type
configItems.description: Returns true if the supplied message type matches the type from the message. Standard message types are as follows:

configItems.name: subtype
configItems.description: Returns true if the supplied message subtype matches the type from the message.

configItems.name: sensor_name
configItems.description: Returns true if the message is a WSF_TRACK_MESSAGE, WSF_IMAGE_MESSAGE or WSF_VIDEO_MESSAGE, and if the supplied sensor name matches the sensor name from the message.

configItems.name: sensor_type
configItems.description: Returns true if the message is a WSF_TRACK_MESSAGE, WSF_IMAGE_MESSAGE or WSF_VIDEO_MESSAGE, and if the supplied sensor type matches the sensor type from the message.

configItems.name: sensor_mode
configItems.description: Returns true if the message is a WSF_TRACK_MESSAGE, WSF_IMAGE_MESSAGE or WSF_VIDEO_MESSAGE, and if the supplied sensor mode matches the sensor mode from the message.

configItems.name: system_name
configItems.description: Returns true if the message is a WSF_STATUS_MESSAGE and if the supplied system name matches the system name from the message.

configItems.name: sender
configItems.description: Returns true if the sender of the message was one of the identified platforms.

configItems.name: script
configItems.description: Defines a script that returns true if the message is to be selected. The script variable MESSAGE refers to the current message.

configItems.name: delay_time
configItems.description: Specifies the amount of time the message should be delayed before being processed,

configItems.name: ignore_message
configItems.description: Indicates the message should be ignored.

configItems.name: clear_internal_links
configItems.description: Remove all of the currently defined internal links defined by the internal_link or processor commands. This is useful if one wants to reuse an existing platform definition with some modifications.

configItems.name: processor
configItems.description: Specify that messages that originate from this object are to be routed to the specified platform part object on the same platform. This command may be specified multiple times to route the message to multiple recipients.

configItems.name: table
configItems.description: A named ‘table’ block supplies a set of four probabilities to be considered as a set under given conditions, and will be referenced by name elsewhere. It calculates a fifth probability, and assures that the aggregate probability is unity.

configItems.name: probability_of_damage_given_proximity_hit
configItems.description: Specifies the probability threshold for applying damage to the target platform. (A shortcut of “Pd_hit” is also permitted.) A value of 0.90 indicates a 90% likelihood of some damage occurring, or a 10% likelihood of no damage occurring. Only if the threshold for damage is reached, is any further damage probability considered (as below).

configItems.name: probability_of_mk_given_damage
configItems.description: Specifies the probability that the platform (if damaged) will suffer a mobility kill only. (A shortcut of “Pmk_damage” is also permitted.)

configItems.name: probability_of_fk_given_damage
configItems.description: Specifies the probability that the platform (if damaged) will suffer a firepower kill only. (A shortcut of “Pfk_damage” is also permitted.)

configItems.name: probability_of_kk_given_damage
configItems.description: Specifies the probability that the target platform (if damaged) will suffer a catastrophic kill. (A shortcut of “Pkk_damage” is also permitted.)

configItems.name: vulnerability
configItems.description: A ‘vulnerability’ block specifies a degrading effect upon this offensive weapon, if it encounters the existence of countermeasure(s) of type <cm-type> employed by the target for self-protection. This block is accepted as a sub-command within target_type block.

configItems.name: minimum_duration
configItems.description: Specifies the minimum time the CM must be present to have its effect upon the inbound offensive weapon. Default = 0.0, or immediately.

configItems.name: maximum_half_cone_angle
configItems.description: Specifies the maximum field of view angle allowable and still be regarded as a potentially valid CM. This is the 3-D angle measured between the LOS munition-to-CM, and LOS munition-to-target. Default = 180 deg, or always visible.

configItems.name: minimum_distance
configItems.description: Specifies the minimum distance allowable and still be regarded as a potentially valid CM. Measurement is determined by the distance_value setting. Default = 0.

configItems.name: maximum_distance
configItems.description: Specifies the maximum distance allowable and still be regarded as a potentially valid CM. Measurement is determined by the distance_value setting. Default = <huge>.

configItems.name: distance_value
configItems.description: Specifies the type of distance measurement to use in distance constraints. Possibilities are: “missile_to_target”, “countermeasure_to_target”, or “missile_to_countermeasure”. Default = “missile_to_target”.

configItems.name: alternate_table_name
configItems.description: Specifies the name of the table that will replace the table_name in the event that this CM is deemed “effective”. The CM is “effective” if it simultaneously passes the distance, half-cone, and duration tests above.

configItems.name: probability_of_weapon_defeat
configItems.description: Specifies the probability that the given CM type will decoy the munition. The CM must first pass the “effective” criteria above. If this value is non-zero, a one-time random draw will taken for each instance of a CM of this type. If the random draw is successful, the offensive munition will not be diverted, but will instead be immediately removed from the simulation. Constrained to [0.0, 1.0]. Default = 0.0.

configItems.name: target_type
configItems.description: A ‘target_type’ block provides the probabilities to be used and applied only to an engagement of a specific target type. It should contain one table_name to use, and zero or more vulnerability blocks.

configItems.name: table_name
configItems.description: Specifies the name of the probability Table to be referenced for an engagement against the given target type. The Table values will defined outside of the target_type block scope. Default = “default”.

configItems.name: update_interval
configItems.description: Specifies the interval between countermeasure state evaluations, which computes at what time they may be considered as “effective”. Default = 1.0 sec.

configItems.name: subtype
configItems.description: Specify the computation subtype.

configItems.name: output
configItems.description: Specify a form of output to produce for a measure of effectiveness. The allowed values for <output_type> are:

configItems.name: orbital_state
configItems.description: Specify the orbital state in the form of an epoch or epoch_date_time, and one of the following:

configItems.name: position
configItems.description: Sets the initial location of the space mover. This command must be used in conjunction with the velocity command.

configItems.name: velocity
configItems.description: Sets the initial velocity of the space mover. This command must be used in conjunction with the position command.

configItems.name: epoch
configItems.description: Specify the epoch that corresponds with the reference epoch at which the orbital elements are valid.

configItems.name: epoch_date_time
configItems.description: Specify the date and time that corresponds with the reference epoch at which the orbital elements are valid.

configItems.name: designator
configItems.description: Specify the designator for the space mover.

configItems.name: eccentricity
configItems.description: Specify the eccentricity of the orbit. The specified value must be greater than or equal to zero (circular orbit).

configItems.name: semi_major_axis
configItems.description: Specify the semi-major axis of the ellipse defining the orbit.

configItems.name: revolutions_per_day
configItems.description: Specify the number revolutions per day the satellite orbits the Earth.

configItems.name: periapsis_radius
configItems.description: Specify the periapsis radius of the ellipse defining the orbit. This is the smallest distance between the satellite and the center of the central body.

configItems.name: apoapsis_radius
configItems.description: Specify the apoapsis radius of the ellipse defining the orbit. This is the largest distance between the satellite and the center of the central body.

configItems.name: periapsis_altitude
configItems.description: Specify the periapsis altitude of the ellipse defining the orbit. This is the smallest distance between the satellite and the surface of the central body.

configItems.name: apoapsis_altitude
configItems.description: Specify the apoapsis altitude of the ellipse defining the orbit. This is the largest distance between the satellite and the surface of the central body.

configItems.name: raan
configItems.description: Specify the right ascension of the ascending node (“raan”). This is the angle, measured counterclockwise along the celestial equator from the vernal equinox (the angle of right ascension) that the satellite crosses the equator from south to north (the ascending node).

configItems.name: inclination
configItems.description: Specify the separation angle of the tangent to the orbital plane with the Earth’s axis of rotation.

configItems.name: mean_anomaly
configItems.description: Specify the angular location of the satellite in its orbit at the epoch time. This angle is measured from the periapsis and represents the angle the satellite would traverse at a constant angular rate.

configItems.name: true_anomaly
configItems.description: Specify the angular location of the satellite in its orbit at the epoch time. This angle is measured from the periapsis and represents the true angular location of the satellite.

configItems.name: argument_of_periapsis
configItems.description: Specify the angle of the perigee (periapsis) with respect to the Earth’s surface. This angle is measured from the ascending node.

configItems.name: descriptor
configItems.description: Specify an arbitrary descriptor (tag) for the space vehicle.

configItems.name: central_body
configItems.description: Specify the central body and related ellipsoid model that defines the origin of the coordinate system used for orbital propagation. Depending on the propagator type, propagation is affected by the central body’s associated gravitational parameter.

Providing these values (of the order of tenths of arc-seconds) enables very precise conversions between ECI and WCS coordinates.

configItems.name: orbit_color
configItems.description: Specify the color of the orbit.

Two Line Elements are usually acquired from an existing source such as the Spacetrak database (http://www.space-track.org) or Celestrak (http://www.celestrak.com/NORAD/elements). Unlike ordinary AFSIM inputs, the column formatting, field length, and character format must be exactly as specified below.:

configItems.description: Specify the central body and related ellipsoid model to be used by simulation platforms. Options for <central body type> are the following:

configItems.name: polar_offset_angles
configItems.description: Specify the central_body’s polar offset angles ( and , respectively) of the Celestial Intermediate Pole (CIP) with respect to the WCS (ITRS) coordinate system. Providing these values (of the order of tenths of arc-seconds) enables very highly accurate conversions between ECI and WCS coordinates.

configItems.name: heliocentric
configItems.description: Specify use of the wgs_84 gravitational parameter, the egm_96 gravitational parameter, or the heliocentric gravitational parameter for propagation. The heliocentric option is used to simulate bodies orbiting the sun.

configItems.name: debug_output_wsf
configItems.description: Write additional information to standard output that can be processed by the CME tool “sedit’.

configItems.name: debug_output_oe
configItems.description: Write additional information about the orbital elements to standard output.

configItems.name: debug_output_stk
configItems.description: Write additional information to standard output that can be used for comparing the orbit with the Systems Tool Kit (STK) from Analytical Graphics, Inc.

configItems.name: debug_output_xyz
configItems.description: Write additional information to standard output that can be used for comparing the orbit with the Systems Tool Kit (STK) from Analytical Graphics, Inc.

configItems.name: conjunction_setup
configItems.description: Set this spacecraft’s initial conditions such that a conjunction with a given target spacecraft will occur at a specified time. During initialization an attempt will be made to find a solution with the given boundary conditions. If successful, this platform’s state will be set so that the specified conjunction occurs. If there is no solution (for example, the orbit would take the satellite through the Earth), the velocity of the spacecraft will be set to a default value (see below).

configItems.name: from_lla
configItems.description: Set the initial position of this spacecraft to the given latitude, longitude and altitude. If there is no solution to the conjunction, the velocity of the spacecraft will be set to that of a circular orbit with a heading of 90 degrees.

configItems.name: from_eci
configItems.description: Set the initial position of this spacecraft to the given position in the ECI frame. If there is no solution to the conjunction, the velocity of the spacecraft will be set to that of a circular orbit with a heading of 90 degrees.

configItems.name: from_initial
configItems.description: Set the initial position of this spacecraft using other means to specify the initial orbit of the spacecraft. If there is no solution to the conjunction, the velocity of the spacecraft will be set to that provided by the other initialization methods.

configItems.name: with_target
configItems.description: Specify the name of the target platform of the conjunction. This spacecraft will move to the position of the target platform at the time specified in the at_time command. The specified target must be the name of a platform that moves in the space spatial domain.

configItems.name: at_time
configItems.description: Specify the time at which this spacecraft should suffer a conjunction with the specified target.

configItems.name: tolerance
configItems.description: Specify the tolerance for the conjunction solution. The default value of the tolerance is 1.0e-9.

configItems.name: attitude_controller
configItems.description: Specify the attitude controller for the platform. All platforms having a WSF_SPACE_MOVER or WSF_NORAD_SPACE_MOVER will have an attitude controller of some kind. If no attitude controller block is specified, the mover will operate as if the instant attitude controller was selected.

configItems.name: maneuvering
configItems.description: Specifiy a model for executing orbital maneuvers in space.

configItems.name: mission_sequence
configItems.description: Specify a sequence of pre-determined orbital mission events. The first mission event specified is executed first, then the second, etc. An optional constraint can be specified to delay execution of the sequence; otherwise the mission event will begin executing at the creation time of the platform.

configItems.name: subtype
configItems.description: Specify the computation subtype.

configItems.name: output
configItems.description: Specify a form of output to produce for a measure of effectiveness. The allowed values for <output_type> are:

configItems.name: subtype
configItems.description: Specify the computation subtype.

configItems.name: output
configItems.description: Specify a form of output to produce for a measure of effectiveness. The allowed values for <output_type> are:

configItems.name: target_blanking_effect
configItems.description: Input block to provide the saturation effect and its associated input commands. See also the base target blanking effect for more types.

configItems.name: update_interval
configItems.description: If non-zero, specifies a periodic time interval at which the simulation will call the mover. If zero then the mover will be called only when it is necessary to determine the position of the containing platform.

configItems.name: update_time_tolerance
configItems.description: When a position update is requested by the simulation, if the time since the previous update is less than or equal to this value then the mover will ignore the update.

configItems.name: attachment_type
configItems.description: Specifies how the follower is attached to the leader.

configItems.name: reference_platform
configItems.description: Specifies the name of the reference or ‘lead’ platform (the platform to be followed).

configItems.name: offset_from_reference
configItems.description: Specifies the offset of the following platform in relation to the entity coordinate system of the reference platform.

configItems.name: orphan_action
configItems.description: Defines the action that should be performed if the reference platform is removed from the simulation. The values are as follows

configItems.name: guide_to_truth
configItems.description: Specifies if the perceived target location (as defined by the current target track) or the truth target location should be used in the guidance computations.

configItems.name: proportional_navigation_gain
configItems.description: Specifies the gain to apply to a perceived inertial line-of-sight rate, to null the rate to zero. The default value may be inadequate, as the appropriate value is usually a matter of experimentation. Reducing the value to 0.0 would result in no guidance to intercept, and increasing the gain by an order of magnitude (10.0) would likely saturate the control system into a “bang-bang” type of oscillation, and wash out any ability to simultaneously accomplish g-biasing.

configItems.name: velocity_pursuit_gain
configItems.description: Specifies the gain to apply to a perceived off-boresight target angle, to place the velocity vector back on the target. (The gain comments made for proportional_navigation_gain also apply here.)

configItems.name: g_bias
configItems.description: Specifies the degree to which the trajectory should be compensated for vertical acceleration due to gravity. The default value of unity results in a somewhat flat trajectory along the line of sight to the target. Some missiles may be intentionally over-biased to fly an arcing trajectory to the target, descending upon it from above (use > 1.0, but < 10.0). Some inexpensive infrared-guided missiles do not contain an attitude reference gyro, and cannot “know” which way is up. Because they cannot compensate for gravity, they tend to fly a “sagging” trajectory below the line-of-sight to the target (use 0.0). Extreme positive values of g-bias (> 10.0) may possibly vertically saturate the control system, and wash out any ability to accomplish target homing guidance in the lateral direction.

configItems.name: continuous_g_bias
configItems.description: This flag requests that g bias be used throughout the whole flight profile. The default behavior is not to turn on g bias compensation until the horizontal target distance is large relative to the vertical drop to the target. If a ballistic falling trajectory to the target has the ability to intercept, then further g-bias is not needed, and would likely even increase the miss distance.

configItems.name: max_commanded_g
configItems.description: This sets the maximum commanded lateral turn acceleration that the guidance computer will request of the guided mover. This models a guidance-imposed structural limit constraint to prevent airframe destruction.

configItems.name: guidance_delay
configItems.description: This keyword specifies a time interval after launch when guidance request is clamped to null. This models a no-guidance period to clear the launch rail, or perhaps a time before uplink guidance has been established.

configItems.name: aspect_angle_for_pro_nav_switch
configItems.description: After the velocity-vector to target line-of-sight angle decreases below this value, the guidance algorithm will switch from velocity pursuit to proportional navigation. This value is not used if either omit_velocity_pursuit or omit_proportional_navigation is specified.

configItems.name: omit_velocity_pursuit
configItems.description: This flag forces the trajectory guidance to include only pure proportional navigation, from the very beginning of the flight, with no velocity pursuit segment.

configItems.name: omit_proportional_navigation
configItems.description: This flag forces the trajectory guidance to include only velocity pursuit, with no switch to proportional navigation.

configItems.name: time_between_GPS_fixes
configItems.description: For the drift model, this duration specifies how often a positional update is received. The value will not be used unless the drift rate (below) is input as non-zero.

configItems.name: IMU_drift_rate
configItems.description: For the drift model, this specifies the rate of drift of positional perception.

configItems.name: pitchover_guidance
configItems.description: Specifies that the weapon will use a proportional navigation guidance scheme only that is modified for weapons that must perform a pitchover maneuver to point at the target. The proportional_navigation_gain is adjusted throughout the weapon’s flight based upon the weapon’s closure rate. (All indented commands below require that this option be enabled.)

configItems.name: maximum_loft_time
configItems.description: Specifies the time the missile will loft using the specified loft angle.

configItems.name: loft_angle
configItems.description: Specifies the angle the missile will initially climb at for the specified maximum_loft_time.

configItems.name: frequency_cutoff
configItems.description: A method of specifying the doppler frequency that determines the method of computing the pitchover gain. The guidance computer assumes a frequency of 10 GHz to compute the closing doppler frequency (i.e., doppler shift = 10.0e9 / light_speed * doppler_range_rate).

configItems.name: min_nav_gain
configItems.description: The minimum pitchover gain that is used when the doppler shift is less than zero.

configItems.name: max_nav_gain
configItems.description: The maximum pitchover gain that is used when the doppler shift is equal to or greater than the frequency_cutoff.

configItems.name: nav_gain_factor
configItems.description: A factor that is applied to the computed pitchover gain.

configItems.name: nav_gain_slope_1
configItems.description: Used to compute the pitchover gain when the doppler shift is less than the specified frequency_cutoff. The pitchover gain is computed as follows: Pitchover_gain = nav_gain_slope_1 * doppler_shift + min_nav_gain.

configItems.name: nav_gain_slope_2
configItems.description: Used to compute the pitchover gain when the doppler shift is greater than or equal to the specified frequency_cutoff. The pitchover gain is computed as follows, unless limited by the max_nav_gain: Pitchover_gain = nav_gain_slope_2 * (doppler_shift - frequency_cutoff) + 0.5.

configItems.name: show_status
configItems.description: Enables a debug printout that indicates when a staging operation takes place. Automatically enabled if debug is also enabled.

configItems.name: show_trajectory
configItems.description: Enables debug printouts on mass changes and trajectory data points. (Normal debug information includes [LLA] location and NED Orientation [hdg,pitch,roll]). This option provides downrange distance, speed, Mach number, and applied aerodynamic forces.

configItems.name: disable_guidance
configItems.description: Disables generation of any aerodynamic lift (lateral or vertical forces). Turns a guided weapon into a “dumb” ballistic one. This option is the default setting for the WSF_UNGUIDED_MOVER.

configItems.name: integration_method
configItems.description: Specify the method used to integrate the equations of motion.

configItems.name: integration_timestep
configItems.description: Specifies the global value of timestep to be used for integrating the equations of motion. This value is used for any stage that does not specify a local integration timestep.

configItems.name: stage
configItems.description: Defines the attributes of the only stage of a single stage vehicle or one of the stages in a multistage vehicle. <stage number> must be a value that is greater than or equal to 1 and less than or equal to the current number of defined stages plus one. If the value specifies a stage that already exists then the enclosed subcommands override the values in that stage. If the value is equal to the current number of defined stages plus one then a new stage is created and populated with the enclosed subcommands. It is invalid to specify a stage number that is more than one higher than the current highest defined stage number.

configItems.name: aero
configItems.description: Specifies the aerodynamics type name for this stage. Type must be known at initialization time.

configItems.name: empty_mass
configItems.description: Specifies the mass of the stage without fuel.

configItems.name: fuel_mass
configItems.description: Specifies the mass of the fuel on the stage.

configItems.name: total_mass
configItems.description: Specifies the total mass of the stage, which is the sum of empty_mass and fuel_mass but does not include the mass of any upper stages on top of this one (considered payload). Note: For backward compatibility, this same value may be supplied via the keywords: ‘launch_mass’, ‘mass’, ‘initial_mass’, or ‘weight’, but future support of these keywords is not guaranteed.

configItems.name: pre_ignition_coast_time
configItems.description: Specifies the amount of time that will elapse between the start of the stage and when the engine will ignite.

configItems.name: pre_separation_coast_time
configItems.description: Specifies the amount of time that will elapse between the burnout of this stage and its separation from the vehicle. This command has no effect for single-stage vehicles or the last stage of a multistage vehicle.

configItems.name: thrust
configItems.description: Specifies the thrust of the propulsion system.

configItems.name: thrust_duration
configItems.description: Specifies the amount of time the engine will produce the specified thrust.

configItems.name: burn_rate
configItems.description: Specifies the propellant burn rate while thrusting.

configItems.name: specific_impulse
configItems.description: Specific impulse of the propulsion system.

configItems.name: thrust_vectoring_angle_limit
configItems.description: Specifies the angle off the longitudinal axis that the thrust is vectored during thrust_vectoring_time_limits in order to introduce a pitch-over maneuver.

configItems.name: thrust_vectoring_time_limits
configItems.description: Specifies the time window after stage ignition in which thrust vectoring may be employed. This is applicable only if thrust_vectoring_angle_limit is greater than zero.

configItems.name: internal_table
configItems.description: Specifies that attenuation is to be computed using the internal table with the specified name. The name of the table is constructed as follows:

configItems.name: external_table
configItems.description: Specifies that attenuation is to be computed using the table loaded from the specified file. The file will have typically been created using either the spectral_data_conversion or optical_table_conversion command. However, a manually created file of the form documented below in Simple Table Format is also acceptable.

configItems.name: atmosphere_model
configItems.description: Specifies the MODTRAN atmosphere number. See internal_table for a description of the allowable values.

configItems.name: haze_model
configItems.description: Specifies the MODTRAN haze_model number. See internal_table for a description of the allowable values.

configItems.name: adjustment_factor
configItems.description: Specifies a multiplier to be applied to returned values. This would typically be used to account for the fact that values integrated over a wide band (i.e.: lwir, mwir, visual) represent an average that may include many ‘dead-zones’ that the sensor may exclude. Thus, the effective transmittance may be higher.

configItems.name: spectral_data_conversion
configItems.description: This command is used to take the spectral results from MODTRAN and convert them into a form that can be used by external_table or into code that can be compiled into the executable.

configItems.name: spectral_data
configItems.description: Specifies the name of the spectral transmittance file from which the table is to be created. If run using the defined processes it will have the suffix _cpt.plt’. This file is currently produced by a process that runs MODTRAN in transmittance mode using the ‘constant pressure altitude’ geometry specification.

configItems.name: table_output
configItems.description: Specifies the name of the file that will contain the converted results in a form usable as the argument to the external_table command.

configItems.name: code_output
configItems.description: Specifies the name of the file that will contain the converted results in a form that is useful for compiling in as one of the embedded models available by internal_table.

configItems.name: maximum_segment_count
configItems.description: The maximum number of linear segments that will be allowed per altitude.

configItems.name: maximum_absolute_error
configItems.description: Maximum allowed absolute error between the input transmittance and the modeled transmittance within a segment.

configItems.name: maximum_relative_error
configItems.description: Maximum allowed relative error between the input transmittance and the modeled transmittance within a segment.

configItems.name: optical_path_conversion
configItems.description: This command is used to convert one of the legacy atmospheric_coefficients tables used by WSF_LASER_WEAPON and WSF_CUED_LASER_WEAPON into a form that can be used by the external_table command.

configItems.name: wavelength
configItems.description: Specifies the wavelength of the coefficient table to the selected.

configItems.name: interpolate_tables
configItems.description: Specifies whether to apply interpolation to the defined Azimuth-Elevation Table Definition. The type of interpolation can be either linear or logarithmic (see interpolation_type).

configItems.name: interpolation_type
configItems.description: Specifies whether to use linear or logarithmic interpolation when interpolating data in the azimuth elevation tables.

configItems.name: state
configItems.description: Indicates that the following table definition will be used when the platform is in the signature state <state-name>. If default is specified then the subsequent table will be used if the platform is in a signature state that does not match any of the states defined in the signature.

configItems.name: atmospheric_attenuation
configItems.description: The fraction of the signal (in the closed range 0 to 1) that is attenuated per unit of distance traveled at sea level. The attenuation is adjusted to account for the density of air with the change in an altitude.

configItems.name: background_radiance
configItems.description: Specifies the radiance of the background.

configItems.name: path_radiance
configItems.description: Specifies the path radiance.

configItems.name: reacquisition_time
configItems.description: Specifies the sensor reacquisition time when a track is dropped.

configItems.name: track_glimpse_data
configItems.description: Specifies the data necessary to compute a glimpse probability table for each optical detection sequence.

configItems.name: minimum_elevation
configItems.description: Specifies the sensor’s lowest elevation look-angle for the given glimpse probability.

configItems.name: maximum_elevation
configItems.description: Specifies the sensor’s maximum elevation look-angle for the given glimpse probability.

configItems.name: number_of_iterations
configItems.description: Specifies the number of Monte-Carlo iterations that will be performed to create the probability table.

configItems.name: magnification
configItems.description: Specifies the sensor’s magnification.

configItems.name: apparent_half_angle_FOV
configItems.description: Specifies the sensor’s apparent half-angle FOV.

configItems.name: minimum_resolution
configItems.description: Specifies the sensor’s minimum resolution.

configItems.name: contrast_gain
configItems.description: Specifies the sensor’s contrast gain.

configItems.name: ocular_integration_level
configItems.description: Specifies the sensor’s ocular integration level.

configItems.name: interpolate_tables
configItems.description: Specifies whether to apply interpolation to the defined Azimuth-Elevation Table Definition. The type of interpolation can be either linear or logarithmic (see interpolation_type).

configItems.name: interpolation_type
configItems.description: Specifies whether to use linear or logarithmic interpolation when interpolating data in the azimuth elevation tables.

configItems.name: state
configItems.description: Indicates that the following table definition will be used when the platform is in the signature state <state-name>. If default is specified then the subsequent table will be used if the platform is in a signature state that does not match any of the states defined in the signature.

configItems.name: process_noise_sigmas_XYZ
configItems.description: Defines the filter’s noise standard deviation for the three directions. The values correspond with accelerations in the entity coordinate system (ECS) of the tracked platform.

configItems.name: propagator
configItems.description: Specifies the propagator type that will be used to track the target.

configItems.name: range_measurement_sigma
configItems.description: Defines the standard deviation that is applied to the measurement’s range prior to filtering.

configItems.name: bearing_measurement_sigma
configItems.description: Defines the standard deviation that is applied to the measurement’s bearing prior to filtering.

configItems.name: elevation_measurement_sigma
configItems.description: Defines the standard deviation that is applied to the measurement’s elevation prior to filtering.

configItems.name: debug
configItems.description: When specified, writes filtered measurements data and filter performance data to the file KFILT_DEBUG.out.

configItems.name: search_interval
configItems.description: Declares the time tracked objects will be predicted into the future to search for conjunctions. This search is performed anew during each update, and this duration begins at the time of the update. The means that a conjunction can be predicted during more than one update if this interval is long enough.

configItems.name: filter_cut_distance
configItems.description: Declares the distance used in the fast filter.

configItems.name: search_step_size
configItems.description: Declares the step size used in prediction. As this angle is made larger, the amount of computation needed by the processor is decreased, at the cost of some additional error.

configItems.name: exclusion_factor
configItems.description: Declares the size of the exclusion zone as the combined covariance ellipsoid scaled by this factor.

configItems.name: default_variance
configItems.description: Declares a default position variance for cases where the track does not have state covariance data. In those cases, the covariance ellipsoid is taken to be a sphere with this radius.

configItems.name: default_object_size
configItems.description: Declares an object size used in the computation of the conjunction probability. The probability estimate is sensitive to the size of the object, so reasonable values should be used.

configItems.name: prediction_model
configItems.description: Declares the prediction model used by the processor, which can be one of the following:

configItems.name: primary
configItems.description: Declare a list of objects by name to be considered as primary objects.

configItems.name: debug
configItems.description: Turn on additional output concerning the operation of this processor.

configItems.name: on_conjunction_predicted
configItems.description: This is an optional script that can be defined that allows one to react to the discovery of a possible conjunction. If defined, this script is only called if conjunctions are discovered, so the input Array will always have at least one entry.

configItems.name: leo_data
configItems.description: Specify the file name to use when computing a low-Earth orbit (LEO) launch solution. This file is created using the ORBITAL_LAUNCH_COMPUTER_GENERATOR command of the weapon_tools utility.

configItems.name: noise
configItems.description: Controls the computation of galactic noise, atmospheric noise, and man-made noise. The noise is computed and applied ONLY if the noise environment command is used. If it is not present, no additional noise is computed.

configItems.name: solar_characteristics
configItems.description: This command allows the initialization of time of day and day of year. These control the solar declination angle and the solar zenith angles used by the routine to determine if an ionospheric bounce can occur.

configItems.name: ionosphere_characteristics
configItems.description: This command allows the initialization of data that will control if and where an ionospheric bounce can occur.

configItems.name: add_subobject
configItems.description: Specifies the base name of a subobject on the WSF_P6DOF_MOVER that will be launched/fired. Each individual subobject supported by the weapon (launcher) requires its own add_subobject command line. Each subobject must have a unique name. The subobject weapons will be launched in the order they are listed. Note that the launched platform type associated with the subobject is specified using the definition contained in the P6DOF platform mappings.

configItems.name: initial_quantity
configItems.description: Defines the initial quantity of fuel to be loaded on the vehicle. WSF_P6DOF_FUEL will interact with WSF_P6DOF_MOVER to set the initial fuel.
