Fuel will be added to internal tanks first, keeping the percentage filled for each tank in sync. For example, if the initial_quantity was 75% of the total internal fuel capacity, each internal fuel tank would be filled to 75% and no external tanks would be filled.

configItems.name: reserve_quantity
configItems.description: Defines the threshold such that when the quantity of fuel remaining falls below this value, the platform is considered to be operating on reserves. If an on_reserve block is defined, it will be executed when this state is reached.

configItems.name: bingo_quantity
configItems.description: Defines the threshold such that when the quantity of fuel remaining falls below this value, the platform is considered to have reached a BINGO state. If an on_bingo block is defined, it will be executed when this state is reached.

configItems.name: maximum_quantity
configItems.description: The fuel capacity is determined by fuel tank definitions in a WSF_P6DOF_MOVER. If maximum_quantity is specified, it will be ignored and WSF_P6DOF_FUEL will output a warning.

configItems.name: mode
configItems.description: WSF_P6DOF_FUEL and WSF_P6DOF_MOVER do not use a fuel mode. If mode is specified, it will be ignored and WSF_P6DOF_FUEL will output a warning.

configItems.name: consumption_rate
configItems.description: Fuel consumption rate is not a single/constant value for a WSF_P6DOF_MOVER. If consumption_rate is specified, it will be ignored and WSF_P6DOF_FUEL will output a warning.

configItems.name: on_bingo
configItems.description: Defines a script to be executed when the quantity of fuel remaining falls below the threshold defined by bingo_quantity.

configItems.name: on_empty
configItems.description: Defines a script to be executed when all fuel has been expended.

configItems.name: on_reserve
configItems.description: Defines a script to be executed when the quantity of fuel remaining falls below the threshold defined by reserve_quantity.

configItems.name: on_refuel
configItems.description: Defines a script to be executed when a refueling operation has been completed.

configItems.name: show_status
configItems.description: Specifies that information should be written to standard output whenever a phase or stage transition occurs.

configItems.name: show_commands
configItems.description: Specifies that calls from script commands should be written to standard output.

configItems.name: show_evaluations
configItems.description: Specifies that phase change rule evaluations should be written to standard output.

configItems.name: guide_to_truth
configItems.description: Specifies if the guidance target should be the location specified in the current target track (false), or should be the true location of the platform specified in the current target track (true).

configItems.name: phase
configItems.description: The ‘phase’ block is used to define the guidance for the various phases of flight and the rules to transition between phases.

configItems.name: edit
configItems.description: This command is typically used when creating a new guidance computer type by deriving from another guidance computer type.

configItems.name: guidance_delay
configItems.description: Specifies the elapsed time since the start of the phase when guidance commands should start being computed. This is useful during lift-off and other phases where pursuit of the target is not desirable.

configItems.name: on_entry
configItems.description: These commands define scripts to be executed when entering and exiting the phase.

configItems.name: on_update
configItems.description: Define a script to be executed on every phase update.

configItems.name: maximum_commanded_g
configItems.description: Specifies the magnitude of the maximum acceleration that can be commanded.

configItems.name: proportional_navigation_gain
configItems.description: Specifies the gain for proportional navigation. A value of zero indicates proportional navigation will not be performed.

configItems.name: proportional_navigation_limit_angle
configItems.description: Specifies the 3D aspect angle of the target with respect to the weapon at which the navigation method will switch between proportional and velocity pursuit. Proportional navigation will be used if the target aspect angle is less than or equal to this value, otherwise velocity pursuit will be used.

configItems.name: proportional_navigation_method
configItems.description: Specifies whether additional acceleration should be commanded because of current target acceleration.

configItems.name: velocity_pursuit_gain
configItems.description: Specifies the gain for velocity pursuit navigation. A value of zero indicates velocity pursuit navigation will not be performed.

configItems.name: g_bias
configItems.description: Specifies the bias factor used to overcome gravity. This is typically used during midcourse to prevent the trajectory from sagging. If zero is specified then gravity bias will not be applied.

configItems.name: lateral_g_bias
configItems.description: Specifies the bias factor used skew the horizontal component of the trajectory in a particular direction. If zero is specified then gravity bias will not be applied.

configItems.name: commanded_azimuth_offset
configItems.description: Specifies the azimuth angle to the target that should be maintained. The angle is defined to be the angle in the local horizontal plane between the weapon velocity vector and the line-of-sight vector from the weapon to the target. (This is consistent with the ‘target_azimuth’ conditional tests in the next_phase command.)

configItems.name: guidance_target
configItems.description: Overrides the top-level guide_to_truth command for the current phase. This is expanded to include the options:

configItems.name: aimpoint_altitude_offset
configItems.description: Modify the aimpoint to be above or below the perceived target location. This is typically used to create an air burst.

configItems.name: aimpoint_azimuth_offset
configItems.description: These commands provide a method to produce an aimpoint that is laterally offset from the perceived target location. This is typically used to meet some tactical requirement.

configItems.name: aimpoint_evaluation_interval
configItems.description: Controls how often a new aimpoint is computed when using aimpoint_azimuth_offset and aimpoint_range_offset. This is a fairly time-consuming operation that does not need to be performed on every call to the guidance computer.

configItems.name: next_phase
configItems.description: The next_phase command defines a condition under which a phase transition occurs. A phase block may have multiple next_phase commands to define a number of conditions that might trigger a phase change. The next_phase commands are evaluated on each guidance update and are evaluated in the order specified.

configItems.name: commanded_altitude
configItems.description: Specifies a commanded altitude. Typically used to climb or dive to a cruise altitude and hold the altitude. The altitude reference tag (’msl’, or ‘above mean sea level’; ‘agl’, or ‘above ground level’) may be omitted, in which case ‘msl’ is assumed.

configItems.name: commanded_flight_path_angle
configItems.description: Specifies a commanded flight path angle. If from_launch_computer is specified then the value produced by the launch computer will be used (if present).

configItems.name: commanded_mach
configItems.description: Specifies the commanded speed/mach to be used during this phase. Typically used for cruise.

configItems.name: commanded_throttle
configItems.description: Specifies a throttle factor in the range [0..1] that overrides and throttle specification in the mover.

configItems.name: allow_route_following
configItems.description: If true, the computer will follow a route if it has been provided to the associated mover. If the mover does not have a route then this command has no effect. Conventional target point selection will resume at the end of the route.

configItems.name: p6dof_object_type
configItems.description: This defines the type of p6dof object used by the mover. The p6dof_object_type is defined in a p6dof_object_types block and must be defined before being referenced.

configItems.name: autopilot_no_control
configItems.description: This will command the autopilot to “zero” all controls, which will center the stick and rudder and pull back throttle(s) to zero (idle). It is similar to enable_controls but is commanding the autopilot, rather than the controls themselves.

configItems.name: enable_controls
configItems.description: This enables/disables control inputs from any source (autopilot, external manual pilot, P6Net interface, etc.). Controls are enabled by default, so this command is typically used to disable controls at the start. This is often used to allow a weapon to drop ballistically and without control inputs as it is released from the carrying aircraft and then calling the script method WsfP6DOF_Mover.EnableControls with true to establish control input after the weapon is safely clear of the aircraft.

configItems.name: enable_thrust_vectoring
configItems.description: Indicates whether thrust vectoring is enabled or not.

configItems.name: engines_on
configItems.description: Indicates whether the engines should be on or off when the scenario begins.

configItems.name: follow_vertical_track
configItems.description: Normally, the autopilot will climb/dive as quickly as possible (within the current limits – see WsfP6DOF_Mover.SetVerticalSpeedMax and WsfP6DOF_Mover.SetVerticalSpeedMin) when changing altitude, but when “follow_vertical_track” is set, the autopilot will instead use a vertical speed that will allow the object to smoothly/slowly change altitude along a straight line vertical track between waypoints.

configItems.name: ignore_all_crashes
configItems.description: Indicates whether the mover ignore all forms of crashes. This is often used in testing.

configItems.name: landing_gear_down
configItems.description: Indicates whether the landing gear should be down or not when the scenario begins.

configItems.name: nws_enabled
configItems.description: Indicates whether nose-wheel steering should be enabled or not. Nose-wheel steering is commonly used when taxiing but should be removed prior to the takeoff roll.

configItems.name: p6dof_alt
configItems.description: This command sets the initial altitude of the mover.

configItems.name: p6dof_initsetup
configItems.description: This is deprecated – use wash_in_conditions instead.

configItems.name: p6dof_ned_heading
configItems.description: This command sets the initial heading of the mover.

configItems.name: p6dof_ned_pitch
configItems.description: This command sets the initial pitch angle of the mover.

configItems.name: p6dof_ned_roll
configItems.description: This command sets the initial roll angle of the mover.

configItems.name: p6dof_position
configItems.description: This command sets the initial position (using decimal latitude longitude) of the mover.

configItems.name: p6dof_set_velocity_ned_fps
configItems.description: This command sets the initial velocity of the mover in NED coordinates using ft/sec.

configItems.name: parking_brake_on
configItems.description: This command sets whether the parking brake should be on or off when the scenario begins.

configItems.name: produces_launch_smoke
configItems.description: This command sets how long the vehicle will produce a launch smoke/flash effect (appearance only) when launched. If no launch effect is desired, this should not be defined at all.

configItems.name: taxi_mode_enabled
configItems.description: This command set whether the autopilot should be in taxi mode when the scenario begins. This should be used only be used when the platform is on ground.

configItems.name: throttle_afterburner
configItems.description: This command sets the throttle to afterburner when the scenario begins.

configItems.name: throttle_full
configItems.description: This command sets the throttle to mil power when the scenario begins.

configItems.name: throttle_idle
configItems.description: This command sets the throttle to idle when the scenario begins.

configItems.name: wash_in_conditions
configItems.description: Including this flag indicates that this mover should “wash-in” conditions on initialization. This means that the object will run in a special mode to help “ramp-in” and “stabilize” the object on initialization by allowing it to have some time to settle in the needed angle of attack (alpha) as well as the proper throttle setting. This is useful to ensure vehicles are stable when they start the simulation – they may otherwise lack the correct alpha, for example, when they start in the simulation.

configItems.name: route
configItems.description: Specifies the latitude and longitude of the waypoint.

configItems.name: position
configItems.description: Specifies the latitude and longitude of the waypoint.

configItems.name: altitude
configItems.description: Specifies the altitude (MSL) at the waypoint.

configItems.name: speed
configItems.description: Specifies the speed at the waypoint.

configItems.name: label
configItems.description: Associates a label with the immediately following waypoint definition. This can be used as the target of a goto command.

configItems.name: goto
configItems.description: Go to the waypoint with the specified label in the current route.

configItems.name: bank_angle_limit
configItems.description: Specifies the maximum bank angle to be used for turns when making heading changes on the route segment that starts with this waypoint. This effectively sets the radial_acceleration to .

configItems.name: radial_acceleration
configItems.description: Specifies the radial acceleration to be used for turns when making heading changes on the route segment that starts with this waypoint.

configItems.name: turn_g_limit
configItems.description: Specifies the maximum turn g-load to be used for turns when making heading changes on the route segment that starts with this waypoint. This effectively sets the radial_acceleration to .

configItems.name: switch_on_approach
configItems.description: Defines the condition when the mover should declare that it has reached this waypoint and should start moving towards the next waypoint. switch_on_passing is sometimes known as ‘turn long’ and causes the switch to occur when the platform passes over or along side of the waypoint. switch_on_approach is sometimes known as ‘turn short’ and causes the switch to occur before the waypoint.

configItems.name: use_route
configItems.description: Supplies the name of the route to follow. The route is assumed to be a predefined absolute route.

configItems.name: update_interval
configItems.description: If non-zero, specifies a periodic time interval at which the simulation will call the mover. If zero then the mover will be called only when it is necessary to determine the position of the containing platform.

configItems.name: update_time_tolerance
configItems.description: When a position update is requested by the simulation, if the time since the previous update is less than or equal to this value then the mover will ignore the update.

configItems.name: tof_and_impact_lat_lon_alt
configItems.description: The desired final conditions: time of flight and impact latitude, longitude, and altitude.

configItems.name: tof_and_impact_lat_lon
configItems.description: The desired final conditions: time of flight and impact latitude, longitude. Altitude is determined by finding the terrain elevation at the given latitude and longitude.

configItems.name: reported_target_type
configItems.description: Defines how the passive sensor reports target type information in tracks.

configItems.name: default_time_to_declare
configItems.description: Defines the duration of time after the initial detection that is required to make a determination of the target type.

configItems.name: default_time_to_reevaluate
configItems.description: Defines the time interval used for reevaluating the identification of the target. A value of 0 seconds indicates no reevaluation will take place.

configItems.name: type
configItems.description: Specifies the truth type to which the following subcommands apply.

configItems.name: default_type
configItems.description: Specifies that the following type subcommands apply for any type not defined with the type command.

configItems.name: time_to_declare
configItems.description: Defines the duration of time after the initial detection that is required to make a determination of the target type.

configItems.name: time_to_reevaluate
configItems.description: Defines the time interval used for reevaluating the identification of the target.

configItems.name: report_type
configItems.description: Defines the reporting type-name as the target type based on the listed emitter-type(s) being reported in the emitter list. Currently exact matches between the emitter’s defined for the report_type and a track’s emitter list must happen for the given report_type to be reported. If there are differences another report_type or the default_type will be reported.

configItems.name: report_truth
configItems.description: Specifies that the sensor will report the truth type. This is only valid under the default_type command.

configItems.name: reported_emitter_type
configItems.description: Defines how the passive sensor reports emitter type information in tracks.

configItems.name: unframed_detection_optimization
configItems.description: This command indicates if unframed detection optimization will be used. If enabled, once the sensor successfully detects a given transmitter within a frame, subsequent attempts to detect the same transmitter in the same frame will be suppressed. For instance, if multiple messages are sent from a single transmitter during the passive frame, the passive sensor will only report on the first message that it can detect (if any). If the first message cannot be detected because of transmitter antenna pointing, it will report the second message if it can be detected, an so on.

configItems.name: unframed_detection_coast_time
configItems.description: If the passive sensor is running at a faster frame time than the sensors it is trying to detect, it may detect the transmitter one frame and not the next. This can cause a lot of track creation and deletion. This value indicates how long a successful detection from a transmitter will be reported.

configItems.name: frequency_band
configItems.description: Defines a band of frequencies this sensor can detect. This command may be specified more than once if the sensor can detect multiple bands.

configItems.name: revisit_time
configItems.description: These two commands pertain to the immediately preceding frequency_band and define how long the sensor dwells in the band and the interval between dwells. These commands are effectively only when the scan_on_scan_model is enabled and are used to determine the temporal probability that the sensor would be looking at the frequency of the target emitter when a detection chance occurs.

configItems.name: detection_sensitivity
configItems.description: Defines the minimum signal strength that can be ‘reliably’ detected. If detection_probability is defined then this is the signal strength that would result in a Pd of 0.5. If detection_probability is not defined then this defines the signal strength for which a successful detection will be declared.

configItems.name: detection_sensitivities
configItems.description: This command allows the definition of frequency-dependent or signal-type- and frequency-dependent detection sensitivities.

configItems.name: detection_threshold
configItems.description: This is an alternative to detection_sensitivity. It defines the minimum signal-to-noise ratio that can be ‘reliably’ detected. If detection_probability is defined then this is the signal-to-noise ratio that would result in a Pd of 0.5. If detection_probability is not defined then this defines the signal-to-noise ratio for which a successful detection will be declared.

configItems.name: detection_thresholds
configItems.description: This command allows the definition of frequency-dependent or signal-type- and frequency-dependent detection thresholds.

configItems.name: detection_probability
configItems.description: Defines a function of probability of detection (Pd) versus received signal strength (expressed as a ratio of the received power to the detection sensitivity). The table is defined as follows:

configItems.name: scan_on_scan_model
configItems.description: Specifies if the Probabilistic Scan-On-Scan (PSOS) model should be employed. This model attempts to probabilistically capture the temporal effects in which the passive sensor is scanning in frequency and the emitter may be scanning in angle.

configItems.name: range_error_sigma_table
configItems.description: These commands provide the ability to define error sigmas that are a function of the frequency of the received signal instead of the fixed sigmas that are provided by the single-valued azimuth_error_sigma, elevation_error_sigma and range_error_sigma commands. The points define a curve on a plot whose x-axis is the log_10 of the frequency and the y-axis is the error sigma. Linear interpolation is used to derive the values for intermediate frequencies. Signals whose frequencies are outside the range of the table use the value from the appropriate endpoint (i.e., extrapolation is not performed).

configItems.name: ranging_time
configItems.description: Adds range information to any track generated by this sensor after the specified time has elapsed. This basically simulates that the system could triangulate and get the range after a sufficient period of time.

configItems.name: ranging_time_track_quality
configItems.description: If the ranging time is used to generate a track with range information, this parameter controls the track quality once range is valid. The quality-value must be non-negative.

configItems.name: report_interval
configItems.description: Specifies the interval at which asset state messages are sent to friends.

configItems.name: reporting_self
configItems.description: Specifies whether or not to report out asset status messages about this platform.

configItems.name: reporting_others
configItems.description: Specifies whether or not to report out messages of all received and known asset status (of other platforms).

configItems.name: asset_perception
configItems.description: status_messages: asset perception will utilize any received WSF_ASSET_MESSAGE messages.

configItems.name: perceive_self
configItems.description: Include this platform in the list of perceived assets.

configItems.name: threat_update_interval
configItems.description: Specifies the interval at which the processor updates its threat perception.

configItems.name: max_threat_load
configItems.description: Specifies the maximum number of entries held in the threat perception.

configItems.name: threat_importance_function
configItems.description: Specify a script function name used to measure threat importance. If specified, it completely over-rides the use of any script functions that try to set threat importance or unimportance (see WsfPerceptionProcessor). Only useful when max_threat_load is defined, otherwise no limit is imposed and importance is not necessary. Script function must match the signature of “double FunctionName(WsfLocalTrack)”. Values returned by the script will be interpreted as lower being more important (golf scoring).

configItems.name: asset_update_interval
configItems.description: Specifies the interval at which the processor updates its asset perception.

configItems.name: max_asset_load
configItems.description: Specifies the maximum number of entries held in the asset perception.

configItems.name: asset_importance_function
configItems.description: Specify a script function name used to measure asset importance. If specified, it completely over-rides the use of any script functions that try to set asset importance or unimportance (see WsfPerceptionProcessor). Only useful when max_asset_load is defined, otherwise no limit is imposed and importance is not necessary. Script function must match the signature of “double FunctionName(WsfAssetPerception)”. Values returned by the script will be interpreted as lower being more important (golf scoring).

configItems.name: position
configItems.description: Specifies the latitude and longitude of the center point of the heat map grid.

configItems.name: altitude
configItems.description: Specifies the altitude of the center point of the heat map grid.

configItems.name: grid_extent
configItems.description: Specifies the distance the heat map grid extends from the center point.

configItems.name: cell_size
configItems.description: Specifies the length of one side of a cell in the heat map grid.

configItems.name: heat_decay
configItems.description: Optional value that specifies the amount a heat cell will change in value as it gets stale.

configItems.name: decay_interval
configItems.description: Optional value that specifies the time between updates of a heat map cell’s value. Heat value in a cell will decay toward zero by heat_decay each interval update.

configItems.name: expansion_timeout
configItems.description: Optional value that specifies how long a heat source will continue to expand.

configItems.name: use_asset_perception
configItems.description: Optional value that indicates the perception processor should use the sensor coverage of assets to generate the “cold” coverage of the heat map.

configItems.name: sensor_range
configItems.description: The distance from its source that a sensor is considered to “clear” the heat map. This should be shorter than the actual maximum range of the sensor and cover a distance where there is 95% or higher Pd.

configItems.name: draw_sensor_outline
configItems.description: Optional values that indicate WsfDraw commands should be issued for the heat map grid lines, the heat/cold values of the heat cells, or sensor coverage outlines respectively. These commands can be used to visualize the information represented by the heat map but leaving them off will speed up simulation runs.

configItems.name: update_interval
configItems.description: Specifies how often the processor should update the track.

configItems.name: central_body
configItems.description: Specify the central body and related ellipsoid model to be used by simulation platforms. Options for <central body type> are the following:

configItems.name: polar_offset_angles
configItems.description: Specify the central_body’s polar offset angles ( and , respectively) of the Celestial Intermediate Pole (CIP) with respect to the WCS (ITRS) coordinate system. Providing these values (of the order of tenths of arc-seconds) enables very highly accurate conversions between ECI and WCS coordinates.

configItems.name: vehicle_type
configItems.description: This defines the type of object used by the mover. The point-mass vehicle_type is defined in a six_dof_object_types block and must be defined before being referenced.

configItems.name: polarization_switching_rate
configItems.description: Specifies polarization switching rate (frequency). See the WSF_SLC_EFFECT and its canceller_settling_time for more information on its use and effect.

configItems.name: system_type_data
configItems.description: Input block to provide the system type (e.g., SENSOR-TYPE, JAMMER-TYPE) specific data necessary to implement this technique for a given system type. Default data can be set up for system types not defined using the “default” string as the system type.

configItems.name: modulation_gain
configItems.description: Specifies a mitigating adjustment to the effective jamming gain level created by this technique. This adjustment modifies the normally-determined processed jamming power. If this input is specified within the system_type_data input block then it is specific to a system-type, otherwise this input is defined as the ‘default’ data to use for undefined system-types in the system_type_data.

configItems.name: power_gain
configItems.description: Specifies a mitigating adjustment to the effective jamming power level created by this technique. This adjustment modifies the normally-determined physical jamming power. If this input is specified within the system_type_data input block then it is specific to a system-type, otherwise this input is defined as the ‘default’ data to use for un-defined system-types in the system_type_data.

configItems.name: signal_power_gain
configItems.description: Specifies a mitigating adjustment to the effective signal level created by this technique. This adjustment modifies the normally-determined received signal power. If this input is specified within the system_type_data input block then it is specific to a system-type, otherwise this input is defined as the ‘default’ data to use for undefined system-types in the system_type_data.

configItems.name: receiver_noise_power_gain
configItems.description: Specifies a mitigating adjustment to the effective receiver noise power level created by this technique. This adjustment modifies the normally-determined noise power with a multiplier that is applied for signal-to-noise calculations. If this input is specified within the system_type_data input block then it is specific to a system-type, otherwise this input is defined as the ‘default’ data to use for undefined system-types in the system_type_data.

configItems.name: system_type_data
configItems.description: Input block to provide the system type (e.g., SENSOR-TYPE, JAMMER-TYPE) specific data necessary to implement this technique for a given system type. Default data can be set up for system types not defined using the “default” string as the system type.

configItems.name: jamming_pulse_density
configItems.description: Specifies the pulse density of the jamming signal in range [0,1] to use for this radar type. This input is used only for Electronic Attack based effects.

configItems.name: allow
configItems.description: Specifies the rejected or allowed suppression-type and required input variables that are dependent upon the suppression-type specified.

configItems.name: ignore_ally_tracks
configItems.description: Indicates that the Quantum Tasker should not pass tracks of allies to the task generator, and subsequently should not have any tasks related to ally tracks.

configItems.name: asset_representation
configItems.description: Indicates how the Quantum Tasker should represent asset perception objects. If ‘systems’ is defined then each platform subsystem is considered as an individual asset that can receive task assignments separate from other subsystems. If ‘resources’ is defined then each resource of a subsystem is considered as a taskable individual asset (missiles, sensor/jammer beams). However, the task assignments are still sent to the owning platform for processing as required.

configItems.name: generator
configItems.syntax: generator [ simple_weapon | simple_jammer | simple_sensor | custom <script method name> ]
configItems.description: Indicates which task generator the Quantum Tasker is to use.

configItems.name: evaluator
configItems.syntax: evaluator [ simple | distance | intercept_time | custom <script method name> ]
configItems.description: Indicates which task evaluator the Quantum Tasker is to use.

configItems.name: allocator
configItems.syntax: allocator [ simple | greedy_isolated | greedy_priority | greedy_value | greedy_profit | optimal_profit | custom <script method name> ] [type <task_type>]
configItems.description: Indicates which allocation algorithm the Quantum Tasker is to use to assign tasks to assets given the current evaluation values.

configItems.name: allocator_extra_tasks
configItems.syntax: allocator_extra_tasks [ simple | greedy_isolated | greedy_priority | greedy_value | greedy_profit | optimal_profit | custom <script method name> ]
configItems.description: Indicates which allocator will be used on any extra tasks that were not allocated by the primary allocator. If used, this means assets might have more than one task to perform. This allocator will be called repeatedly as long there are tasks that are still remaining and as long as it keeps finding at least one new allocation each pass. If no assets evaluated a task positively, then that task will not be allocated.

configItems.name: allocator_extra_assets
configItems.syntax: allocator_extra_assets [ simple | greedy_isolated | greedy_priority | greedy_value | greedy_profit | optimal_profit | custom <script method name> ]
configItems.description: Indicates which allocator will be used on any extra assets that were not allocated by the primary allocator. If used, this means tasks might have more than one asset performing them. This allocator will be called repeatedly as long there are assets that are still remaining and as long as it keeps finding at least one new allocation each pass. If an asset did not evaluate any task positively, then that asset will not be allocated to a task.

configItems.name: reallocation_strategy
configItems.description: Indicates how the Quantum Tasker handles previously assigned tasks and changes in task assignments.

configItems.name: update_assignments
configItems.description: If declared, a task assign message is sent to all assigned assets every update. This is only useful when task data (like aux data) is updated regularly on the tasks.

configItems.name: comm_retry_attempts
configItems.description: Indicates the number of attempts to retry failed communications.

configItems.name: comm_retry_interval
configItems.description: Indicates the amount of time between attempts to retry failed communications.

configItems.name: operating_level
configItems.description: Indicates the operating condition or state and the associated level.

configItems.name: track_processor
configItems.description: Specifies the name of a WSF_TRACK_PROCESSOR (typically operating as a non_master_track_processor) whose track list will provide the tracks used in the evaluation process.

configItems.name: time_to_recognize_messages
configItems.description: Indicates the amount of time it takes to recognize a message.

configItems.name: track_update_interval
configItems.description: Indicates the time interval for sending track updates to assignees.

configItems.name: track_update_strategy
configItems.description: Indicates how track updates are sent. With default behavior, if a task has been accepted then periodic track updates are sent to the assignee. With the Suppressor behavior, track updates are sent to assignees only when the track manager indicates a track has been updated.

configItems.name: show_task_messages
configItems.description: Indicates that information related task assignment, cancellation and completion are to be written to standard output.

configItems.name: show_uncompleted_tasks
configItems.description: This is a debugging tool that indicates information about uncompleted tasks is to be written to standard output during the destruction of the task processor.

configItems.name: queuing_method
configItems.description: Only used if time_to_recognize_messages is defined and greater than zero. Specifies how incoming messages are to be queued if all of the servers are busy. A value of none indicates the message will be discarded.

configItems.name: number_of_servers
configItems.description: Only used if time_to_recognize_messages is defined and greater than zero. Specifies the maximum number of messages that can be ‘in process’ at any given instant of time. If a new message is received and all the servers are busy, the message will be queued according to the queuing_method

configItems.name: show_calibration_data
configItems.description: Write information about the characteristics of the radar to standard output. This will include the one square meter detection range as well as any other values that may need to be derived.

configItems.name: receive_only
configItems.description: Indicate that only the transmitter or receiver will be used.

configItems.name: compute_measurement_errors
configItems.description: If true, measurement errors will be computed using standard radar error model equations. If false, measurement errors will be computed using the common sensor error model.

configItems.name: override_measurement_with_truth
configItems.description: This command will compute the measurement errors and report the errors in the track, but will report the truth location in the track instead of using the location with the measurement errors applied. This is typically used for testing trackers.

configItems.name: frequency_select_delay
configItems.description: Specifies the delay when selecting between different frequencies as defined on the transmitter.

configItems.name: maintain_track_measurement_history
configItems.description: If true, the mode will maintain a track’s history of measurements produced from successful detections.

configItems.name: doppler_resolution
configItems.description: Defines the target Doppler speed resolution (i.e., opening or closing speed) capability of the radar.

configItems.name: adjustment_factor
configItems.description: A method of adjusting a beam’s detection capability. Positive value increase the sensor’s detection capability.

configItems.name: operating_loss
configItems.description: Defines the beam’s operating loss.

configItems.name: integration_gain
configItems.description: Defines the integration gain when using the binary detector (detection_threshold). This is not applicable when using the Swerling detector (swerling_case) or detection_probability.

configItems.name: detection_threshold
configItems.description: An alternative method of defining the receiver’s detection threshold. The value can be entered here for readability of the input file.

configItems.name: swerling_case
configItems.description: Indicates that the Marcum-Swerling detector model is to be used and specifies the ‘case’ to be used.

configItems.name: number_of_pulses_integrated
configItems.description: Specifies the number of pulses the Marcum-Swerling detector integrates.

configItems.name: probability_of_false_alarm
configItems.description: Specifies the false alarm probability.

configItems.name: detector_law
configItems.description: Specifies the type of Marcum-Swerling detector.

configItems.name: no_swerling_case
configItems.description: Specifies not to use a Marcum-Swerling detector. Detections will be based on the detection_threshold. This is the default configuration.

configItems.name: detection_probability
configItems.description: Defines a function of probability of detection (Pd) versus received signal-to-noise ratio (more specifically, it is really the signal-to-interference ratio, which includes the effects of receiver noise, interference and unsuppressed clutter). This is an alternative to using the Swerling detector (swerling_case) or the binary detector (detection_threshold). The table is defined as follows:

configItems.name: post_lockon_detection_threshold_adjustment
configItems.description: Defines a value by which the detection threshold will be adjusted once a ‘locked-on’ state has been achieved for the current mode of the sensor. This is typically used with tracking sensors to indicate that the detection threshold is less once a locked-on state has been achieved. The value is typically a negative ‘dB’ value, although it can be 0 dB or greater if that is what is desired.

configItems.name: post_lockon_adjustment_delay_time
configItems.description: Defines the time that must elapse from when a sensor declares that a ‘locked-on’ state has been achieved before applying the post_lockon_detection_threshold_adjustment.

configItems.name: loop_gain
configItems.description: Alternative methods to specify a radar beam’s detection capability. If specified, the receiver’s noise value will be calibrated to yield the specified detection range.

configItems.name: look_down_factor
configItems.description: Defines a beam’s look-down loss. The ratio will adjust the received signal power for targets that are located below the beam’s antenna.

configItems.name: prf_factor
configItems.description: Defines a factor that represents the detection difference for a beam that uses interleaved HPRF and MPRF waveforms. The prf_factor is applied to the received signal power if the absolute value of the target closing speed is less than the ownship velocity.

configItems.name: clutter_attenuation_factor
configItems.description: Specifies a constant value in the range [ 0 .. 1 ] by which the clutter returned will be multiplied to create an ‘attenuated clutter return.’ If the signal_processor type mti_processor is supplied and this value is not provided, a clutter attenuation value will be computed.

configItems.name: signal_processor
configItems.description: Specifies the signal processor identified by <type-name> form the following list:

configItems.name: error_model_parameters
configItems.description: radar_sensor_error

configItems.name: azimuth_beamwidth
configItems.description: Specifies the azimuth beamwidth to be used by the error_model.

configItems.name: elevation_beamwidth
configItems.description: Specifies the elevation beamwidth to be used by the error_model.

configItems.name: pulse_width
configItems.description: Specifies the pulse width to be used by the error_model.

configItems.name: receiver_bandwidth
configItems.description: Specifies the receiver bandwidth to be used by the error_model.

configItems.name: jam_strobe_detector
configItems.description: The jam_strobe_detector allows a WSF_RADAR_SENSOR mode to detect and report the azimuth and/or elevation of jamming power it receives via indicator or strobe tracks. These recorded strobes can be combined with angle-only measurements from other radars using a jam strobe estimator (JSE) algorithm to produce pseudo-measurements passed to a tracking algorithm. Reporting information as well as errors are specified outside the general sensor error models due to differences in the error calculations.

configItems.name: uniform_elevation_error_bound
configItems.description: Specifies the standard deviation for a Gaussian or Uniform distribution of errors to be applied to the azimuth and elevation of the track. The standard deviation may be specified directly as an angle value or as a fraction of the beamwidth of the receiver. In the case of a Uniform distribution, the error bound may be specified instead of the standard deviation. The standard deviation of a symmetric Uniform distribution on the interval is defined to be .

configItems.name: reports_bearing
configItems.description: The bearing from the sensor to the target is reported. This angle is measured in radians from the sensor’s north orientation, and it is in the range .

configItems.name: reports_elevation
configItems.description: The elevation angle from the sensor to the target is reported.

configItems.name: reports_nothing
configItems.description: Has the effect of canceling any previous ‘reports’ commands. This is useful if one wants to reuse an existing sensor definition with embedded ‘reports’ commands but needs to change what is reported.

configItems.name: track_quality
configItems.description: Specify the ‘quality’ of the track when produced from this jam strobe detector.

configItems.name: jamming_perception_timeout
configItems.description: Specifies the time after which jamming that was perceived is no longer perceived, so that the perception of jamming will be returned to a ‘false’ state. If jamming is perceived again before this time has elapsed then the perception of jamming will remain or become ‘true’.

configItems.name: coherent_jamming_perception_threshold
configItems.description: Specifies the minimum threshold value that jamming will be perceived by the operator. Often used in conjunction with jamming_perception_timeout, JammingPerceived script method and electronic_protect techniques.

configItems.name: close_target_detection
configItems.description: The Close Target Detection (CTD) model allows for closely spaced targets and other platform types to be detected and their results used for location measurement and track creation.

configItems.name: debug
configItems.description: If specified debug messages to standard output are available.

configItems.name: acquire_deltas
configItems.description: Defines the deltas for azimuth, elevation and range, with-respect-to the current target cue or request, for which targets will be acquired.

configItems.name: azimuth_delta
configItems.description: Specifies the azimuth delta wrt to the current target cue or request for which other targets will be considered. Value must be >= 0.0.

configItems.name: elevation_delta
configItems.description: Specifies the elevation delta wrt to the current target cue or request for which other targets will be considered. Value must be >= 0.0.

configItems.name: range_delta
configItems.description: Specifies the range delta wrt to the current target cue or request for which other targets will be considered. Value must be >= 0.0.

configItems.name: reacquire_deltas
configItems.description: Defines the deltas for azimuth, elevation and range, with-respect-to the current target cue or request, for which the target can no longer be reacquired.

configItems.name: snr_transfer_rate_table
configItems.description: Specifies a table that maps signal-to-noise-ratio values to message transfer rates. The SNR-Transfer-Rate table will be interpolated. If a table is specified, the table transfer rate values will override the value used specified with the transfer_rate command.

configItems.name: bit_error_probability
configItems.description: Optional parameter that defines the system designed bit error rate probability. It is used to pick the Eb/No values from the Eb/No v.s BER table. Must be greater than or equal to zero.

configItems.name: error_correction
configItems.description: Optional parameter that determines how much error correction will be applied when using Eb/No to calculate data rate. Must be between 0.0 and 1.0.

configItems.name: bit_error_rate_ebno_table
configItems.description: Optional table that defines the Energy per Bit to the Spectral Noise Density (Eb/No) vs. Bit Error Rate (BER). Used in conjunction with the bit_error_probability and error_correction to calculate the data transfer rate of the radio. When using this table Data Rate = SNR* Error Correction * ( Bandwidth / Eb/No ). The Bit-Error-Rate-EbNo-Table will be interpolated. If a table is specified, the table transfer rate values will override the value used specified with the transfer_rate command.

configItems.name: jamming_radius_factor
configItems.description: Specifies an adjustment factor of the effective jamming level based on the targets location type wrt to the sensor’s receiver and jammer transmitter. This adjustment modifies the normally-determined jamming power. If this input is specified within the system_type_data input block then it is specific to a system-type, otherwise this input is defined as the ‘default’ data to use for undefined system-types in the system_type_data. This input can be listed multiple times for defining different <target-position-type> values.

configItems.name: system_type_data
configItems.description: Input block to provide the system type (e.g., SENSOR-TYPE, JAMMER-TYPE) specific data necessary to implement this technique for a given system type. Default data can be set up for system types not defined using the “default” string as the system type.

configItems.name: repeater_effect_control_method
configItems.description: Specifies a repeater control method as described in the table below for setting the type of data that will be used in calculating the repeater factor that will be applied to the jamming power. This adjustment modifies the normally-determined jamming power. If this input is specified within the system_type_data input block then it is specific to a system-type, otherwise this input is defined as the ‘default’ data to use for undefined system-types in the system_type_data.

configItems.name: gain_control_method
configItems.description: Specifies the control method that will be used to determine the minimum gain value for use in calculating the repeater factor. This adjustment modifies the normally-determined jamming power. If this input is specified within the system_type_data input block then it is specific to a system-type, otherwise this input is defined as the ‘default’ data to use for undefined system-types in the system_type_data. If more than one type is to be used then this input can be entered multiple times.

configItems.name: repeater_factor_limits
configItems.description: Specifies the minimum and maximum gain factors, respectively, that the calculated repeater factor will be limited by. If this input is specified within the system_type_data input block then it is specific to a system-type, otherwise this input is defined as the ‘default’ data to use for undefined system-types in the system_type_data.

configItems.name: desired_false_target_rcs
configItems.description: Specifies the desired RCS value for false target blips that the repeater factor will be calculated for when false target effects are turned on within the technique also. This input automatically sets the gain_control_method to desired_rcs. If this input is specified within the system_type_data input block then it is specific to a system-type, otherwise this input is defined as the ‘default’ data to use for undefined system-types in the system_type_data.

configItems.name: desired_jammer_to_noise
configItems.description: Specifies the desired J/N value, where J is the jamming power and N is the receiver noise power, that the repeater factor will calculated for. This input automatically sets the gain_control_method to jammer_to_noise. If this input is specified within the system_type_data input block then it is specific to a system-type, otherwise this input is defined as the ‘default’ data to use for undefined system-types in the system_type_data.

configItems.name: desired_jammer_to_signal
configItems.description: Specifies the desired J/S value, where J is the jamming power and S is the signal power in the receiver, that the repeater factor will calculated for. This input automatically sets the gain_control_method to jammer_to_signal. If this input is specified within the system_type_data input block then it is specific to a system-type, otherwise this input is defined as the ‘default’ data to use for undefined system-types in the system_type_data.

configItems.name: minimum_detect_factor
configItems.description: Specifies the factor that will be added to (in db, multiplied in absolute) to the calculated minimum detect repeater factor when the gain_control_method is set to minimum_detect. If this input is specified within the system_type_data input block then it is specific to a system-type, otherwise this input is defined as the ‘default’ data to use for undefined system-types in the system_type_data.

configItems.name: masking_factor
configItems.description: Specifies the factor that will be added to (in db, multiplied in absolute) to the calculated minimum detect repeater factor when the gain_control_method is set to masking. If this input is specified within the system_type_data input block then it is specific to a system-type, otherwise this input is defined as the ‘default’ data to use for undefined system-types in the system_type_data.

configItems.name: system_type_data
configItems.description: Input block to provide the system type (e.g., SENSOR-TYPE, JAMMER-TYPE) specific data necessary to implement this technique for a given system type. Default data can be set up for system types not defined using the “default” string as the system type.

configItems.name: subtype
configItems.description: Specify the computation subtype. WSF_REVISIT_TIME_MOE has the following subtypes that take no parameter:

configItems.name: output
configItems.description: Specify a form of output to produce for a measure of effectiveness. The allowed values for <output_type> are:

configItems.name: ignore
configItems.description: Indicates the jammer should deny interaction with the objects that are a member of the specified category. This command may be specified multiple times to deny interaction with multiple categories.

configItems.name: ignore_domain
configItems.syntax: ignore_domain [ land | air | surface | subsurface | space ]

configItems.name: ignore_side
configItems.description: Indicates the jammer should deny interaction with platforms or objects contained on platforms that are of the specified side. This command may be specified multiple times to deny interactions with multiple sides.

configItems.name: ignore_same_side
configItems.description: Indicates the jammer should deny interaction with platforms or objects contained on platforms that are on the same side of the platform to which the jammer is attached.

configItems.name: jammer_group
configItems.description: The jammer group name, which this jammer is to be a member of. This input also adds this group name as a category, which enables script category checking as defined in WsfPlatformPart. However, the inverse of this is not true. A category does not add a jammer group name to the jammer.

configItems.name: group_power_distribution
configItems.description: The group power distribution across the jammer group. If average is selected, the total power is averaged across the active group members.

configItems.name: frequency_band
configItems.description: Specifies the frequency band. This input can be used in lieu of the transmitter frequency and bandwidth inputs with the last input definition being used.

configItems.name: repeater
configItems.description: Defines the logic necessary to use an ESM system to start, stop and maintain jamming assignments (i.e., closed loop [automated]) jamming assignments. Furthermore, the repeater logic is currently implemented to block jamming power if the current geometry from the transmitter (e.g., radar/comm) to the ESM for the repeater does not allow for a detection. This blocking logic is crude and may be overachieving the desired results. The repeater will require an ESM sensor(s) to have internal_link to it to operate in any mode other than manual.

configItems.name: debug
configItems.description: Sets debug mode for the repeater, if specified within the repeater … end_repeater input block.

configItems.name: operating_mode
configItems.description: Specifies the operating mode of the repeater as defined below:

configItems.name: signal_following
configItems.description: Specifies that the repeater (i.e., ESMs) will follow signal changes of a track as they are updated, allows the repeater to watch for ESM sensor track updates for signal changes.

configItems.name: debug_repeater
configItems.description: Sets debug mode to ‘true’ for the repeater on this mode only.

configItems.name: maximum_number_of_beams
configItems.description: The maximum number of beams on the jammer.

configItems.name: beam_power_distribution
configItems.description: The beam power distribution across the jammer beams. If average is selected, the total power is averaged across the active beams.

configItems.name: maximum_spots_per_beam
configItems.description: The maximum number of spots on each beam of the jammer.

configItems.name: maximum_number_of_spots
configItems.description: The maximum number of spots when simulating a jammer. If maximum_number_of_beams and/or maximum_spots_per_beam is input after this input, then this input equals the product of these two inputs. If this input is input after maximum_number_of_beams and/or maximum_spots_per_beam then this will limit the total number of active spots available for this jammer.

configItems.name: spot_power_distribution
configItems.description: The spot power distribution across the jammer spots on all beams. If average is selected, the total power is averaged across the active spots on each beam.

configItems.name: vehicle_type
configItems.description: This defines the type of object used by the mover. The vehicle_type is defined in a six_dof_object_types block and must be defined before being referenced.

configItems.name: landing_gear_down
configItems.description: Indicates whether the landing gear should be down or not when the scenario begins.

configItems.name: nws_enabled
configItems.description: Indicates whether nose-wheel steering should be enabled or not. Nose-wheel steering is commonly used when taxiing but should be removed prior to the takeoff roll.

configItems.name: parking_brake_on
configItems.description: This command sets whether the parking brake should be on or off when the scenario begins.

configItems.name: taxi_mode_enabled
configItems.description: This command set whether the autopilot should be in taxi mode when the scenario begins. This should be used only be used when the platform is on ground.

configItems.name: channel_job_type
configItems.description: Specifies that the indicated channel on this RIPR agent processor will be allowed to bid on and win jobs of the indicated type. If no types are specified for a channel than all types are allowed on that channel. The channel-index is an integer value and the job-type is a string that equals the job name (also called the job type). Users can specify many job types for particular channels, or one, or none. If a particular channel bids on a job of type that is not allowed, that bid is ignored. A job of the wrong type will never be awarded to a channel.

configItems.name: job_board_comm
configItems.description: Specifies the name of a comm device that all job interactions will take place over. This includes bidding, status update, and winning jobs.

configItems.name: job_pass_through
configItems.description: If specified, this RIPR processor will simply act as a pass-through for jobs and bids. If asked for its jobs or job board, it will reply with its commander’s jobs or job board. It will not hold any jobs on its own board. Subsequently, all bids from its subordinates go up to its commander and its subordinates will win jobs from its commander’s job board.

configItems.name: job_stickiness
configItems.description: A RIPR processor’s job stickiness is the value used to provide a little extra stability to the current job allocation. When a RIPR processor has won a job and is performing that job, then all of it bids on that job are multiplied by the job_stickiness value. In this way, it’s harder to dislodge somebody from their job once they have won it.

configItems.name: num_job_channels
configItems.description: The number of channels a RIPR processor has represents its capability to perform jobs at the same time. If the RIPR processor is bidding on tracking jobs and its radar can track four targets at once, then it might have four job channels. This way, each channel can bid on jobs, win jobs separately, and allow the agent to perform them concurrently. The responsibility lies with the scenario developer to use the channels. The extended forms of these methods must be used to specify the channel index as parameter aChannelIndex, referenced here:

configItems.name: auto_exclusive_mode
configItems.description: If set to true, the RIPR processor job board will use the time values given with “job_window_open_length” and “bid_window_open_length” to automatically alternate the windows for job bidding and job awarding of the job board according to the proper durations. While the bidding window is closed, all bids given to the job board are ignored. While the job window is closed, all jobs maintain a constant allocation (nobody changes jobs).

configItems.name: bid_window_open_length
configItems.description: Specifies the amount of time the bidding window will be open each cycle. While the bidding window is closed, all bids given to the job board are ignored.

configItems.name: job_window_open_length
configItems.description: Specifies the amount of time the job window will be open each cycle. While the job window is closed, all jobs maintain a constant allocation (nobody changes jobs).

configItems.name: max_weapon_uplinks
configItems.description: Specifies the maximum number of active uplinks the RIPR agent is capable of.

configItems.name: use_remote_tracks_for_uplink
configItems.description: If set to true, the RIPR processor will send tracks from any sensor and any source to weapons it is supporting with an uplink.

configItems.name: weapon_uplink_path
configItems.description: If a weapon uplink path is specified for a RIPR processor, then the processor will support uplinks for all fired weapons. It will send track updates over the designated comm to the fired weapon platform using tracks from the designated sensor. Uplinks can be stopped and started from script, see WSF_RIPR_PROCESSOR.

configItems.name: query_bid_type
configItems.description: Determines and returns an agent’s bid on a given job of the indicated type. No other query_bid_type block for the same job type is allowed to be defined on this agent. The script method WsfRIPRProcessor.QueryBid will execute this block on the given job. You can access the job object by using the “JOB” keyword within the query_bid_type script block. This input is the preferred and explicit method for providing bid values from agents.

configItems.name: query_bid
configItems.description: This input block is obsolete and now deprecated. See the “query_bid_type” script block definition above.

configItems.name: road_network
configItems.description: The name of the route_network to follow.

configItems.name: end_position
configItems.description: Defines the starting location and ending locations. The resulting path will be the points from the road network that define the shortest path between the specified locations.

configItems.name: speed
configItems.description: Defines the platform speed while traveling on the road network.

configItems.name: off_road_speed
configItems.description: Defines the platform speed while traveling off the road network.

configItems.name: linear_acceleration
configItems.description: The linear acceleration to be used to accelerate the platform.

configItems.name: pause_time
configItems.description: The time the mover is paused at the user-specified start position.

configItems.name: use_closest_waypoint
configItems.description: The mover will use the closest waypoints to the user-specified start and end positions when calculating the shortest path along the road network. No off-road segments at the start or the end will be generated.

configItems.name: consider_off_road_shortcut
configItems.description: If this command has a value of true, a second path will be considered as a possible route, that being an off-road ‘shortcut’ path between the start position and the end position. If the shortcut path takes less time to traverse using the off_road_speed than the normal path, it will be used as the route.

configItems.name: update_interval
configItems.description: If non-zero, specifies a periodic time interval at which the simulation will call the mover. If zero then the mover will be called only when it is necessary to determine the position of the containing platform.

configItems.name: update_time_tolerance
configItems.description: When a position update is requested by the simulation, if the time since the previous update is less than or equal to this value then the mover will ignore the update.

configItems.name: desired_heading
configItems.description: Sets the desired heading for the mover, which will take effect at speeds below the “weathercocking speed.”

configItems.name: position_hold_capture_radius
configItems.description: The rotorcraft mover uses a rate guidance mechanism when transiting from one location to another. When approaching a target point, guidance fundamentally changes to capture a position value, and so must decelerate in anticipation of capturing and holding the target position. This value determines the transition point from one guidance type to the other. The default value is set to 200 meters, which should suffice for the vast majority of Rotorcraft models.

configItems.name: start_mode
configItems.description: Specifies the initial mover mode of the platform. The mover mode may be changed externally via script settings or at waypoint transitions. Mover modes are discussed separately.

configItems.name: ned_filter_time_constant
configItems.description: Specifies a filter time constant to apply to commanded acceleration values to smooth transient responses. A larger value will apply a greater amount of smoothing to the commands. Value must be greater than zero. The default is 1 second and is adequate for most purposes.

configItems.name: altitude_error_to_rate_of_climb_gain
configItems.description: Specifies a gain to apply to an altitude error to arrive at a vertical acceleration value. The default is 1 and is adequate for most purposes.

configItems.name: lateral_acceleration_value_pid
configItems.description: Each of the above four input blocks may contain tuning parameters to apply to the Proportional Integral Derivative (PID) controllers, which determine acceleration values which drive the motion state of the platform. It is not necessary for the end-user to modify the default gains, unless a particular dynamic response is required. Tuning PID controllers is outside the scope of this document, but many separate resources are available to assist. PID controller response should be adequate for most purposes.

configItems.name: mode
configItems.description: Ground speed above which the platform will assume a heading that matches the course angle. Below this speed, the platform will assume a desired heading angle, as set by script commands.

configItems.name: weathercock_speed
configItems.description: Ground speed above which the platform will assume a heading that matches the course angle. Below this speed, the platform will assume a desired heading angle, as set by script commands.

configItems.name: maximum_attitude_rate
configItems.description: Maximum angular rate for body attitude changes. This is primarily used in concert with weathercock_speed to determine how quickly the platform will transition in and out of weathercocking mode.

configItems.name: maximum_total_acceleration
configItems.description: Maximum magnitude of linear acceleration. Sets the upper limit during hard lateral accelerations.

configItems.name: minimum_upward_acceleration
configItems.description: Minimum upward acceleration value. When aircraft is rising, and then a command is given to descend quickly, this value sets the minimum vertical acceleration constraint. Note that many rotorcraft with teetering rotor heads are not permitted to pull negative g, by design.

configItems.name: body_rates_gain
configItems.description: Gain to apply to an angular heading error to obtain the rate at which the heading error is removed. Used primarily in removing a heading error when transitioning to fast forward flight, above weathercock speed.

configItems.name: maximum_ground_speed
configItems.description: Maximum permitted ground speed in this motion mode. Typical use would be for <mode> speed constraint.

configItems.name: maximum_rate_of_climb
configItems.description: Maximum permitted rate of climb in this motion mode. Typical use would be to set a realistic climb rate for <mode>.

configItems.name: maximum_rate_of_descent
configItems.description: Magnitude of maximum permitted rate of descent in this motion mode. Value must be greater than zero but will be negated when applied. Typical use would be to set a realistic descent rate for <mode>.

configItems.name: proportional_gain
configItems.description: Gain to apply to current error to attempt to null the error to zero. Larger values will more forcibly attempt to null the error but are prone to induce oscillation in the output.

configItems.name: derivative_gain
configItems.description: Gain to apply to current rate-of-change of error to attempt to prevent the error from overshooting the desired target value. Larger values will oppose any change in the output, causing drift.

configItems.name: integral_gain
configItems.description: Gain to oppose a steady-state bias, which attempts to drive the bias to zero.

configItems.name: input_threshold
configItems.description: Comparison value to determine whether to apply integral summing of the input error sample. While the input value differs more than <input_threshold> from the target value no input integration is performed. Once the input threshold is near the target value, a continuous integration is performed to discern and react to an input bias. If so, integral_gain is applied to the bias to remove it over time.

configItems.name: coherency_ratio
configItems.description: Specifies the ratio of pulses that are coherently processed by the victim’s receiver. Divides the power between the coherent and noise jammer power by this ratio.

configItems.name: jamming_pulse_density
configItems.description: Specifies the pulse density of the jamming signal in range [0,1] to use for this radar type.

configItems.name: samples_per_detection
configItems.description: Specifies the number of pulse samples used in a single detection attempt for a target (e.g., number of Fast Fourier Transform, Integration bins used by the radar). Must be greater than 1.

configItems.name: minimum_jammer_to_noise_threshold
configItems.description: Specifies the minimum jammer-to-noise ratio that this effect is able to effect this radar type’s receiver.

configItems.name: jammer_gain_table
configItems.description: This block defines the jammer gain this effect exhibits as a function of the jammer-to-noise ratio and the pulse density present (i.e., achieved from the input jammer pulse density) in the victim’s receiver.

configItems.name: jammer_to_noise_ratio
configItems.description: Specifies the jammer-to-noise ratio the following set of pulse_density_to_jamming_gain is valid for. This input can be repeated for multiple jammer-to-signal input values as required.

configItems.name: pulse_density_to_jamming_gain
configItems.description: Specifies the jammer power gain factor on the receiver for the achieved pulse density at the victim receiver. This input can be repeated for multiple pulse_density_to_jamming_gain input values for a given jammer_to_noise_ratio as required. Pulse density input range [0.0,…1.0]. The gain lookup values are interpolated for pulse density’s that fall between two values in the table. A pulse_density of 0.0 is automatically mapped to a jammer_gain of -300.0 dB in the tables but can be overridden by the input.

configItems.name: system_type_data
configItems.description: Input block to provide the system type (e.g., SENSOR-TYPE, JAMMER-TYPE) specific data necessary to implement this technique for a given system type. Default data can be set up for system types not defined using the “default” string as the system type.

configItems.name: report_interval
configItems.description: Specifies the update interval for reporting asset status data

configItems.name: engagement_data_update_interval
configItems.description: Specifies the update interval for reporting engagement data (MsgSA_EngagementSummaryData messages)

configItems.name: flight_data_update_interval
configItems.description: Specifies the update interval for reporting flight data (MsgSA_FlightKinematicsData messages)

configItems.name: fuel_data_update_interval
configItems.description: Specifies the update interval for reporting fuel data (MsgSA_FuelData messages)

configItems.name: nav_data_update_interval
configItems.description: Specifies the update interval for reporting navigational data (MsgSA_NavData messages)

configItems.name: flight_controls_data_update_interval
configItems.description: Specifies the update interval for reporting controls data (MsgSA_FlightControlsData messages)

configItems.name: weapons_data_update_interval
configItems.description: Specifies the update interval for reporting weapons data (MsgSA_WeaponsData messages)

configItems.name: track_data_update_interval
configItems.description: Specifies the update interval for reporting track data (MsgSA_TrackData messages)

configItems.name: asset_data_update_interval
configItems.description: Specifies the update interval for reporting asset data (MsgSA_PerceivedAssetsData messages)

configItems.name: asset_purge_lifetime
configItems.description: Specifies the maximum lifetime of assets that lack an update. Assets will be automatically purged if they have not been updated within the specified lifetime limit.

configItems.name: perceived_item_data_update_interval
configItems.description: Specifies the update interval for reporting bogie, bandit, and group data (MsgSA_PerceivedBogiesAndBanditsData and MsgSA_GroupsData messages).

configItems.name: prioritized_item_data_update_interval
configItems.description: Specifies the update interval for reporting prioritized threat data (MsgSA_PrioritizedThreatsAndTargetsData messages).

configItems.name: perceived_item_calculation_update_interval
configItems.description: Specifies the update interval for calculating bogie, bandit, and group data.

configItems.name: prioritized_item_calculation_update_interval
configItems.description: Specifies the update interval for calculating prioritized threat data.

configItems.name: behavior_calculation_update_interval
configItems.description: The SA Processor is unique in that the rate at which WsfAdvancedBehaviorTrees and WsfStateMachines update can be optionally set separately from the processor’s update rate. As a result, the default value of 0 means that it will update at the same rate as the processor, as opposed to never updating.

configItems.name: cognitive_update_interval
configItems.description: The following group of Update Interval Commands is set to a common value by this command:

configItems.name: platform_update_interval
configItems.description: The following group of Update Interval Commands is set to a common value by this command:

configItems.name: universal_update_interval
configItems.description: All Update Interval Commands are set to a common value by this command (excludes asset_purge_lifetime and all calculation update interval commands).

configItems.name: enemy_side
configItems.description: Specifies the name(s) of the enemy’s side(s). If a track has the same side identification as the enemy_side, then the track is considered to be a bandit. Note that multiple entries allows multiple sides to be enemy.

configItems.name: friendly_side
configItems.description: Specifies the name(s) of the friendly side(s). If a track has the same side identification as the friendly_side, then the track is considered to be a friendly. Note that multiple entries allows multiple sides to be friendly. In addition, the same side of the platform containing the SA Processor is always considered friendly, even without specifying it in this manner.

configItems.name: neutral_side
configItems.description: Specifies the name(s) of the neutral side(s). If a track has the same side identification as the neutral_side, then the track is considered to be a neutral. Note that multiple entries allows multiple sides to be neutral.

configItems.name: enemy_type
configItems.description: Adds the enemy type to the list of known enemy types. If a track has the same type identification as the enemy_type, then the track is considered to be a bandit. Note that the type does not necessarily have to be a platform type, it may also be a sensor type, since some sensors will report a sensor type rather than a platform type.

configItems.name: friendly_type
configItems.description: Adds the friendly type to the list of known friendly types. If a track has the same type identification as the friendly_type, then the track is considered to be friendly. Note that the type does not necessarily have to be a platform type, it may also be a sensor type, since some sensors will report a sensor type rather than a platform type.

configItems.name: neutral_type
configItems.description: Adds the neutral type to the list of known neutral types. If a track has the same type identification as the neutral_type, then the track is considered to be neutral. Note that the type does not necessarily have to be a platform type, it may also be a sensor type, since some sensors will report a sensor type rather than a platform type.

configItems.name: missile_type
configItems.description: Adds the missile type to the list of known missile types. If a track has the same type identification as the missile_type, then the track is considered to be a missile. Note that the type does not necessarily have to be a platform type, it may also be a sensor type, since some sensors will report a sensor type rather than a platform type.

configItems.name: asset_ignore
configItems.description: Adds the platform category to a list of assets that will be ignored on the ACES Display.

configItems.name: filter_assets_from_tracks
configItems.description: If true, assets/friendlies will be filtered from track lists

configItems.name: use_iff_id
configItems.description: If true, includes the use of IFF in determining identification. When used, iff_mapping must be defined.

configItems.name: use_simple_id_by_type
configItems.description: If true, a simple identification-by-type approach will be used. In this case, rather than specifying list of enemy, friendly, and neutral types using enemy_side, friendly_side, and neutral_side, a much simpler approach is used, where identification-by-type is performed merely if the track supports type id.

configItems.name: missile_speed_any_alt
configItems.description: If the speed of the track is greater than the specified speed and at any altitude, it will be considered to be a missile/weapon (not an aircraft).

configItems.name: missile_alt_any_speed
configItems.description: If the altitude of the track is greater than the specified altitude and at any speed, it will be considered to be a missile/weapon (not an aircraft).

configItems.name: missile_speed_with_alt
configItems.description: If the speed of the track is greater than the specified speed at (or greater than) the altitude specified in missile_alt_with_speed, it will be considered to be a missile/weapon (not an aircraft).

configItems.name: missile_alt_with_speed
configItems.description: If the altitude of the track is greater than the specified altitude at (or greater than) the speed specified in missile_speed_with_alt, it will be considered to be a missile/weapon (not an aircraft).

configItems.name: missile_nose_angle
configItems.description: If the ownship lies outside of the specified angle off the nose of the track, it will not be considered to be a missile/weapon (not an aircraft). This allows filtering-out tracks that are not heading towards the ownship.

configItems.name: missile_time_to_intercept
configItems.description: If the time to intercept of the track is greater than than the specified time, it will not be considered to be a missile/weapon (not an aircraft). This allows filtering-out tracks that will not intercept the ownship within the specified time.

configItems.name: missile_distance
configItems.description: If the distance to the track is greater than the specified distance, it will not be considered to be a missile/weapon (not an aircraft). This allows filtering-out tracks at a long distance from being considered as missiles.

configItems.name: max_range_for_perceived_assets
