configItems.description: Range limit to include an asset in the perceived asset list. If not specified, no range filter will be used for assets.

configItems.name: max_range_for_perceived_bogies_and_bandits
configItems.description: Range limit to include a bogie/bandit in the perceived bogie/bandit list. If not specified, no range filter will be used for bogies or bandits.

configItems.name: max_range_for_engagement_data
configItems.description: Range limit to report engagement data. If not specified, no range filter will be used on the reporting of engagement data.

configItems.name: assumed_range_for_angle_only_targets
configItems.description: Range assumed for angle-only tracks. If not specified, the range for angle-only tracks will be assumed to be 2.0E+13 meters, which is greater than 100 times the distance from the Earth to the Sun.

configItems.name: filter_requires_same_side
configItems.description: If true, filters out platforms that are not on the same side

configItems.name: filter_requires_not_same_side
configItems.description: If true, filters out platforms that are on the same side

configItems.name: filter_requires_air_domain
configItems.description: If true, filters out platforms that are not in the air domain

configItems.name: filter_requires_not_air_domain
configItems.description: If true, filters out platforms that are in the air domain

configItems.name: filter_requires_land_or_surface_domain
configItems.description: If true, filters out platforms that are not in the land or surface domains

configItems.name: filter_requires_not_subsurface_domain
configItems.description: If true, filters out platforms that are in the subsurface domain

configItems.name: filter_requires_not_space_domain
configItems.description: If true, filters out platforms that are in the space domain

configItems.name: filter_requires_sa_processor
configItems.description: If true, filters out platforms that lack a WSF_SA_PROCESSOR

configItems.name: esm_track_processor
configItems.description: Optional name of a track processor for ESM/RWR tracks. This allows perception of tracks related to ESM and/or RWR sensor systems.

configItems.name: mws_track_processor
configItems.description: Optional name of a track processor for Missile Warning System (MWS) tracks. This allows perception of tracks related to MWS sensor systems.

configItems.name: radar_track_processor
configItems.description: Optional name of a track processor for radar tracks. This allows perception of tracks related to radar sensor systems.

configItems.name: irst_track_processor
configItems.description: Optional name of a track processor for IRST tracks. This allows perception of tracks related to IRST and/or other IR sensors used for detection of airborne platforms.

configItems.name: das_track_processor
configItems.description: Optional name of a track processor for DAS (Distributed Aperture System) tracks. This allows perception of tracks related to DAS and/or other multi-aperture IR/EO sensor systems.

configItems.name: flir_track_processor
configItems.description: Optional name of a track processor for FLIR tracks. This allows perception of tracks related to FLIRs and/or other imaging IR sensor systems that are primarily used for detection of surface-based platforms.

configItems.name: eyes_track_processor
configItems.description: Optional name of a track processor for eyes (visual) tracks. This allows perception of tracks related to any aircrew visual (eyes) sightings.

configItems.name: perception_master_track_processor
configItems.description: Optional name of a track processor for collecting/coordinating perceived tracks. If this is defined, the specified track processor will be used by the SA Processor when perceiving and assessing tracks. If not specified, the master track processor is used (default).

configItems.name: flight_id
configItems.description: Optional flight id (used to denote aircraft in a particular flight). A value of zero indicates that the aircraft is not a member of any flight.

configItems.name: id_flag
configItems.description: Optional string that provides an id within a flight.

configItems.name: bingo_fuel
configItems.description: Optional bingo fuel level. If not specified, the mover value is used (if available), else zero is used.

configItems.name: joker_fuel
configItems.description: Optional joker fuel level. If not specified, the mover value is used (if available), else zero is used.

configItems.name: reporting_self
configItems.description: Specifies whether or not to report out asset status messages about this platform.

configItems.name: reporting_others
configItems.description: Specifies whether or not to report out messages of all received and known asset status (of other platforms).

configItems.name: asset_perception
configItems.description: status_messages: asset perception will utilize any received WsfSA_EntityMessage messages.

configItems.name: perceive_self
configItems.description: Include this platform in the list of perceived assets.

configItems.name: max_threat_load
configItems.description: Specifies the maximum number of bogie/bandit entities and unfocused groups (i.e. perceived items) that may be perceived.

configItems.name: max_asset_load
configItems.description: Specifies the maximum number of assets that may be perceived.

configItems.name: asset_coast_time
configItems.description: Specifies the amount of time that asset perceptions should persist after losing a track.

configItems.name: bandit_coast_time
configItems.description: Specifies the amount of time that bandit perceptions should persist after losing a track.

configItems.name: bogey_coast_time
configItems.description: Specifies the amount of time that bogey perceptions should persist after losing a track.

configItems.name: use_simple_countermeasures
configItems.description: If true, the processor will use num_chaff, num_flares, and num_decoys as the initial countermeasure quantities. When WsfSA_Processor.DispenseChaff, WsfSA_Processor.DispenseFlare, and WsfSA_Processor.DispenseDecoy are invoked, these quantities are simply decremented (nothing is physically fired). If false, the processor will model countermeasures using instances of WSF_CHAFF_WEAPON, WSF_FLARE_WEAPON, and WSF_DECOY_WEAPON defined on the parent platform. When WsfSA_Processor.DispenseChaff, WsfSA_Processor.DispenseFlare, and WsfSA_Processor.DispenseDecoy are called, the respective countermeasures are fired.

configItems.name: num_chaff
configItems.description: When used together with use_simple_countermeasures, specifies the initial chaff quantity.

configItems.name: num_flares
configItems.description: When used together with use_simple_countermeasures, specifies the initial flare quantity.

configItems.name: num_decoys
configItems.description: When used together with use_simple_countermeasures, specifies the initial decoy quantity.

configItems.name: filter_assets_from_bogies
configItems.description: If true, known assets will automatically be filtered from bogies.

configItems.name: consideration_score_randomness
configItems.description: If set, the consideration scores for perceived items will be randomly increased or decreased by an amount less than or equal to this value.

configItems.name: display_perception_delay
configItems.description: Specifies the time to wait before recognizing a new non-visual track as a perceived entity that is available for processing and classification.

configItems.name: visual_perception_delay
configItems.description: Specifies the time to wait before recognizing a new visual track (i.e. eyes_track_processor) as a perceived entity that is available for processing and classification.

configItems.name: bogie_threat_score_multiplier
configItems.description: Multiplier that is used when scoring bogies for the prioritized threat list.

configItems.name: bogie_target_score_multiplier
configItems.description: Multiplier that is used when scoring bogies for the prioritized target list.

configItems.name: ignore_bogies_when_grouping
configItems.description: If true, bogies will not be considered when forming groups.

configItems.name: mission_task
configItems.description: Specifies the primary mission task. This is used in Air Combat Event Pipe data and for display purposes in the Air Combat Visualization Plugin’s Air Combat Overlays.

configItems.name: max_prioritized_threats
configItems.description: Specifies limitation to prioritized threat list count.

configItems.name: max_prioritized_targets
configItems.description: Specifies limitation to prioritized target list count.

configItems.name: max_grouping_distance_centroid
configItems.description: If use_centroid_grouping is true, the maximum distance an entity can be from a group centroid to be considered part of the group.

configItems.name: max_grouping_distance_neighbor
configItems.description: If use_neighbor_grouping is true, the maximum distance an entity can be from another entity in a group to be considered part of the same group.

configItems.name: max_grouping_speed_difference
configItems.description: If use_speed_grouping is true, the maximum difference in speed an entity can be from a group centroid to be considered part of the group.

configItems.name: max_grouping_heading_difference
configItems.description: If use_neighbor_grouping is true, the maximum difference in heading an entity can be from a group centroid to be considered part of the group.

configItems.name: min_group_radius
configItems.description: The minimum radius for a group. The group radius is the maximum of the min_group_radius and the largest distance between a group member and the group centroid.

configItems.name: use_centroid_grouping
configItems.description: Specifies whether an entity must be within max_grouping_distance_centroid of the group centroid to be considered part of the group.

configItems.name: use_neighbor_grouping
configItems.description: Specifies whether an entity must be within max_grouping_distance_neighbor of another entity in a group to be considered part of that group.

configItems.name: use_speed_grouping
configItems.description: Specifies whether an entity must be within max_grouping_speed_difference of the group centroid to be considered part of the group. This only applies when entities are considered for joining a group, not for continuing to stay in the group.

configItems.name: use_heading_grouping
configItems.description: Specifies whether an entity must be within max_grouping_heading_difference of the group centroid to be considered part of the group. This only applies when entities are considered for joining a group, not for continuing to stay in the group.

configItems.name: use_type_grouping
configItems.description: Specifies whether an entity must be the same type as the other members of a group to be considered part of the group. This only applies when entities are considered for joining a group, not for continuing to stay in the group.

configItems.name: ignore_missiles_as_threats
configItems.description: Specifies whether perceived missile entities should be ignored when calculating threat values. Typically, perceived missiles are considered threats and are not ignored.

configItems.name: ignore_bogies_as_threats
configItems.description: Specifies whether perceived bogie entities should be ignored when calculating threat values. Typically, perceived bogies are considered threats and are not ignored.

configItems.name: ignore_missiles_as_targets
configItems.description: Specifies whether perceived missile entities should be ignored when calculating target values. Typically, perceived missiles are not considered targets and are ignored.

configItems.name: ignore_bogies_as_targets
configItems.description: Specifies whether perceived bogie entities should be ignored when calculating target values. Typically, perceived bogies are not considered targets and are ignored.

configItems.name: missile_wez_parameters
configItems.description: Defines parameters for WEZ calculations. See missile_wez_parameters.

configItems.name: aircraft_signature_parameters
configItems.description: Defines parameters for aircraft signatures. See aircraft_signature_parameters.

configItems.name: AssetConsiderationScoring
configItems.description: This is an optional script used to measure asset importance, which is used to determine how strongly the asset should be considered for maintaining perception. If this function is present, it completely overrides the use of any script functions that try to set asset importance or unimportance. This is only useful when max_asset_load is defined, otherwise no limit will be imposed and importance is not necessary. Values returned by the script may be any value (positive or negative), but assets presenting negative scores will be discarded from consideration. High scores indicate a greater interest in the asset, as compared to others.

configItems.name: BogieBanditConsiderationScoring
configItems.description: This is an optional script used to measure bogie/bandit importance, which is used to determine how strongly the bogie/bandit should be considered for maintaining perception. If this function is present, it completely overrides the use of any script functions that try to set bogie/bandit importance or unimportance. This is only useful when max_threat_load is defined, otherwise no limit will be imposed and importance is not necessary. Values returned by the script may be any value (positive or negative), but bogies/bandits presenting negative scores will be discarded from consideration. High scores indicate a greater interest in the bogie/bandit, as compared to others.

configItems.name: MissileConsiderationScoring
configItems.description: This is an optional script used to measure perceived missile bogie/bandit importance, which is used to determine how strongly the missile bogie/bandit should be considered for maintaining perception. If this function is present, it completely overrides the use of any script functions that try to set missile bogie/bandit importance or unimportance. This is only useful when max_threat_load is defined, otherwise no limit will be imposed and importance is not necessary. Values returned by the script may be any value (positive or negative), but missile bogies/bandits presenting negative scores will be discarded from consideration. High scores indicate a greater interest in the missile bogie/bandit, as compared to others.

configItems.name: UnfocusedGroupConsiderationScoring
configItems.description: This is an optional script used to measure perceived unfocused group importance, which is used to determine how strongly the group should be considered for maintaining perception. If this function is present, it completely overrides the use of any script functions that try to set bogie/bandit importance or unimportance. This is only useful when max_threat_load is defined, otherwise no limit will be imposed and importance is not necessary. Values returned by the script may be any value (positive or negative), but bogies/bandits presenting negative scores will be discarded from consideration. High scores indicate a greater interest in the bogie/bandit, as compared to others.

configItems.name: CreatePerceivedItemPruningArray
configItems.description: This is an optional script used to override the default behavior to keep the number of perceived items within max_threat_load.

configItems.name: CalculateRisk
configItems.description: This is an optional script used to calculate the overall operational/tactical risk as assessed by the WSF_SA_PROCESSOR. This should return a normalized value between 0.0 and 1.0. This optional script will override the default calculation.

configItems.name: CalculateSelfRisk
configItems.description: This is an optional script used to calculate the operational/tactical “self-risk” as assessed by the WSF_SA_PROCESSOR, considering only the risk faced by this platform. This should return a normalized value between 0.0 and 1.0. This optional script will override the default calculation.

configItems.name: CalculateFlightRisk
configItems.description: This is an optional script used to calculate the operational/tactical “flight risk” as assessed by the WSF_SA_PROCESSOR, considering the risk that the flight of aircraft (often two or four aircraft) is facing. This should return a normalized value between 0.0 and 1.0. This optional script will override the default calculation.

configItems.name: CalculatePackageRisk
configItems.description: This is an optional script used to calculate the operational/tactical “package risk” as assessed by the WSF_SA_PROCESSOR, considering the risk that the package of aircraft (often multiple flights of aircraft) is facing. This should return a normalized value between 0.0 and 1.0. This optional script will override the default calculation.

configItems.name: CalculateMissionRisk
configItems.description: This is an optional script used to calculate the operational/tactical “mission risk” as assessed by the WSF_SA_PROCESSOR, considering the risk(s) that might prevent the success of the current mission. This should return a normalized value between 0.0 and 1.0. This optional script will override the default calculation.

configItems.name: CalculateDefensiveness
configItems.description: This is an optional script used to calculate the degree of defensiveness that the platform has assessed for the current operational/tactical situation as assessed by the WSF_SA_PROCESSOR. This should return a normalized value between 0.0 and 1.0. This optional script will override the default calculation.

configItems.name: CalculateUrgency
configItems.description: This is an optional script used to calculate the sense of urgency imposed by the operational/tactical situation as assessed by the WSF_SA_PROCESSOR. This should return a normalized value between 0.0 and 1.0. This optional script will override the default calculation.

configItems.name: CalculateWeaponSupport
configItems.description: This is an optional script used to calculate if a weapon is being supported (i.e., is being provided track update information by the parent platform). If a weapon is being supported, it should return true. There is no default implementation for weapon support, so if this function is omitted, the weapon support condition will always be false.

configItems.name: CalculateThreatLevel
configItems.description: This is an optional script used to calculate the threat level presented by the specified bogie/bandit (aThreat). The boolean (aIsBogie) should be true if the threat is a bogie and false if the threat is a bandit. This should return a normalized value between 0.0 and 1.0. This optional script will override the default calculation.

configItems.name: CalculateMissileThreatLevel
configItems.description: This is an optional script used to calculate the threat level presented by the specified missile bogie/bandit (aThreat). The boolean (aIsBogie) should be true if the threat is a bogie and false if the threat is a bandit. This should return a normalized value between 0.0 and 1.0. This optional script will override the default calculation. This is used with CalculateThreatLevel, where CalculateMissileThreatLevel is used for perceived missiles, while CalculateThreatLevel is used for aircraft (and even missiles that are not yet perceived as missiles).

configItems.name: CalculateGroupThreatLevel
configItems.description: This is an optional script used to calculate the threat level presented by the specified unfocused group of bogies/bandits (aThreat). The boolean (aIsBogie) should be true if the threat is a bogie and false if the threat is a bandit. This should return a normalized value between 0.0 and 1.0. This optional script will override the default calculation. This is used with CalculateThreatLevel, where CalculateGroupThreatLevel is used for perceived unfocused groups, while CalculateThreatLevel is used for aircraft (and even missiles that are not yet perceived as missiles).

configItems.name: CalculateTargetValue
configItems.description: This is an optional script used to calculate the target value offered by the specified bogie/bandit (aTarget). The boolean (aIsBogie) should be true if the target is a bogie and false if the target is a bandit. This should return a normalized value between 0.0 and 1.0. This optional script will override the default calculation.

configItems.name: CalculateMissileTargetValue
configItems.description: This is an optional script used to calculate the target value offered by the specified missile bogie/bandit (aTarget). The boolean (aIsBogie) should be true if the target is a bogie and false if the target is a bandit. This should return a normalized value between 0.0 and 1.0. This optional script will override the default calculation. This is used with CalculateTargetValue, where CalculateMissileTargetValue is used for perceived missiles, while CalculateTargetValue is used for aircraft (and even missiles that are not yet perceived as missiles).

configItems.name: CalculateGroupTargetValue
configItems.description: This is an optional script used to calculate the target value offered by the specified unfocused group of bogies/bandits (aTarget). The boolean (aIsBogie) should be true if the target is a bogie and false if the target is a bandit. This should return a normalized value between 0.0 and 1.0. This optional script will override the default calculation. This is used with CalculateTargetValue, where CalculateGroupTargetValue is used for unfocused groups, while CalculateTargetValue is used for aircraft (and even missiles that are not yet perceived as missiles).

configItems.name: CalculateRiskPosedByEntity
configItems.description: This is an optional script used to calculate the risk posed by the specified bogie/bandit entity. This should return a normalized value between 0.0 and 1.0. This optional script will override the default calculation.

configItems.name: CalculateDefensivenessInducedByEntity
configItems.description: This is an optional script used to calculate the degree of defensiveness induced by the specified bogie/bandit entity. This should return a normalized value between 0.0 and 1.0. This optional script will override the default calculation.

configItems.name: CalculateUrgencyInducedByEntity
configItems.description: This is an optional script used to calculate the sense of urgency induced by the specified bogie/bandit entity. This should return a normalized value between 0.0 and 1.0. This optional script will override the default calculation.

configItems.name: ProjectPositionInTime
configItems.description: This is an optional script used to estimate a future location for an entity. This should return a valid WsfGeoPoint. This script will override the default calculation.

configItems.name: ProjectPositionForward
configItems.description: This is an optional script used to estimate a future location for an entity, assuming forward motion. This should return a valid WsfGeoPoint. This script will override the default calculation.

configItems.name: ProjectPositionLevelTurnLeft
configItems.description: This is an optional script used to estimate a future location for an entity, assuming it carries out a constant-g turn to its left. This should return a valid WsfGeoPoint. This script will override the default calculation.

configItems.name: ProjectPositionLevelTurnRight
configItems.description: This is an optional script used to estimate a future location for an entity, assuming it carries out a g-limited level turn to its right. This should return a valid WsfGeoPoint. This script will override the default calculation.

configItems.name: ProjectPositionTurnToHeading
configItems.description: This is an optional script used to estimate a future location for an entity, assuming it carries out a g-limited level turn to the provided heading. This should return a valid WsfGeoPoint. This optional script will override the default calculation.

configItems.name: ProjectPositionGoToPoint
configItems.description: This is an optional script used to estimate a future location for an entity, assuming it carries out a g-limited level turn toward the provided location. This should return a valid WsfGeoPoint. This optional script will override the default calculation.

configItems.name: ProjectPositionSlice
configItems.description: This is an optional script used to estimate a future location for an entity, assuming it carries out a g-limited roll-and-pull maneuver away from its current heading. This should return a valid WsfGeoPoint. This optional script will override the default calculation.

configItems.name: ProjectPositionSliceToHeading
configItems.description: This is an optional script used to estimate a future location for an entity, assuming it carries out a g-limited roll-and-pull maneuver to the provided heading. This should return a valid WsfGeoPoint. This optional script will override the default calculation.

configItems.name: ProjectPositionSplitS
configItems.description: This is an optional script used to estimate a future location for an entity, assuming it carries out a g-limited split-S maneuver. This should return a valid WsfGeoPoint. This optional script will override the default calculation.

configItems.name: lateral_offsets
configItems.description: Provides a listing of the lateral offsets used as the first independent variable (slowest-changing index) in the intercept_envelope which follows. Lateral offset is the horizontal distance with which the target would overfly the launcher if the current track is maintained. Values are to be provided in increasing order, and the effect is assumed symmetrical about the launcher’s line-of-sight axis.

configItems.name: altitudes
configItems.description: Specifies the target altitudes used as the second independent variable in the intercept_envelope below. May be uneven but must be in increasing numerical order.

configItems.name: ranges
configItems.description: Specifies the ground ranges used as the third independent variable in the intercept_envelope. May be uneven but must be in increasing numerical order.

configItems.name: speeds
configItems.description: Specifies the target speeds used as the fourth independent variable in the intercept_envelope. May be uneven but must be in increasing numerical order.

configItems.name: intercept_envelope
configItems.description: This block contains the data that defines the intercept envelope. By convention, any unsuccessful intercept point may be omitted from the tabulation, and a time-of-flight of -1.0 seconds (a miss) is assumed. The five index values given in the example below are printed out by the class weapon_tools generator, and are used to assure proper indexing when the data is read in by the stream parser.

configItems.name: interpolation_test
configItems.description: For debug purposes only, and optional. Inside this block one may place one or more ‘lateral_offset <distance-value>’, ‘altitude <distance-value>’, ‘target_speed <speed_value>’ and ‘ground_range <distance_value>’ specifications. Each time the keyword ‘test’ appears, the most recent value of (offset, altitude, speed, range) is saved off as a test point, and stored into a test point array. After the launch computer is initialized, each of these test points will be evaluated, and the corresponding interpolated time-of-flight value will be printed to the screen. The example given below saves off three points for testing.

configItems.name: intensity_limits
configItems.description: Specifies the range used to map signal strength to normalized pixel intensity in the resulting image. A signal strength less than <min-db-power> will have a pixel intensity of zero, while a signal strength greater than <max-db-power> will have a pixel intensity of one.

configItems.name: intensity_range
configItems.description: Specifies the range used to map signal strength to a normalized pixel intensity. A signal strength less than noise_power will have a pixel intensity of zero, while a signal strength greater than receiver noise power plus the value of this command will have a pixel intensity of one.

configItems.name: rescale_substandard_image
configItems.description: For ‘spot’ mode only. Specifies if a ‘substandard image’ should be rescaled so its aspect ratio of the pixels is the same as a ‘standard image.’ A ‘substandard image’ is one where the the collection time was insufficient to produce the desired cross range resolution (as defined by resolution command or derived from the dwell_time command.

configItems.name: show_calibration_data
configItems.description: If specified, the model will display general sensor performance data (e.g., power, frequency, antenna gains) when the sensor is created.

configItems.name: show_status
configItems.description: If specified, the model will display certain key calculated parameters whenever the sensor changes state (turned on or off or mode changed).

configItems.name: call_sensor_track_observers
configItems.description: Specify if the ‘sensor track observers’ should be called. If true, sensor track observer events will be invoked which enables the generation of data that allows many visualization tools to display detection lines during the image formation process. These extra events, however, may cause problems to some observers if they haven’t been modified to ignore these events (which is the reason for the default being ‘false’).

configItems.name: sar_constraint_plotting
configItems.description: If ‘true’, the model will internally remove certain internal limits to allow a ‘SAR Constraint plot’ to be properly created within using the horizontal_map function of sensor_plot.

configItems.name: operating_mode
configItems.description: Specifies the operating mode. In ‘spot’ mode, when the sensor is turned on, it will be trained on the current cued location and an ‘image will be formed. The image will be delivered when the sensor is subsequently turned off, either as a result of automatic_turn_off or by an explicit external request (WsfSensor.TurnOff).

configItems.name: automatic_turn_off
configItems.description: For ‘spot’ mode only. If specified the sensor will automatically turn itself off after the dwell_time or by the time required to form an image whose resolution is at least that specified by resolution.

configItems.name: resolution
configItems.description: Specifies the desired cross range resolution of an image cell/pixel. This is used to compute the dwell time necessary form a image of the specified cross range resolution.

configItems.name: dwell_time
configItems.description: Specifies the ‘collection time,’ or the amount of time the sensor will dwell on the location in order to form the image. This is also used to predict cross range resolution.

configItems.name: maximum_dwell_time
configItems.description: For ‘spot’ mode only. If specified, the dwell time computed to achieve the desired resolution will be limited to this value.

configItems.name: maximum_detectable_speed
configItems.description: Specifies the maximum possible speed at which an object can be traveling and still be present in the image.

configItems.name: minimum_clutter_to_noise_ratio
configItems.description: For ‘spot’ mode only. Specifies the clutter-to-noise ratio below, which the image will be declared to be ‘substandard.’ See inhibit_substandard_collection for more information.

configItems.name: inhibit_substandard_collection
configItems.description: For ‘spot’ mode only. If true, the request to collect an image will be suppressed if the internally computed clutter-to-noise ratio for the desired resolution is below the minimum_clutter_to_noise_ratio. This effectively prohibits the sensor from being turned on until the conditions are present that would allow collection of an image of the desired image resolution.

configItems.name: doppler_filter_broadening_factor
configItems.description: This accounts for the fact that Doppler filters do not have rectangular weighting. Slightly widens the filter to control “bleeding” energy into adjacent filters. This is typically in the range of [ 1.0, 2.0 ].

configItems.name: doppler_overcollect_ratio
configItems.description: A ‘safety margin’ to be used when computing the minimum PRF that is allowed. This is typically in the range of [ 1.0, 2.0 ].

configItems.name: image_height
configItems.description: Specify the width and height respectively of SAR image area as measured on the ground. This provides a more precise means of specifying the size image area rather than attempting to use the azimuth and elevation field of view, which would need to vary based on the depression angle.

configItems.name: image_size
configItems.description: An alternative means of specify the height and width of SAR image area as measured on the ground. This is the same as specifying the same value for image_width and image_height.

configItems.name: sar_error_model_parameters
configItems.description: This command will invoke the range and Doppler error computation and application to generate SAR Target Location Errors. This involved translating SUPPRESSOR’s mtsar.f routine, which was merely a translation from TRIMSIM. This generates a Range and Doppler variance that was then used in an error application routine coded from equations to compute SAR Target Location Errors (TLEs). The new input data is as follows, and if used will supersede the baseline error computation method.

configItems.name: platform_position_error_sigmas
configItems.description: Defines the sensing platform’s location errors due to GPS or INS inaccuracies. These are in an NED coordinate frame.

configItems.name: platform_velocity_error_sigmas
configItems.description: Defines the sensing platform’s velocity errors due to GPS and/or IMU inaccuracies. These are in an NED coordinate frame.

configItems.name: inter_system_time_delay
configItems.description: Needs description.

configItems.name: range_error_sigma
configItems.description: Sensor’s range measurement accuracy error standard deviation.

configItems.name: doppler_frequency_error_sigma
configItems.description: Sensor’s doppler measurement accuracy error standard deviation.

configItems.name: transmit_frequency_error_sigma
configItems.description: Sensor’s transmit frequency error standard deviation.

configItems.name: range_cursor_location_error_sigma
configItems.description: Needs description.

configItems.name: range_target_selection_error_sigma
configItems.description: Needs description.

configItems.name: doppler_cursor_location_error_sigma
configItems.description: Needs description.

configItems.name: doppler_target_selection_error_sigma
configItems.description: Needs description.

configItems.name: atmospheric_refraction_residual
configItems.description: Needs description.

configItems.name: on_initialize
configItems.description: This block defines a script that is executed during ‘phase 1’ initialization of the processor. During phase 1 initialization the processor may not assume anything about state of platform or any of its constituent parts.

configItems.name: on_initialize2
configItems.description: This block defines a script that is executed during ‘phase 2’ initialization of the processor. During phase 2 initialization the processor may assume the platform and its constituent parts have completed phase 1 initialization.

configItems.name: update_interval
configItems.description: Specify the interval at which the on_update script should be executed. If this value is not specified then the on_update script will not be executed (even if it is defined).

configItems.name: on_update
configItems.description: This block defines a script that is executed in response to the processors periodic update (as defined by the update_interval). If update_interval is not defined or is zero then this block will not be executed.

configItems.name: on_message
configItems.description: This command block defines a script that is executed whenever the processor receives a message. If the script block is preceded by a type / subtype commands, the script will process any messages matching the type/subtype. If the script block is preceded by default, it will process the any message type not yet processed in this block.

configItems.name: show_state_evaluations
configItems.description: Indicates that information about state evaluations should be written to standard output. This essentially shows the true or false status of the evaluation of each next_state block.

configItems.name: show_state_transitions
configItems.description: Indicates that information about state transitions should be written to standard output.

configItems.name: state
configItems.description: Defines a state in a state machine with the name <state-name>. Each state can use a different behavior_tree. Each state can have child states defined inside of it.

configItems.name: on_message_create
configItems.description: This is an optional script that can be defined, which allows one to modify a message internally created by a processor prior to it being sent. This is typically used to override the default priority of a message using WsfMessage.SetPriority

configItems.name: grid
configItems.description: Use the coverage grid with the given name as the grid over which this coverage will be computed.

configItems.name: assets
configItems.description: Specify the free assets to use for this coverage.

configItems.name: platform
configItems.description: Specify the platform with the given name is to be included among the free assets for this coverage. Unless ‘none’ is supplied as the device name, the given platform must have a relevant device with the given name.

configItems.name: platform_type
configItems.description: Specify that all platforms with the given type are to be included among the free assets for this coverage. Unless ‘none’ is supplied as the device name, the given platform type must have a relevant device with the given name.

configItems.name: category
configItems.description: Specify that any platforms in the given category with a relevant device are to be included among the free assets for this coverage. If ‘none’ is specified as the device name, then all platforms in this category will be added to the set of free assets for this coverage.

configItems.name: group
configItems.description: Specify that any platform in the given group with a relevant device are to be included among the free assets for this coverage. If ‘none’ is specified as the device name, then all platforms in this group will be added to the set of free assets for this coverage.

configItems.name: moe
configItems.description: Specify a measure of effectiveness (MOE) to be computed by the coverage. See Predefined Measures of Effectiveness for a list of available MOEs.

configItems.name: start_time
configItems.description: Set the start of the coverage interval to the given simulation time. Either this command or start_epoch can be used to specify the coverage interval’s start time. If no start time is specified the coverage interval’s start is set to the simulation’s start time.

configItems.name: end_time
configItems.description: Set the end time of the coverage interval to the given simulation time. Either this command or end_epoch can be used to specify the coverage interval’s end time. If no end time is specified the coverage interval’s end is set to the simulation’s end time.

configItems.name: start_epoch
configItems.description: Set the start of the coverage interval to the given date and time. Either this command or start_time can be used to specify the coverage interval’s start time. If no start time is specified the coverage interval’s start is set to the simulation’s start time.

configItems.name: end_epoch
configItems.description: Set the end of the coverage interval to the given date and time. Either this command or end_time can be used to specify the coverage interval’s end time. If no end time is specified the coverage interval’s end time is set to the simulation’s end time.

configItems.name: output_dir
configItems.description: Set the directory into which all file produced by this coverage will be generated. The default output directory is the working directory.

configItems.name: raw_data_file
configItems.description: If this filename is set, the coverage computation will store raw access intervals and write those intervals to the named file at the end of the coverage computation.

configItems.name: overlay_file
configItems.description: If this filename is set, the coverage computation will produce a data file with the given name that can be displayed by the CoverageOverlay plugin. This command will append the canonical extension for these files, “.cvg”, to the specified filename.

configItems.name: interval_constraint
configItems.description: Specifying an interval constraint for a coverage computation allows intervals that are too short or long in duration to be excluded from the computation. There are a number of ways to specify for which assets these constraints apply. Multiple specifications can be included in a single interval constraint block, and multiple interval constraint blocks can be specified for a single coverage computation.

configItems.name: output_file
configItems.description: Specify the name of the file into which the intervals that were filtered out of the coverage computation will be written. The format of these files will match the output from raw_data_file produced files.

configItems.name: device
configItems.description: Specify that access intervals involving the named device will be filtered according to the given <constraint-type>.

configItems.name: device_type
configItems.description: Specify that access intervals involving devices with the given <device-type> will be filtered according to the given <constraint-type>.

configItems.name: ttr_tracking_mode_name
configItems.description: Sets the name of the TTR tracking mode.

configItems.name: max_tar_acquisition_time
configItems.description: The maximum time the TAR is allowed to search for the assigned target without finding it.

configItems.name: max_ttr_acquisition_time
configItems.description: The maximum time the TTR is allowed to search for the assigned target without finding it.

configItems.name: turn_off_tar_if_no_tracks
configItems.description: When true, the TAR is turned off when the radar has no targets assigned.

configItems.name: turn_off_ttr_if_no_tracks
configItems.description: When true, the TTR is turned off when the radar has no targets assigned.

configItems.name: unitary
configItems.description: The azimuth to which the TTR will return when it has no more assignments. This azimuth is defined in the PCS frame of the the TTR (thus, setting this value to 0 degrees points the resting azimuth directly in front of the sensor, 90 degrees points it to the right, -90 to the left, and 180 degrees directly behind). Since this is an azmiuth, it should be in the range [-180, 180] degrees.

configItems.name: output
configItems.description: Specify a form of output to produce for a measure of effectiveness. The allowed values for <output_type> are:

configItems.name: apply_electronic_protect_effects
configItems.description: Specifies whether or not electronic_protect effects should be applied to the calculated number of false targets.

configItems.name: combine_multi_beam_counts
configItems.description: Specifies whether or not radars with multiple beams should combine their false target counts for total comparison. Once the number of false targets exceeds the maximum_false_target_capacity then subsequent beams will not be calculated.

configItems.name: jamming_pulse_density
configItems.description: Specifies the pulse density of the jamming signal in range [0,1] to use for this radar type. Mutually exclusive with the number_of_false_targets.

configItems.name: maximum_false_target_capacity
configItems.description: Specifies the maximum number of false targets that this radar type is able to process before becoming flooded.

configItems.name: number_of_false_targets
configItems.description: Specifies the number of false targets that will be created for this radar type. Mutually exclusive with the jamming_pulse_density.

configItems.name: percent_of_beamwidth_for_detection
configItems.description: Specifies the percent of the radar beamwidth that a detection will occur for this radar type in the range [0,1]. For example a value of 0.5 means it takes a half a beamwidth of consecutive pulses to declare a detection, and a value of 1.0 means it takes the full beamwidth.

configItems.name: update_once_per_frame
configItems.description: Specifies whether or not the false target counts for a radar sensor mode should be update more than once per frame time.

configItems.name: use_random_calculation_draw
configItems.description: Specifies whether or not to use a random calculation draw to determine if a detection is blocked or not per the following equation:

configItems.name: system_type_data
configItems.description: Input block to provide the system type (e.g., SENSOR-TYPE, JAMMER-TYPE) specific data necessary to implement this technique for a given system type. Default data can be set up for system types not defined using the “default” string as the system type.

configItems.name: add_subobject
configItems.description: Specifies the base name of a subobject on the WSF_SIX_DOF_MOVER that will be launched/fired. Each individual subobject supported by the weapon (launcher) requires its own add_subobject command line. Each subobject must have a unique name. The subobject weapons will be launched in the order they are listed. Note that the launched platform type associated with the subobject is specified using the definition contained in the SixDOF platform mappings.

configItems.name: initial_quantity
configItems.description: Defines the initial quantity of fuel to be loaded on the vehicle. WSF_SIX_DOF_FUEL will interact with WSF_SIX_DOF_MOVER to set the initial fuel. Fuel will be added to internal tanks first, keeping the percentage filled for each tank in sync. For example, if the initial_quantity was 75% of the total internal fuel capacity, each internal fuel tank would be filled to 75% and no external tanks would be filled.

configItems.name: reserve_quantity
configItems.description: Defines the threshold such that when the quantity of fuel remaining falls below this value, the platform is considered to be operating on reserves. If an on_reserve block is defined, it will be executed when this state is reached.

configItems.name: bingo_quantity
configItems.description: Defines the threshold such that when the quantity of fuel remaining falls below this value, the platform is considered to have reached a BINGO state. If an on_bingo block is defined, it will be executed when this state is reached.

configItems.name: maximum_quantity
configItems.description: The fuel capacity is determined by fuel tank definitions in a WSF_SIX_DOF_MOVER. If maximum_quantity is specified, it will be ignored and WSF_SIX_DOF_FUEL will output a warning.

configItems.name: mode
configItems.description: WSF_SIX_DOF_FUEL and WSF_SIX_DOF_MOVER do not use a fuel mode. If mode is specified, it will be ignored and WSF_SIX_DOF_FUEL will output a warning.

configItems.name: consumption_rate
configItems.description: Fuel consumption rate is not a single/constant value for a WSF_SIX_DOF_MOVER. If consumption_rate is specified, it will be ignored and WSF_SIX_DOF_FUEL will output a warning.

configItems.name: on_bingo
configItems.description: Defines a script to be executed when the quantity of fuel remaining falls below the threshold defined by bingo_quantity.

configItems.name: on_empty
configItems.description: Defines a script to be executed when all fuel has been expended.

configItems.name: on_reserve
configItems.description: Defines a script to be executed when the quantity of fuel remaining falls below the threshold defined by reserve_quantity.

configItems.name: on_refuel
configItems.description: Defines a script to be executed when a refueling operation has been completed.

configItems.name: commanded_throttle
configItems.description: Specifies a throttle factor in the range [0..1] that overrides and throttle specification in the mover.

configItems.name: vehicle_type
configItems.description: This defines the type of object used by the mover. See vehicle_type and vehicle_type.

configItems.name: autopilot_no_control
configItems.description: This will command the autopilot to “zero” all controls, which will center the stick and rudder and pull back throttle(s) to zero (idle). It is similar to enable_controls but is commanding the autopilot, rather than the controls themselves.

configItems.name: enable_controls
configItems.description: This enables/disables control inputs from any source (autopilot, external manual pilot, etc.). Controls are enabled by default, so this command is typically used to disable controls at the start. This is often used to allow a weapon to drop ballistically and without control inputs as it is released from the carrying aircraft and then calling the script method WsfSixDOF_Mover.EnableControls with true to establish control input after the weapon is safely clear of the aircraft.

configItems.name: enable_thrust_vectoring
configItems.description: Indicates whether thrust vectoring is enabled or not.

configItems.name: engines_on
configItems.description: Indicates whether the engines should be on or off when the scenario begins.

configItems.name: follow_vertical_track
configItems.description: Normally, the autopilot will climb/dive as quickly as possible (within the current limits – see WsfSixDOF_Mover.SetVerticalSpeedMax and WsfSixDOF_Mover.SetVerticalSpeedMin) when changing altitude, but when “follow_vertical_track” is set, the autopilot will instead use a vertical speed that will allow the object to smoothly/slowly change altitude along a straight line vertical track between waypoints.

configItems.name: ignore_all_crashes
configItems.description: Indicates whether the mover ignore all forms of crashes. This is often used in testing.

configItems.name: six_dof_alt
configItems.description: This command sets the initial altitude of the mover.

configItems.name: six_dof_ned_heading
configItems.description: This command sets the initial heading of the mover.

configItems.name: six_dof_ned_pitch
configItems.description: This command sets the initial pitch angle of the mover.

configItems.name: six_dof_ned_roll
configItems.description: This command sets the initial roll angle of the mover.

configItems.name: six_dof_position
configItems.description: This command sets the initial position (using decimal latitude longitude) of the mover.

configItems.name: six_dof_set_velocity_ned_fps
configItems.description: This command sets the initial velocity of the mover in NED coordinates using ft/sec.

configItems.name: produces_launch_smoke
configItems.description: This command sets how long the vehicle will produce a launch smoke/flash effect (appearance only) when launched. If no launch effect is desired, this should not be defined at all.

configItems.name: throttle_afterburner
configItems.description: This command sets the throttle to afterburner when the scenario begins.

configItems.name: throttle_full
configItems.description: This command sets the throttle to mil power when the scenario begins.

configItems.name: throttle_idle
configItems.description: This command sets the throttle to idle when the scenario begins.

configItems.name: wash_in_conditions
configItems.description: Including this flag indicates that this mover should “wash-in” conditions on initialization. This means that the object will run in a special mode to help “ramp-in” and “stabilize” the object on initialization by allowing it to have some time to settle in the needed angle of attack (alpha) as well as the proper throttle setting. This is useful to ensure vehicles are stable when they start the simulation – they may otherwise lack the correct alpha, for example, when they start in the simulation.

configItems.name: route
configItems.description: Specifies the latitude and longitude of the waypoint.

configItems.name: position
configItems.description: Specifies the latitude and longitude of the waypoint.

configItems.name: altitude
configItems.description: Specifies the altitude (MSL) at the waypoint.

configItems.name: speed
configItems.description: Specifies the speed at the waypoint.

configItems.name: label
configItems.description: Associates a label with the immediately following waypoint definition. This can be used as the target of a goto command.

configItems.name: goto
configItems.description: Go to the waypoint with the specified label in the current route.

configItems.name: bank_angle_limit
configItems.description: Specifies the maximum bank angle to be used for turns when making heading changes on the route segment that starts with this waypoint. This effectively sets the radial_acceleration to .

configItems.name: radial_acceleration
configItems.description: Specifies the radial acceleration to be used for turns when making heading changes on the route segment that starts with this waypoint.

configItems.name: turn_g_limit
configItems.description: Specifies the maximum turn g-load to be used for turns when making heading changes on the route segment that starts with this waypoint. This effectively sets the radial_acceleration to .

configItems.name: switch_on_approach
configItems.description: Defines the condition when the mover should declare that it has reached this waypoint and should start moving towards the next waypoint. switch_on_passing is sometimes known as ‘turn long’ and causes the switch to occur when the platform passes over or along side of the waypoint. switch_on_approach is sometimes known as ‘turn short’ and causes the switch to occur before the waypoint.

configItems.name: use_route
configItems.description: Supplies the name of the route to follow. The route is assumed to be a predefined absolute route.

configItems.name: auxiliary_antenna_pattern
configItems.description: Specifies the antenna pattern name to be used.

configItems.name: auxiliary_beam_tilt
configItems.description: Specifies the beam tilt of the auxiliary receiver. The default tilt is angle is derived from the receiver this effect is attached to if this is not defined.

configItems.name: blanking_threshold
configItems.description: Specifies the blanking threshold level at which the signal will be blanked. Signal blanking will occur if the (auxiliary receiver channel)/(main channel power) >= blanking_threshold.

configItems.name: main_jnr_thresholds
configItems.description: Specifies the main channel JNR threshold levels to use as the lower and upper levels, respectively, at which the SLB will operate with the input jamming signal.

configItems.name: auxiliary_jnr_thresholds
configItems.description: Specifies the auxiliary channel JNR threshold levels to use as the lower and upper levels, respectively, at which the SLB will operate with the input jamming signal.

configItems.name: saturation_effect
configItems.description: Input block to provide the saturation effect and it’s associated input commands.

configItems.name: duty_cycle_limit
configItems.description: Specifies the maximum duty-cycle of the incoming jamming signal at which blanking will occur. Any jamming signal with a duty-cycle greater than this value will not be blanked (i.e., the blanker will not be operational). Valid values in range of [0..1].

configItems.name: number_slc_channels_saturated
configItems.description: specifies the number of sidelobe canceler (slc) channels this technique will saturate (occupy).

configItems.name: signal_modulation
configItems.description: specifies the signal modulation used by this technique.

configItems.name: slc_degradation_factor
configItems.description: specifies the degradation factor to apply to the slc cancellation ratio defined by the WSF_SLC_EFFECT.

configItems.name: system_type_data
configItems.description: input block to provide the system type (e.g., sensor-type, jammer-type) specific data necessary to implement this technique for a given system type. Default data can be set up for system types not defined using the “default” string as the system type.

configItems.name: auxiliary_antenna_pattern
configItems.description: Specifies the antenna pattern name to be used.

configItems.name: auxiliary_beam_tilt
configItems.description: Specifies the beam tilt of the auxiliary receiver. The default tilt angle is derived from the receiver this effect is attached to if this is not defined.

configItems.name: number_of_canceler_channels
configItems.description: Specifies the number of canceler channels (i.e., canceling loops or cancelers).

configItems.name: cancellation_lock_ratio
configItems.description: Specifies the canceling threshold level at which the signal will be canceled. Signal canceling will occur if the (auxiliary receiver channel)/(main channel power) >= cancellation_lock_ratio.

configItems.name: minimum_cancelled_pulsewidth
configItems.description: Specifies the minimum pulsewidth from pulse type jamming the canceler is able to operate on.

configItems.name: loop_settling_time
configItems.description: Specifies the canceler loop settling time. This time is currently only used to interact with the WSF_POL_MOD_EFFECT polarization_switching_rate to negate any degradation and or multiple channels canceled by this EA effect.

configItems.name: main_jnr_thresholds
configItems.description: Specifies the main channel JNR threshold levels to use as the lower and upper levels, respectively, at which the SLC will operate with the input jamming signal.

configItems.name: auxiliary_jnr_thresholds
configItems.description: Specifies the auxiliary channel JNR threshold levels to use as the lower and upper levels, respectively, at which the SLC will operate with the input jamming signal.

configItems.name: cancellation_ratio
configItems.description: Specifies the steady state cancellation ratio applied to jamming signals when the number of jammers is less than or equal to the number_of_canceler_channels.

configItems.name: saturation_ratio
configItems.description: Specifies the steady state cancellation ratio applied to jamming signals when the number of jammers is greater than the number_of_canceler_channels.

configItems.name: cancellation_ratios
configItems.description: This command allows the definition of cancellation ratios that are:

configItems.name: saturation
configItems.description: This command allows the definition of saturation cancellation ratios that are nondependent or jammer-to-noise-dependent

configItems.name: orbital_state
configItems.description: Specify the orbital state in the form of an epoch or epoch_date_time, and one of the following:

configItems.name: position
configItems.description: Sets the initial location of the space mover. This command must be used in conjunction with the velocity command.

configItems.name: velocity
configItems.description: Sets the initial velocity of the space mover. This command must be used in conjunction with the position command.

configItems.name: epoch
configItems.description: Specify the epoch that corresponds with the reference epoch at which the orbital elements are valid.

configItems.name: epoch_date_time
configItems.description: Specify the date and time that corresponds with the reference epoch at which the orbital elements are valid.

configItems.name: designator
configItems.description: Specify the designator for the space mover.

configItems.name: eccentricity
configItems.description: Specify the eccentricity of the orbit. The specified value must be greater than or equal to zero (circular orbit).

configItems.name: semi_major_axis
configItems.description: Specify the semi-major axis of the ellipse defining the orbit.

configItems.name: revolutions_per_day
configItems.description: Specify the number revolutions per day the satellite orbits the Earth.

configItems.name: periapsis_radius
configItems.description: Specify the periapsis radius of the ellipse defining the orbit. This is the smallest distance between the satellite and the center of the central body.

configItems.name: apoapsis_radius
configItems.description: Specify the apoapsis radius of the ellipse defining the orbit. This is the largest distance between the satellite and the center of the central body.

configItems.name: periapsis_altitude
configItems.description: Specify the periapsis altitude of the ellipse defining the orbit. This is the smallest distance between the satellite and the surface of the central body.

configItems.name: apoapsis_altitude
configItems.description: Specify the apoapsis altitude of the ellipse defining the orbit. This is the largest distance between the satellite and the surface of the central body.

configItems.name: raan
configItems.description: Specify the right ascension of the ascending node (“raan”). This is the angle, measured counterclockwise along the celestial equator from the vernal equinox (the angle of right ascension) that the satellite crosses the equator from south to north (the ascending node).

configItems.name: inclination
configItems.description: Specify the separation angle of the tangent to the orbital plane with the Earth’s axis of rotation.

configItems.name: mean_anomaly
configItems.description: Specify the angular location of the satellite in its orbit at the epoch time. This angle is measured from the periapsis and represents the angle the satellite would traverse at a constant angular rate.

configItems.name: true_anomaly
configItems.description: Specify the angular location of the satellite in its orbit at the epoch time. This angle is measured from the periapsis and represents the true angular location of the satellite.

configItems.name: argument_of_periapsis
configItems.description: Specify the angle of the perigee (periapsis) with respect to the Earth’s surface. This angle is measured from the ascending node.

configItems.name: descriptor
configItems.description: Specify an arbitrary descriptor (tag) for the space vehicle.

configItems.name: initial_state_lla
configItems.description: Specify the initial state of the platform in terms of a location and velocity. The location is in lat, lon, alt format; the velocity is in a local North, East, Down frame. This input is similar to the position input above, but in this case it completely specifies the physical state of the object.

configItems.name: initial_state_eci
configItems.description: Specify the initial state of the platform in terms of a location and velocity. The location and velocity are in the ECI frame. This input is similar to the position input above, but in this case it completely specifies the physical state of the object.

configItems.name: oblate_earth
configItems.description: Enable or disable a first-order oblate earth perturbation. When enabled, the simulated effect is that of two bodies and an oblate Earth. When disabled, the effect is that of two bodies and a spherical earth.

configItems.name: orbit_color
configItems.description: Specify the color of the orbit.

configItems.name: orbit
configItems.description: Specify a Two Line Element (TLE) that defines mean orbital elements and other data used to propagate a satellite. Two Line Elements are usually acquired from an existing source such as the Spacetrak database (http://www.space-track.org) or Celestrak (http://www.celestrak.com/NORAD/elements). Unlike ordinary AFSIM inputs, the column formatting, field length, and character format must be exactly as specified below.:

configItems.name: central_body
configItems.description: Specify the central body and related ellipsoid model to be used by simulation platforms. Options for <central body type> are the following:

configItems.name: polar_offset_angles
configItems.description: Specify the central_body’s polar offset angles ( and , respectively) of the Celestial Intermediate Pole (CIP) with respect to the WCS (ITRS) coordinate system. Providing these values (of the order of tenths of arc-seconds) enables very highly accurate conversions between ECI and WCS coordinates.

configItems.name: heliocentric
configItems.description: Specify use of the wgs_84 gravitational parameter, the egm_96 gravitational parameter, or the heliocentric gravitational parameter for propagation. The heliocentric option is used to simulate bodies orbiting the sun.

configItems.name: debug_output_wsf
configItems.description: Write additional information to standard output that can be processed by the CME tool “sedit’.

configItems.name: debug_output_oe
configItems.description: Write additional information about the orbital elements to standard output.

configItems.name: debug_output_stk
configItems.description: Write additional information to standard output that can be used for comparing the orbit with the Systems Tool Kit (STK) from Analytical Graphics, Inc.

configItems.name: debug_output_xyz
configItems.description: Write additional information to standard output that can be used for comparing the orbit with the Systems Tool Kit (STK) from Analytical Graphics, Inc.

configItems.name: conjunction_setup
configItems.description: Set this spacecraft’s initial conditions such that a conjunction with a given target spacecraft will occur at a specified time. During initialization an attempt will be made to find a solution with the given boundary conditions. If successful, this platform’s state will be set so that the specified conjunction occurs. If there is no solution (for example, the orbit would take the satellite through the Earth), the velocity of the spacecraft will be set to a default value (see below).

configItems.name: from_lla
configItems.description: Set the initial position of this spacecraft to the given latitude, longitude and altitude. If there is no solution to the conjunction, the velocity of the spacecraft will be set to that of a circular orbit with a heading of 90 degrees.

configItems.name: from_eci
configItems.description: Set the initial position of this spacecraft to the given position in the ECI frame. If there is no solution to the conjunction, the velocity of the spacecraft will be set to that of a circular orbit with a heading of 90 degrees.

configItems.name: from_initial
configItems.description: Set the initial position of this spacecraft using other means to specify the initial orbit of the spacecraft. If there is no solution to the conjunction, the velocity of the spacecraft will be set to that provided by the other initialization methods.

configItems.name: with_target
configItems.description: Specify the name of the target platform of the conjunction. This spacecraft will move to the position of the target platform at the time specified in the at_time command. The specified target must be the name of a platform that moves in the space spatial domain.

configItems.name: at_time
configItems.description: Specify the time at which this spacecraft should suffer a conjunction with the specified target.

configItems.name: tolerance
configItems.description: Specify the tolerance for the conjunction solution. The default value of the tolerance is 1.0e-9.

configItems.name: attitude_controller
configItems.description: Specify the attitude controller for the platform. All platforms having a WSF_SPACE_MOVER or WSF_NORAD_SPACE_MOVER will have an attitude controller of some kind. If no attitude controller block is specified, the mover will operate as if the instant attitude controller was selected.

configItems.name: maneuvering
configItems.description: Specifiy a model for executing orbital maneuvers in space.

configItems.name: mission_sequence
configItems.description: Specify a sequence of pre-determined orbital mission events. The first mission event specified is executed first, then the second, etc. An optional constraint can be specified to delay execution of the sequence; otherwise the mission event will begin executing at the creation time of the platform.

configItems.name: state
configItems.description: Indicates that the following table definition will be used when the platform is in the signature state <state-name>. If default is specified then the subsequent table will be used if the platform is in a signature state that does not match any of the states defined in the signature.

configItems.name: high_resolution_eclipse
configItems.description: This command enables a more accurate computation of the eclipse state of the platform. This affects both the modeled temperature for the surfaces that make up the signature, and the amount of incident solar radiation.

configItems.name: reflectance
configItems.description: Default: 1.0

configItems.name: temperature_change_rate
configItems.description: Specifies the time rate of change of the surface. When the Sun is no longer visible then the temperature of the surface starts to decrease until it reaches minimum_temperature. When the Sun is subsequently visible then the temperature of the surface starts to increase until it reaches maximum_temperature.

configItems.name: minimum_temperature
configItems.description: Specifies the minimum temperature to which the surface will decrease when not illuminated by the Sun.

configItems.name: maximum_temperature
configItems.description: Specifies the maximum temperature to which the surface will increase when illuminated by the Sun.

configItems.name: yaw
configItems.description: Specifies the yaw angle of the surface with respect to the entity to which it is attached.

configItems.name: pitch
configItems.description: Specifies the pitch of the surface with respect to the entity to which it is attached.

configItems.name: roll
configItems.description: Specifies the roll of the surface with respect to the entity to which it is attached.

configItems.name: cue_to
configItems.description: Specify the vector with which the PCS X axis will be aligned, subject to the azimuth_cue_limits and elevation_cue_limits defined below.

configItems.name: azimuth_cue_limits
configItems.description: Specify the absolute minimum and maximum angle about which the surface can be cued in azimuth (rotated about the PCS Z axis) when performing cue_to operations.

configItems.name: elevation_cue_limits
configItems.description: Specify the absolute minimum and maximum angle about which the surface can be cued in elevation (rotated about the PCS Y axis) when performing cue_to operations.

configItems.name: size
configItems.description: Defines the size of a box. The first value is the dimension along the part coordinate system (PCS) X axis, the second is the dimension along the PCS Y axis, and the third is the dimension along the PCS Z axis.

configItems.name: area
configItems.description: Defines the area of the plane.

configItems.name: radius
configItems.description: Defines the radius of the sphere.

configItems.name: minimum_radius
configItems.description: Specifies the value of R min in the damage equation.

configItems.name: maximum_radius
configItems.description: Specifies the value of R max in the damage equation.

configItems.name: minimum_damage
configItems.description: Specifies the value of D min in the damage equation.

configItems.name: maximum_damage
configItems.description: Specifies the value of Dmax in the damage equation.

configItems.name: exponent
configItems.description: Specifies the value of X in the above equation.

configItems.name: threshold_damage
configItems.description: If the target platform has never been damaged, then this is the damage factor threshold that must be achieved by the blast before any damage will occur.

configItems.name: use_pk_table
configItems.description: Sets the name of a Pk table to evaluate upon weapon fusing, in order to compute the threshold value for intercept_pk. At platform initialization, this table name must be known by the PkTable Manager to supply to the weapon. Table will override any value supplied for intercept_pk.

configItems.name: pk_table
configItems.description: Following is an example input to specify a PkTable while using the use_pk_table option. The pk_table…end_pk_table block must occur either in global context (as all tables are read in by the PkTableManager, and supplied by reference to the weapon), or nested inside of a weapon_effects block. The weapon must request use of the table by employing the use_pk_table option. Each of the one or more tables listed within the pk_table block is tied to a target_type. The independent variables for the table lookup, if not a constant Pk value, will include: target azimuth, target elevation, weapon speed, and target speed. The first target_type listed must be DEFAULT, which is used if there is no more specific match provided below the DEFAULT option. PkTables may be specified as inline_tables, and the “inline_table” keyword is always followed by two integers, the (n) number of azimuths (beginning with zero, as the pk is assumed to be symmetric about the weapon’s XZ plane), and the (m) number of elevations (not assumed symmetric) in increasing order. Then the inline table will contain n X m values of Pk for the weapon to interpolate as the Pk threshold. The kill determination will be 1.0 (total kill) if the uniform random draw is less than the threshold value.

configItems.name: show_state_evaluations
configItems.description: Indicates that information about state evaluations should be written to standard output. This essentially shows the true or false status of the evaluation of each next_state block.

configItems.name: show_state_transitions
configItems.description: Indicates that information about state transitions should be written to standard output.

configItems.name: state
configItems.description: Defines a state in a state machine with the name <state-name>. Besides transition conditions, notice a state can have its own behavior_tree inside.

configItems.name: update_interval
configItems.description: If non-zero, specifies a periodic time interval at which the simulation will call the mover. If zero then the mover will be called only when it is necessary to determine the position of the containing platform.

configItems.name: update_time_tolerance
configItems.description: When a position update is requested by the simulation, if the time since the previous update is less than or equal to this value then the mover will ignore the update.

configItems.name: average_speed
configItems.description: Specifies the weapon’s average speed that will be used for the duration of flight.

configItems.name: tof_and_speed
configItems.description: Specifies the weapon’s speed versus time profile that will be used. The time values must be in increasing numerical order.

configItems.name: maximum_lateral_acceleration
configItems.description: Specifies the weapon’s maximum lateral acceleration that will be used for weapon maneuvers.

configItems.name: guidance_mode
configItems.description: Specifies the weapon’s guidance mode. Using lead_pursuit, the velocity vector will always be aimed toward the current target track if stationary, and if the track is moving, will be extrapolated as necessary for a predicted time to intercept, mimicking proportional navigation guidance. Using pure_pursuit, the velocity vector will always be aimed toward the current target track.

configItems.name: guide_to_truth
configItems.description: Specifies if the perceived target location (as defined by the current target track) or the truth target location should be used in the guidance computations.

configItems.name: update_interval
configItems.description: If non-zero, specifies a periodic time interval at which the simulation will call the mover. If zero then the mover will be called only when it is necessary to determine the position of the containing platform.

configItems.name: update_time_tolerance
configItems.description: When a position update is requested by the simulation, if the time since the previous update is less than or equal to this value then the mover will ignore the update.

configItems.name: altitude_offset
configItems.description: When set, this offset will offset the parent platform’s location by the given amount from the current waypoint’s altitude.

configItems.name: at_end_of_path
configItems.description: Specify the action to take when the mover reaches the end of its defined path.

configItems.name: draw_route
configItems.description: This command is the same as print_route, except the route text is not printed, only drawn with WsfDraw.

configItems.name: on_turn_failure
configItems.description: Defines the behavior of the mover when a point on a route cannot be reached exactly due to the turn radius.

configItems.name: pathfinder
configItems.description: The name of the pathfinder object to use.

configItems.name: print_route
configItems.description: When enabled, the route is printed to the screen whenever it is modified. Additionally, WsfDraw is used to output a visual of the route, which can be viewed with many visualization tools.

configItems.name: start_at
configItems.description: The label identifying the waypoint in the route to use as the starting location.

configItems.name: start_time
configItems.description: Indicates the platform is to start moving at the time specified. The current velocity is set to zero and once the simulation time is reached, the platform starts moving at the speed specified in the first waypoint. If an elapse time is desired at a waypoint, use the subcommand pause_time.

configItems.name: switch_on_approach
configItems.description: Switches to the next waypoint when approaching within one turn radius of the current target waypoint.

configItems.name: switch_on_passing
configItems.description: Switches to the next waypoint only when abreast of the current target waypoint.

configItems.name: turn_failure_threshold
configItems.description: Defines the threshold for which the on_turn_failure behavior is triggered, given as a ratio of the turn radius. For example, a turn_failure_threshold of 0.01 and a turn radius of 1000 meters, on_turn_failure logic would be triggered if the point is missed by more than 10 meters.

configItems.name: use_route
configItems.description: Supplies the name of the route to follow. The route is assumed to be a predefined absolute route.

configItems.name: angle_of_attack_table
configItems.description: speed <speed-value> angle <angle-value> speed <speed-value> angle <angle-value>

configItems.name: altitude
configItems.description: Specifies the altitude that the subsequent data is valid for. The altitude blocks must be in increasing numerical order. Linear interpolation of the altitude blocks is used.

configItems.name: speed
configItems.description: Specifies the speed that the listed angle of attack is valid for. The speed entries must be in increasing numerical order. The angle of attack will be computed using a linear interpolation of the speed data.

configItems.name: angle
configItems.description: The angle of attack. The angle of attack entries must be in increasing numerical order.

configItems.name: bank_angle_limit
configItems.description: The roll angle limit. Value must be between 0 degrees to 85 degrees. Used to calculate the maximum radial acceleration.

configItems.name: body_g_limit
configItems.description: The body g-limit. Value must be greater than the acceleration of earth’s gravity.

configItems.name: heading_pursuit_gain
configItems.description: The heading pursuit gain.

configItems.name: maximum_climb_rate
configItems.description: Specifies the maximum climb rate and dive rate used when changing altitude. Other climb rates specified by waypoints or scripts are bounded by this value.
