configItems.name: maximum_flight_path_angle
configItems.description: Specifies maximum flight path angle (angle of climb/dive). Value must be greater than or equal to 0.

configItems.name: maximum_linear_acceleration
configItems.description: Specifies the maximum linear acceleration to use when acceleration is necessary. This value is used if the waypoint does not include a linear _acceleration specification.

configItems.name: maximum_radial_acceleration
configItems.description: Specifies the maximum radial acceleration to use when turning. This value is used if the waypoint does not include a radial_acceleration specification.

configItems.name: maximum_altitude
configItems.description: Maximum altitude constraint.

configItems.name: minimum_altitude
configItems.description: Minimum altitude constraint.

configItems.name: maximum_speed
configItems.description: Maximum speed constraint. Value must be greater than 0.

configItems.name: minimum_speed
configItems.description: Minimum speed constraint. Value must be greater than or equal to 0.

configItems.name: path_variance_radius
configItems.description: This value will randomly vary the location of the waypoint within the radius given. A random bearing and distance are chosen and applied to the next waypoint when calculating the path.

configItems.name: roll_rate_limit
configItems.description: The roll rate limit. Value must be greater than 0. Note: When applied to a WSF_AIR_MOVER or other waypoint mover types, the roll rate will not affect the platform’s movement along a route. To affect route following behavior use maximum_radial_acceleration.

configItems.name: speed_variance_percent
configItems.description: This value will randomly vary the speed at each waypoint as the mover travels within +/- the pct given. Value must be greater than 0.

configItems.name: turn_rate_limit
configItems.description: The turn rate limit. Value must be greater than 0.

configItems.name: no_pitch
configItems.description: Restricts the mover from pitching the platform. This has no effect on kinematics.

configItems.name: on_road
configItems.description: Restricts the mover from rolling the platform. This has no effect on kinematics.

configItems.name: off_road
configItems.description: Turns off the ‘on_road’ option. This allows the platform to roll.

configItems.name: path_compute_timestep
configItems.description: Waypoint movers precompute movement along paths. This behavior forces turns to have a constant radius. If path_compute_timestep is specified as a positive value, the turn rate will update on that interval if any changes in speed occur.

configItems.name: max_underwater_range_filter
configItems.description: Prevents unrealistically long underwater ranges by specifying a range constraint for the underwater portion of the transmission path. This keyword also has an additional effect of permitting communication over the short range without regard to horizon or terrain.

configItems.name: max_communication_depth
configItems.description: Specifies the maximum depth at which a submerged platform is permitted to exchange communication events. In order to reduce user input issues, the absolute value of the numeric input is used, and the value is converted to be a negative altitude to represent the depth below the surface for the submerged platform.

configItems.name: minimum_horizon_angle
configItems.description: Specifies the minimum angle acceptable for transmissions through the water’s surface. This angle is measured from the horizon upward. Communications with angles less than this limit are stopped. The effect is to require platforms to reduce their slant range to be able to communicate.

configItems.name: unset_VLF_comm
configItems.description: When the command is set_VLF_comm, then all horizon checks are ignored and the message is delivered.

configItems.name: water_attenuation_factor
configItems.description: Specifies a factor by which signals are attenuated as they pass through the water part of the transmission path. The format for data is a number followed by a dB ratio value, followed by a backslash, and then followed by a <length-value>.

configItems.name: update_interval
configItems.description: If non-zero, specifies a periodic time interval at which the simulation will call the mover. If zero then the mover will be called only when it is necessary to determine the position of the containing platform.

configItems.name: update_time_tolerance
configItems.description: When a position update is requested by the simulation, if the time since the previous update is less than or equal to this value then the mover will ignore the update.

configItems.name: altitude_offset
configItems.description: When set, this offset will offset the parent platform’s location by the given amount from the current waypoint’s altitude.

configItems.name: at_end_of_path
configItems.description: Specify the action to take when the mover reaches the end of its defined path.

configItems.name: draw_route
configItems.description: This command is the same as print_route, except the route text is not printed, only drawn with WsfDraw.

configItems.name: on_turn_failure
configItems.description: Defines the behavior of the mover when a point on a route cannot be reached exactly due to the turn radius.

configItems.name: pathfinder
configItems.description: The name of the pathfinder object to use.

configItems.name: print_route
configItems.description: When enabled, the route is printed to the screen whenever it is modified. Additionally, WsfDraw is used to output a visual of the route, which can be viewed with many visualization tools.

configItems.name: start_at
configItems.description: The label identifying the waypoint in the route to use as the starting location.

configItems.name: start_time
configItems.description: Indicates the platform is to start moving at the time specified. The current velocity is set to zero and once the simulation time is reached, the platform starts moving at the speed specified in the first waypoint. If an elapse time is desired at a waypoint, use the subcommand pause_time.

configItems.name: switch_on_approach
configItems.description: Switches to the next waypoint when approaching within one turn radius of the current target waypoint.

configItems.name: switch_on_passing
configItems.description: Switches to the next waypoint only when abreast of the current target waypoint.

configItems.name: turn_failure_threshold
configItems.description: Defines the threshold for which the on_turn_failure behavior is triggered, given as a ratio of the turn radius. For example, a turn_failure_threshold of 0.01 and a turn radius of 1000 meters, on_turn_failure logic would be triggered if the point is missed by more than 10 meters.

configItems.name: use_route
configItems.description: Supplies the name of the route to follow. The route is assumed to be a predefined absolute route.

configItems.name: angle_of_attack_table
configItems.description: speed <speed-value> angle <angle-value> speed <speed-value> angle <angle-value>

configItems.name: altitude
configItems.description: Specifies the altitude that the subsequent data is valid for. The altitude blocks must be in increasing numerical order. Linear interpolation of the altitude blocks is used.

configItems.name: speed
configItems.description: Specifies the speed that the listed angle of attack is valid for. The speed entries must be in increasing numerical order. The angle of attack will be computed using a linear interpolation of the speed data.

configItems.name: angle
configItems.description: The angle of attack. The angle of attack entries must be in increasing numerical order.

configItems.name: bank_angle_limit
configItems.description: The roll angle limit. Value must be between 0 degrees to 85 degrees. Used to calculate the maximum radial acceleration.

configItems.name: body_g_limit
configItems.description: The body g-limit. Value must be greater than the acceleration of earth’s gravity.

configItems.name: heading_pursuit_gain
configItems.description: The heading pursuit gain.

configItems.name: maximum_climb_rate
configItems.description: Specifies the maximum climb rate and dive rate used when changing altitude. Other climb rates specified by waypoints or scripts are bounded by this value.

configItems.name: maximum_flight_path_angle
configItems.description: Specifies maximum flight path angle (angle of climb/dive). Value must be greater than or equal to 0.

configItems.name: maximum_linear_acceleration
configItems.description: Specifies the maximum linear acceleration to use when acceleration is necessary. This value is used if the waypoint does not include a linear _acceleration specification.

configItems.name: maximum_radial_acceleration
configItems.description: Specifies the maximum radial acceleration to use when turning. This value is used if the waypoint does not include a radial_acceleration specification.

configItems.name: maximum_altitude
configItems.description: Maximum altitude constraint.

configItems.name: minimum_altitude
configItems.description: Minimum altitude constraint.

configItems.name: maximum_speed
configItems.description: Maximum speed constraint. Value must be greater than 0.

configItems.name: minimum_speed
configItems.description: Minimum speed constraint. Value must be greater than or equal to 0.

configItems.name: path_variance_radius
configItems.description: This value will randomly vary the location of the waypoint within the radius given. A random bearing and distance are chosen and applied to the next waypoint when calculating the path.

configItems.name: roll_rate_limit
configItems.description: The roll rate limit. Value must be greater than 0. Note: When applied to a WSF_AIR_MOVER or other waypoint mover types, the roll rate will not affect the platform’s movement along a route. To affect route following behavior use maximum_radial_acceleration.

configItems.name: speed_variance_percent
configItems.description: This value will randomly vary the speed at each waypoint as the mover travels within +/- the pct given. Value must be greater than 0.

configItems.name: turn_rate_limit
configItems.description: The turn rate limit. Value must be greater than 0.

configItems.name: no_pitch
configItems.description: Restricts the mover from pitching the platform. This has no effect on kinematics.

configItems.name: on_road
configItems.description: Restricts the mover from rolling the platform. This has no effect on kinematics.

configItems.name: off_road
configItems.description: Turns off the ‘on_road’ option. This allows the platform to roll.

configItems.name: path_compute_timestep
configItems.description: Waypoint movers precompute movement along paths. This behavior forces turns to have a constant radius. If path_compute_timestep is specified as a positive value, the turn rate will update on that interval if any changes in speed occur.

configItems.name: transmitter
configItems.description: A transmitter block that defines the properties of the transmitter. There is a unique propagation model for surface wave radar sensors.

configItems.name: propagation_model
configItems.description: The relative permittivity of the surface of the earth.

configItems.name: relative_permittivity
configItems.description: The relative permittivity of the surface of the earth.

configItems.name: conductivity
configItems.description: The conductivity of the earth’s surface (Siemens/meter).

configItems.name: troposphere_refractivity
configItems.description: The refractivity of the troposphere at the surface of the earth (N-units).

configItems.name: troposphere_height_scale
configItems.description: The scale height of the troposphere.

configItems.name: minimum_computation_distance
configItems.description: The minimum distance from the radar that propagation will be computed for.

configItems.name: computation_distance_interval
configItems.description: The distance interval between cell centers for propagation computation.

configItems.name: noise_environment
configItems.description: Defines the man-made noise environment that the sensor operates in.

configItems.name: attenuation
configItems.description: Specifies a table that defines the attenuation values. The table must be a function of at least three independent variables:

configItems.name: adjustment_factor
configItems.description: Specifies a multiplier to be applied to returned values. This would typically be used to account for the fact that values integrated over a wide band (i.e.: visual) represent an average that may include many ‘dead-zones’ that the sensor may exclude. Thus, the effective transmittance may be higher.

configItems.name: sort_end_points
configItems.description: Specifies end-points (source and target points) for a given interaction can be logically interchanged so the path goes from the highest object to the lowest object. This would be applicable if the attenuation values are independent of direction. This would allow a table to be computed for air-to-ground purposes to also be used for ground-to-air purposes.

configItems.name: two_way_attenuation
configItems.description: Specifies if the table values represent two-way attenuation (transmitter-to-target-to-receiver).

configItems.name: spectral_data_conversion
configItems.description: This command is used to convert spectral data produced by a program like MODTRAN into a form that can be used as input for the attenuation command.

configItems.name: target_to_background_radiance
configItems.description: Specifies the name of the file which contains the raw spectral target-to-background radiance as a function of observer altitude and elevation angle and slant range to the target. Using the current processes, this file name will be of the form <filename>_tbr.plt.

configItems.name: spectral_response_curve
configItems.description: This defines the response of the sensor as a function of wavelength. The curve is defined as a series of points where each point is defined as:

configItems.name: output
configItems.description: Specifies the name of the file to which the converted results are to be written. The file can be used at the argument for the attenuation command (See the example at the start of the section.)

configItems.name: fuel_table
configItems.description: One or more fuel_table blocks may be provided.

configItems.name: mode
configItems.description: This specifies the fuel mode that a table is valid for. If only one fuel flow table is supplied, and is to be used regardless of the fuel mode, then do not supply this value. If multiple fuel rate tables are provided, then each table must be supplied this discriminator, to allow switching between tables. Fuel mode is accessible for change via script interface.

configItems.name: constant
configItems.description: This specifies a constant fuel consumption rate.

configItems.name: speeds
configItems.description: This specifies an independent variable arbitrary-sized array of speed values (must be in increasing order) that will apply to the independent fuel flow rate values that follow. This command is mutually exclusive with the mach command.

configItems.name: mach
configItems.description: This specifies an independent variable arbitrary-sized array of mach values (must be in increasing order) that will apply to the independent fuel flow rate values that follow. This command is mutually exclusive with the speeds command.

configItems.name: altitudes
configItems.description: This specifies an independent variable arbitrary-sized array of altitude values (must be in increasing order) that will apply to the independent fuel flow rate values that follow.

configItems.name: weights
configItems.description: This specifies an independent variable arbitrary-sized array of weight values (must be in increasing order) that will apply to the independent fuel flow rate values that follow. (The keyword “masses” is equivalent.)

configItems.name: masses
configItems.description: This specifies an independent variable arbitrary-sized array of mass values (must be in increasing order) that will apply to the independent fuel flow rate values that follow. (The keyword “weights” is equivalent.)

configItems.name: rates
configItems.description: This specifies the dependent variable values corresponding to the 1-D, 2-D, or 3-D independent variables that precede this keyword. The number of values supplied must match the product of the number of independent values in each supplied dimension (i.e. a table of 6 speeds and 4 altitudes must contain 24 fuel flow values).

configItems.name: circular_error_probable
configItems.description: This value specifies the 50th percentile intrinsic nominal accuracy of the weapon, when used as intended, within standard constraints. This value may be drawn upon to determine the end-game target offsets or miss distances.

configItems.name: target_type
configItems.description: Indicates the target platform type for which the following Pk table is valid. As many tables as desired may be specified, for different expected target platform types.

configItems.name: pk_at_cep
configItems.description: Specify an entry in the Pk vs. CEP table. Multiple points may be provided for each target platform type.

configItems.name: desired_top_off_quantity
configItems.description: Specifies the lower value on a band of desired operating fuel quantity. This value, along with maximum_refuel_quantity specifies the hysteresis band to stay within while operating in proximity to a refueling tanker, such as during a group ferry flight. In other words, when fuel quantity transitions from above this quantity to below, it is desired to begin a fuel receive operation from a nearby tanker if possible. Script operations may key upon this transition, in order to take a desired action. Conversely, when the fuel quantity transitions from below maximum_refuel_quantity to above, a separate scripted action may be taken, such as to terminate the receive-in-process action.

configItems.name: maximum_receive_rate
configItems.description: Specifies the maximum rate at which the platform can be refueled.

configItems.name: maximum_refuel_quantity
configItems.description: Specifies the upper value on a band of desired operating fuel quantity. See desired_top_off_quantity for more detail.

configItems.name: receive_method
configItems.description: Sets the method that this tanked fuel may use to receive fuel. At the time a fuel supply operation between two tanks is initiated, the Tanker must have an available fuel supply point that matches the Receiver’s configuration, or the transfer cannot begin. See supply_method_preference.

configItems.name: supply_location_preference
configItems.description: Sets the preferred location that this tanked fuel may use to supply fuel. Often a tanker may have multiple stations to supply fuel, leading to some ambiguity about which transfer point should be used, so this setting is consulted to resolve the ambiguity, if necessary. Run-time software is permitted to change this setting to reconfigure to an anticipated receiver arrival.

configItems.name: supply_method_preference
configItems.description: Sets the preferred method that this tanked fuel may use to supply fuel. Often a tanker may have multiple methods to supply fuel, leading to some ambiguity about which type of transfer should be attempted, so this setting is consulted to resolve the ambiguity, if necessary. At the time a fuel supply operation between two tanks is initiated, the Tanker must have an available fuel supply point type that matches the Receiver’s configuration, or the transfer cannot begin. See receive_method. Run-time software is permitted to change this setting to reconfigure to an anticipated receiver arrival.

configItems.name: supply_point
configItems.syntax: supply_point [ left | center | right ] [ boom | hose ] ‘<mass-flow-rate>’
configItems.description: Specify the maximum flow rate for a fuel supply point station. This value may be reduced if the receiver’s maximum receive rate is less. This command should be repeated for each available refueling station.

configItems.name: evaluate_candidate_tracks
configItems.description: Indicates if ‘candidate tracks’ are to be evaluated. A candidate track is one that has been received but has not yet been determined to be ‘stable’ as defined by the filter.

configItems.name: evaluation_interval
configItems.description: Specifies how often a track in the indicated state should be (re)evaluated.

configItems.name: number_of_servers
configItems.description: Indicates the maximum number of track evaluations that can occur simultaneously. The time to perform the evaluation is set using the time_to_evaluate command.

configItems.name: show_state_evaluations
configItems.description: Indicates that information about state evaluations should be written to standard output. This essentially shows the true or false status of the evaluation of each next_state block.

configItems.name: show_state_transitions
configItems.description: Indicates that information about state transitions should be written to standard output.

configItems.name: state
configItems.description: Defines a state in a state machine with the name <state-name>.

configItems.name: on_entry
configItems.description: When entering this state, performs these script commands. This is an optional subcommand.

configItems.name: on_exit
configItems.description: When leaving this state, performs these script commands. This is an optional subcommand.

configItems.name: next_state
configItems.description: This optional subcommand is a script block that must return a true/false value. When evaluated, the return value determines whether to transition to the named state defined by the <next-state-name>. If next_state is not defined, it will “dead end” in this state.

configItems.name: time_to_evaluate
configItems.description: Specifies how long it takes to perform an evaluation of track in the indicated state. This simulates how long it takes to “think’ or perform an evaluation in a logical sense.

configItems.name: track_processor
configItems.description: Specifies the name of a WSF_TRACK_PROCESSOR (typically operating as a non_master_track_processor) whose track list will provide the tracks used in the evaluation process.

configItems.name: comm_retry_attempts
configItems.description: Indicates the number of attempts to retry failed communications.

configItems.name: comm_retry_interval
configItems.description: Indicates the amount of time between attempts to retry failed communications.

configItems.name: operating_level
configItems.description: Indicates the operating condition or state and the associated level.

configItems.name: time_to_recognize_messages
configItems.description: Indicates the amount of time it takes to recognize a message.

configItems.name: track_update_interval
configItems.description: Indicates the time interval for sending track updates to assignees.

configItems.name: track_update_strategy
configItems.description: Indicates how track updates are sent. With default behavior, if a task has been accepted then periodic track updates are sent to the assignee. With the Suppressor behavior, track updates are sent to assignees only when the track manager indicates a track has been updated.

configItems.name: weapon_uplink_path
configItems.description: Indicates the sensor and communication device to use when supporting a weapon uplink. If a tracking task is assigned to the sensor and a weapon is fired, the weapon is supported with an uplinked track.

configItems.name: uplink_source
configItems.description: Indicates the source of the track when uplinking. If this command is not used, the uplink will be sent any time the track is updated in the track manager. If this command is used, only sensor tracks originating from the uplink source will be used. The sensor must report tracks to the track manager.

configItems.name: uplink_comm
configItems.description: Indicates the comm system used to transmit an uplink. If this command is not used, the first compatible comm system will be chosen.

configItems.name: uplink_delay
configItems.description: Indicates the delay before an uplink is initiated after an uplink task is received.

configItems.name: auto_weapon_uplink
configItems.description: Indicates that the task manager will automatically assign an uplink task for each weapon fired when the FireAt() script is called. Other commands that determine the uplink parameters are uplink_source uplink_comm uplink_delay auto_weapon_uplink_platform.

configItems.name: auto_weapon_uplink_platform
configItems.description: Indicates the assignee of the uplink task initiated with auto_weapon_uplink. This allows specifying a specific uplink platform.

configItems.name: uplink_send_interval
configItems.description: Minimum interval between sending uplink tracks (for task-based uplinking only)

configItems.name: show_task_messages
configItems.description: Indicates that information related task assignment, cancellation and completion are to be written to standard output.

configItems.name: show_uncompleted_tasks
configItems.description: This is a debugging tool that indicates information about uncompleted tasks is to be written to standard output during the destruction of the task processor.

configItems.name: on_task_assign
configItems.description: This is invoked when a task assignment is received.

configItems.name: on_task_cancel
configItems.description: This is invoked when a task cancel is received.

configItems.name: on_task_complete
configItems.description: This is invoked when the assigner of task receives notification that an assignee has completed the specified task.

configItems.name: on_task_assign_sent
configItems.description: This is invoked when a task assignment is sent.

configItems.name: on_task_cancel_sent
configItems.description: This is invoked when a task cancel is sent.

configItems.name: on_task_complete_sent
configItems.description: This is invoked when the assignee of task sends a task compete message.

configItems.name: on_operating_level_change
configItems.description: This is invoked whenever a change in ‘operating level’ in detected. This is mostly used when a commander changes the operating level of a subordinate to reflect a change in ‘alert status’.

configItems.name: on_track_drop
configItems.description: This is invoked whenever a processor is informed of a track drop by the track manager. The implicitly defined script variable TRACK (of type WsfLocalTrack) represents the last known state of the track that is being dropped.

configItems.name: trajectory_type
configItems.description: Specify the type of trajectory to be used to reach the target. This is not used if a target was not specified.

configItems.name: target_position
configItems.description: Specify the position of the target. Not used if ignore_target is used. May miss the target if cep or cep_table is used.

configItems.name: ignore_target
configItems.description: Indicate that any target position (defined either by target_position or the ‘current target track’) is to be ignored. The orientation of the platform to which the mover is attached defines the initial state.

configItems.name: show_status
configItems.description: Display status information at launch time.

configItems.name: stage
configItems.description: Define the attributes of the only state of a single stage vehicle or one of the stages in a multistage vehicle. <stage number> must be a value that is greater than or equal to 1 and less than or equal to the current number of defined stages plus one. If the value specifies a stage that already exists then the enclosed subcommands override the values in that stage. If the value is equal to the current number of defined stages plus one then a new stage is created and populated with the enclosed subcommands. It is invalid to specify a stage number that is more than one higher than the current highest defined stage number.:

configItems.name: ballistic_coefficient
configItems.description: The ballistic coefficient. This is a required value and there is no default.

configItems.name: empty_mass
configItems.description: Specify the mass of the stage without fuel.

configItems.name: fuel_mass
configItems.description: Specify the mass of the fuel on the stage. This, or fuel_mass_fraction, must be specified if a non-zero thrust_duration is specified.

configItems.name: fuel_mass_fraction
configItems.description: Specify the fraction (0.0 to 1.0) of the total_mass of the stage that is fuel. This, or fuel_mass, must be specified if a non-zero thrust_duration is specified.

configItems.name: pre_ignition_coast_time
configItems.description: Specify the amount of time that will elapse between the start of the stage and when the engine will ignite.

configItems.name: pre_separation_coast_time
configItems.description: Specify the amount of time that will elapse between the burnout of this stage and its separation from the vehicle. This command has no effect for single-stage vehicles or the last stage of a multistage vehicle.

configItems.name: specific_impulse
configItems.description: An alternative mechanism for specifying the thrust of the engine. This, or thrust, must be specified if a non-zero thrust_duration is specified.

configItems.name: total_mass
configItems.description: Specify the total mass of the stage.

configItems.name: thrust
configItems.description: Specify the thrust of the engine. This, or specific_impulse, must be specified if a non-zero thrust_duration is specified.

configItems.name: thrust_duration
configItems.description: Specify the amount of time the engine will burn.

configItems.name: cep
configItems.description: Specify the inaccuracy of the missile in guiding to its target. This is a 50th-percentile statistically expected radial horizontal deviation from the targeted aim point. If neither cep distance or cep_table is specified, the missile will hit the specified target_position above. It is mutually exclusive to use either cep or a cep_table.

configItems.name: cep_table
configItems.description: Define a table of 50th percentile statistical errors that quantify the inaccuracy of the missile in hitting its intended target. (This option is mutually exclusive of the fixed cep keyword.) The error may be specified in either of two ways: circular error probability (CEP) or range and azimuth errors. In either case, the values are dependent values within a table lookup with nominal ground range to target as the independent variable. Only one table is allowed per missile, and a derived object that defines one will override its parent definition. For both of the ways of specifying accuracy below, the quantified error is for a given nominal target range. At least two such ranges must be given to enable a linear interpolation. One input line per nominal range, and each subsequent range value must be greater than the previous.

configItems.name: range
configItems.description: Expected radial horizontal impact error at a given nominal target range. (Mutually exclusive of the [range, range_error, azimuth_error] triples below.) At least two ranges must be specified.

configItems.name: threat_velocity
configItems.description: Declares the speed in above which a track will be classified as a threat.

configItems.name: threat_angle_spread
configItems.description: Declares the width of the angle in front of the platform within which it may consider a track threatening.

configItems.name: threat_time_to_intercept
configItems.description: Declares the time to intercept limit within which a track may be considered threatening. Based on speed and distance.

configItems.name: require_iff_foe
configItems.description: If set to true, this threat processor ignores all potential threats that don’t have IFF set to FOE in their track.

configItems.name: ignore_lower_altitude_threats
configItems.description: If set to true, this threat processor ignores all potential threats that are at a lower altitude and traveling downward.

configItems.name: ignore_without_location
configItems.description: If set to true, the threat processor ignores tracks that do not have location data; such tracks are always non-threatening.

configItems.name: ignore_without_velocity
configItems.description: If set to true, the threat processor ignores tracks that do not have velocity data; such tracks are always non-threatening.

configItems.name: output
configItems.description: Specify a form of output to produce for a measure of effectiveness. The allowed values for <output_type> are:

configItems.name: update_interval
configItems.description: If non-zero, specifies a periodic time interval at which the simulation will call the mover. If zero then the mover will be called only when it is necessary to determine the position of the containing platform.

configItems.name: tow_length
configItems.description: Specifies the desired distance between the lead platform and the towed asset.

configItems.name: reel_out_speed
configItems.description: Specifies the speed or rate at which the towed asset is reeled out from the lead platform. While being reeled out, the state is set to REELING_OUT. When the desired tow length has been reached, the state is set to DEPLOYED and the distance is maintained.

configItems.name: reel_in_speed
configItems.description: Specifies the speed or rate at which the towed asset is to be reeled back onto the lead platform. If not set, the towed asset will be deployed and remain in the simulation until killed or until the lead platform is removed from the simulation.

configItems.name: reel_in_at_absolute_time
configItems.description: Defines the absolute simulation time to start reeling the towed asset back onto the lead platform. A reel in rate must be set. Use ‘reel_in_speed’ or a script command to set the reel in rate for the towed asset.

configItems.name: reel_in_time_after_deployed
configItems.description: Specifies the speed or rate at which the towed asset is to be reeled back onto the lead platform after the towed asset has been fully deployed.

configItems.name: restore_quantity
configItems.description: If set to ‘true’, the quantity remaining for the towed asset is reset to the initial loadout after the towed asset was reeled out, deployed and then reeled back onto the lead platform. This allows for an unlimited number of towed launches.

configItems.name: follow_lead_trajectory
configItems.description: If set to ‘true’, the towed asset will follow the lead platform’s trajectory. The towed asset’s state is taken from the lead platform’s state history, with the time offset calculated by dividing the tether length by the lead platform’s speed. If set to ‘false’, the towed asset will follow as though it were rigidly attached, fixed in the lead platform’s entity coordinate system for a given deployed tether length and desired relative geometry (specified with the azimuth_relative_to_lead and elevation_relative_to_lead commands.

configItems.name: azimuth_relative_to_lead
configItems.description: Towed asset azimuth with respect to the lead platform, when follow_lead_trajectory flag is not set. Value must be in range [-90 deg, 90 deg] with 0 corresponding to the -X axis in the lead platform’s entity coordinate system, and positive values counter-clockwise.

configItems.name: elevation_relative_to_lead
configItems.description: Towed asset elevation with respect to the lead platform. Value must be in range [-90 deg, 90 deg], with positive elevation corresponding to -Z direction of the lead platform’s entity coordinate system.

configItems.name: track_behavior
configItems.description: Set the mitigating track behavior of the technique.

configItems.name: required_j_to_s
configItems.description: Specifies the minimum J/S ratio required for effectiveness.

configItems.name: range_error
configItems.description: Specifies the inducing/mitigating range error introduced by this technique.

configItems.name: azimuth_error
configItems.description: Specifies the inducing/mitigating azimuth error introduced by this technique.

configItems.name: elevation_error
configItems.description: Specifies the inducing/mitigating elevation error introduced by this technique.

configItems.name: velocity_error
configItems.description: Specifies the inducing/mitigating velocity error introduced by this technique.

configItems.name: range_walkoff_rate
configItems.description: Specifies the linear rate of change of the range error introduced by this technique.

configItems.name: azimuth_walkoff_rate
configItems.description: Specifies the linear rate of change of the azimuth error introduced by this technique.

configItems.name: elevation_walkoff_rate
configItems.description: Specifies the linear rate of change of the elevation error introduced by this technique.

configItems.name: velocity_walkoff_rate
configItems.description: Specifies the linear rate of change of the velocity error introduced by this technique.

configItems.name: range_holdout
configItems.description: Specifies the upper bound of the range error walkoff introduced by this technique. Can be used as an alternative to range_holdout_time and will override any range_holdout_time previously specified.

configItems.name: range_holdout_time
configItems.description: Specifies the time for each range walkoff cycle. Can be used as an alternative to range_holdout and will override any range_holdout previously specified.

configItems.name: azimuth_holdout
configItems.description: Specifies the upper bound of the azimuth error walkoff introduced by this technique. Can be used as an alternative to azimuth_holdout_time and will override any azimuth_holdout_time previously specified.

configItems.name: azimuth_holdout_time
configItems.description: Specifies the time for each azimuth walkoff cycle. Can be used as an alternative to azimuth_holdout and will override any azimuth_holdout previously specified.

configItems.name: elevation_holdout
configItems.description: Specifies the upper bound of the elevation error walkoff introduced by this technique. Can be used as an alternative to elevation_holdout_time and will override any elevation_holdout_time previously specified.

configItems.name: elevation_holdout_time
configItems.description: Specifies the time for each elevation walkoff cycle. Can be used as an alternative to elevation_holdout and will override any elevation_holdout previously specified.

configItems.name: velocity_holdout
configItems.description: Specifies the upper bound of the velocity error walkoff introduced by this technique. Can be used as an alternative to velocity_holdout_time and will override any velocity_holdout_time previously specified.

configItems.name: velocity_holdout_time
configItems.description: Specifies the time for each velocity walkoff cycle. Can be used as an alternative to velocity_holdout and will override any velocity_holdout previously specified.

configItems.name: range_recycle
configItems.description: Specifies whether the walkoff should recycle to the minimum range error or stay at holdout. Only used if range_holdout or range_holdout_time is given.

configItems.name: azimuth_recycle
configItems.description: Specifies whether the walkoff should recycle to the minimum azimuth error or stay at holdout. Only used if azimuth_holdout or azimuth_holdout_time is given.

configItems.name: elevation_recycle
configItems.description: Specifies whether the walkoff should recycle to the minimum elevation error or stay at holdout. Only used if elevation_holdout or elevation_holdout_time is given.

configItems.name: velocity_recycle
configItems.description: Specifies whether the walkoff should recycle to the minimum velocity error or stay at holdout. Only used if velocity_holdout or velocity_holdout_time is given.

configItems.name: recycle_table
configItems.description: This command provides the means to define either a delay, holdout or recycle time factor that is dependent on the J/S ratio, where J is the jamming power and S is the signal power in the receiver. If the range with non-zero delta is entered then a uniform random number draw is performed within the specified range. Linear interpolation is used to derive the values for intermediate J/S ratios before the random draw. J/S values outside the range of the table use the value from the appropriate endpoint (i.e., extrapolation is not performed). If this input is specified within the system_type_data input block then it is specific to a system-type, otherwise this input is defined as the ‘default’ data to use for undefined system-types in the system_type_data.

configItems.name: system_type_data
configItems.description: Input block to provide the system type (e.g., SENSOR-TYPE, JAMMER-TYPE) specific data necessary to implement this technique for a given system type. Default data can be set up for system types not defined using the “default” string as the system type.

configItems.name: master_track_processor
configItems.description: Indicates that this processor should be used as the platform’s master track processor. It will directly access the platform’s Master Track Manager object and associated Master Track List. This is the default behavior.

configItems.name: non_master_track_processor
configItems.description: Indicates that this processor will not be used as the platform’s master track processor. It will create its own track manager object, and it will maintain a track list separate from the platform’s Master Track List.

configItems.name: track_manager
configItems.description: This is a block for processing track manager input for track processors that are not their platform’s master track processor. Place track manager sub-commands within this block.

configItems.name: drop_after_inactive
configItems.description: Specifies that a track will be dropped if it goes for more than the specified time without an update. If fused tracks are reported (see report_fused_tracks), a WsfTrackDropMessage will be sent over external links, and attached local observers will be notified.

configItems.name: track_history_retention_interval
configItems.description: Specifies that track histories should be kept for the given time interval. This option is valid only if retain_track_history is set in the associated track manager.

configItems.name: report_interval
configItems.description: Report tracks (raw or fused depending on the following inputs) at the given interval. Each track in the respective track lists will be sent to externally connected entities once per report interval.

configItems.name: report_method
configItems.description: All tracks are reported to externally connected entities at the beginning of the reporting interval. New tracks will be reported immediately.

configItems.name: fused_track_reporting
configItems.description: Indicates that the object should report fused (local) tracks to externally connected entities via comm devices.

configItems.name: raw_track_reporting
configItems.description: Indicates whether nonlocal (‘raw’) tracks are to be reported to externally connected entities via comm devices.

configItems.name: pass_through_reporting
configItems.description: Indicates that any nonlocal (‘raw’) tracks are to be reported immediately to externally connected entities. This is the same as ‘raw_track_reporting’, except that reporting is in a ‘pass-through’ mode, rather than interval-based.

configItems.name: candidate_track_reporting
configItems.description: Indicates whether ‘candidate tracks’ (i.e., filtered sensor measurements for which the filter is not yet stable) should be reported to externally connected entities. Setting this option allows the data to be made available in the master track list as soon as it is received.

configItems.name: unchanged_track_reporting
configItems.description: Indicates whether tracks whose data have not changed since the last reporting interval should be reported again.

configItems.name: report_raw_tracks
configItems.description: Same as raw_track_reporting on.

configItems.name: report_fused_tracks
configItems.description: Same as fused_track_reporting on.

configItems.name: report_pass_through
configItems.description: Same as pass_through_reporting on.

configItems.name: report_candidate_tracks
configItems.description: Same as candidate_track_reporting on.

configItems.name: circular_report_rejection
configItems.description: Indicates how received track reports that are determined to be ‘circular’ should be processed. A received track report is declared to be a ‘circular report’ if one of the following conditions is true:

configItems.name: inbound_filter
configItems.description: By default, the processor will attempt to submit all received reports to the track manager for correlation and fusion. There are situations, however, where a given track processor may not desire this activity. This block allows control over what is assimilated.

configItems.name: show_state_evaluations
configItems.description: Indicates that information about state evaluations should be written to standard output. This essentially shows the true or false status of the evaluation of each next_state block.

configItems.name: show_state_transitions
configItems.description: Indicates that information about state transitions should be written to standard output.

configItems.name: state
configItems.description: Defines a state in a state machine with the name <state-name>.:

configItems.name: number_of_servers
configItems.description: Specifies the maximum number of evaluations that can occur simultaneously. See Method of Operation below.

configItems.name: evaluate_candidate_tracks
configItems.description: Indicates if ‘candidate tracks’ are to be evaluated. A candidate track is one that has been received but has not yet been determined to be ‘stable’ as defined by the filter.

configItems.name: evaluation_interval
configItems.description: Specifies how often a track in the indicated state should be (re)evaluated.

configItems.name: time_to_evaluate
configItems.description: Specifies how long it takes to perform an evaluation of track in the indicated state. This simulates how long it takes to “think’ or perform an evaluation in a logical sense.

configItems.name: void
configItems.description: This is invoked whenever a processor is informed of a track drop by the track manager. The implicitly defined script variable TRACK (of type WsfLocalTrack) represents the last known state of the track that is being dropped.

configItems.name: sensors
configItems.description: Specifies the name of the sensor, <sensor-name>, on the same platform as the processor.

configItems.name: sensor
configItems.description: Specifies the name of the sensor, <sensor-name>, on the same platform as the processor.

configItems.name: platform_sensor
configItems.description: Specifies the name of the sensor, <sensor-name>, on an external platform with name <platform-name>.

configItems.name: minimum_detections
configItems.description: Specifies the minimum_number of detections required from the sensors in the sensor list to declare a detection by the primary sensor.

configItems.name: message_length
configItems.description: Specify the logical length assigned to the track messages that are created from the image.

configItems.name: message_priority
configItems.description: Specify the priority assigned to the track messages that are created from the image.

configItems.name: TSPI_filename
configItems.description: Specify the name of the file containing the TSPI data. (Note that this is also a separately scriptable command. See WsfMover SetTSPI_FileName() for details.)

configItems.name: start_time
configItems.description: Specify the simulation time that corresponds with the time of the first TSPI data value. This is the simulation time at which the associated platform will begin moving.

configItems.name: at_end_of_path
configItems.description: Specify what occurs when the end of the TSPI file is encountered.

configItems.name: extrapolation
configItems.description: This is retained for compatibility with old input files. A value of ‘true’ is the same as ‘at_end_of_path extrapolate’, while a value of ‘false’ is the same as ‘at_end_of_path stop’.

configItems.name: time_in
configItems.description: Specify that the units of the <time> values in the TSPI data file are in units <time-units>

configItems.name: altitude_in
configItems.description: Specify that the units of the <altitude> values in the TSPI data file are in units <length-units>.

configItems.name: speed_in
configItems.description: Specify that the units of the <speed> values in the TSPI data file are in units <speed-units>.

configItems.name: roll_in
configItems.description: Specify that the units of the <heading>, <pitch>, or <roll> values in the TSPI data file are in units <angular-units>.

configItems.name: roll_inverted
configItems.description: Specify that the given value name in the TSPI data file is to be inverted (i.e., the values are negated).

configItems.name: relocate_and_rotate
configItems.description: The relocate_and_rotate … end_relocate_and_rotate block is a means to move a trajectory from one locale to another, including a change in orientation. Two keywords will move a TSPI trajectory from one (latitude, longitude) to another (latitude, longitude), either: A) initial_endpoint_anchor <lat> <lon>, or B) terminal_endpoint_anchor <lat> <lon>. After the path is relocated, it can them be re-oriented. To do so, use either A) great_circle_heading_at_anchor_point <angle-value>, or B) align_to_great_circle_through <lat> <lon>. In the later case, the <lat> <lon> value must be different than the anchor point. Note that due to the spherical geometry calculations used, and the ellipsoidal earth, the path translation process will be approximate. Also note that the initial or terminal heading value to be specified is along a great circle arc between initial and final trajectory points, not necessarily the true heading being flown at the beginning or end of trajectory.

configItems.name: stale_asset_time
configItems.description: Amount of time after which the battle manager will consider a friendly stale and until updated, will no longer consider for evaluation.

configItems.name: shot_doctrine
configItems.description: Shot doctrine to be used when giving out assignments to weapons.

configItems.name: max_firing_time
configItems.description: Maximum firing time allotted for a weapon to engage a target before the battle manager will consider it incomplete and cancel the assignment.

configItems.name: valid_units
configItems.description: This command sets printing basic evaluation information on or off.

configItems.name: valid_unit_details
configItems.description: This command sets printing detailed evaluation information on or off.

configItems.name: invalid_unit_details
configItems.description: This command sets printing of failed evaluation information on or off.

configItems.name: speed_attributes
configItems.description: attrib <name> <speed-value> [ < <= ] <speed-value>

configItems.name: altitude_attributes
configItems.description: attrib <length-value> [ < <= ] <length-value>

configItems.name: weapon_rows
configItems.description: target_pref priority [<integer>] [<target type string> “Any”] [<target subtype string> “Any”] [speed attribute] [altitude attribute] [min pk (0.1-1)] [<AI priority (integer)> <SAM priority (integer)> <Other priority (integer)>]

configItems.name: weapon_type
configItems.description: The scoring factor applied to weapon type in weapon score calculation. An integer value in the range 0 to 10.

configItems.name: weapon_subtype
configItems.description: The scoring factor applied to weapon subtype in weapon score calculation. An integer value in the range 0 to 10.

configItems.name: intercept_range
configItems.description: The scoring factor applied to weapon intercept range in weapon score calculation. An integer value in the range 0 to 10.

configItems.name: intercept_time
configItems.description: The scoring factor applied to weapon intercept time in weapon score calculation. An integer value in the range 0 to 10.

configItems.name: pk
configItems.description: The scoring factor applied to weapon probability of kill in weapon score calculation. An integer value in the range 0 to 10.

configItems.name: workload
configItems.description: The scoring factor applied to weapon work load in weapon score calculation. An integer value in the range 0 to 10.

configItems.name: max_weapon_uplinks
configItems.description: Specifies the maximum number of active uplinks the RIPR agent is capable of.

configItems.name: weapon_uplink_path
configItems.description: If a weapon uplink path is specified, then the processor will support uplinks by sending track updates over the designated comm to the fired weapon platform using tracks from the designated sensor. Uplinks can be stopped and started from script, see WsfUplinkProcessor.

configItems.name: table_for_mode
configItems.description: Indicates that the following rate definitions are for the named mode. Modes are typically used to specify the rate of consumption for various configurations (e.g., ‘cruise’). The user is responsible for changing modes either through the script interface or from custom code. If this command is not supplied then the rate definitions apply universally, and fuel mode is ignored.

configItems.name: rates
configItems.description: Specifies the altitude that the subsequent speed data is valid for. The altitude blocks must be in increasing numerical order. The consumption rate will be computed using a linear interpolation on the current altitude.

configItems.name: altitude
configItems.description: Specifies the altitude that the subsequent speed data is valid for. The altitude blocks must be in increasing numerical order. The consumption rate will be computed using a linear interpolation on the current altitude.

configItems.name: speed
configItems.description: Specifies the speed that the listed consumption rate is valid for. The speed entries must be in increasing numerical order. The consumption rate will be computed using a linear interpolation on the current altitude and speed.

configItems.name: gross_update_interval
configItems.description: Update interval for the fuse processor, when not in proximity to any platforms of interest. (The update interval may be temporarily reduced internally when close to target platforms of interest.)

configItems.name: fine_update_interval
configItems.description: Update interval for the fuse processor, when considered to be in proximity to a platform of interest. This value must be smaller than update_interval, and is used to increase the resolution and accuracy of a proximity pass to a target of interest. Appropriate values for this parameter will depend upon closing speed of the weapon. As a rough guide, allow that one fine_update_interval should elapse during the time the weapon traverses the lethal radius of the weapon.

configItems.name: time_of_flight_to_arm
configItems.description: Do not consider detonating before the specified time of flight elapses. This value is relative to when the weapon first leaves the “rail” or “pad”. This will allow a safe launch separation before arming the weapon for detonation. If a detonation is commanded (by various means) before the weapon is armed, the weapon will be removed from the simulation with no damaging effect upon any platform.

configItems.name: max_time_of_flight_to_detonate
configItems.description: Automatically detonate when the specified time of flight elapses. This value is relative to when the weapon first leaves the “rail” or “pad.” This will prevent a weapon that misses a proximity hit from flying forever.

configItems.name: detonate_below_height_msl
configItems.description: As the weapon is descending, detonate upon crossing below the specified AGL or MSL altitude.

configItems.name: detonate_above_height_msl
configItems.description: As the weapon is ascending, detonate upon crossing above the specified AGL or MSL altitude.

configItems.name: detonate_below_mach
configItems.description: As the weapon is descending and the speed is decreasing, detonate if the speed or Mach number falls below the specified value.

configItems.name: detonate_on_mach_decreasing_to
configItems.description: As the weapon accelerates, the peak Mach number is stored. After burnout, when decelerating, detonate if the Mach number falls below the specified value. Detonation is triggered _only_ after a peak Mach greater than the specified value is attained.

configItems.name: gross_proximity_range
configItems.description: This value must be specified for weapon-target proximity checks to occur. This input specifies the minimum separation distance in which the weapon is considered close to the target. During the time when a weapon is with this range of a target of interest, finer resolution time steps (see fine_update_interval) will be used to improve the accuracy of intercept determination for the weapon.

configItems.name: hit_proximity_range
configItems.description: If proximity checks are enabled (gross_proximity_range non-zero) and do_not_use_current_target is specified, this indicates the maximum range between the weapon and target’s point of closest approach in which a detonation will be triggered. If the weapon and target do not pass within this distance at their point of closest approach then the platforms will continue on without a detonation.

configItems.name: fuse_function_range
configItems.description: If non-zero, point-of-closest-approach (PCA) calculations are prematurely terminated (the fuse actions) when just inside this specified standoff range. Default is zero, which causes fusing to occur at PCA. Some small standoff is recommended when a PkTable is used, because the un-modified PCA fusing will almost always result in Azimuth and Elevation values at PCA greater than 90 degrees.

configItems.name: do_not_use_current_target
configItems.description: If proximity checks are enabled (gross_proximity_range non-zero), this specifies against which platforms proximity checks will occur. The options are, respectively:

configItems.name: proximity_all_on_loss_of_target
configItems.description: The inputs each specify what to do if use_current_target or exclusive_target_name is enabled, and then an existing target is lost. The options (respectively) are to:

configItems.name: excluded_category
configItems.description: For use only when proximity to all platforms is being considered. This input will exclude consideration of all platforms belonging to <category-name>. This command can be specified multiple times to exclude multiple categories from consideration.

configItems.name: air_to_ground_mode
configItems.description: This flag will raise the intercept value for an AGL limit by the height of a specified target type (either the current target or the specified exclusive_target_name). This is done to permit the weapon to detonate as close as possible to the center of gravity of the intended target, without artificially increasing miss distance by the vertical height of a ground target.

configItems.name: on_intercept
configItems.description: This setting allows a weapon platform to freeze and remain in the simulation after the fuse has computed an intercept condition. Normally the platform will be detonated and deleted upon intercept. If set to “halt”, then motion will freeze at the intercept location, and the fuse-controlled engagement object will be interrupted. It will be up to scripting, or some other mechanism, to Terminate() the engagement, which will then remove the weapon platform from the simulation.

configItems.name: script
configItems.description: This script is executed when the fuse is just about to detonate but prior to the assessment of weapon lethality. The weapon engagement object (available through PLATFORM.WeaponEngagement()) has been populated with the detonation reason and location.

configItems.name: wpn_server_type
configItems.description: Acceptable weapon server choices are DREAMS, WSF and VENDOR_R.

configItems.name: wpn_server_site
configItems.description: Unsigned 16-bit integer value that matches weapon server site.

configItems.name: wpn_server_application
configItems.description: Unsigned 16-bit integer value that matches weapon server application.

configItems.name: wpn_server_entity
configItems.description: Unsigned 16-bit integer value that matches weapon server entity.

configItems.name: ack_time_tolerance
configItems.description: Time allowed before the Set Data PDU to allocate the weapon is resent to the weapon server on receipt of a NACK or no reply.

configItems.name: reallocate_on_NACK
configItems.description: Keep resending even if weapon server sends a NACK signal back for a weapon. If this flag is set to false, will only try to send once, may assume the data is bad going to the weapon server.

configItems.name: debug
configItems.description: Allows some debug statements to be written to console.

configItems.name: coast_time
configItems.description: The amount of time the weapon will remain active without receiving a track update. When the coast time is reached, the weapon engagement is terminated. See also uplink_required.

configItems.name: switch_time
configItems.description: Specifies a time to intercept when the processor switches to terminal guidance.

configItems.name: switch_range
configItems.description: Specifies a range to intercept that, when reached, switches the processor to terminal guidance.

configItems.name: ignore_uplink_target_change
configItems.description: Forces the processor to ignore track messages that do not pertain to the current target.

configItems.name: uplink_required
configItems.description: Specifies if uplinked (external) track updates are required. This is used in conjunction with coast_time to decide which track sources are to be used for deciding if the coast time has been exceeded. If ‘true’, then only the time of the last received uplink is used. If ‘false’ then the maximum time of the last uplink received and the last local sensor track received is used. A value of ‘true’ would be appropriate for a command-guided weapon, with or without a terminal seeker. A value of ‘false’ would be appropriate for a track-via-missile system.

configItems.name: haveco_reporting_strategy
configItems.description: Specifies when to assess an engagement in order to report HAVCO success or failure. On_launch behavior will cause assignments to be considered complete while missiles are still in flight, and therefore may cause multiple unnecessary assignments and shots against a target.

configItems.name: ew_targets
configItems.description: When true, the weapons manager will conduct engagements against target tracks derived from an EW radar.

configItems.name: tar_targets
configItems.description: When true, the weapons manager will conduct engagements against target tracks derived from a TAR.

configItems.name: ttr_targets
configItems.description: When true, the weapons manager will conduct engagements against target tracks derived from a TTR.

configItems.name: engage_local_ttr_targets_only
configItems.description: When true, the weapons manager will conduct engagements only against targets derived from a local TTR.

configItems.name: track_quality
configItems.description: The weapons manager will conduct engagements only against tracks with a quality meeting or exceeding the value specified.

configItems.name: time_between_engagements
configItems.description: The delay between assignment engagements. For example, if the weapons manager has two different assignments and both need to be engaged at the current time, when one will be engaged, this delay will take place, then the next will be engaged. Meant to serve as a way to prevent simultaneous assignment engagements.

configItems.name: expected_sensor_acquisition
configItems.description: The delay associated with expected sensor acquisition time. This delay allows battle managers to adjust assignment time sufficiently to optimize engagement shot timelines. Assignments will be assessed and created early by an amount of time equal to this delay, which allows the IADS to acquire tracks of sufficient quality to engage targets according to an optimized timeline.

configItems.name: library
configItems.description: Set WEZ libary name.

configItems.name: tactical_range
configItems.description: When specified, the weapon manager will use the range specified by the accompanying doctrine.

configItems.name: enable
configItems.description: Enable self defense. Self defense is not currently implemented.

configItems.name: disable
configItems.description: Disable self defense.

configItems.name: range
configItems.description: Default: 0 meters

configItems.name: shot_doctrine
configItems.description: Default: Shoot-1

configItems.name: shot_expiry
configItems.description: Default: 10 seconds

configItems.name: alert_time
configItems.description: For a parked AI, alert time represents the amount of time it takes before the AI is ready to scramble.

configItems.name: assess_engage_via
configItems.description: Collision-Intercept-PT-Inside-Zone assesses engagements by evaluating if the AI can intercept the target within a FEZ, if any. Munition-Intercept-PT assesses engagements by evaluating if an AI’s weapon can currently intercept the target; Inside-Zone requires the target be inside a FEZ, if any, whereas Ignore-Zone does not use zones.

configItems.name: debug
configItems.description: When set, logs debugging information.

configItems.name: home_base_position
configItems.description: Establishes the latitude and longitude of the AI’s home base, which may be used if the AI egresses.

configItems.name: intercept_speed
configItems.description: Intercept speed is the speed at which the AI will move as it attempts to intercept a track.

configItems.name: my_place_in_formation
configItems.description: When taking action, an AI’s place in formation determines which action to perform and for which duration. For details, see the documentation for take_action above.

configItems.name: pursuit_range
configItems.description: If an AI is beginning to engage a track, and the track is within the AI’s pursuit range, the AI will pursue the track rather than intercepting it. If the AI is currently intercepting a track and comes close enough that the track falls within the pursuit range, the AI will stop intercepting and begin pursuing.

configItems.name: disable
configItems.description: When enabled, the Weapons Manager AI will assess whether to “take action” in the form of presentation versus the target while intercepting or pursuing a track.

configItems.name: action_distance
configItems.description: When evaluating whether to take action, the Weapons Manager AI will only perform an action behavior if it is within action_distance of the threat.

configItems.name: ai_action_1
configItems.description: Default: Break-Left

configItems.name: duration_1
configItems.description: Default: 3 seconds

configItems.name: ai_action_2
configItems.description: Default: Break-Right

configItems.name: duration_2
configItems.description: Default: 3 seconds

configItems.name: ai_action_3
configItems.description: Default: Straight

configItems.name: duration_3
configItems.description: Default: 0 seconds

configItems.name: ai_action_4
configItems.description: Default: Straight

configItems.name: duration_4
configItems.description: Default: 10 seconds

configItems.name: beam_duration
configItems.description: The Weapons Manager AI begins to evade a threat with a “beam response” (moving along a vector that’s 90 degrees left or right of the threat’s velocity on a horizontal plane). If the Weapons Manager AI determines that the threat has not been evaded once the beam time has elapsed, it may decide to continue evading using a “drag response” (flying away from the threat at the highest possible speed). The beam_duration determines how long the Weapons Manager AI will execute a beam response before considering a drag response.

configItems.name: sam_response_range
configItems.description: If a threat has a spatial domain of land or surface, the Weapons Manager AI will consider evasion responses relative to the threat only if the threat is within the SAM response range. If a threat has a spatial domain of subsurface, the Weapons Manager AI will also default to using the SAM response range, and an error message will be logged stating that evasion behaviors have not been properly implemented for the domain.

configItems.name: ai_response_range
configItems.description: If a threat has a spatial domain of air, the Weapons Manager AI will consider evasion responses relative to the threat only if the threat is within the AI response range. For threats with a spatial domain of space or with an unknown spatial domain, the Weapons Manager AI will also default to using the AI response range, and an error message will be logged stating that evasion behaviors have not been properly implemented for the domain.

configItems.name: restore_after_break_lock
configItems.description: The Weapons Manager AI will conclude that the platform has succesfully broken a lock by a threat that it is evading if the RWR has not received any updates corresponding to the threat for a certain amount of time. The value set by restore_after_break_lock establishes the time that must elapse after the most recent update before a lock will be considered broken.

configItems.name: priority
configItems.description: Even if the RWR senses that multiple threats are within range, the Weapons Manager AI will only evalulate whether to perform evasion behaviors relative to one threat per time step. The “priority” command allows the user to select the criteria for choosing which threat to prioritize when deciding whether to evade. “Default” simply chooses the threat that appears first in the RWR’s active track list; this method is most similar to HELIOS, but it can lead to surprising results, such as attempting to evade a threat that is barely within the response range while ignoring a much closer threat. “Choose-Closest-Threat” evaluates evasion behaviors relative to the threat that is closest to the platform.
